children.translated_text: <s>Śrī</s> (Auspiciousness)!

children.text: śukasaptatiḥ //
children.translated_text: <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: "vinodinī' saṃskṛta-hindī-vyākhyopetā //
children.translated_text: '<s>Vinodinī</s>' — with Sanskrit-Hindi commentary.

children.text: START Suk 1:
children.translated_text: START Suk 1:

children.text: praṇamya śāradāṃ devīṃ divyavijñānaśālinīm /
children.translated_text: Having bowed to the goddess <s>Śāradā</s>, who is endowed with divine wisdom,

children.text: vacmi cetovinādārthamuddhāraṃ kīrasammateḥ // Suk_1.1 (=1) //
children.translated_text: I narrate the deliverance from the parrot's assembly, for the amusement of the mind. Suk_1.1 (=1)

children.text:
asti candrapuraṃ nāma nagaram /
tatra vikramaseno nāma rājā babhūva /
tasminnagare haridatto nāma śreṣṭhī tasya bhāryā śṛṅgarasundarīnāmnī /
tatputro madanāvinodanāmā babhūva /
tasya patnī prabhāvatī /
sā somadattaśreṣṭhinaḥ kanyā /
madanavinodastu atīvaviṣayāsaktaḥ kuputraḥ pituḥ śikṣāṃ na śṛṇoti /
tasya dyūtamṛgayāveśyāmadyādiṣu atīva āsaktiḥ /
kumārgacāriṇaṃ taṃ kuputraṃ dṛṣṭvā tatpitā haridattaḥ sapatnīkaḥ atīva duḥkhitaḥ sañjātaḥ /
taṃ haridattaṃ kuputraduḥkhena pīḍitaṃ dṛṣṭvā tasya sakhā trivikramanāmā dvijaḥ svagṛhato nītinipuṇaṃ śukaṃ sārikāṃ ca gṛhītvā tadgṛhe gatvā prāha-"sakhe haridatta! enaṃ śukaṃ sapatnīkaṃ putravattvaṃ paripālaya /
etatsaṃrakṣaṇena tava duḥkhaṃ dūrībhaviṣyati' /
haridattastu taṃ śukaṃ gṛhītvā putrāya samarpayāmāsa /
madanavinodena śayanamandire svarṇapañjarasthaḥ sthāpitaḥ paripoṣitaśca /
athaikadā rahasi śuko madanaṃ prāha-
he sakhe!
children.translated_text: There is a city named <s>Candrapura</s>. There lived a king named <s>Vikramasena</s>. In that city there was a merchant named <s>Haridatta</s>, whose wife was named <s>Śṛṅgārasundarī</s>. Their son was named <s>Madanavinoda</s>. His wife was <s>Prabhāvatī</s>. She was the daughter of the merchant <s>Somadatta</s>. Now <s>Madanavinoda</s> was an extremely pleasure-addicted wicked son who did not heed his father's instructions. He had excessive attachment to gambling, hunting, courtesans, liquor, and the like. Seeing that wicked son walking the path of evil, his father <s>Haridatta</s>, together with his wife, became extremely distressed. Seeing <s>Haridatta</s> afflicted by grief over his wicked son, his friend, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Trivikrama</s>, taking from his own home a parrot skilled in moral wisdom and a <s>sārikā</s> (mynah bird), went to his house and said: 'Friend <s>Haridatta</s>! Protect this parrot together with its mate as you would a son. By guarding them, your sorrow will be removed.' <s>Haridatta</s> then took the parrot and entrusted it to his son. <s>Madanavinoda</s> placed it in a golden cage in the bedchamber and nourished it. Then one day, in private, the parrot said to <s>Madana</s>: 'O friend!

children.text: pitroste duḥkhinorduḥkhātpatatyaśrucayo bhuvi /
children.translated_text: From the tears falling to the ground born of sorrow of your grieving parents,

children.text: tena pāpena te vatsa patanaṃ devaśarmavat // Suk_1.2 (=2) //
children.translated_text: by that sin, O child, you shall fall, like <s>Devaśarman</s>.' Suk_1.2 (=2)

children.text:
sa prāha-"kathametat?' śuka āha-asti pañcapuraṃ nāma nagaram /
tatra satyaśarmā brāhmaṇaḥ /
tadbhāryā dharmaśīlānāmnī putrastu devaśarmā /
sa ca adhītavidyaḥ pitṛpracchannavṛttyā deśāntaraṃ gatvā bhāgīrathītīre tapaḥ kṛtavān /
ekadā sa tapasvī gaṅgātīre japārthamupaviṣṭaḥ /
tasminkāle kayācit balākayā uḍḍīyamānayā tadaṅgopari purīṣotsargaḥ kṛtaḥ /
sa ca tapasvī krodhākulitanetraḥ yāvadūrdhvaṃ paśyati tāvattatkrodhāgninā bhasmībhūtāṃ balākāṃ bhūmau patitāṃ dṛṣṭvā [balākāṃ dagdhvā] nārāyaṇadvijagṛhe bhikṣārthaṃ yayau /
svabhartṛśuśrūṣāparayā tatpatnyā kopābhiviṣṭo nirbhartsitaḥ satpakṣihāyamuktaśca- "nāhaṃ balākeva tvatkopasthānam' /
sa ca pracchannapātakajñānādbhīto vismitaśca, preṣitaśca tayā dharmavyādhapārśva vāraṇasīṃ nagarīṃ yayau /
tatra raktāktahastaṃ yamapratibhaṃ māṃsavikrayaṃ vidadhānaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā dṛśāmantaḥsthitaḥ /
vyādhena svāgatapraśnapūrvakaṃ svagṛhaṃ nītvā nijapitarau sabhaktikaṃ bhojayitvā paścāttasya bhojanaṃ dattam /
tadanantaraṃ sa ca vyādhaṃ jñānakāraṇaṃ papraccha-"kathaṃ satī jñānavatī, kathaṃ ca tvaṃ jñānavān' /
tena vyādhenoktam-
children.translated_text: He asked: 'How so?' The parrot said: There is a city named <s>Pañcapura</s>. There lived a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Satyaśarman</s>. His wife was named <s>Dharmaśīlā</s>, and their son was <s>Devaśarman</s>. He, having completed his studies, secretly left his parents and went to another land, where he performed austerities on the bank of the <s>Bhāgīrathī</s> (Ganges). One day, that ascetic was seated on the bank of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> for the purpose of recitation. At that time, a crane flying overhead dropped its excrement upon his body. That ascetic, with eyes clouded by anger, looked upward and saw the crane, burned to ashes by the fire of his wrath, fallen to the ground [having burned the crane]. He then went to the house of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> to beg for alms. The wife [of Nārāyaṇa], devoted to serving her husband, being occupied, rebuked him angrily and said, like one who destroys a bird: 'I am not like that crane, a target for your anger.' He, frightened and astonished by her knowledge of his hidden sin, was directed by her to the righteous hunter (<s>Dharmavyādha</s>) and went to the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>. There he saw that [hunter], with blood-stained hands, resembling <s>Yama</s> (Death), engaged in selling meat, and stood within his sight. The hunter, having first greeted him with words of welcome, took him to his own house, devoutly fed his own parents, and afterwards gave him food. Then he asked the hunter about the cause of his knowledge: 'How is that woman wise, and how are you wise?' The hunter said:

children.text: nijānvayapraṇītaṃ yaḥ samyagdharmaṃ niṣevate /
children.translated_text: He who properly follows the <s>dharma</s> (righteous conduct) established by his own lineage,

children.text: uttamādhamamadhyeṣu vikāreṣu parāṅmukhaḥ // Suk_1.3 (=3) //
children.translated_text: turning away from transformations of the highest, lowest, and middle [kinds], Suk_1.3 (=3)

children.text: sa gṛhī sa muniḥ sādhuḥ sa ca yogī sa dhārmikaḥ /
children.translated_text: he is [truly] a householder, he is a sage, a virtuous man, he is a <s>yogī</s>, he is righteous,

children.text: pitṛśuśrūṣako nityaṃ jantuḥ sādhāraṇaśca yaḥ // Suk_1.4 (=4) //
children.translated_text: a being who is always devoted to serving his parents and who is compassionate to all. Suk_1.4 (=4)

children.text:
ahaṃ sāpi ca evaṃ jñāninau tvaṃ ca nijapitarau parityajya bhramanmādṛśāṃ na sambhāṣaṇārhaḥ /
paramatithiṃ matvā jalpitaḥ /
evamuktaḥ sa brāhmaṇo vinayaparaṃ vyādhaṃ papraccha /
tenoktam-
children.translated_text: I and she are wise in this way; but you, having abandoned your own parents and wandering about, are not worthy of conversation with one like me. I have spoken [only] considering you a supreme guest.' Thus addressed, that <s>brāhmaṇa</s> asked the humble hunter [further]. He said:

children.text: na pūjayanti ye pūjyānmānyānna mānayanti ye /
children.translated_text: Those who do not honor the honorable, who do not respect the respectable,

children.text: jīvanti nindyamānāste mṛtāḥ svargaṃ na yānti ca // Suk_1.5 (=5) //
children.translated_text: they live being reviled, and when dead they do not go to heaven. Suk_1.5 (=5)

children.text: vyādhena bodhitastena sa yayau gṛhamātmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: Instructed by the hunter, he went to his own home,

children.text: abhavatkīrtimāṃlloke parataḥ kīrtibhājanam // Suk_1.6 (=6) //
children.translated_text: and became famous in this world, and [became] a recipient of glory in the next. Suk_1.6 (=6)

children.text:
tasmādvaṇigdharmaṃ svakulodbhavaṃ smara pitrośca vinayaparo bhava' /
evamuktaḥ sa madanaḥ pitarau namaskṛtya tadanujñāto bhāryāñcāpṛcchyapravahaṇamadhirūḍhaṃvān gato deśāntaram /
paścāttatpatnī katiciddināni śokayuktā nirvāhya svairiṇībhiḥ sakhībhiḥ pratibodhitā puruṣāntarābhilāṣukābhavat /
yatastābhirevamuktam-
children.translated_text: Therefore, remember the merchant's <s>dharma</s> (duty) born of your own family, and be obedient to your parents.' Thus instructed, <s>Madana</s> bowed to his parents and, having obtained their permission and taken leave of his wife, boarded a vessel and went to another land. Afterwards, his wife, having spent some days in sorrow, was persuaded by her wanton friends and became desirous of another man. For they spoke thus:

children.text: tāvatpitā tathā bandhuryāvajjīvati mānavaḥ /
children.translated_text: A father and kinsman exist only as long as a man lives;

children.text: mṛto mṛta iti jñātvā kṣaṇātsneho nivartate // Suk_1.7 (=7) //
children.translated_text: knowing that the dead are dead, affection ceases in a moment. Suk_1.7 (=7)

children.text:
atastvaṃ svapatimaprāpyamāṇā nijaśarīrasya katiciddinasthāyiyauvanasya puruṣāntararamaṇād gṛhāṇa phalam /
tatastāsāṃ vacanena puruṣāntarasya guṇacandrasaṃjñasya ramaṇāya śṛṅgāraṃ vidhāya yāvatpracalitā tāvatsārikayā mā gacchetyādivacanairnirbhartsitā /
tato yāvatsā tāṃ sārikāṃ galamoṭanapūrvaṃ vināśayati tāvaduḍḍīya yayau /
tataḥ kṣaṇaṃ sthitvā sveṣṭadevatāṃ hṛdi smṛtvā tāmbūlaṃ pragṛhya yāvaccalitā tāvat śukaḥ prāha-"siddhirastu /
kva gantavyam', ityādivākyaiḥ pṛṣṭā /
sā ca śukavacanaṃ śakunamiti kṛtvā prahasya tamāha-"he śukarāja! narāntarāsvādaṃ vijñātuṃ pracalitāsmi' /
śuka uvāca- "yuktamidaṃ karttavyameva paraṃ duṣkaraṃ ninditaṃ ca kulastrīṇām /
kiñca, tadā gamyatā yadi viparīte samāyāte sati tava buddhirasti /
yadi nāsti tadā parābhavapadaṃ bhaviṣyasi /
yataḥ-
children.translated_text: Therefore, unable to obtain your own husband, from this body whose youth lasts but a few days, seize the fruit of pleasure with another man.' Then, at their words, having adorned herself for the enjoyment of another man named <s>Guṇacandra</s>, just as she was about to leave, she was rebuked by the <s>sārikā</s> (mynah bird) with words such as 'Do not go!' Thereupon, as she was about to kill that <s>sārikā</s> by wringing its neck, it flew away. Then, pausing a moment, having remembered her chosen deity in her heart, taking <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel), just as she was about to leave, the parrot said: 'May there be success! Where are you going?' — and questioned her with such words. She, taking the parrot's words as an omen, laughed and said to him: 'O king of parrots! I have set out to experience the taste of another man.' The parrot said: 'This is fitting and should indeed be done, but it is difficult and condemned for women of good family. Moreover, go then, if when an adverse situation arises you have the wit [to handle it]. If not, you will become an object of disgrace. For:

children.text: kautukānveṣiṇo nityaṃ durjanā vyasanāgame /
children.translated_text: The wicked are always seeking curiosity at the onset of calamity,

children.text: māsopavāsinī yadvadvaṇikputrakacagrahe // Suk_1.8 (=8) //
children.translated_text: like the woman who fasted for a month [and was caught] by a merchant's son seizing her hair. Suk_1.8 (=8)

children.text: papraccha sā tadā sārdhaṃ puṃścalībhiḥ kṛtādarā /
children.translated_text: She then asked, together with the courtesans, with eagerness,

children.text: sasambhramā jagādedaṃ kimidaṃ bhāṣitaṃ śukaḥ // Suk_1.9 (=9) //
children.translated_text: and with excitement spoke thus: 'What is this that the parrot has said?' Suk_1.9 (=9)

children.text: yadi te kautukaṃ subhru parārthaṃ gaccha sundari /
children.translated_text: 'If you have curiosity, O fair-browed one, go for another's sake, O beautiful one,

children.text: sthirībhūya tvayā paścāt śrāvyeyaṃ mahatī kathā // Suk_1.10 (=10) //
children.translated_text: but having returned with composure, you must hear this great tale.' Suk_1.10 (=10)

children.text:
evaṃ śukoktaṃ śrutvā yadā sā kautukākulacetasā nijagṛha āsīnāsti tadā śukaḥ kathāṃ prāha- asti candrāvatī puro /
tasyāṃ bhīmanāmā nṛpaḥ /
tatra sudhano nāma mohanaśreṣṭhisutaḥ tannagaravāsino haridattasya kalatraṃ lakṣmīṃ rantumīhate /
tadvatsā na manyate /
tato māsopavāsinīṃ pūrṇābhidhānāṃ gatvā pūrṇadhanāvarjitāṃ kṛtvā haridatte nagarādbahirgate tadgṛhe dūtītvena preṣayāmāsa /
sāpi cāṭūktibhirlakṣmīṃ prasādayāmāsa /
prasannayā ca tayetyuktam- "yattvaṃ yācase tatkaromi" /
pūrṇayoktam- "tarhi manmataṃ naraṃ bhaja" /
tayoktam- "kulastrīṇāṃ naitadyujyate paraṃ yattavāgre pratipannaṃ tatkaromi' /
children.translated_text: Thus, having heard the parrot's words, when she sat in her own house with a mind agitated by curiosity, the parrot told a story: There is a city named <s>Candrāvatī</s>. In it there was a king named <s>Bhīma</s>. There, a man named <s>Sudhana</s>, the son of the merchant <s>Mohana</s>, desired to enjoy <s>Lakṣmī</s>, the wife of <s>Haridatta</s>, a resident of that city. But she did not consent. Then, having gone to a woman named <s>Pūrṇā</s>, who observed month-long fasts, and having won her over with wealth, when <s>Haridatta</s> had gone out of the city, he sent her to his house as a go-between. She too, with flattering words, propitiated <s>Lakṣmī</s>. And she, being pleased, said: 'Whatever you ask, I will do.' <s>Pūrṇā</s> said: 'Then accept the man I desire.' She said: 'This is not proper for women of good family; but what I have promised before you, that I will do.'

children.text: uktañca-
children.translated_text: And it is said:

children.text: chijjau sīsaṃ aha hou bandhaṇaṃ caau savvahā lacchī /
children.translated_text: Let the head be cut off, let there be imprisonment, let wealth depart entirely —

children.text: paḍivaṇṇapālaṇe supurisāṇaṃ jaṃ hou taṃ hou // Suk_1.11 (=11) //
children.translated_text: in keeping a promise, for virtuous people, whatever happens, let it happen. Suk_1.11 (=11)

children.text: [śīrṣa chidyatām atha bhavatu bandhanaṃ calatu savathā lakṣmīḥ /
children.translated_text: [Let the head be cut off, or let there be imprisonment, let wealth depart entirely —

children.text: pratipannapālane supuruṣāṇāṃ yad bhavatu tad bhavatu] // Suk_1.11* (=11*) //
children.translated_text: in keeping a promise, for virtuous people, whatever happens, let it happen.] Suk_1.11* (=11*)

children.text: tathāca
children.translated_text: And likewise,

children.text: diḍhalohasiṃkhalāṇaṃ assāṇa vivihapāsabandhāṇaṃ /
children.translated_text: Let there be firm iron chains, let there be bonds of various fetters —

children.text: tāṇaṃ cia ahiaraaro vāābandho supurisassa // Suk_1.12 (=12) //
children.translated_text: even greater than those is the bond of a word for a virtuous person. Suk_1.12 (=12)

children.text: [dṛḍhalohaśṛṅkhalānāṃ bhavatu vivadhapāśabandhanam /
children.translated_text: [Let there be firm iron chains, let there be bonds of various fetters —

children.text: tābhyāmapi adhikataro vācābandhaḥ supuruṣasya] // Suk_1.12* (=12*) //
children.translated_text: even greater than those is the bond of a word for a virtuous person.] Suk_1.12* (=12*)

children.text: adyāpi nojjhati haraḥ kila kālakūṭaṃ, kūrmo bibharti dharaṇīṃ khalu cātmapṛṣṭhe /
children.translated_text: Even now <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) does not abandon the <s>kālakūṭa</s> poison; the tortoise indeed bears the earth upon its own back;

children.text: ambhonidhirvahati duḥsahavāḍavāgnimaṅgīkṛtaṃ sukṛtinaḥ paripālayanti // Suk_1.13 (=13) //
children.translated_text: the ocean bears the unbearable submarine fire — the virtuous protect what they have undertaken. Suk_1.13 (=13)

children.text:
tacchrutvā hṛṣṭā pūrṇā /
"evamevaitat' /
tatastāṃ lakṣmīṃ pratividhāya guṇamohanārthe pradoṣe svagṛhe nināya /
tataḥ sa mohanaḥ kathitavelopari nāgataḥ kiñcitkāryādivaiyagryeṇa /
tato lakṣmyā sakāmayoktam- "yatkamapi naraṃ samānaya' /
tataḥ pūrṇayā mūḍhayā tatpatireva samānītaḥ /
svabhartari samāyāte sā kathaṃ bhavatviti kathaṃ gṛhaṃ yātviti tvaṃ sakhyastava vā kathayantu /
tā āhuḥ- "na jānīmaḥ /
tvameva kathaya' /
śuka āha- "yadi na yāsi tadā kathayāmi' /
tayoktam-- "na yāsyāmi' /
śukaḥ-sā āgacchanneva svapatiriti jñātvā taṃ kacagrahaṃ pragṛhyaivamuvāca-he śaṭha! sarvadā tvamiti mamāgre jalpasi yanme tvāṃ vinā nānyā vallabhā asti /
adhunā tu mayā parīkṣito jñātaśceti kopaṃ cakre' /
sa ca tāṃ kaṣṭena sukomalavacanairanunīya svagṛhaṃ ninye /
children.translated_text: Hearing this, <s>Pūrṇā</s> was delighted. 'So it is indeed.' Then, having prepared <s>Lakṣmī</s>, she brought her at dusk to her own house for the enjoyment of <s>Guṇamohana</s>. But that <s>Mohana</s> did not come at the appointed time due to some engagement or other. Then <s>Lakṣmī</s>, being desirous, said: 'Bring any man whatsoever.' Then the foolish <s>Pūrṇā</s> brought her very own husband. When her own husband arrived, [<s>Lakṣmī</s> wondered] 'What shall happen?' and 'How shall I go home?' — 'You, O friends, or you tell [me what to do].' They said: 'We do not know. You yourself say [what to do].' The parrot said: She, knowing that the arriving man was her own husband, seized him by the hair and spoke thus: 'O scoundrel! You always declare before me that besides me you have no other beloved. But now I have tested and found you out!' — and feigned anger. And he, with great difficulty, pacified her with very gentle words and took her home.

children.text: kathāṃ śrutvā śukenoktāṃ bhayavismayakāriṇīm /
children.translated_text: Having heard the tale told by the parrot, which caused fear and wonder,

children.text: puṃścalīvṛndasaṃyuktā suptā rātrau vaṇikpriyā // Suk_1.14 (=14) //
children.translated_text: the merchant's wife, together with the group of courtesans, slept that night. Suk_1.14 (=14)

children.text: iti śukasaptatau prathamā kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 2:
children.translated_text: START Suk 2:

children.text: sā tathaiva samaṃ tābhirdvitīyo 'hni niśāmukhe /
children.translated_text: She, in the same manner, together with them, on the second day at the approach of night,

children.text: śukamāpṛcchya calitā śukastāmidamabravīt // Suk_2.1 (=15) //
children.translated_text: having taken leave of the parrot, set out; the parrot spoke this to her: Suk_2.1 (=15)

children.text: yatheṣṭaṃ gaccha suśroṇi yadi jānāsi duḥkṛte /
children.translated_text: Go as you wish, O fair-hipped one, if you know [what to do] when a misdeed [is discovered],

children.text: pratyuttaraṃ samāyāte yaśodevīva saṅkaṭe // Suk_2.2 (=16) //
children.translated_text: [if you know] a fitting reply when [trouble] comes, like <s>Yaśodevī</s> in a predicament. Suk_2.2 (=16)

children.text:
tataḥ prabhāvato pṛcchati- "kā yaśodevī /
kadā kasminsaṅkaṭe tayā ka upāyaḥ kṛta' iti /
śukaḥ- "yadā kathayāmi tadā mayi suratavighātena tava kopaḥ prāṇaniṣūdanaḥ syāt' /
sā āha- "suhṛdāṃ sādhvasādhvapi śrotavyameva' ityanujñātaḥ śukaḥ āha- asti nandanaṃ nāma nagaram /
tatra nandano nāma rājā /
tatputro rājaśekharaḥ /
tadvadhūḥ śaśiprabhā /
tāṃ dhanasenasuto vīranāmā dṛṣṭvā sakāmaḥ san jvarapīḍito 'bhūt /
bhojanādi na vidhatte /
sa ca mātrā yaśodevyā pṛṣṭaḥ sansagadgadaṃ kāraṇamāha- "sā ca rājakanyā durlabhā /
sa kathaṃ jīvatu' iti praśnaḥ /
tayoktam- "tvameva kathaya' /
śukaḥ-yadi prabhāvati! adya na yāsi tadā kathayāmi, ityukte sā āha- "kathayeti' /
atha śukaḥ-sā yaśodevī ekāṃ śunīṃ bhojanādyairāvarjayitvā ābharaṇāni paridhāyātmanā sārdhaṃ gṛhītvā śaśiprabhāpārśve gatvā tāṃ vijane sagadgadā jagāda-ahaṃ ca tvaṃ ca iyaṃ ca pūrvabhave bhaginyo 'bhūvan /
mayā niḥśaṅkayā tvayā tu saśaṅkayā paranarābhilāṣaḥ pūritaḥ /
anayā tu naiva /
ato 'syāḥ śīlaprabhāvātkevalaṃ jātismaraṇameva na bhogāḥ śunikā ca sañjātā /
sambhogavighnājjātismaraṇaṃ ca na te vartate /
mama punarbhogānnirvighnānnirvighnajātismaraṇaṃ ca /
ato 'hamanukampayā imāṃ śunakīṃ tvāṃ ca dṛṣṭvā kathayitumāgatā /
atastvayārthināṃ kāṅkṣitaṃ dātavyameva /
yo dānaṃ kuryātsa bhavetsarvasampadāṃ sthānam /
uktañca--
children.translated_text: Then <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asks: 'Who is <s>Yaśodevī</s>? When and in what difficulty did she employ what stratagem?' The parrot [says]: 'When I tell the story, your anger at the interruption of lovemaking will be fatal to me.' She says: 'One must listen to what friends say, whether good or bad.' Thus permitted, the parrot says: There is a city called <s>Nandana</s>. There [lives] a king named <s>Nandana</s>. His son is <s>Rājaśekhara</s>. His wife is <s>Śaśiprabhā</s>. <s>Dhanasena</s>'s son, named <s>Vīra</s>, having seen her and become desirous, fell ill with fever. He does not take food and such. Asked by his mother <s>Yaśodevī</s>, he stammered out the reason: 'But she is a royal princess, unattainable. How can he live?' — that is the question. She said: 'You yourself tell [me].' The parrot [says]: 'If, O <s>Prabhāvatī</s>, you do not go today, then I shall tell.' She says: 'Tell [me].' Then the parrot [continues]: That <s>Yaśodevī</s>, having won over a female dog with food and such, adorned it with ornaments, and taking it with her, went to <s>Śaśiprabhā</s>'s side. In private, she spoke to her with a choked voice: 'I, you, and this one were sisters in a former birth. I, being without shame, and you, being with shame, fulfilled [our] desire for other men. But this one did not at all. Therefore, by the power of her chastity, she obtained only the memory of past births but not pleasures, and was born as a female dog. Because of the obstruction of pleasures, the memory of past births does not exist for you either. But for me, because pleasures were unobstructed, there is unobstructed memory of past births. Therefore, out of compassion, I have come to tell [this], having seen this female dog and you. Therefore, you should give to those who desire what they wish. One who gives becomes the abode of all prosperities.' And it is said —

children.text: kathayanti na yācante bhikṣāhārā gṛhe gṛhe /
children.translated_text: They tell [their needs] but do not beg, subsisting on alms, going from house to house;

children.text: arthibhyo dīyatāṃ nityamadātuḥ phalamīdṛśam // Suk_2.3 (=17) //
children.translated_text: Let it always be given to the needy — such is the fruit of not giving.

children.text:
tataḥ śaśiprabhā sakaṇṭhagrāhaṃ ruditvā prāha-- "māmapi kalyāṇi! puruṣāntareṇa yojaya' /
tato yaśodevī tāṃ svasthīkṛtya bhartṛviditāṃ svagṛhaṃ nītvā svaputreṇa yojayāmāsa /
sa ca rājaśekharo dravyādidānatoṣitaḥ sakhīyamiti kṛtvā na nivārayāmāsa /
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śaśiprabhā</s>, having wept with a choking throat, said: 'O virtuous one, unite me too with another man!' Then <s>Yaśodevī</s>, having reassured her and brought her to her own house with her husband's knowledge, united her with her own son. And <s>Rājaśekhara</s>, gratified by gifts of wealth and such, thinking 'this is [just] friendship,' did not prevent [it].

children.text: rājaputraṃ rājaputrīṃ pratāryaivaṃ ca bhāmini /
children.translated_text: Having thus deceived the prince and the princess, O beautiful one,

children.text: yaśodevyā mahadbuddhya nijakāryamanuṣṭhitam // Suk_2.4 (=18) //
children.translated_text: <s>Yaśodevī</s> accomplished her own purpose through great intelligence.

children.text: buddhirasti yadaiṣā te vraja subhru parāntikam /
children.translated_text: If you possess such intelligence, then go to your lover's side;

children.text: bhaja nidrāṃ viśālākṣi mānyathā svaṃ viḍambaya // Suk_2.5 (=19) //
children.translated_text: Embrace sleep, O large-eyed one — do not otherwise make a fool of yourself.

children.text: iti śukakathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text: Thus, having heard the parrot's tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau dvitīyā kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the second tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s>.

children.text: START Suk 3:
children.translated_text: Beginning of the third tale of the <s>Śukasaptati</s>:

children.text:
athānyadine prabhāvatī śukaṃ pṛcchati /
śukaḥ-
children.translated_text: Then on another day, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asks the parrot. The parrot [says] —

children.text: gaccha deva kimāścaryaṃ yatra te ramate manaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Go, lady, what is the wonder, wherever your mind delights;

children.text: nṛpavadyadi jānāsi paritrāṇaṃ tvamātmanaḥ // Suk_3.1 (=20) //
children.translated_text: If you know, like a king, how to protect yourself.'

children.text:
prabhāvatī pṛcchati-kathametat /
śukaḥ kathayati-asti viśālā nagarī /
tatra sudarśano rājā /
tatra ca vimalo nāma vaṇik /
tasya ca patnīdvayaṃ subhagaṃ rūpasampannaṃ dṛṣṭvā kuṭilanāmā dhūrtastadbhāryādvayagrahaṇecchayā ambikāṃ devīmārādhya vimalarūpaṃ yayāce /
labdhvā ca tatprakṛtiṃ vimale bahirgate tadgṛhaṃ gatvā prabhutvaṃ cakāra /
prasādadhanadānairvaśīkṛto 'khilo 'pi parijanavargaḥ /
tadbhāryādvayaṃ bahumānadānādinā santoṣya svecchayā bhuṅkte /
vimalo 'yaṃ dhanādyanityatāṃ śrutvā dātā babhūveti parijano 'navarataṃ cintayati /
atha satyavimalo 'pi dvāramāgataḥ kuṭilājñayā dvārapālena niṣiddhaḥ /
tato bahiḥsthaḥ phutkaroti "vañcito 'haṃ dhūrtarājena' /
tasya caivaṃ krandato gotrajā janāḥ kautukācca militāḥ /
tatkṣaṇāt haṭṭāni muktvā vaṇiksārtho militvā ārakṣikamantrimukhyānāṃ purataḥ phūccakre /
"rājanvañcito 'smi dhūrtarājena' /
tato rājñā tadavalokanāya prahitāḥ puruṣāḥ /
tenāpi te dravyādidānena sānukūlāḥ kṛtāḥ /
taṃ dhanadāyakaṃ gṛhe dṛṣṭvā jano vadati-"svāminvimalo gṛhe vidyate /
ayaṃ ca dhūrtarāṭ dvārasthaḥ' /
tato nṛpeṇa dvāvapyekatra kṛtau /
tato dvayormadhyānna ko 'pi dhūrtetarayorvyaktiṃ jānāti /
jātaḥ kolāhalo 'khilalokavyavahāranāśakaro rājñaścapavādaḥ /
yato rājñāṃ duṣṭanigrahaḥ śiṣṭapālanaṃ ca svargāya /
uktañca-
children.translated_text: And it is said —

children.text: prajāpīḍanasantāpātsamudbhūto hutāśanaḥ /
children.translated_text: The fire born from the torment of afflicting subjects

children.text: rājñaḥ kulaṃ śriyaṃ prāṇānnādagdhvā vinivartate // Suk_3.2 (=21) //
children.translated_text: Does not turn back without burning the king's lineage, prosperity, and life.

<s>Prabhāvatī</s> asks: 'How is this [to be understood]?' The parrot tells: There is a city called <s>Viśālā</s>. There [rules] King <s>Sudarśana</s>. And there [lives] a merchant named <s>Vimala</s>. A rogue named <s>Kuṭila</s>, having seen his two beautiful and handsome wives, worshipped the goddess <s>Ambikā</s> and begged for <s>Vimala</s>'s form, desiring to seize his two wives. Having obtained it and [assuming] his appearance, when <s>Vimala</s> had gone out, he went to his house and exercised authority. The entire household was brought under control through gifts of favors and wealth. Having satisfied his two wives through great honor and gifts, he enjoyed [them] at his pleasure. The household constantly thought: 'This <s>Vimala</s>, having heard of the impermanence of wealth, has become a giver.' Then the real <s>Vimala</s> arrived at the door [but] was prevented [from entering] by the doorkeeper on <s>Kuṭila</s>'s order. Standing outside, he cried out: 'I have been cheated by the rogue-king!' As he wailed thus, kinsmen gathered, and out of curiosity [others too]. At that very moment, merchants abandoned their shops, assembled together, and protested before the chief ministers and police officers: 'O king, I have been cheated by the rogue-king!' Then the king sent men to investigate. But [<s>Kuṭila</s>] also won them over with gifts of wealth. The people, seeing the generous one in the house, said: 'Sir, <s>Vimala</s> is in the house; this one standing at the door is the rogue-king.' Then the king brought both together in one place. Between the two, no one could tell which was the rogue and which the real one. An uproar arose, destroying all public transactions, bringing reproach upon the king — for the punishment of the wicked and protection of the good leads kings to heaven.

children.text:
tato rājā ekānte tayornirṇayamacintayat /
tatkathaya kathaṃ niścayaḥ syāditi praśnaḥ /
śukaḥ-sa rājā labdhopāyastadvimalabhāryādvayaṃ pṛthakpṛthaksaṃsthāpya pṛṣṭavān-"kiṃ yuvayoḥ pāṇigrahaṇe bhartrā vibhūṣaṇaṃ pradattaṃ dhanaṃ ca /
paścātkiṃ jalpitaṃ prathamasaṅgena ca kā vārttā bhartrā sahābhūt /
kā mātā kaśca pitā /
kiṃ kulam /
kā jātiḥ' /
ityevaṃ pṛṣṭābhyāṃ yathālabdhaṃ yathāvṛttaṃ yathāproktaṃ yathāsuptaṃ sarvaṃ tābhyāṃ kathitam /
paścātu tau puruṣau pṛṣṭau parasparaṃ visaṃvadantau /
tato bhāryādvayasya rukmiṇīsundarīnāmadheyasya yaḥ saṃvādaṃ vadati sa satyaḥ /
itarastu dhūrto rājñā nirvāsitaḥ /
children.translated_text: The other, being a rogue, was banished by the king.

children.text: satyastu rājñā sabhāryaḥ saskṛtaḥ svagṛhaṃ gataḥ /
children.translated_text: The true [<s>Vimala</s>] was honored by the king and went home with his wives.

children.text: iti mahārājabuddhiḥ /
children.translated_text: Such is the wisdom of a great king.

children.text: iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā //
children.translated_text: Thus, having heard the tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

Then the king privately pondered the judgment between the two. 'Tell me how a determination can be made' — this is the question. The parrot [says]: That king, having found a stratagem, stationed <s>Vimala</s>'s two wives separately and asked [each]: 'What ornaments and wealth did your husband give at your wedding? What was said afterward? What was the conversation during the first union with your husband? Who is [your] mother and who is [your] father? What is [your] family? What is [your] caste?' When thus questioned, both told everything as it had been received, as it had happened, as it had been spoken, and as it had been experienced. But afterward, when the two men were questioned, they contradicted each other. Then, of the two wives named <s>Rukmiṇī</s> and <s>Sundarī</s>, whichever [man's account] agreed [with theirs] was the true [<s>Vimala</s>].

children.text: iti śukasaptatau tṛtīyā kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the third tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s>.

children.text: START Suk 4 :
children.translated_text: Beginning of the fourth tale of the <s>Śukasaptati</s>:

children.text:
athānyadā prabhāvatī śukaṃ pṛcchati /
śukaḥ-"māṃ kṛtāvajñaṃ kṛtvā mā gaccha /
yato bālakādapi hitaṃ vākyaṃ grāhyam /
children.translated_text: Then on another day, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asks the parrot. The parrot [says]: 'Do not go, having treated me with contempt — for even from a child, beneficial words should be accepted.

children.text: kṛtāvajñaḥ purā devi vṛddhavākyaparāṅmukhaḥ /
children.translated_text: Formerly, O queen, a brahmin who treated [the wise] with contempt and turned away from the words of the elders

children.text: patito brāhmaṇo 'narthe viṣakanyāvivāhane // Suk_4.1 (=22) //
children.translated_text: Fell into misfortune through marriage with a poison-maiden.'

children.text:
prabhāvatī pṛcchati-"kathametat" /
śukaḥ-asti somaprabhaṃ nāma dvijasthānam /
tatra vidvāndhārmikaḥ somaśarmā nāma vipraḥ /
tatputrī rūpaudāryaguṇopetā viṣakanyeti vijñātābhūt /
tena tāṃ bhayena ko 'pi na vivāhayati /
tataḥ somaśarmā varārthaṃ bhuvaṃ paryaṭan samprāpto dvijasthānaṃ janasthāna nāma /
tatra govindanāmā brāhmaṇo jaḍo nirdhanaśca /
tasmai kanyā pradattā /
tena suhṛdāṃ nivārayatāmapi kṛtāvajñenoḍhā sarvarūpalāvaṇyaguṇopetā mohinī viṣakanyā /
sā vidagdhā govindastu mūrkhaḥ laghuvayāśca /
tataśca sā ātmano rūpalāvaṇyayauvanaṃ śuśoca /
children.translated_text: <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asks: 'How is this [to be understood]?' The parrot [says]: There is a brahmin settlement called <s>Somaprabha</s>. There [lives] a learned and righteous brahmin named <s>Somaśarman</s>. His daughter, endowed with beauty, generosity, and virtue, became known as a <s>viṣakanyā</s> (poison-maiden). Therefore, no one would marry her out of fear. Then <s>Somaśarman</s>, wandering the earth in search of a groom, arrived at a brahmin settlement called <s>Janasthāna</s>. There [lives] a brahmin named <s>Govinda</s>, who is dull-witted and poor. The girl was given to him. Despite friends trying to dissuade him, the contemptuous [<s>Govinda</s>] married the enchanting poison-maiden endowed with all beauty and charm. She was clever, but <s>Govinda</s> was a fool and of young age. Then she lamented her own beauty, charm, and youth.

children.text: avidagdhaḥ patiḥ strīṇāṃ, prauḍhānāṃ nāyako 'guṇī /
children.translated_text: A dull-witted husband for women, an unworthy leader of the mature,

children.text: guṇināṃ tyāgināṃ stoko vibhavaśceti duḥkhakṛt // Suk_4.2 (=23) //
children.translated_text: And scant wealth for the generous and those who renounce — these cause suffering.

children.text: pāusasamaapavāso jovvaṇadiahe tahā a dāliddaṃ /
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] Exile in the rainy season, poverty in the days of youth,

children.text: paḍhamasiṇehavioo tiṇi vi garuāidukkhāiṃ // Suk_4.3 (=24) //
children.translated_text: And separation from one's first love — these three are heavy sorrows.

children.text: [pravṛṭsamayapravāso yauvanadivase tathā ca dāridryam /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit chāyā:] Exile during the rains, poverty in the days of youth,

children.text: prathamasnehaviyogastrīṇyapi gurukāṇi duḥkhāni] // Suk_4.24* (=24*) //
children.translated_text: And separation from one's first love — these three are indeed heavy sorrows.

children.text: appatthāve paḍhiaṃ kaṇṭhavihūṇaṃ ca gāiaṃ gīaṃ /
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] Study at an inappropriate time, song sung without a voice,

children.text: mā mā bhaṇanti suraaṃ tiṇi vi garuāi dukkhāiṃ // Suk_4.4 (=25) //
children.translated_text: And lovemaking while she says 'no, no' — these three are heavy sorrows.

children.text: [aprastāve paṭhitaṃ kaṇṭhavihīnaṃ ca gāyanaṃ gītam /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit chāyā:] Study at an inappropriate time, song sung without a voice,

children.text: mā mā bhaṇantyāṃ surataṃ trīṇyapi gurukāṇi duḥkhāni] // Suk_4.4* (=25*) //
children.translated_text: And lovemaking while she says 'no, no' — these three are indeed heavy sorrows.

children.text:
sānyadā govindaṃ patimityabravīt-"mama piturgehātsamāgatāyā bahūni dināni sañjātāni /
tato 'haṃ tvayaiva saha gamiṣye nānyathā' /
tataḥ śakaṭaṃ mārgayitvā sabhāryakaḥ sa calitaḥ /
yāvatprayāti tāvatpathi eko yuvā vāggmī surūpaḥ śūraśca viṣṇunāmā brāhmaṇo militaḥ /
children.translated_text: As they traveled, on the path they met a young man — eloquent, handsome, and brave — a brahmin named <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: tasya brāhmaṇasya tasyāścānyonmanurāgaḥ sañjātaḥ /
children.translated_text: Between that brahmin and her, a mutual infatuation arose.

children.text: uktañca- prītiḥ syāddarśanādyaiḥ prathamamatha manaḥsaṅgasaṅkalpabhāvo, nidrāchedastanutvaṃ vapuṣi kaluṣatā cendriyāṇāṃ nivṛttiḥ /
children.translated_text: And it is said: First comes attraction through sight and such, then mental attachment and imaginings, loss of sleep, thinness of body, dullness of the senses, and withdrawal;

children.text: hrīnāśonmādamūrcchāmaraṇamiti jagadyātyavasthā deśaitāḥ, lagnairyatpuṣpabāṇaiḥ sa jayati madanaḥ sannirastānyadhanvī // Suk_4.5 (=26) //
children.translated_text: Then loss of shame, madness, fainting, and death — the world passes through these ten stages, struck by the flower-arrows of <s>Madana</s> (the god of love), who conquers, having vanquished all other archers.

She once said to her husband <s>Govinda</s>: 'Many days have passed since I came from my father's house. Therefore, I shall go only with you, not otherwise.' Then, having procured a cart, he set out with his wife.

children.text:
sa pathiko dampatyoḥ pūgapatroccayaṃ dadāti /
ityevaṃ grāmyabrāhmaṇorohaviṣṇorviśvastaḥ ātmano nirodhasaṅgabhayāduttīrya ta gantrīvāhamārohayati /
viṣṇunā ca patyau vṛkṣāntaragate sā mohino bhuktā ātmavaśīkṛtā /
tayā cātmīyaṃ nāma gotraṃ kulakramaṃ cājñāpitaḥ /
patyuśca samāgatasya "tvaṃ coro 'sīti' gantryārohaṇaṃ kuvato niṣedhaḥ kṛtaḥ /
viṣṇurapi tāṃ kṛhītvā govindaṃ dharṣitavān /
tatastayoḥ keśākeśi saṃvṛttam /
govindastu viṣṇunā viṣakanyāprabhāveṇa nirjitaḥ /
tatastāṃ gṛhītvā viṣṇuḥ svagṛhaṃ praticalitaḥ /
govindaḥ pṛṣṭhastho mārgāsanne grāme gatvā phūtkṛtavān-"yadanena caureṇa mama bhāryā gṛhītā /
trāyatāṃ tām /
mama śaraṇaṃ bho janāḥ' /
atha grāmādhipena viṣṇurmohinīyuto dhṛtaḥ /
pṛṣṭenottaraṃ dattaṃ viṣṇunā yatheyaṃ mayā pariṇītā /
madīyāṃ ca bhāryāmeṣa pathiko mārge dṛṣṭvā grahilo babhūva /
govindenāpi pṛṣṭena idamevottaritam /
tato mantrī tayorekamevottaraṃ śratvā jātyādikaṃ pṛṣṭavān /
trayamapi tu saṃvadati tataḥ kathaṃ niścayaḥ" /
iti śukapraśnaḥ /
tatastayā pṛṣṭaḥ śuka āha-mantriṇoktam, "kiyanti dināni saṅgamasya yuṣmākaṃ prayāṇe" /
tairuktam-"kalye bhojanāntaraṃ saṃvṛttaḥ samāgamaḥ' /
tato mantriṇā brāhmaṇau pṛthakpṛthakpṛṣṭau-"kimanayā kalye bhojanavelāyāṃ bhuktam' /
yacca tayā bhuktaṃ tadgovindo jānāti itarastu na /
tataḥ sa viḍambitaḥ sacivena /
gonindaḥ śikṣitaḥ /
dhigimāṃ brāhmaṇīṃ paratreha ca duḥkhadāṃ muñca śīghram /
uktañca-
children.translated_text: That traveler gives the couple betel leaves and nut preparations. Thus, the rustic brahmin having become trusting of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, [<s>Viṣṇu</s>], overcoming his fear of being caught, makes him climb a carriage-pole. And when the husband had gone behind a tree, <s>Viṣṇu</s> enjoyed <s>Mohinī</s> and brought her under his control. And she informed him of her own name, lineage, and family succession. When the husband returned, [<s>Viṣṇu</s>] prevented him from climbing the carriage, [saying] 'You are a thief!' <s>Viṣṇu</s>, having seized her, overpowered <s>Govinda</s>. Then there was a hair-pulling fight between them. But <s>Govinda</s> was defeated by <s>Viṣṇu</s> through the poison-maiden's power. Then <s>Viṣṇu</s>, taking her, set out for his own home. <s>Govinda</s>, following behind, went to a village near the road and cried out: 'This thief has seized my wife! Save her! Help me, O people!' Then <s>Viṣṇu</s>, together with <s>Mohinī</s>, was apprehended by the village chief. When questioned, <s>Viṣṇu</s> replied that she was married to him. 'This traveler, having seen my wife on the road, became covetous.' <s>Govinda</s> too, when questioned, gave this very same answer. Then the minister, hearing one and the same answer from both, asked about caste and other details. But all three [accounts] agreed. 'Then how can a determination be made?' — this is the parrot's question. Then, when asked by her, the parrot says: The minister said, 'How many days [have passed] since your union [and] your journey?' They said: 'The union took place yesterday during mealtime.' Then the minister questioned the two brahmins separately: 'What did she eat yesterday at mealtime?' What she ate, <s>Govinda</s> knew, but the other did not. Thus he [<s>Viṣṇu</s>] was exposed by the minister. <s>Govinda</s> was admonished: 'Shame on this brahmin woman who gives suffering both here and hereafter — release her at once!' And it is said —

children.text: vaidyaṃ pānarataṃ naṭaṃ kupaṭhitaṃ mūrkhaṃ parivrājakaṃ yodhaṃ kāpuruṣaṃ viṭaṃ vivayasaṃ svādhyāyahīnaṃ dvijam /
children.translated_text: A physician addicted to drink, an actor who recites poorly, a foolish mendicant, a warrior who is a coward, an old libertine, a brahmin devoid of Vedic study,

children.text: rājyaṃ bālanarendramantrirahitaṃ mitraṃ chalānveṣi ca bhāryāṃ yauvanagarvitāṃ pararatāṃ muñcanti ye paṇḍitāḥ // Suk_4.6 (=27) //
children.translated_text: A kingdom with a child-king and no minister, a friend who seeks to deceive, and a wife proud of her youth and devoted to others — the wise abandon [all of] these.

children.text: tathāpi kāminīlubdho dhikkṛtaḥ sādhubhistadā /
children.translated_text: Even so, the one lusting after the woman, though condemned by the virtuous then,

children.text: tāmevādāya calitastatkṛte nihataḥ pathi // Suk_4.7 (=28) //
children.translated_text: Took her and departed — and was killed on the road on her account.

children.text: taddevi yaḥ karotyevamavajñāṃ vṛddhaśikṣitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, O queen, one who thus shows contempt, having been instructed by elders,

children.text: sa parābhavamāpnoti govindo brāhmaṇo yathā // Suk_4.8 (=29) //
children.translated_text: Meets with ruin, just as the brahmin <s>Govinda</s> did.

children.text: iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā //
children.translated_text: Having heard this story, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau caturtho kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s>.

children.text: START Suk 5:
children.translated_text: Beginning of the 5th tale:

children.text:
punaranyadine sā gamanāya śukaṃ pṛcchati /
śukaḥ-
children.translated_text: On another day, she asks the parrot for permission to go. The parrot says—

children.text: gaccha devi vijānāsi yadi kartuṃ tvamuttaram /
children.translated_text: Go, O lady, if you know how to give an answer,

children.text: sabhāyāṃ nṛpateryadvadviṣame bālapaṇḍitā // Suk_5.1 (=30) //
children.translated_text: as <s>Bālapaṇḍitā</s> did in the king's court in a difficult situation.

children.text:
prabhāvatīpṛṣṭaḥ śukaḥ kathāṃ prāha-asti ujjayinī nāma nagarī /
tatra vikramādityo rājā /
tasya rājño kāmalīlā nāma uttamakule jātā /
sā ca rājño 'tīva vallabhā /
ekadā nṛpastayā sārdhaṃ bhojanaṃ kurvanbhṛṣṭamatsyāṃstasyai dāpayāmāsa /
sā āha-svāmin! nāhametānpuruṣānavalokayitumapi samarthā kiṃ punaḥ sparśanam /
iti śṛtvā matsyā aṭṭahāsena tathā jahasuryathā nāgarikaloke śrutam /
rājā ca tanmatsyahāsyakāraṇaṃ mantrijyotirvicchākunikakovidānpṛcachati /
yadā na ko 'pi jānāti tadā sarvadvijāgresaraṃ purohitaṃ prāha-yathā tvayaiva matsyahāsyakāraṇaṃ kathanīyamanyathātvaṃ deśānnirvāsaṃ prāpnoṣi /
purodhā apyetadvacaḥ śrutvā dinapañcakaṃ vyavadhāne yācayitvā saviṣādo gṛhamagamat /
sa purohitaḥ taduttaramajānanpurastādrājñā nirvāsyate /
sa kathaṃ bhavatviti praśnaḥ /
uttaramapyāha śukaḥ-sa brāhmaṇo viṣādāpannaḥ putryā bālapaṇḍitayā babhāṣe, tāta! kathamudvignacitta iva lakṣyase /
kathaya viṣādasya kāraṇam /
vidvadbhirvipadyapyuccaiḥ sthātavyam /
uktañca-
children.translated_text: Asked by <s>Prabhāvatī</s>, the parrot told the story— There is a city called <s>Ujjayinī</s>. There ruled King <s>Vikramāditya</s>. His queen was named <s>Kāmalīlā</s>, born of a noble family, and she was exceedingly dear to the king. One day, while dining with her, the king had fried fish served to her. She said— "My lord! I am not even able to look at these males, let alone touch them." Hearing this, the fish burst into such loud laughter that it was heard throughout the city. The king asked his ministers, astrologers, augurs, and experts the reason for the fish's laughter. When no one knew, he told the chief priest, foremost among all the Brahmins— "You must explain the reason for the fish's laughter, otherwise you shall be banished from the kingdom." The priest, hearing these words, requested a delay of five days and went home full of sorrow. That priest, not knowing the answer, would be banished by the king. How could this be resolved? That is the question. The parrot also gave the answer— That Brahmin, stricken with grief, was addressed by his daughter <s>Bālapaṇḍitā</s>: "Father! Why do you appear so troubled in mind? Tell me the cause of your sorrow. The wise should hold their heads high even in misfortune." And it is said—

children.text: sampadi yasya na harṣo vipadi viṣādo raṇe ca bhīrutvam /
children.translated_text: He in whom there is no elation in prosperity, no despair in adversity, and no cowardice in battle—

children.text: taṃ bhuvanatrayatilakaṃ jananī janayati sutaṃ viralam // Suk_5.2 (=31) //
children.translated_text: such a rare son, the jewel of the three worlds, does his mother bring forth.

children.text:
tato brāhmaṇo 'viralaṃ vṛttāntamācaṣṭe anena kāraṇena rājā māṃ nāgarānnirvāsayati /
yataḥ-
children.translated_text: Then the Brahmin related the whole matter without reserve— "For this reason the king will banish me from the city. Because—"

children.text: na sauhṛdaṃ na viśvāso na sneho na ca bandhutā /
children.translated_text: There is no friendship, no trust, no affection, and no kinship

children.text: kenāpi saha saṃsāre kuto rājñā chalārthinā // Suk_5.3 (=32) //
children.translated_text: with anyone in this world— how much less with a king who seeks pretexts!

children.text: uktañca-
children.translated_text: And it is said—

children.text: kāke śaucaṃ dyūtakāre ca satyaṃ sarpe kṣāntiḥ strīṣu kāmopaśāntiḥ /
children.translated_text: Cleanliness in a crow, truthfulness in a gambler, patience in a serpent, cessation of desire in women,

children.text: klībe dhairyaṃ madyape tattvacintā rājā mitraṃ kena dṛṣṭaṃ śrutaṃ vā // Suk_5.4 (=33) //
children.translated_text: courage in a eunuch, contemplation of truth in a drunkard— who has ever seen or heard of a king being a friend?

children.text: kiñca- nadīnāṃ nakhināñcaiva śṛṅgiṇāṃ śastrapāṇinām /
children.translated_text: Moreover— Of rivers, of those with claws, of those with horns, and of those who bear weapons,

children.text: viśvāso naiva kartavyaḥ śtrīṣu rājakuleṣu ca // Suk_5.5 (=34) //
children.translated_text: one should never place trust— nor in women, nor in royal families.

children.text: bhoginaḥ kañcukāsaktāḥ krūrāḥ kuṭilagaminaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who possess hoods, who are encased in skin, who are cruel, who move crookedly,

children.text: duḥkhopasarpaṇīyāśca rājāno bhujagā iva // Suk_5.6 (=35) //
children.translated_text: and who are difficult to approach— kings are like serpents.

children.text: hasannapi nṛpo hanti mānayannapi durjanaḥ /
children.translated_text: A king kills even while laughing; a wicked person harms even while honoring;

children.text: spṛśannapi gajo hanti jighrannapi bhujaṅgamaḥ // Suk_5.7 (=36) //
children.translated_text: an elephant kills even while caressing; a snake kills even while smelling.

children.text:
eṣa rājā ā bālyātsevito 'pi mayi viparīto babhūva /
tasmānmayā jīvitumicchatā dvijaiḥ saha paradeśaṃ gantavyam /
uktañca-
children.translated_text: This king, though served by me since childhood, has turned against me. Therefore, wishing to live, I must go to another land with the Brahmins. And it is said—

children.text: tyajedekaṃ kulasyārthe grāmasyārthe kulaṃ tyajet /
children.translated_text: One should abandon one person for the sake of the family; one should abandon a family for the sake of the village;

children.text: grāmaṃ janapadasyārthe ātmārthe pṛthivīṃ tyajet // Suk_5.8 (=37) //
children.translated_text: one should abandon a village for the sake of the country; and for the sake of oneself, one should abandon the whole earth.

children.text:
tataḥ sā bālikā tātavacanaṃ śrutvā prāha-tāta! tvayā yuktamuktam /
paraṃ svāmirahitānāṃ na kvāpi pūjā /
yata uktam-
children.translated_text: Then that girl, having heard her father's words, said— "Father! What you say is reasonable. But those without a master are honored nowhere. As it is said—"

children.text: apradhānaḥ pradhānaḥ syādyadi seveta pārthivam /
children.translated_text: An insignificant person becomes important if he serves a king;

children.text: pradhāno 'pyapradhānaḥ syādyadi sevāvivarjitaḥ // Suk_5.9 (=38) //
children.translated_text: even an important person becomes insignificant if he is devoid of service.

children.text: āsannameva nṛpatirbhajate manuṣyaṃ vidyāvihīnamakulīnamasaṃstutaṃ vā /
children.translated_text: A king favors the person who is near him, even if unlearned, lowborn, or unrenowned;

children.text: prāyeṇa bhūmipatayaḥ pramadā latāśca yaḥ pārśvato bhavati taṃ pariveṣṭayanti // Suk_5.10 (=39) //
children.translated_text: generally, kings, women, and creeping vines embrace whoever is at their side.

children.text: ārohanti śanairmṛtyā dhunvantamapi pārthivam /
children.translated_text: Slowly they mount upon a king, even one who shakes them off;

children.text: kopaprasādavastūnāṃ vicinvanti samīpagāḥ // Suk_5.11 (=40) //
children.translated_text: those who remain near him examine the grounds of his anger and favor.

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And likewise—

children.text: vidyāvatāṃ mahecchānāṃ śilpavikramaśālinām /
children.translated_text: For the learned, for those of great ambition, for those skilled in arts and valor,

children.text: sevāvṛttividāñcaiva nāśrayaḥ pārthivaṃ vinā // Suk_5.12 (=41) //
children.translated_text: and for those who live by service— there is no refuge without a king.

children.text: ye jātyādimahotsāhā nopagacchanti pārthivam /
children.translated_text: Those who, though born of noble lineage and great enthusiasm, do not approach a king—

children.text: teṣāmāmaraṇaṃ bhikṣā prāyāścittaṃ vinirmitam // Suk_5.13 (=42) //
children.translated_text: for them, begging until death has been ordained as their penance.

children.text: rogairgrahairnṛpargraisto yo na vetti jaḍakriyaḥ /
children.translated_text: One who, afflicted by diseases, planets, and the king's seizure, does not know, being dull in action,

children.text: madhyamantramupāyaṃ ca so 'vaśyaṃ tāta na sthiraḥ // Suk_5.14 (=43) //
children.translated_text: the counsel, the mantra, and the stratagem— he, O father, is surely not steadfast.

children.text: uktañca-
children.translated_text: And it is said—

children.text: sarpānvyāghrān gajānsiṃhāndṛṣṭvopāyairvaśīkṛtān /
children.translated_text: Seeing that serpents, tigers, elephants, and lions have been subdued by stratagems,

children.text: rājeti kiyatī mātrā dhīmatāmapramādinām // Suk_5.15 (=44) //
children.translated_text: what great matter is a king for the wise and vigilant?

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And likewise—

children.text: rājānameva saṃśritya vidvānyāti paronnatim /
children.translated_text: Only by depending on a king does a learned person attain great eminence;

children.text: vinā malayamanyatra candanaṃ na vivardhate // Suk_5.16 (=45) //
children.translated_text: sandalwood does not flourish anywhere other than the <s>Malaya</s> mountains.

children.text: dhavalānyātapatrāṇi vājinaśca manoramāḥ /
children.translated_text: White parasols, splendid horses,

children.text: sadā mattāśca mātaṅgāḥ prasanne sati bhūpatau // Suk_5.17 (=46) //
children.translated_text: and ever-rutting elephants— all come when the king is pleased.

children.text:
tasmāttāt, tvaṃ rājñā mānyaḥ prasādapātrañca /
tataḥ sandehe 'sminmā viṣādībhava /
yataḥ-
children.translated_text: Therefore, father, you are honored by the king and a vessel of his favor. So in this doubt, do not despair. Because—

children.text: rājagrahe samāyāte viṣame kāryasaṃśaye /
children.translated_text: When a crisis comes upon the royal house, in a difficult and doubtful matter,

children.text: sandigdhamanasāṃ rājñāṃ pradhānāḥ saṃśayacchidaḥ // Suk_5.18 (=47) //
children.translated_text: the chief ministers are the ones who resolve the doubts of kings whose minds are uncertain.

children.text:
tato he tāta! sthirībhava /
matsyahasanottaraṃ rājñaḥ purato mayābhidheyamiti /
snāhi bhuṅkṣva /
tataḥ sa evaṃ kṛtvā rājño 'grato gatvā sarvaṃ nivedayāmāsa /
nṛpo 'pi tuṣṭastāmājuhāva /
sā āśīrvādaṃ dattvā rājānamabravīt-rājanmā mudhā viprānviḍambaya /
kiṃ tvayā evaṃvidhaṃ matsyānāṃ hāsyaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ śrutaṃ vā /
kathaṃ māmabalājana pṛcchanna vilajjase /
children.translated_text: So, O father, be steadfast! I shall declare the answer to the fish's laughter before the king. Bathe and eat. Then he, having done so, went before the king and reported everything. The king, pleased, summoned her. She, giving her blessing, said to the king— "O king, do not torment the Brahmins in vain. Have you yourself ever seen or heard of fish laughing in such a manner? How are you not ashamed to ask me, a mere girl?"

children.text: yataḥ- itaro 'pi na sāmānyo nṛpatirdivyarūpabhṛt /
children.translated_text: Because— Even another king would not be ordinary, bearing a divine form;

children.text: tvaṃ punarvikramādityo yathārtho 'si parantapa // Suk_5.19 (=48) //
children.translated_text: but you are <s>Vikramāditya</s>, true to your name, O scorcher of foes!

children.text: uktañca-
children.translated_text: And it is said—

children.text: indrātprabhutvaṃ jvalanātpratāpaṃ krodhaṃ yamādvaiśravaṇācca vittam /
children.translated_text: Sovereignty from <s>Indra</s>, splendor from <s>Agni</s>, wrath from <s>Yama</s>, and wealth from <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>,

children.text: sattvasthite rāmajanārdanābhyāmādāya rājñaḥ kriyate śarīram // Suk_5.20 (=49) //
children.translated_text: steadfastness from <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Janārdana</s>— taking these, the body of a king is fashioned.

children.text: tathā ca bhārate-
children.translated_text: And so in the <s>Bhārata</s>—

children.text: mā vṛkodara pādena ekādaśacamūpatim /
children.translated_text: "Do not, O <s>Vṛkodara</s>, kick with your foot the lord of eleven armies;

children.text: pañcanāmapi yo bharttā nāsāprakṛtimānavī <1> <1. `māninā' iti pā-> // Suk_5.21 (=50) //
children.translated_text: she who is the wife of five is no ordinary woman."

children.text:
svāminkathaṃ na tvaṃ svayameva vicārayasi /
yatastvameva sarvasaṃśayacchettā /
athānyebhyaścet śrotuṃ kautukaṃ tarhi śṛṇu /
children.translated_text: "My lord, why do you not consider the matter yourself? For you yourself are the dispeller of all doubts. But if you are curious to hear it from another, then listen—"

children.text: iyaṃ rājñī na spṛśati hyasmānmatsyānmahāsatī /
children.translated_text: "This queen does not touch us fish, being a great chaste woman;

children.text: puruṣākhyānato rājan hasitāḥ śapharā dhruvam // Suk_5.22 (=51) //
children.translated_text: it is because she called us 'males,' O king, that we fish surely laughed."

children.text: paribhāvyastvayā rājan ślokārtho 'yaṃ sadā hṛdi /
children.translated_text: "You should ponder this, O king— keep the meaning of this verse always in your heart;

children.text: mūḍhadhīranyathā deva yadi pṛcchasi māṃ punaḥ // Suk_5.23 (=52) //
children.translated_text: otherwise, O dull-witted lord, you will ask me again."

children.text: rājanrājapatnyāḥ sūryamapaśyantyāstatkathamasatītvaśaṅkā syāt /
children.translated_text: "O king, how can there be a suspicion of unchastity against the queen who does not even look at the sun?"

children.text: ślokārthe prastutārthe ca matsyānāṃ hasanaṃ budhāḥ /
children.translated_text: "The meaning of the verse regarding the fish's laughter in the matter at hand,

children.text: sanṛpā na vijānanti api sarvārthakovidāḥ // Suk_5.24 (=53) //
children.translated_text: even those who are learned in all matters, together with their kings, do not understand."

children.text: tataḥ sado mūḍhaṃ dṛṣṭvā bālapaṇḍitā utthāya yayau /
children.translated_text: Then, seeing the court bewildered, <s>Bālapaṇḍitā</s> rose and departed.

children.text: śuko 'pyāha-ahaṃ prātaḥ kathayiṣye /
children.translated_text: The parrot also said— "I shall tell the rest in the morning."

children.text: iti kīroktiṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā //
children.translated_text: Hearing the parrot's words, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau pañcamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s>.

children.text: START Suk 6:
children.translated_text: Beginning of the 6th tale:

children.text:
athāparasmindivase prabhāvatī śukaṃ prāha-
śuka! sa matsyahāsyavyatikaro rājñā jñāto na veti /
śuka āha- nṛpaḥ ślokārthamajānanna nidrāṃ lebhe /
uktañca-
children.translated_text: And it is said—

children.text: nidrā bhadre kutasteṣāṃ ye ṛṇavyādhipīḍitāḥ /
children.translated_text: "How can there be sleep, O good lady, for those who are afflicted by debt and disease,

children.text: avidheyakalatrāśca ye cānye kṛtavairiṇaḥ // Suk_6.1 (=54) //
children.translated_text: whose wives are disobedient, and others who have made enemies?"

Then on another day, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> said to the parrot— "Parrot! Was the reason for the fish's laughter discovered by the king or not?" The parrot said— "The king, not understanding the meaning of the verse, could not sleep."

children.text:
rājā nidrābhāve kaṣṭena niśāṃ nītvā prātarbālapaṇḍitāmākārya prāha-bālike! ślokārtho na jñāto mayā /
tasmānmatsyahāsyakāraṇe nivedaya /
sā āha-rājanmāṃ mā pṛccha /
yataḥ-
children.translated_text: The king, having passed the night with difficulty due to sleeplessness, summoned <s>Bālapaṇḍitā</s> in the morning and said— "Girl! I have not understood the meaning of the verse. Therefore explain the reason for the fish's laughter." She said— "O king, do not ask me. Because—"

children.text: paścāttāpo 'tra bhavitā bhāryāyā vaṇijo yathā /
children.translated_text: "There will be remorse afterwards, just as the merchant's wife felt

children.text: āgraheṇa kṛtaḥ patyau maṇḍakāgamanaṃ prati // Suk_6.2 (=55) //
children.translated_text: when she insisted to her husband regarding the arrival of the cakes."

children.text:
rājā-kathametat /
śukaḥ-astyatra jayantī nāma nagarī /
tatra vaṇikasutaḥ sumatirnāma tasya priyā padminī nāma /
tasya ca vaṇijaḥ puṇyakṣayāddhanaṃ kṣīṇam /
sa ca janaiḥ parityaktaḥ /
yato jano dhanamitraḥ /
uktañca-
children.translated_text: The king asked— "How is that?" The parrot said— There is a city called <s>Jayantī</s>. There lived a merchant's son named <s>Sumati</s>, and his beloved wife was named <s>Padminī</s>. Due to the exhaustion of his merit, the merchant's wealth was depleted. He was abandoned by people, for people are friends only of wealth. And it is said—

children.text: yasyārthāstasya mitrāṇi yasyārthāstasya bāndhavāḥ /
children.translated_text: He who has wealth has friends; he who has wealth has kinsmen;

children.text: yasyārthāḥ sa pumāṃlloke yasyārthāḥ sa ca paṇḍitaḥ // Suk_6.3 (=56) //
children.translated_text: he who has wealth is a man in this world; he who has wealth is considered wise.

children.text: tathā ca bhārate-
children.translated_text: And so in the <s>Bhārata</s>—

children.text: jīvanto 'pi mṛtāḥ pañca śrūyante kila bhārata /
children.translated_text: "Five types of people, though living, are said to be dead, O <s>Bhārata</s>:

children.text: daridro vyādhito mūrkhaḥ pravāsī nityasevakaḥ // Suk_6.4 (=57) //
children.translated_text: the poor, the diseased, the foolish, the exile, and the perpetual servant."

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And likewise—

children.text: iha loke hi dhanināṃ paro 'pi svajanāyate /
children.translated_text: In this world, even a stranger becomes one's own kin for the wealthy;

children.text: svajano 'pi draridrāṇāṃ tatkṣaṇāddurjanāyate // Suk_6.5 (=58) //
children.translated_text: but even one's own kin instantly becomes hostile toward the poor.

children.text:
so 'pi ca tṛṇakāṣṭhādikamānīya purīmadhye vikrīṇāti /
anyadā anena tṛṇakāṣṭhādikaṃ kimapi vane na prāptam /
dṛḍhakāṣṭhamayo 'pi vighnavināyakaḥ prāptaḥ /
tataścintitam-kimasau mama vidhāsyati? uktañca-
children.translated_text: He would bring grass, firewood, and such things and sell them in the city. One day he could find nothing— no grass, no firewood, nothing in the forest. But he found a <s>Vighnavināyaka</s> (obstacle-removing <s>Gaṇeśa</s>) idol made of solid wood. Then he thought— "What will this do for me?" And it is said—

children.text: bubhukṣitaḥ kiṃ na karoti pāpaṃ kṣīṇā narā niṣkaruṇā bhavanti /
children.translated_text: What sin does a starving man not commit? People reduced to nothing become merciless;

children.text: prāṇārthamete hi samācaranti mataṃ satāṃ yanna mataṃ tadeṣām // Suk_6.6 (=59) //
children.translated_text: they act for the sake of their very lives— what the righteous approve is not what such people approve.

children.text:
yāvatsa tasya vināyakasya pāṭanāyottiṣṭhati tāvattuṣṭaḥ san jagāda-ahaṃ tava pratidinaṃ pañca pañca maṇḍakāndāsye khaṇḍaghṛtayutān /
mamālaye prātaryāyāḥ /
paraṃ kasyāpi idaṃ rahasyaṃ na kathanīyam /
kathite tu madvaco vitathaṃ bhaviṣyati /
so 'pi ca "tathe'ti pratipādya nityaṃ maṇḍakapañcakaṃ bhāryāyā arpayati /
taddaivaṃ maṇḍakapañcakaṃ ghṛtakhaṇḍayuktamādāya tadbhāryā nijakuṭumbaṃ tṛptīkaroti /
nityaṃ ca tānmaṇḍakān gotriṇāṃ gṛhe vāhayāmāsa /
nijasakhyā mandodaryāstṛptyarthaṃ nityaṃ prāhiṇot /
anyadā sā sakhī tāṃ papraccha /
padminyapi maṇḍakāgamanamidaṃ na jānāti /
tatastasyāḥ purā sā sakhī kapaṭādbrūte-sakhi! yadi tvaṃ mama purato guhyaṃ na kathayasi tatkaḥ snehaḥ /
uktañca-
children.translated_text: Just as he rose to break that <s>Vināyaka</s> idol, it, being pleased, spoke— "I shall give you five cakes daily, with sugar and ghee. Come to my shrine each morning. But this secret must not be told to anyone. If told, my promise shall become void." He agreed, saying "So be it," and daily gave the five cakes to his wife. His wife, receiving the five cakes with ghee and sugar through this divine gift, sustained her family. She would regularly send those cakes to the homes of relatives. She also sent some daily for the satisfaction of her friend <s>Mandodarī</s>. One day that friend asked her about it. <s>Padminī</s> herself did not know the source of the cakes. Then her friend craftily said to her— "Friend! If you do not reveal your secret before me, then what kind of affection is this?" And it is said—

children.text: dadāti pratigṛhṇāni guhyamākhyāti pṛcchati /
children.translated_text: One gives and receives, reveals secrets and asks about them,

children.text: bhuṅkte bhojayate caiva ṣaḍvidhaṃ prītilakṣaṇam // Suk_6.7 (=60) //
children.translated_text: eats and feeds— these are the six marks of affection.

children.text:
tataḥ padminyāha-madīyaḥ patiridaṃ guhyaṃ mamāgre kathamapi na brate mayā śataśaḥ pṛṣṭo 'pi /
tayoktam-tarhi tvadīyaṃ jīvitaṃ rūpaṃ yauvanaṃ savamapi nirarthakameva yadidaṃ nājñāyi /
tataḥ padminī patiṃ pṛcchati-kathaṃ maṇḍakaprāptiḥ? patirāha-vidheḥ prasādāt /
uktañca-
children.translated_text: Then <s>Padminī</s> said— "My husband does not reveal this secret to me no matter how much I ask, even though I have asked him hundreds of times." She replied— "Then your life, beauty, and youth are all worthless if you do not even know this." Then <s>Padminī</s> asked her husband— "How do you obtain the cakes?" The husband said— "By the grace of fate." And it is said—

children.text: dvīpādanyasmādapi madhyādapi jalanidherdiśo 'pyantāt /
children.translated_text: From another island, from the middle of the ocean, from the ends of the directions—

children.text: ānīya jhaṭiti ghaṭayati vidhirabhimatamabhimukhobhūtaḥ // Suk_6.8 (=61) //
children.translated_text: fate, when favorably disposed, swiftly brings and arranges what is desired.

children.text: kiñca-
children.translated_text: Moreover—

children.text: kṣutkṣāmasya karaṇḍapiṇḍitatanormlāndriyasya kṣudhā kṛtvākhurvivaraṃ svayaṃ nipatito naktaṃ mukhe bhoginaḥ /
children.translated_text: For one emaciated by hunger, body contracted into a ball, senses withered by starvation— a mouse, having dug a hole, itself fell at night into the mouth of a serpent;

children.text: tṛptastatpiśitena satvaramasau tenaiva yātaḥ pathā svasthāstiṣṭhata daivameva hi nṛṇāṃ vṛddhau kṣaye kāraṇam // Suk_6.9 (=62) //
children.translated_text: Satisfied with that flesh, he swiftly departed by that very path. Remain at ease — for fate alone is the cause of prosperity and decline among men. // Suk_6.9 (=62) //

children.text:
yadā na kathayati tadānaśanaṃ cakre /
patirāha-asminkathite mahatī hāniḥ paścāttāpaśca bhaviṣyati /
evaṃ bodhitāpi sā yāvannāgrahaṃ muñcati tadā tena daivopahatacittena kathitam /
uktañca-
children.translated_text:
When [the parrot] did not tell a story, she [<s>Prabhāvatī</s>] undertook a fast.
The husband said: 'If this is told, there will be great loss and regret afterwards.'
Even though thus warned, when she would not abandon her insistence, then he, his mind afflicted by fate, told [the story].
And it is said:

children.text: yasmai devāḥ prayacchanti puruṣāya parābhavam /
children.translated_text: To whichever man the gods grant defeat,

children.text: buddhiṃ tasyāpakarṣanti na sa vetyātmano hitam // Suk_6.10 (=63) //
children.translated_text: they draw away his intellect — he does not know what is good for himself. // Suk_6.10 (=63) //

children.text:
tena ca rājanvikramārkabuddhimuktena guhyaṃ kīrtitam /
yato hīnapuṇyo buddhyā mucyate /
uktañca-
children.translated_text:
And by that king <s>Vikramārka</s>, whose intellect was thus released [by fate], the secret was revealed.
For one whose merit is diminished is abandoned by his intellect.
And it is said:

children.text: rāmo hemamṛgaṃ na vetti nahuṣo yāne yunakti dvijān viprādeva savatsadhenuharaṇe jātā matiścārjune /
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> did not recognize the golden deer; <s>Nahuṣa</s> yoked <s>brāhmaṇas</s> to his chariot; in <s>Arjuna</s> arose the idea of stealing a cow with its calf from a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>;

children.text: dyūte bhrātṛcatuṣṭayaṃ ca mahiṣīṃ dharmātmajo dattavān prāyaḥ satpuruṣo 'pyanarthasamaye buddhyā parityajyate // Suk_6.11 (=64) //
children.translated_text: In the dice-game, the righteous <s>Dharmarāja</s> [<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>] wagered his four brothers and his queen — generally, even a good man is abandoned by his intellect in times of calamity. // Suk_6.11 (=64) //

children.text:
sā ca patimukhāt śrutvā sakhīpurī jagāda /
tayā cātmapatiḥ kuṭhārahastaḥ preṣito vināyakapārśve /
so 'pi padminīpatiśca prātastatra jagāma /
vināyako 'pi dvāvapi mayūrabandhairbandhayāmāsa /
so 'pi ca padminīpatiruktaḥ re tvadīya evāyamanarthaḥ /
tatastvayyeva daṇḍo yujyate /
tataḥ sakhīpatiryayāce /
tānpañca maṇḍakāntasmai sa pradadau /
tau dvāvapi svaṃ svaṃ gṛhaṃ jagmatuḥ /
tataḥ patyā dāpitāḥ /
paścāttāpaṃ ca kurute /
tatastvamapi rājendra! māṃ mā pṛccha /
tava paścāttāpo bhaviṣyati /
idaṃ ślokaṃ svayameva vicintaya /
iti kathayitvā bālapaṇḍitā utthāya svagṛhaṃ gatā /
iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text:
And she [the wife], having heard from her husband's mouth, told her friend <s>Purī</s>.
And she [the friend] sent her own husband, axe in hand, to <s>Vināyaka</s>'s [temple].
He and <s>Padminī</s>'s husband went there in the morning.
<s>Vināyaka</s> bound both of them with peacock-snares.
And <s>Padminī</s>'s husband said: 'This calamity is indeed yours alone!
Therefore the punishment should fall on you alone.'
Then the friend's husband pleaded.
He gave those five <s>maṇḍakas</s> (cakes) to him [<s>Vināyaka</s>].
Both of them went to their respective homes.
Then [the five cakes] were made to be given by the husband.
And he feels remorse afterwards.
Therefore, you too, O king! Do not ask me.
You will have regret afterwards.
Ponder this verse yourself.
Having spoken thus, <s>Bālapaṇḍitā</s> rose and went to her own house.
Having heard this story, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau ṣaṣṭhī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus [ends] the sixth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 7:
children.translated_text: [Beginning of the Seventh Tale (<s>Suk</s> 7)]

children.text:
anyasmindine prabhāvatī śukaṃ papraccha-kīra! punastanmatsyahāsyakāraṇaṃ rājñā jñātaṃ śṛtaṃ na vā /
śukaḥ prāha-prātaḥ punarbālapaṇḍitāmākārayitvā rājā prāha-ki tanmatsyahāsyakāraṇam? brūhi śīghraṃ bālike! sā cāha-
children.translated_text:
On another day, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked the parrot: 'O parrot! Was the cause of the fish's laughter then discovered by the king, or not?'
The parrot said: 'In the morning, the king again summoned <s>Bālapaṇḍitā</s> and said: "What is the cause of the fish's laughter? Tell me quickly, girl!" And she said:

children.text: devāgraho na kartavyaḥ paścāttāpo bhaviṣyati /
children.translated_text: 'O lord, one should not persist — there will be regret afterwards,

children.text: sthagikāsaktacittasya viprasyābhūtpurā yathā // Suk_7.1 (=65) //
children.translated_text: just as it happened formerly to the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> whose mind was attached to <s>Sthagikā</s>.' // Suk_7.1 (=65) //

children.text:
asti dharaṇītale vatsonanāma paṭṭanam /
tatra vīrākhyo rājā tatra ca keśavo nāma brāhmaṇaḥ /
tena kadāciditi cintitaṃ yadahaṃ pitṛdhanaṃ na bhokṣye /
uktañca-
children.translated_text:
There is on the surface of the earth a city called <s>Vatsonā</s>.
There [ruled] a king named <s>Vīra</s>, and there [lived] a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Keśava</s>.
He once resolved: 'I shall not enjoy my father's wealth.'
And it is said:

children.text: uttamāḥ svaguṇaiḥ khyātā madhyamāśca piturguṇaiḥ /
children.translated_text: The best are known by their own virtues, the middling by their father's virtues,

children.text: adhamā mātulaiḥ khyātā śvaśuraiścādhamādhamāḥ // Suk_7.2 (=66) //
children.translated_text: the low are known by their maternal uncles, and the lowest of the low by their fathers-in-law. // Suk_7.2 (=66) //

children.text: kiñca- piara viḍhattai davvḍai caḍḍiri ko ṇa karei /
children.translated_text: Moreover [in Prakrit]: 'What the father has accumulated — who does not enjoy inherited wealth?

children.text: saiṃ biḍhavai saiṃ bhojaai viralā jaṇaṇi jaṇei // Suk_7.3 (=67) //
children.translated_text: He who earns himself and enjoys himself — rare is the mother who gives birth [to such a son].' // Suk_7.3 (=67) //

children.text: [pitrarjitaṃ dravyaṃ bhoginaṃ kaṃ na karoti /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: 'The wealth earned by the father — whom does it not make an enjoyer?

children.text: svayamarjayati svayaṃ bhuṅkte viralā jananī janayati] // Suk_7.3* (=67*) //
children.translated_text: He who earns by himself and enjoys by himself — rare is the mother who gives birth [to such a one].'] // Suk_7.3* (=67*) //

children.text:
ityavadhārya sa medinyāṃ babhrāma devatīrthaśmaśānanagareṣu dhanārtham /
anyadā sa nirjane pradeśe prasiddhe śivacatvare karālāyāḥ śmaśāne ca paribhramya pariśrāntaḥ kapilakamaṭhamapaśyat /
tatra ca paryaṅkasanasthaṃ tāpasaṃ dadarśa sa ca viprastasyāgre kṛtāñjalipuṭastasthau /
tāpaso dhyānaṃ śanairmuktvā evamuktavān-
children.translated_text:
Having resolved thus, he wandered on the earth — in sacred sites, cremation grounds, and cities — seeking wealth.
Once, in a desolate place, at the famous <s>Śiva</s>-square and in the cremation ground of <s>Karālā</s>, having wandered about and become exhausted, he saw a tawny tortoise.
There he beheld an ascetic seated cross-legged on a couch. The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> stood before him with palms joined in reverence.
The ascetic, slowly emerging from meditation, spoke thus:

children.text: kiṃ kasmai dīyate loke trāyate ko bhavārṇavāt /
children.translated_text: 'What is given to whom in this world? Who is saved from the ocean of existence?

children.text: asādhyaṃ sādhyate kasya kāle 'sminnatitheraho // Suk_7.4 (=68) //
children.translated_text: Whose impossible [task] is accomplished in this time — O [you who are] beyond the holy ford?' // Suk_7.4 (=68) //

children.text:
tataḥ sa brāhmaṇa ūrdhvabāhurjagāda-tavāhamatithirdhanārthī /
tāpaso 'pi taṃ vipramalpayācaka dṛṣṭvā manasi duḥkhībabhūva /
uktañca-
children.translated_text:
Then that <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, raising his arms, declared: 'I am your guest, seeking wealth.'
The ascetic, seeing that <s>brāhmaṇa</s> as a petty supplicant, became sorrowful in his mind.
And it is said:

children.text: stokārthaprārthanāndīnāndṛṣṭvodārānhi yācakān /
children.translated_text: Seeing generous supplicants who are content with little,

children.text: khidyante 'tīva manasi api prāṇapradāyinaḥ // Suk_7.5 (=69) //
children.translated_text: even those who would give their very lives are exceedingly distressed in mind. // Suk_7.5 (=69) //

children.text: kiñca-
children.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: ahihūo vi a vivaā karei suaṇo parassa upaāraṃ /
children.translated_text: [In Prakrit:] 'Even when afflicted, a good man performs service for others;

children.text: oṇei aṇṇadādhaṃ candaṇataruo sakhaṇḍo vi // Suk_7.6 (=70) //
children.translated_text: the sandalwood tree removes the heat of others, even when cut into a thousand pieces.' // Suk_7.6 (=70) //

children.text: [abhibhūto 'pi vipadā karoti sujanaḥ parasya upakāram /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering: 'Even when overwhelmed by misfortune, a good man performs service for others;

children.text: apanayatyanyatāpaṃ candanatarukaḥ sahasrakaṇḍo 'pi] // Suk_7.6* (=70*) //
children.translated_text: the sandalwood tree removes the heat of others, even when cut into a thousand pieces.'] // Suk_7.6* (=70*) //

children.text:
tato yogīndro "yadā tvametatsparśanaṃ kariṣyasi tadā hemnaḥ pañcaśatāni nityaṃ dāsyatī'tyuktvā viprāya paryaṅkīkṛtaṃ sindūramarpayāmāsa /
uktaśca-"etattvayānyasmai na dātavyaṃ na kathanīyañca /
anyathā mama samīpe vyāvṛtya sameṣyati /
tadarpitaṃ yadā sa dvijaḥ prātaḥ spṛśati tadā suvarṇaśatapañcakaṃ dadāti /
sa ca ratnāvatīṃ purīṃ gataḥ /
tatra sthagikāṃ nāma veśyāṃ nityaṃ kāmayate /
sā ca taddravyāgamanaṃ na jānāti /
kuṭṭinī pṛcchati-hale! eṣa vipraḥ kimapi vyavasāyādikaṃ na vidhatte /
paraṃ dravyaṃ kuto 'smākaṃ vitarati kasmādvilasatīti /
tato veśyā taṃ pṛcchati /
sa vipraḥ sarvathā na kathayati /
tato veśyayā svakalayā bhaktyā cārādhitaḥ /
tataḥ pṛṣṭaḥ sankathayāmāsa yatsindūrāddravyāgamaḥ /
tayā ca suptasya sindūraṃ gṛhītam /
tato dravyābhāve kuṭṭinyā gṛhānniṣkāsitaḥ /
uktañca-
children.translated_text:
Then the lord of <s>yogins</s> said: 'When you touch this, it will daily yield five hundred [coins] of gold,' and gave the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> a portion of vermilion made into a ball.
And he said: 'This must not be given to anyone else, nor spoken of.
Otherwise it will return to me.'
When that <s>brāhmaṇa</s> touched what was given in the morning, it yielded five hundred gold [coins].
He went to the city of <s>Ratnāvatī</s>.
There he constantly desired a courtesan named <s>Sthagikā</s>.
She did not know the source of his wealth.
The bawd (<s>kuṭṭinī</s>) asked: 'Girl! This <s>brāhmaṇa</s> does not engage in any trade or the like. From where does he give us wealth? Why does he live so lavishly?'
Then the courtesan asked him.
The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> would not tell her at all.
Then [he was] won over by the courtesan through her arts and devotion.
Then, when asked, he confessed that the wealth came from the vermilion.
And she stole the vermilion while he slept.
Then, in the absence of wealth, he was expelled from the house by the bawd.
And it is said:

children.text: viśvāsapratipannānāṃ vañcane kā vidagdhatā /
children.translated_text: 'What cleverness is there in deceiving those who have given their trust?

children.text: aṅkamāruhya suptaṃ hi hantuṃ kiṃ nāma pauruṣam // Suk_7.7 (=71) //
children.translated_text: What manliness is there in killing one who has climbed into one's lap and fallen asleep?' // Suk_7.7 (=71) //

children.text:
sa viprastatsindūramapaśyanphūtkurvanrājadvāraṃ yayau, muṣito 'hamiti vadan /
tato vivādaḥ sañjātaḥ /
kuṭṭinyāha-
children.translated_text:
That <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, not finding the vermilion, went cursing to the king's gate, crying 'I have been robbed!'
Then a dispute arose.
The bawd said:

children.text: dhūrto 'sau matsutālubdho dhanahīno bhavatyasau /
children.translated_text: 'He is a cheat, greedy for my daughter; he has become penniless.

children.text: manobhavagrahagrasto asamañjasamīdṛśam // Suk_7.8 (=72) //
children.translated_text: Seized by the demon of lust — this is all nonsense.' // Suk_7.8 (=72) //

children.text: janairguṇairasambhāvyaṃ rājñā kathaṃ sambhāvyate /
children.translated_text: 'What is not believed by people on account of [his lack of] virtues — how can it be believed by the king?

children.text: paraṃ satyamidaṃ jātaṃ sindūraṃ dhanadaṃ yataḥ // Suk_7.9 (=73) //
children.translated_text: But this is the truth: because the vermilion was wealth-giving.' // Suk_7.9 (=73) //

children.text:
sa ca janairvaideśiko 'yamiti jñātvā nirvāsitaḥ /
tacca sindūraṃ yogīndrameva yayau /
tato rājanvikramāditya! sthagikāprītinibandhanāttenākhyāte ca sindūre sthagikā naiva viprasya babhūva na ca sindūram /
evaṃ tavāpi rājan! ratiḥ prītiśca na bhaviṣyati /
evamuktvā bālapaṇḍitā gṛhaṃ jagāma /
iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text:
The people, knowing him to be a foreigner, had him banished.
And that vermilion returned to the lord of <s>yogins</s>.
Therefore, O king <s>Vikramāditya</s>! Because he revealed the vermilion out of his attachment to <s>Sthagikā</s>, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> obtained neither <s>Sthagikā</s> nor the vermilion.
Likewise, for you too, O king, there will be neither love nor joy.
Having spoken thus, <s>Bālapaṇḍitā</s> went home.
Having heard this story, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau saptamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus [ends] the seventh tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 8:
children.translated_text: [Beginning of the Eighth Tale (<s>Suk</s> 8)]

children.text:
athāparedyuḥ prabhāvatī śukaṃ pṛcchati /
śuka uttaraṃ dadau-devi! bālapaṇḍitā dvitīye 'hni saṃyāte rājānaṃ prāha-deva! nāgrahaḥ kartuṃ yujyate /
yataḥ-
children.translated_text:
Then on the following day, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked the parrot.
The parrot replied: 'O queen! On the second day, when [the minister] had departed, <s>Bālapaṇḍitā</s> said to the king: "O lord! Persistence is not proper, for:

children.text: rājñā naivāgrahaḥ kāryaḥ śubhe vāśubhakarmaṇi /
children.translated_text: A king should not persist, whether in good or bad deeds,

children.text: tadaṅgāni hi bhūtāni rājñāṃ hi mahatī tanuḥ // Suk_8.10 (=74) //
children.translated_text: for all beings are his limbs — great indeed is the body of kings.' // Suk_8.10 (=74) //

children.text: ākhyāte ca tava mayā viṇikputryā yathābhavat /
children.translated_text: 'And when I tell you [the story of] the merchant's daughter, as it happened,

children.text: na bahirna gṛhaṃ rājaṃstathā te 'pi bhaviṣyati // Suk_8.11 (=75) //
children.translated_text: [you will see that] neither outside nor at home, O king — so too it will be for you.' // Suk_8.11 (=75) //

children.text:
rājā pṛcchati-kathametat? bālapaṇḍitā prāha-asti pṛthvītale tripuraṃ nāma sthānam /
tasmintrivikramo nāma rāja /
tatra sundarābhidhāno vaṇik /
tadbhāryā subhagā nāmātīva kulaṭā /
sā ca bhartrā gṛhānniryāntī prayatnena niyantritā /
tāñca niyantraṇātpūrvameko vaṇigyakṣagṛhe sthitaḥ sakāmāmabhajat /
yadā ca bahirnirgacchanto patinā nivāritā tadā sakhīṃ prāha-sakhi! adya tvayā sa mānavo yakṣāyatana ākāraṇīyaḥ yathāhaṃ tatra gatvā taṃ rame /
tvayā ca mayi gatāyāṃ paścādasmadgṛhaṃ jvālanīyaṃ yathā gṛhakāryāsakto jano māṃ gātaṃ na jānāti /
atrāntare 'haṃ taṃ svecchayā bhuktvā samupāgacchāmi /
tataḥ sakhīvacanātsa pumāṃstatrāyātaḥ /
sāpyāgatā /
tadā ca gatāyāṃ tasyāṃ sā sakhī tadgṛhaṃ prajvālitavatī /
sa pumānprajvalane kutūhalī yakṣāyatanaṃ muktvā tatrāvalokanāya gataḥ /
sā ca tatra sthitāsamāptātmaprayojanā yāvatā gṛhamāgatā tāvatā gṛhaṃ dagdham /
children.translated_text:
The king asked: 'How is that?' <s>Bālapaṇḍitā</s> said: 'There is on the earth a place called <s>Tripura</s>.
In it [ruled] a king named <s>Trivikrama</s>. There [lived] a merchant named <s>Sundara</s>.
His wife, named <s>Subhagā</s>, was extremely wanton.
She was carefully restrained by her husband from leaving the house.
Before this restraint, a certain merchant staying in a <s>Yakṣa</s>-temple had enjoyed her willing favors.
When, going out, she was prevented by her husband, she said to her friend: "Friend! Today you must summon that man to the <s>Yakṣa</s>-temple so that I may go there and enjoy him.
And after I have gone, you must set fire to our house, so that the household members, busy with the house, will not know I have gone.
Meanwhile, I shall enjoy him at my pleasure and return."
Then, at the friend's word, that man came there.
She too came.
And when she had gone, that friend set fire to the house.
That man, curious about the fire, leaving the <s>Yakṣa</s>-temple, went there to look.
And she, standing there with her purpose unfulfilled — by the time she came home, the house was burnt down.
