children.text: na gṛhaṃ na bahirbhūpa vaṇigvadhvā yathābhavat /
children.translated_text: 'Neither the house nor the outside [remained], O king — as happened to the merchant's wife,

children.text: tathā tava mahārāja bhaviṣyati suniścayam // Suk_8.12 (=76) //
children.translated_text: so too, O great king, it will certainly be for you.' // Suk_8.12 (=76) //

children.text: atha cet jñātena ślokārthena prayojanaṃ tadā kalye svayameva jñāpayiṣyāmi /
children.translated_text: 'And if, knowing the meaning of the verse, there is [still] a purpose [to inquire], then tomorrow I shall myself reveal it.'

children.text: ityuktvā sā gṛhaṃ yayau /
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, she went home.

children.text: iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā //
children.translated_text: Having heard this story, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau aṣṭamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus [ends] the eighth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 9:
children.translated_text: [Beginning of the Ninth Tale (<s>Suk</s> 9)]

children.text:
athāparedyuḥ savismayā prabhāvatī śukaṃ pṛcchati sma-śuka! kiṃ vijñātaṃ vikramārkeṇa matsyahasanakāraṇam? śukaḥ prāha-devi! na kimapi rājñā svayaṃ jñātam /
tato rājā prātardvijasutāmāhuya bālapaṇḍitāṃ prāha-tvayā ityuktaṃ yattvaṃ svayameva jñāsyasi /
mayā tu kimapi na jñātam /
bālapaṇḍitā prāha-yadi rājannevamapi mayā kathyamānaṃ na vetsi, tataḥ śṛṇu /
puṣpahāso nāma mantrī sarvamantriṇāmagraṇīrnirdeṣo guptaḥ /
kimiti niyantrito 'sti /
rājā prāha-anvartho 'yaṃ puṣpahāsaḥ /
yataḥ yadāso madīyāyāṃ saṃsadi hasati tadāsyāsyātpuṣpaprakaro nipatati /
iyañca kathāpararājyamaṇḍaleṣu khyātābhūt /
tatastaiḥ preṣitāḥ svīyapumāṃsaḥ kutūhalānveṣaṇāya /
teṣu samāyāteṣu tena na hasitaṃ puṣpaprakaro 'pi nābhūt /
iti kāraṇātguptibandhaḥ /
bālapaṇḍitā prāha-kenāpi kāraṇena mantriṇā na hasitam, rājan! tatkāraṇaṃ tvayā jñātaṃ na vā? rājā prāha-mayā kimapi na jñātam /
bālapaṇḍitā prāha-tarhi kathamidaṃ daṇḍaṃ kurvanpāpabhāk na bhavasi? uktañca-
children.translated_text:
Then on the following day, <s>Prabhāvatī</s>, filled with wonder, asked the parrot: 'O parrot! Was the cause of the fish's laughter discovered by <s>Vikramārka</s>?' The parrot said: 'O queen! Nothing was discovered by the king himself.
Then in the morning, the king summoned the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> girl <s>Bālapaṇḍitā</s> and said: "You said that I would know it myself. But I have not understood anything."
<s>Bālapaṇḍitā</s> said: "If, O king, you still do not understand even as I tell you, then listen.
<s>Puṣpahāsa</s>, the minister, the foremost among all ministers, is [being kept] confined in secret.
Why is he being restrained?"
The king said: "This <s>Puṣpahāsa</s> [whose name means 'Flower-laugh'] lives up to his name.
For whenever he laughs in my assembly, a shower of flowers falls from his mouth.
And this story became famous in the territories of other kingdoms.
Therefore, they sent their own men to investigate out of curiosity.
When they arrived, he did not laugh and no shower of flowers appeared.
For this reason he was placed in confinement."
<s>Bālapaṇḍitā</s> said: "For some reason the minister did not laugh, O king! Do you know that reason or not?"
The king said: "I do not know anything."
<s>Bālapaṇḍitā</s> said: "Then how, by imposing this punishment, do you not incur sin? For it is said:

children.text: dharmeṇa rāṣṭraṃ vindena dharmeṇaivānupālayet /
children.translated_text: By <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) one wins a kingdom, by <s>dharma</s> alone one protects it;

children.text: dharmāccharaṇyatāṃ yāti rājā sarvabhayāpahaḥ // Suk_9.1 (=77) //
children.translated_text: through <s>dharma</s> the king becomes a refuge, the remover of all fears.' // Suk_9.1 (=77) //

children.text:
yathā āgrahānmāṃ matsyahāsyakāraṇaṃ pṛcchasi tathā tamapi pṛccha hāsyakāraṇam /
sa evātmīyahāsyasya matsyahāsyasya ca kāraṇaṃ vaktā /
rājāpi tadvacanātpuṣpahāsaṃ mantriṇaṃ vastradānapūrvaṃ mantripade pratiṣṭhāpya matsyahāsyakāraṇaṃ papraccha /
mantryāha-yadyapi gṛhaduścaritamakathyam /
yataḥ-
children.translated_text:
'Just as you persistently ask me the cause of the fish's laughter, so too ask him the cause of [his] laughter.
He alone will tell the cause of both his own laughter and the fish's laughter.'
The king, following her words, reinstated the minister <s>Puṣpahāsa</s> in the ministerial office with a gift of garments and asked the cause of the fish's laughter.
The minister said: 'Although the misconduct of one's household should not be spoken of. For:

children.text: arthanāśaṃ manastāpaṃ gṛhe duścaritāni ca /
children.translated_text: 'Loss of wealth, mental anguish, the misdeeds of one's household,

children.text: vañcanaṃ cāpamānaṃ ca matimānna prakāśayet // Suk_9.2 (=78) //
children.translated_text: deception, and dishonor — a wise man should not reveal [these].' // Suk_9.2 (=78) //

children.text: tathāpi tu rājājñā mahatī /
yataḥ-
children.translated_text: For:

children.text: prabhuḥ prītisnigdhāṃ dṛśamapi na pāpeṣu visṛjet kutaḥ ślāghyāmājñāṃ praṇayarasasāndreṇa manasā /
children.translated_text: 'The lord should not cast even an affectionate, kindly glance upon sinners — how much less [should he give] a praiseworthy command from a mind steeped in the sentiment of love?

children.text: atītyādityāgniprabhṛti bhuvi dharmendriyamayaṃ nṛpākhyaṃ hi jyotiḥ prasabhamidamaindraṃ vijayate // Suk_9.3 (=79) //
children.translated_text: Surpassing <s>Āditya</s> (the Sun), <s>Agni</s> (Fire), and others, this sovereign light on earth, composed of <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) and the senses, named after the king, this [light] of <s>Indra</s> prevails by force.' // Suk_9.3 (=79) //
'Nevertheless, the king's command is paramount.

children.text:
tato rājan! me kalatraṃ narāntararataṃ jātaṃ tacca mayā jñātam, tena ca duḥkhena na hasitam /
rājāpīdamākarṇya puṣpahastakai rājñīmāhṛtya sammukhamavalokayāmāsa /
sā ca tena prahāreṇa kapaṭamūrcchāṃ nāṭayati sma /
puṣpahāso 'pi tāmavalokya sahāso babhūva puṣpotkaraśca samajani /
rājāpi tāmāśvāsya kṛtakopo dvijātmajāsyaṃ vilokya mantriṇamavādīt kathamasmadduḥkhe sahāso 'si? mantryapi sabhayamañjaliṃ baddhvābhāṣata-rājan! poṭakajanaistvadīyā rājñī rātrau nāḍikābhirāhatāpi na mūrcchitā, adhunā mūrcchiteti hāsyakāraṇam /
rājāpi sakopo "mantrinnidaṃ tvayā dṛṣṭaṃ śrutaṃ ve'ti papraccha /
mantryāha-svāmindṛṣṭamevedam /
yadi svāmī na pratyeti tadā kañcukamuttāryāvalokayatu /
evaṃ kṛte rājā sarvamajñāsīt /
mantriṇo dvijasutāyāśca mukhamavalokya kimidamityavādīt /
mantryāha-svāmin! yadidaṃ dvijaputryā gūḍhārthaṃ matsyahāsyakāraṇaṃ niveditaṃ tanmayā prakaṭīkṛtam /
ityevamukto rājā āsthānaṃ vyasarjayat /
atha dvijasutāpuṣpahāsāvapi bhītahṛṣṭau svaṃ svaṃ gṛhaṃ jagmatuḥ /
tena ca rājñā tasyā mañjūṣāsthito naro dṛṣṭo vināśitaḥ /
sā ca nijavāsādvisarjitā /
śukaḥ prabhāvatīmāha-
children.translated_text:
Then, 'O king! My wife became attached to another man, and I came to know of it; because of that sorrow, I did not laugh.'
The king too, hearing this, had <s>Puṣpahasta</s> (Flower-hand) bring the queen before him and looked at her face.
She, from that blow, feigned a deceptive swoon.
<s>Puṣpahāsa</s> (Flower-laugh), looking at her, burst into laughter, and a shower of flowers appeared.
The king, consoling her and pretending anger, looked at the face of the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>'s son and said to the minister: 'How is it that you laugh at my distress?' The minister too, fearfully joining his palms, said: 'O king! Your queen, who was beaten at night with rods by the female guards, did not faint, yet now she faints — that is the cause of laughter.'
The king, angered, asked: 'Minister, did you see this or hear of it?'
The minister said: 'My lord, I saw this with my own eyes. If my lord does not believe, then let him remove [her] bodice and look.'
When this was done, the king understood everything.
Looking at the faces of the minister and the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>'s daughter, he said: 'What is the meaning of this?'
The minister said: 'My lord! The hidden meaning that the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>'s daughter communicated through the fish and the laughter — that I have made manifest.'
Thus addressed, the king dismissed the assembly.
Then the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>'s daughter and <s>Puṣpahāsa</s>, fearful yet relieved, each went to their own house.
The man hidden in the queen's chest was discovered by the king and destroyed.
And she was banished from her residence.
The parrot said to <s>Prabhāvatī</s>:

children.text: tathā tvamapi kalyāṇi mā kuruṣva vṛthāgraham /
children.translated_text: 'Likewise, O blessed one, do not make a futile resolve,

children.text: yadāgrahaparo loke vilakṣo vikramārkavat // Suk_9.4 (=80) //
children.translated_text: for one who is excessively stubborn in this world becomes disgraced, like <s>Vikramārka</s>.' Suk_9.4 (=80)

children.text: iti kathā śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text: Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau navamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the ninth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 10:
children.translated_text: START Suk 10:

children.text: anyadā saśṛṅgārā prabhāvatī śukamāha-
children.translated_text: On another occasion, <s>Prabhāvatī</s>, adorned for love, said to the parrot:

children.text: kiṃ kartavyaṃ mayā kīra tvaṃ vadādya priyamvada /
children.translated_text: 'What should I do, O parrot? Speak today, O sweet-tongued one,

children.text: yadi te 'sti sakhī yāhi śṛṅgārīva sahāyinī // Suk_10.1 (=81) //
children.translated_text: if you have a friend, go — like a companion in love's adventure.' Suk_10.1 (=81)

children.text:
prabhāvatyāha-kathametat? śuka āha-asti rājapuraṃ nāma sthānam /
tatra devasākhyaḥ kauṭumbikaḥ, tatkalatre śṛṅgāravatī subhagā ca /
children.translated_text:
<s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked: 'How so?' The parrot said: There is a place called <s>Rājapura</s>.
There lived a householder named <s>Devasā</s>, and his wife was a beautiful woman named <s>Śṛṅgāravatī</s> and <s>Subhagā</s>.

children.text: parasparaparitrāṇakṛtabandhaparāyaṇe /
children.translated_text: Devoted to forming bonds of mutual protection,

children.text: parapuruṣalampaṭe prasiddhe ratakarmaṇi // Suk_10.2 (=82) //
children.translated_text: yet lustful for other men and notorious for their amorous deeds. Suk_10.2 (=82)

children.text:
anyadā yāvatsubhagā upapatinā saha gṛhāntarvidyeta tāvadbahiḥ sthānāt patirjhiṇṭahasto gṛhadvāri samāyayau /
tadā sā kathaṃ bhavatviti praśnaḥ? uttaramāha śukaḥ-tataḥ śṛṅgāradevyā sā nagnīkṛtya gṛhādbahirniṣkāsitā /
patirapi "kimidami'ti bruvāṇo 'tyādarāt śṛṅgāradevyā uktaḥ-yattvayā etāni jhiṇṭāni devyā upavanādānītāni tata iyaṃ grahilā sañjātā /
tato yathāsthānaṃ gatvā muñca yathā praguṇā syāt /
tataḥ sa mūḍho yāvadevaṃ kartuṃ bahirjagāma tāvattayā gṛhādupapatirniṣkāsitaḥ /
iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text:
One day, while <s>Subhagā</s> was inside the house with her paramour, her husband arrived at the door with a broom in hand, returning from outside.
Then, 'What shall happen?' — that is the question. The parrot gives the answer: Then <s>Śṛṅgāradevī</s> stripped her naked and pushed her out of the house.
The husband too, saying 'What is this?', was told by <s>Śṛṅgāradevī</s> with great solicitude: 'Those brooms that you brought from the goddess's garden — from those she has become possessed by a spirit.
Therefore, go back to that place and release [the spirit] so that she may be restored.'
Then the fool, while he went outside to do this, the paramour was sent out of the house by her.
Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau daśamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the tenth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 11:
children.translated_text: START Suk 11:

children.text: pradoṣasamaye 'nyasminkāminī kāmamohitā /
children.translated_text: On another evening, the love-stricken woman, intoxicated with desire,

children.text: vinayena śukaṃ prāha gacchāmi yadi manyase // Suk_11.1 (=83) //
children.translated_text: said respectfully to the parrot: 'I shall go, if you agree.' Suk_11.1 (=83)

children.text: śukaḥ prāha-
children.translated_text: The parrot said:

children.text: avaśyameva gantavyaṃ tvayetthaṃ mama niścayaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'You must certainly go — this is my firm conviction;

children.text: mano 'bhīṣṭe payo nimne gacchatkaḥ prativārayet // Suk_11.2 (=84) //
children.translated_text: the mind [flows] toward its desire as water flows downhill — who could restrain it? Suk_11.2 (=84)

children.text: gatayāpi tvayā tatra kartavyaṃ kiñcidadbhutam /
children.translated_text: But even having gone there, you must do something extraordinary,

children.text: yathā rambhikayā pūrvaṃ brāhmaṇārthe 'dbhutaṃ kṛtam // Suk_11.3 (=85) //
children.translated_text: as <s>Rambhikā</s> once did something extraordinary for a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>'s sake.' Suk_11.3 (=85)

children.text:
prabhāvatyāha-kathametat? śuka āha-asti dābhilākhyo grāmaḥ /
tatra vilocano grāmaṇīḥ /
tadbhāryā rambhikābhidhā paranapriyā /
tāṃ ca tadbhartṛbhayānna ko 'pi kāmayate /
tataḥ sā jalavyājāt ghaṭamādāya vāpīṃ yayau /
dṛṣṭvā ca tatra surūpaṃ pathikaṃ bhaṭṭaputraṃ krīḍārthaṃ dṛṣṭisaṃjñayā babhāṇa /
so 'pi kāminīdṛṣṭisañcāracaturo viveda tadākūtam /
uktañca-
children.translated_text:
<s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked: 'How so?' The parrot said: There is a village called <s>Dābhila</s>.
There lived a village headman named <s>Vilocana</s>.
His wife, named <s>Rambhikā</s>, was fond of other men.
But because of fear of her husband, no one dared to desire her.
Then she, on the pretext of [fetching] water, took a pot and went to the tank.
Seeing there a handsome traveler, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>'s son, she communicated her desire for sport through glances.
He too, skilled in reading the signals of a woman's glances, understood her intention.
And it is said:

children.text: udīrito 'rthaḥ paśunāpi gṛhyate hayāśca nāgāśca vahanti noditāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'A meaning once expressed is grasped even by an animal; horses and elephants carry [their loads] when urged;

children.text: anuktamapyūhati paṇḍito janaḥ pareṅgitajñānaphalā hi buddhayaḥ // Suk_11.4 (=86) //
children.translated_text: but a wise person understands even what is unspoken — for the fruit of intelligence is the knowledge of another's gestures.' Suk_11.4 (=86)

children.text: kiñca ṇaabbhantaragholantīe haaramaṇarāadiṭṭhīe /
children.translated_text: [In Prakrit:] With eyes rolling within, with a gaze delighting the heart,

children.text: puṇaruttapecchirīe bālaa kiṃ kiṃ ṇa bhaṇio si // Suk_11.5 (=87) //
children.translated_text: looking again and again — O lad, what have you not been told! Suk_11.5 (=87)

children.text: [nābhyantaraṃ ghūrṇayantyā hṛdayamanorāma dṛṣṭyā /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] With eyes rolling within, with a gaze delighting the heart,

children.text: punurutprekṣamāṇayā bālaka kiṃ kiṃ na bhaṇito 'si] // Suk_11.5* (=87*) //
children.translated_text: looking up again and again — O lad, what have you not been told! Suk_11.5* (=87*)

children.text: acchīhiṃ cia bhaṇiaṃ hiaattthaṃ jo jaṇo ṇa lakkhei /
children.translated_text: [In Prakrit:] What has been said through the eyes alone, the heart's secret — the person who does not perceive it,

children.text: teṇa paḍibohieṇa e kiṃ kīrai ṇa kkhu alleṇa // Suk_11.6 (=88) //
children.translated_text: what is to be done with that fool who has been alerted [and still does not understand]? Suk_11.6 (=88)

children.text: [akṣibhyāṃ cirabhaṇitaṃ hṛdayasthaṃ yo jano na lakṣayati /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] What has been spoken through the eyes alone, what rests in the heart — the person who does not perceive it,

children.text: tena pratibodhitena ca kiṃ kriyate nu khalu ajñena] // Suk_11.6* (=88*) //
children.translated_text: what is to be done with that fool who has been alerted [and still does not understand]? Suk_11.6* (=88*)

children.text:
tataḥ sa tadantikamāgatya jagāda-bhadre kiṃ vidheyam? sāha-tvayā mama pṛṣṭhalagnena asmadgṛhaṃ samāgantavyaṃ mama patyuśca namaskāro vidheyaḥ /
sarvamanyadahaṃ kariṣye /
tvayā tathaiveti vācyam /
evamuktvā sā gṛhaṃ praviṣṭā /
so 'pi gṛhaṃ praviṣṭastatpatyaragre tasthau /
patirapi vismitaḥ /
tataḥ sā kumbhaṃ muktvā patyuḥ sakāśamāgatyāvravīt- nātha! upalakṣasva enam /
sa āha-ne vedmīti /
tataḥ sā prāha-ayaṃ mātṛmvasuḥ suto yo mayā śiśutve muktaḥ /
sa dhavalo nāma mama milanārthaṃ samāgamat /
tato mayā āliṅgya sarvāpi svajanavārtā pṛṣṭā /
sa ca brāhmaṇa "evamiti' jalpati /
tataḥ patinā sānujñātā taṃ mahānasaṃ nītvā bhojanācchādanasaṃskāraistoṣayāmāsa /
patirapi tuṣṭaḥ prāha-bhadra! tvayā nijabāndhavasya mahatī bhaktiḥ kāryetyuktvā suptaḥ /
tadā ca rambhikā brāhmaṇakhaṭṭavāyāmupāvaśat /
tatastenoktam-tvayā patyugre ityuktaṃ yanmadīyo bhrātā samāgataḥ /
tattvaṃ me pratipannā bhaginī pratipannaṃ ca nirvāhyate /
uktañaca-
children.translated_text:
Then he approached her and said: 'Fair one, what is to be done?' She said: 'You must follow behind me and come to my house, and you must bow before my husband.
All the rest I shall manage.
You need only say "So be it."'
Having said this, she entered the house.
He too entered the house and stood before her husband.
The husband was astonished.
Then she, setting down the pot, came to her husband and said: 'My lord! Look at this man.'
He said: 'I do not know him.'
Then she said: 'This is the son of my maternal uncle's brother, whom I left behind in childhood.
His name is <s>Dhavala</s>, and he has come to meet me.
I embraced him and asked him all the news of my family.'
And the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> confirmed, saying 'Indeed so.'
Then, with the husband's permission, she took him to the kitchen and gratified him with food, clothing, and comforts.
The husband too, being pleased, said: 'Good woman! You should show great devotion to your kinsman' — and went to sleep.
Then <s>Rambhikā</s> went to the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>'s cot.
Then he said: 'You told your husband that your brother has come.
Thus you have become my sister, and what has been assumed must be upheld.'
And it is said:

children.text: chijjau sīsuṃ aha hou bandhaṇaṃ caau savvahā lacchī /
children.translated_text: [In Prakrit:] Let the head be cut off, or let there be imprisonment, let fortune depart entirely —

children.text: paḍivaṇṇapālaṇe supurisāṇa jaṃ hou taṃ hou // Suk_11.7 (=89) //
children.translated_text: in keeping a promise, for virtuous people, whatever happens, let it happen. Suk_11.7 (=89)

children.text: [chidyatāṃ śīrṣamatha bhavatu bandhanaṃ calatu sarvathā lakṣmīḥ /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] Let the head be cut off, or let there be imprisonment, let wealth depart entirely —

children.text: pratipannapālane supuruṣāṇāṃ yad bhavatu tad bhavatu] // Suk_11.7* (=89*) //
children.translated_text: in keeping a promise, for virtuous people, whatever happens, let it happen. Suk_11.7* (=89*)

children.text: lajjijjai jeṇa maṇo mailijjai ṇiakulakkamo jeṇa /
children.translated_text: [In Prakrit:] That by which the mind is shamed, by which one's family tradition is stained —

children.text: kaṇṭhaṭṭhie vi jīe mā sundari taṃ kuṇijjāsu // Suk_11.8 (=90) //
children.translated_text: even while life still clings to the throat, O beautiful one, do not do that. Suk_11.8 (=90)

children.text: [lajjate yena mano malinayati nijakulakramo yena /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] That by which the mind is shamed, by which one's family tradition is stained —

children.text: kaṇṭhasthite 'pi jīve mā sundari taṃ kariṣyasi] // Suk_11.8* (=90*) //
children.translated_text: even while life still clings to the throat, O beautiful one, do not do that. Suk_11.8* (=90*)

children.text: rambhikā prāha-mā evaṃ vada /
children.translated_text: <s>Rambhikā</s> said: 'Do not speak thus.

children.text: yato 'tidurlabhā rāmā pitṛmātṛparāyaṇā /
children.translated_text: For exceedingly rare is a woman devoted to her parents;

children.text: pitṛmātṛmayairbhūtvā bhoktavyā kāminī raiḥ // Suk_11.9 (=91) //
children.translated_text: a woman should be enjoyed by men who have become [like] her father and mother.' Suk_11.9 (=91)

children.text: uktañca-
children.translated_text: And it is said:

children.text: kāmārtāṃ svayamāyātāṃ yo na bhuṅkte nitambinīm /
children.translated_text: 'He who does not enjoy a full-hipped woman who comes of her own accord, driven by desire,

children.text: so 'vaśyaṃ narakaṃ yāti tanniḥśvāsahato naraḥ // Suk_11.10 (=92) //
children.translated_text: surely goes to hell — a man struck down by her sighs.' Suk_11.10 (=92)

children.text: so kiṃ va māṇai para mahila jo ṇavi jaṃpi emva /
children.translated_text: [In Prakrit:] What does he think of other women, he who does not even speak thus —

children.text: [sa kimeva manyate paramahilāṃ yo viparītaṃ jalpatyevam /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] What does he think of other women, he who speaks contrarily thus —

children.text: jo ṇavi māṇai... so kiṃ va māṇai thī avarāi /
children.translated_text: [In Prakrit:] He who does not regard [her]... what then does he think of another woman?

children.text: ... ... ... mā kari ṇeha amhahaṃ bhaṅgu // Suk_11.12 (=94) //
children.translated_text: ... ... ... Do not break the affection between us. Suk_11.12 (=94)

children.text: [yo viparītaṃ manyate...sa kimiva manyate striyamaparām /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] He who thinks contrarily... what then does he think of another woman?

children.text: śrūyate rukmiṇī pūrvaṃ kṛṣṇeva madanāturā /
children.translated_text: It is heard that <s>Rukmiṇī</s> herself was once stricken with love for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>;

children.text: gṛhītā bhrātṛjāyāpi kaḥ kāmamatilaṅghayet // Suk_11.13 (=95) //
children.translated_text: even a brother's wife was seized — who can transgress desire? Suk_11.13 (=95)

children.text: virañcirapi kāmārtaṃ svasutāmabhilāṣukaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even <s>Virañci</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), overcome by desire, lusted after his own daughter;

children.text: dṛśyate 'dyāpi viyati hāriṇīṃ tanumāśritaḥ // Suk_11.14 (=96) //
children.translated_text: he is still seen in the sky to this day, having assumed the form of [a deer chasing] a doe. Suk_11.14 (=96)

children.text: vivāhe pārvatī dṛṣṭvā harasya haravallabhām /
children.translated_text: At the wedding, even [<s>Brahmā</s>], upon seeing <s>Pārvatī</s>, the beloved of <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>),

children.text: caskanda retastasyāpi bālakhilyāstadudbhavāḥ // Suk_11.15 (=97) //
children.translated_text: his seed fell; the <s>Bālakhilyas</s> (thumb-sized sages) were born from that. Suk_11.15 (=97)

children.text: tayaivaṃ bodhito mūrkhaḥ sa yāvadramate na tām /
children.translated_text: Thus instructed by her, the fool — just as he was not enjoying her —

children.text: phūtkṛtaṃ muṣitāsmīti trāyatāṃ trāyatāmaho // Suk_11.16 (=98) //
children.translated_text: she blew [a whistle], [crying] 'I am robbed! Save me! Save me! Oh!' Suk_11.16 (=98)

children.text:
tayā ca phūtkṛte kimidamiti kurvāṇo bāndhavaiḥ saha dhāvito bhartā /
sa ca kathaṃ mucyate? iti praśnaḥ /
uttaram-evaṃ ca sa brāhmaṇaḥ sabhayaḥ sannataḥ pādayoḥ patito jagāda-svāmini! prāṇān rakṣa /
tavehitaṃ kariṣyāmi /
evaṃ sthite sā dugdhasahitaṃ bhaktamaḍhaṇḍholayat antike jvalinamajvālayat /
āgataṃ ca patiṃ jagāda-asya viṣūcikā upapannā /
tato mayā phūtkṛtam /
evamuktvā dugdhabhaktaṃ pradaśitam /
patirapi mūrkho dṛṣṭvā yayau /
tataḥ sā patyau supte yadṛcchayā surataṃ cakāra /
so 'pi ca māndyavyājānmāsamekaṃ sthitaḥ paścājjagāma /
iti śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text:
And when she blew [the whistle], the husband, wondering 'What is this?', came running with his kinsmen.
And how is he [the brāhmaṇa] freed? — that is the question.
The answer: Thus that <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, terrified, fell prostrate at her feet and said: 'My lady! Spare my life!
I will do whatever you desire.'
Things being thus, she stirred the rice with milk, and lit a fire nearby.
And to her arriving husband she said: 'He has been seized by cholera.
Therefore I blew [the whistle].'
Having said this, she showed the milk-rice.
The foolish husband, having seen it, went away.
Then, when her husband was asleep, she made love at her pleasure.
And he [the brāhmaṇa], on the pretext of illness, stayed for one month and then departed.
Having heard this, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau ekādaśī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the eleventh tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 12:
children.translated_text: START Suk 12:

children.text:
athānyadā sā calitā /
śukaḥ prāha-
children.translated_text:
Then on another occasion, she set out [to leave].
The parrot said:

children.text: viparīte samāyāte yadi vetsi tvamutaram /
children.translated_text: 'If when an adverse situation arises you know the answer,

children.text: yathā śobhikayā proktaṃ vavvūle carite sati // Suk_12.1 (=99) //
children.translated_text: as <s>Śobhikā</s> spoke when the <s>vavvūla</s> (bat/tree) incident occurred —' Suk_12.1 (=99)

children.text: astyatra nalauḍāgrāme kulālo mahādhanaḥ /
tasya bhāryā śobhikā nāma paraṃ kulaṭā naralampaṭā ca /
children.translated_text: His wife, named <s>Śobhikā</s>, was exceedingly wanton and lustful for men.

children.text: sā patyau bahirgate upapatisahitā gṛhāntaḥ krīḍati /
children.translated_text: When her husband had gone out, she sported inside the house with her paramour.

children.text: tasyāścaivaṃ sthitāyā bhartā gṛhaṃ samāgamat /
children.translated_text: While she was thus engaged, her husband returned home.

children.text: tadanantaraṃ sā kathaṃ bhavatviti praśnaḥ //
children.translated_text: Then, 'What shall happen?' — that is the question.
There is in <s>Nalauḍā</s> village a potter of great wealth.

children.text:
śukaḥ prāha-yadā ca tayā sa āgacchan jñānastadā upapatiruktaḥ-"ca] tvaṃ vavvūlavṛkṣam' /
evaṃ ca sa tayo proktastathā cakāra /
tasya ca vṛkṣe caṭataḥ paridhānavastraṃ vilagnaṃ nagno 'pi vṛkṣamārūḍhaḥ /
tasmiṃśca vṛkṣamārūḍhe patiḥ prāha-kamidamiti /
sā āha-ayaṃ śatrubhirabhibhūto 'dovastramapi tyaktvā vavvūlamadhirūḍhaḥ /
tataḥ samāgatya tasyāḥ patinā vṛkṣānmandaṃ mandamuttārya sa svagṛhaṃ preṣitaḥ /
tayā dhūrtayā ca sahahastatālaṃ hasitam /
iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text:
The parrot said: When she knew that he was coming, the paramour was told: 'Climb the <s>vavvūla</s> (bat-fig) tree!'
Thus instructed by her, he did so.
But while climbing the tree, his garment got caught, and he climbed the tree naked.
When he had climbed the tree, the husband said: 'What is this?'
She said: 'This man, overwhelmed by enemies, having abandoned even his garment, has climbed the <s>vavvūla</s> tree.'
Then her husband, having come, gently helped him down from the tree and sent him to his own house.
And the cunning woman clapped her hands and laughed [with delight].
Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau dvādaśokathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twelfth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 13:
children.translated_text: START Suk 13:

children.text:
athānyedyuḥ prabhāvatī śukaṃ pṛcchati /
śuka āha-
children.translated_text:
Then on the next day, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> questioned the parrot.
The parrot said:

children.text: vraja devi sukhaṃ bhuṅkṣva ardhabhukte patau yathā /
children.translated_text: 'Go, O lady, enjoy yourself happily, as <s>Rājikā</s> did when her husband had half-eaten —

children.text: kṛtaṃ rājikayā cittamuttaraṃ dhūlisaṃyutam // Suk_13.1 (=100) //
children.translated_text: the answer, mixed with dust, was devised [by her]. Suk_13.1 (=100)'

children.text:
asti nāgapuraṃ nāma sthānam /
yatraiko vaṇika /
tatpatnī rājikānāmnī surūpā paraṃ duścāriṇo /
vaṇiksutaśca tāṃ narāntarāsaktāṃ na jānāti /
tataśca ekadā sa bhojanāya yadopaviṣṭastadā upapatiḥ kṛtasaṃketo mārge gacchan tayā dṛṣṭaḥ /
taṃ ta dṛṣṭvā gṛhe 'dya dhṛtaṃ nāsti ityuktvā dravyaṃ tatsakāśādādāya ghṛtānayanadambhena veśmato nirgatya ca sā bahirjāreṇa saha ciraṃ sthitā /
patistu gṛhe kṣudhārtaḥ kruddhaśca /
tataḥ sā kathaṃ gṛhaṃ gantumarhati-iti praśnaḥ /
uttaram-tataḥ sā hastau pādau mukhaṃ ca dhūlidhūsaraṃ vidhāya sadrammā dhūliṃ gṛhītvā gṛhamāgatā /
patiḥ kruddho raktekṣaṇaḥ kimidamityāha /
sā ca saniḥśvāsaṃ rudatī dhūlipuñjaṃ darśayitvā idamuvāca-yatkṛte tvaṃ kruddhaḥ sa te dravyo 'tra dhūlyāṃ patitaḥ /
enāmutkṣipya gṛhāṇa tvam /
evamuktaḥ sa vilakṣaḥ tadaṅgāni vastrāñcalena sammārjya sāntvayāmāsa vividhalālanaiḥ /
iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text: There is a place named <s>Nāgapura</s>. There lived a merchant. His wife, named <s>Rājikā</s>, was beautiful but of loose conduct. The merchant's son did not know that she was attached to another man. Then one day, when he sat down for a meal, the paramour, with whom she had made an assignation, was seen by her passing on the road. Seeing him, she said 'There is no ghee kept in the house today,' took some money from him, and went out of the house on the pretext of fetching ghee. She stayed outside with her lover for a long time. The husband meanwhile was hungry and angry in the house. Then [the question is]: how should she return home? The answer: Then she made her hands, feet, and face grey with dust, took the coins along with the dust, and came home. The husband, angry, with reddened eyes, said 'What is this?' She, sighing and weeping, showed the heap of dust and said: 'The money for which you are angry — that wealth of yours has fallen here in the dust. Pick it up and take it yourself.' Thus addressed, he was abashed, wiped her limbs with the edge of his garment, and consoled her with various endearments. Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau trayodaśī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the thirteenth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 14:
children.translated_text: START Suk 14:

children.text: sā nitambini anyedyuścalitā /
children.translated_text: That full-hipped woman set out on another day.

children.text: śukenoktam- yuktameva viśālākṣi paraṃ rantuṃ yadṛcchayā /
children.translated_text: The parrot said: 'It is indeed fitting, O large-eyed one, to enjoy another at will,

children.text: yadyāyāte patau vetsi dhanaśrīriva bhāṣitum // Suk_14.1 (=101) //
children.translated_text: if, when your husband returns, you know how to speak like <s>Dhanaśrī</s>.' Suk_14.1 (=101)

children.text:
prabhāvatyāha-kimetat /
śukaḥ prāha-asti padmāvatī purī /
tatra dhanavālo nāma vaṇik /
tasya bhāryā prāṇebhyo 'pi priyā dhanaśrornāma /
tacca mithunaṃ parasparaṃ snehanirbharaṃ krīḍati /
anyadā tu vaṇigdravyasāramādāya tāmāpṛcchya deśāntaraṃ jagāma /
sā ca tasmingate saṃsthiteva gṛhasthitā /
children.translated_text: <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked: 'What is this?' The parrot said: There is a city named <s>Padmāvatī</s>. There lived a merchant named <s>Dhanavāla</s>. His wife, dearer than life itself, was named <s>Dhanaśrī</s>. That couple played together, overflowing with mutual affection. But one day, the merchant, taking his valuable merchandise, took leave of her and went to another land. And she, when he had gone, remained in the house as if lifeless.

children.text: na snāti na ca sā bhuṅkte na jalpati sakhīsamam /
children.translated_text: She does not bathe, she does not eat, she does not converse with her friends,

children.text: nirastāśeṣasaṃskārā svadehe 'pi parāṅmukhī // Suk_14.2 (=102) //
children.translated_text: having abandoned all adornments, she is indifferent even to her own body. Suk_14.2 (=102)

children.text: malayānilamārūḍhaḥ kokilālāpaḍiṇḍimaḥ /
children.translated_text: Borne upon the <s>Malaya</s> breeze, the drumbeat of the cuckoo's song,

children.text: mallikāmodadūtaśca madhupāravamaṅgalaḥ // Suk_14.3 (=103) //
children.translated_text: the messenger of jasmine fragrance, and the auspicious humming of bees — Suk_14.3 (=103)

children.text: anyadā tu samāyāto vasantaḥ kālarāṭ kṣitau /
children.translated_text: one day, spring arrived upon the earth like the king of seasons,

children.text: mano 'pi vikriyāṃ yasminyāti saṃyamināṃ kila // Suk_14.4 (=104) //
children.translated_text: in which even the minds of the self-controlled undergo transformation. Suk_14.4 (=104)

children.text:
tasminvasantotsave gṛhopari sthitā nagarīrāmaṇīyakamālokya yauvanaṃ rūpaṃ ca nininda /
sakhī ca tadiṅgitajñā jagāda-bhāmini! rūpaṃ vayaśca mā vyarthaṃ vidhehi /
children.translated_text: During that spring festival, standing atop her house, gazing upon the beauty of the city, she bemoaned her youth and beauty. And her friend, understanding her gestures, said: 'O passionate one! Do not let your beauty and youth go to waste.'

children.text: yataḥ- vādyate śṛṇu rambhoru kokilārāvaḍiṇḍimaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'For — listen, O beautiful-thighed one, the drumbeat of the cuckoo's song is being played

children.text: madanasya nṛpasyeva vasantena dharātale // Suk_14.5 (=105) //
children.translated_text: as if by <s>Vasanta</s> (Spring) for the king <s>Madana</s> (the Love-god) upon the surface of the earth.' Suk_14.5 (=105)

children.text: muñcantu māninaḥ sarve mānaṃ sevantu vallabhāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Let all the proud ones abandon their pride; let lovers serve [their beloveds];

children.text: gatvaraṃ yauvanaṃ loke jīvitaṃ ca tathā calam // Suk_14.6 (=106) //
children.translated_text: youth is fleeting in this world, and life too is equally transient.' Suk_14.6 (=106)

children.text:
tatastvamapi kuru vayaḥsāphalyamityukte dhanaśrīrjagāda-nāhaṃ vilambituṃ sahāmi /
yattvayā bhavati tat śīghraṃ vidhehi /
tatastayā sā narāntareṇa yojitā /
yadā ca sā tenātmāsaktā jñātā tadā tadīyaśiroveṇī chinnā /
tatkāle ca patirdeśāntarādājagāma /
tadā sā kathaṃ bhavatviti praśnaḥ /
śukaḥ prāha-yadā ca patirgṛhadvāramāyayau tadā tayottaraṃ vicintyokm-nātha! tvayā tādavadgṛhadvāri sthīyatāṃ yāvatsarvaṃ sajjaṃ vidhīyate /
tena caivaṃ pratipanne sā madhye gatvā bhaṭṭārikāṃ pūjayitvā purato veṇīṃ sthāpayāmāsa /
evaṃ kṛtvā bahirnirgatya caraṇamaṇḍakaiḥ patiṃ gṛhantardevīpurato nītvā jagāda-nātha! pūjaya gṛhādhidevatām /
tena pūjayatā veṇīṃ dṛṣṭvā uktam-kimidamiti /
tayoktam-mayopayācitamāsīt /
yadā me patiḥ sameṣyati tadā svāminyahaṃ tavāgre veṇīṃ chetsyāmi /
tadadhunā mayā kṛtam /
sa ca mugdho devīṃ namaskṛtya tāṃ bahu mānayāmāsa /
iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, you too should make your youth fruitful.' Thus addressed, <s>Dhanaśrī</s> said: 'I cannot bear to delay. Whatever you can arrange, do it quickly.' Then her friend united her with another man. But when he discovered that she was attached to him, he cut off her hair-braid. At that very time, her husband returned from the foreign land. Then [the question is]: what should she do? The parrot said: When the husband came to the door of the house, she thought of a reply and said: 'My lord! Please stand at the door for a moment while everything is prepared.' When he agreed to this, she went inside, worshipped the household goddess (<s>Bhaṭṭārikā</s>), and placed the [severed] braid before [the goddess]. Having done this, she came outside and, with foot-ornament offerings, led her husband inside the house before the goddess and said: 'My lord! Worship the household deity.' As he was worshipping, he saw the braid and asked: 'What is this?' She said: 'I had made a vow: when my husband returns, O Mistress, I shall cut my braid before you. Now I have fulfilled it.' And that simple man, bowing to the goddess, honored her greatly. Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau caturdaśī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fourteenth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 15:
children.translated_text: START Suk 15:

children.text: anyadā sā calitā /
children.translated_text: On another day, she set out.

children.text: hasannāha śuko yāhi yadi kartuṃ tvamuttaram /
children.translated_text: The parrot said with a laugh: 'Go, if you know how to give an answer

children.text: vetsi yathā śriyādevyā nūpure 'pahṛte kṛtam // Suk_15.1 (=107) //
children.translated_text: as <s>Śriyādevī</s> did when her anklet was taken away.' Suk_15.1 (=107)

children.text:
asti śālipuraṃ nāma nagaram /
tatra śāligo vaṇik /
tatpatnī jayikā /
tayoḥ suto guṇākaro nāmābhūt /
tadbhāryā śriyādevī /
sā cāpareṇa subuddhināmnā vaṇijā saha ramate /
children.translated_text: She enjoyed herself with another merchant named <s>Subuddhi</s>.

children.text: tato lokāpavāde 'pi saṃjāte 'nuraktastadīyaḥ patirna kimapi karṇe karoti /
children.translated_text: And even when public scandal arose, her infatuated husband paid no heed to anything.

children.text: uktañca- rattā picchanti guṇā dosā picchanti je virattatti /
children.translated_text: And it is said: The infatuated see virtues; the dispassionate see faults;

children.text: majjhatthā uṇa purisā dosā vi guṇā vi picchanti // Suk_15.2 (=108) //
children.translated_text: but impartial people see both faults and virtues. Suk_15.2 (=108)
There is a city named <s>Śālipura</s>. There lived a merchant named <s>Śāligo</s>. His wife was <s>Jayikā</s>. Their son was named <s>Guṇākara</s>. His wife was <s>Śriyādevī</s>.

children.text: [raktāḥ pṛcchanti guṇān doṣān pṛcchanti ye viraktāḥ /
children.translated_text: [The infatuated see virtues; the dispassionate see faults;

children.text: madhyasthāḥ punaḥ puruṣā doṣānapi guṇānapi pṛcchanti] // Suk_15.2* (=108*) //
children.translated_text: but impartial people see both faults and virtues.] Suk_15.2* (=108*)

children.text: kiñca- mahilārattā purisā cheā vi ṇa saṃbharanti appāṇaṃ /
children.translated_text: Moreover: Men infatuated with women, even if clever, do not control themselves;

children.text: iare uṇa taruṇīṇaṃ purisā salilaṃ va hatthagaaṃ // Suk_15.3 (=109) //
children.translated_text: but for other men, women are [like] water slipping from the hand. Suk_15.3 (=109)

children.text: [mahilāraktāḥ puruṣāśchekā api na sambharanti ātmanām /
children.translated_text: [Men infatuated with women, even if clever, do not control themselves;

children.text: itare punastaruṇīnāṃ puruṣāḥ salilameva hastagatam] // Suk_15.3* (=109*) //
children.translated_text: but for other men, women are [like] water slipping from the hand.] Suk_15.3* (=109*)

children.text:
anyadā sā śvaśureṇa narāntarasahitā suptā dṛṣṭā /
tataścaraṇānnūpuraṃ śvaśureṇa cottāritaṃ tayā ca jñātam /
tataḥ sā taṃ jāraṃ prasthāpya bhartāraṃ tatrānīya tena saha suptā /
nidrāntare ca patirutthāpitaḥ kathitañca-tvadoyena pitrā nūpuramasmatpādādavartāya gṛhītam /
evaṃvidhaṃ ca pātakaṃ kvāpi na dṛṣṭaṃ yadvadhūpādāt śvaśuro nūpuraṃ gṛhṇāti /
tenoktam-prātaḥ pituḥ sakāśātsvayamarpayiṣyāmi /
tena ca guṇākareṇa pitara nirbhartsya tatsakāśānnūpuraṃ yācitam /
pitrā coktam-yadiyaṃ parapuruṣeṇa saha suptā dṛṣṭā ato mayā nūpuraṃ gṛhītam /
tayoktam-tvatputreṇa saha suptāhamāsam /
ityarthe divyaṃ karomi /
atraiva grāme uttarasyāṃ diśi yakṣo 'sti /
tasya jaṅghāntarānnirgamiṣyāmi /
yaḥ kaścitsatyo bhavati sa jaṅghayorantarānniṣkrāmyatīti prasiddham /
evaṃ śvaśureṇa cāṅgīkṛte sā kulaṭā sati dine jārasya gṛhe gatvā tamuvāca-bho kānta! prātarahaṃ divyārthaṃ yakṣasya jaṅghāntarānnirgamiṣyāmi /
tvayā tatra samāgatya vātūlatvamāśritya mama kaṇṭhagraho vidheyaḥ /
tena ca tathokte sā svagṛhamājagāma /
atha prāpaḥ samastamahājanaṃ malayitvā puṣpākṣatādikamādaya yakṣāyatane gatvā samīpasarasi snānaṃ kṛtvā yakṣapūjārthaṃ samāgacchantyāstasyāḥ pūrvasaṅketito jāro grahilībhūtastatkaṇṭhe nijabāhudvayaṃ yojayāmāsa /
tata āḥ kimetadityabhidhāya sā punaḥ snānārthaṃ yayau /
so 'pi grahilo lokaiḥ kaṇṭhe gṛhītvā tasmātpradeśāddūrīkṛtaḥ /
sāpi snānaṃ kṛtvā yakṣasamīpamāgatya puṣpagandhādyairabhyarcya sarvalokānāṃ śṛṇvatāmuvāca-bho bhagavanyakṣa! nijabhartāramenaṃ ca grahilaṃ vinā yadyanyapuruṣaḥ spṛśati kadācana māṃ tadā tava jaghābhyāṃ sakāśānmama niṣkramaṇaṃ mā bhavatvityabhidhāya sarvalokasamakṣameva jaṅghayormadhye praviśya niṣkrāntā /
yakṣo 'pi tadbuddhi manasi ślāghamāna eva sthitaḥ /
sāpi satīti samastalokaiḥ pūjitā svabhavanaṃ jagāma /
evaṃ cet śriyādevīvatkartuṃ jānāsi tadā vraja /
iti śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text: One day, she was seen sleeping with another man by her father-in-law. The father-in-law then removed an anklet from her foot, and she noticed it. Then she sent the lover away, brought her husband there, and slept with him. In the middle of the night, she woke her husband and said: 'Your wicked father removed an anklet from my foot. Such a sin has never been seen anywhere — that a father-in-law takes an anklet from his daughter-in-law's foot!' He said: 'In the morning I will get it back from my father myself.' Then <s>Guṇākara</s>, scolding his father, demanded the anklet from him. The father said: 'She was seen sleeping with another man, therefore I took the anklet.' She said: 'I was sleeping with your son! On this matter, I will undergo an ordeal. In this very village, to the north, there is a <s>Yakṣa</s> (spirit). I shall pass between his legs. It is well known that whoever is truthful passes between his legs.' When the father-in-law agreed to this, that unchaste woman went during the day to her lover's house and said to him: 'Dear one! Tomorrow morning, for the purpose of the ordeal, I shall pass between the legs of the <s>Yakṣa</s>. You must come there and, pretending to be a madman, seize me by the throat.' When he agreed, she returned to her own house. Then in the morning, having assembled all the townspeople, taking flowers, rice, and other offerings, she went to the <s>Yakṣa</s> shrine, bathed in the nearby lake, and as she was approaching to worship the <s>Yakṣa</s>, her pre-arranged lover, pretending to be possessed, clasped her throat with both his arms. Then she cried 'Ah! What is this!' and went again to bathe. The possessed man was seized by the neck by the crowd and removed from that place. She too, having bathed, approached the <s>Yakṣa</s>, worshipped with flowers, perfume, and other offerings, and said in the hearing of all the people: 'O Lord <s>Yakṣa</s>! If any man other than my own husband and this possessed man has ever touched me, then may I not pass between your legs!' Having said this, in the sight of all the people, she entered between the legs and emerged. The <s>Yakṣa</s> too stood there, admiring her cleverness in his mind. And she, being honored as a chaste woman by all the people, went to her own home. 'If you know how to act like <s>Śriyādevī</s>, then go.' Having heard this, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau pañcadaśī katā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifteenth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 16:
children.translated_text: START Suk 16:

children.text: anyadā sā calitā śukaṃ prāha-śukāhaṃ narāntaraṃ gamiṣyāmi /
children.translated_text: On another day, she set out and said to the parrot: 'Parrot, I am going to another man.'

children.text: śukaḥ prāha- satyameva tvayābhāṇi kartavyaṃ yanmano 'nugam /
children.translated_text: The parrot said: 'What you have spoken is indeed true — one should do what the mind desires;

children.text: manastu mugdhikā yadvadaśakyānkhedayatyalam // Suk_16.1 (=110) //
children.translated_text: but the mind, like <s>Mugdhikā</s>, causes much trouble to those who are helpless.' Suk_16.1 (=110)

children.text:
tacdhrutvā prabhāvatyāha-kathametat /
so 'bravīt-asti vidiśā nāma purī /
tasyāṃ janavallabho nāma vaṇik /
tasya bhāryā mugdhikā nāma capalā svairiṇī /
yadā ca tayātiśayena vidūṣito 'yaṃ tadā bandhūnāṃ kathayāmāsa yadiyaṃ bahiḥśāyinī /
yadā ca tairevamuktā tadā tayāpyuktam-ayameva bahiḥśāyī sadaiva /
māṃ mudhāpavādayati /
tatastairmilitvā nirbandhaḥ kṛtaḥ "yaḥ ko 'pi adyaprabhṛti bahiḥśāyī so 'parādho" /
evaṃ nirbandhe kṛte 'pi sā suptaṃ patiṃ vihāya bahirgatā /
tasyāṃ ca bahirgatāyāṃ sa patirdvāraṃ datvā suptaḥ /
yadā cabahiḥ krīḍāṃ kṛtvā samāgatāyāḥ sa patirdvāraṃ nodghāṭayati tadā sā kūpe dṛṣadaṃ kṣiptvā dvāradeśa eva sthitā /
patirapi kūpe patitā bhaviṣyatīti jñātvā dvāramudghāṭyabahirnirgataḥ /
tadā sā dvāraṃ pidhāya madhye sthitā /
so 'pi ca bahiḥ sthito "hā priye' evaṃ vadanmahatā śabdena goditumārabdhaḥ /
sāpi vigopakabhayādbahirnirgatya patiṃ madhye nināya /
tatastanmithuna parasparaṃ nirbandhaṃ cakāra /
yadadyaprabhṛti mayā tvayā visaṃvādo na vidheyaḥ /
iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text: Hearing this, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked: 'How is this?' He said: There is a city named <s>Vidiśā</s>. In it lived a merchant named <s>Janavallabha</s>. His wife, named <s>Mugdhikā</s>, was fickle and wanton. When he was excessively disgraced by her, he told his relatives that she was sleeping outside [at night]. When they told her this, she also said: 'He himself always sleeps outside. He falsely defames me.' Then they agreed together and imposed the rule: 'From today onwards, whoever sleeps outside is the guilty one.' Even after this restriction was imposed, she left her sleeping husband and went outside. When she had gone out, the husband locked the door and slept. When, having finished her dalliance outside, she returned and her husband would not open the door, she threw a stone into the well and stood right at the doorway. The husband, thinking she had fallen into the well, opened the door and went outside. Then she went inside and locked the door. He stood outside, crying 'Ah, my dear!' and began to shout loudly. She too, fearing the village watchmen, came outside and led her husband inside. Then that couple made a pact with each other: 'From today onwards, neither of us shall deceive the other.' Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau ṣoḍaśī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the sixteenth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 17:
children.translated_text: START Suk 17:

children.text:
anyadā sā hasantī narāntaragamanāya śukaṃ pṛcchati /
śuka āha-yadeva manaso 'bhīṣṭaṃ tadeva kāryam /
children.translated_text: On another day, she laughingly asked the parrot [for permission] to go to another man. The parrot said: 'Whatever is desired by the mind, that alone should be done.'

children.text: uktañca- dṛṣṭipūtaṃ nyasetpādaṃ vastrapūtaṃ jalaṃ pibet /
children.translated_text: And it is said: 'One should place one's foot [only] where the eye has purified, one should drink water [only] purified through cloth,

children.text: satyapūtaṃ vadedvākyaṃ manaḥpūtaṃ samācaret // Suk_17.1 (=111) //
children.translated_text: one should speak words [only] purified by truth, and one should practice [only] what the mind has purified.' Suk_17.1 (=111)

children.text: mano 'nukūlaṃ kurvantu tanvi te duḥkhamāgatam /
children.translated_text: 'Let those who follow the mind's inclination, O slender one, your suffering has come;

children.text: soḍhuṃ śaktāstathā vaktuṃ guṇāḍhyo brāhmaṇo yathā // Suk_17.2 (=112) //
children.translated_text: [can you] endure it and speak [fittingly], as the virtuous <s>brāhmaṇa</s> [did]?' Suk_17.2 (=112)

children.text:
prabhāvatī pṛcchati-kathametat /
śukaḥ kathayati-asti viśālā purī /
tatra yāyajūko brāhmaṇaḥ /
tasya patnī pāhinī nāma surūpā ativallabhā /
tatputraḥ pitrā sarvāmapi kramādvidyāṃ grāhitaḥ /
anyadā sa pitarau muktvā deśāntaraṃ gataḥ /
guṇāḍhya iti viśruto babhūva /
jayantyāṃ ca nagaryāṃ buddhijīvanaṃ vyacintayat /
tataḥ ṣaṇḍaṃ yavakāśādibhiḥ pupoṣa /
so 'pi ṣaṇḍastamanu paribhramati /
anyadā sabandhanaṃ ṣaṇḍaṃ vidhāya vaṇijārakaveṣadhārī madanāyā veśyāyāḥ kṭuṭinīṃ jagāda-asmadīyā balīvardāḥ savastukā prātareṣyanti /
adyāhaṃ tṛṇānayanārthamāgataḥ /
tadyatra asmadīyasya balīvardasya sthānaṃ bhavati tatrāhaṃ svapimi /
ityukte sā kuṭṭinī balīvadadhanaiṣiṇī taṃ sthāpayāmāsa /
so 'pi taṃ ṣaṇḍaṃ baddhvā vilāsinīpārśve yayau /
tayā ca snāpito bhojitaśca guṇāḍhyo rajanyāṃ śṛṅgāritaḥ tatsakāśe sthitaḥ /
so 'pi ca prabhātāyāṃ niśi prathamamevotthāya svarṇaśṛṅkhalā gṛhītvā jagāma /
gate ca tasminnekā ceṭī utthitā ṣaṇḍamadṛṣṭvā kuṭṭinīṃ pratyāha "āue kimidam' /
tatastaṃ vilāsinīpārśvādgataṃ jñātvā maunaṃ vidhāya sthitā /
children.translated_text:
<s>Prabhāvatī</s> asks: 'How is that?'
The parrot narrates: There is a city named <s>Viśālā</s>. There lived a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who followed the <s>Yajurveda</s>. His wife, named <s>Pāhinī</s>, was beautiful and very dear to him. Their son was taught all the various branches of learning by his father in due order. One day, leaving his parents, he went to another land and became renowned as <s>Guṇāḍhya</s>. In the city of <s>Jayantī</s>, he devised a plan for earning a livelihood by his wits. So he fattened a bull with barley, grass, and the like. That bull followed him about everywhere. One day, having tethered the bull, he disguised himself as a merchant and said to the <s>kuṭṭinī</s> (procuress) of a courtesan named <s>Madanā</s>: 'My bullocks with their goods will arrive in the morning. Today I have come to fetch fodder. Let me sleep wherever my bullock's stall is.' When he said this, the <s>kuṭṭinī</s>, eager for the bullock's profit, gave him a place. He then tied up the bull and went to the courtesan's side. Having been bathed and fed by her, <s>Guṇāḍhya</s> spent the night in amorous enjoyment in her company. And he, rising before dawn at the end of the night, seized a golden chain and departed. When he had gone, a maidservant, having risen and not seeing the bull, said to the <s>kuṭṭinī</s>: 'Mistress, what is this?' Then, learning that he had gone from the courtesan's side, she maintained silence.

children.text: uktañca- arthanāśaṃ manastāpaṃ gṛhe duścaritāni ca /
children.translated_text: And it is said: Loss of wealth, mental anguish, misconduct in the household,

children.text: vañcanaṃ cāpamānaṃ ca matimānna prakāśayet // Suk_17.3 (=113) //
children.translated_text: deception and dishonour — a wise person should not make these public. Suk_17.3 (=113)

children.text:
anyadā guṇāḍhyo dyūtanirjitaḥ khaṭikāhasto veśyayā dhṛtaḥ /
tenopāyaścinnitaḥ-śambalo śambalīti jagāda /
tatastayā rājabhayānmuktaḥ /
tatastasyāṃ calitāyāṃ pṛṣṭhalagna eva śambalīti vadan gacchati /
tatastayā vijane nītvā hastātprasādya svarṇābharaṇaṃ dattam /
children.translated_text: On another occasion, <s>Guṇāḍhya</s>, having been defeated at gambling, was seized by the courtesan while holding a piece of chalk. He devised a stratagem — he cried out '<s>Śambala</s>! <s>Śambalī</s>!' Then, out of fear of the king's men, she released him. But when she started to leave, he followed close behind her, repeatedly saying '<s>Śambalī</s>!' Then she led him to a secluded place and, having appeased him by hand, gave him a gold ornament.

children.text: soḍhuṃ tyaktuṃ ca yaḥ śakto manasā kṛtamanyathā /
children.translated_text: He who is able to endure and to abandon, and who can turn to his own advantage what the mind has done otherwise,

children.text: mano 'nukūlatāṃ kurvanna sa nindyaḥ sadā satām // Suk_17.4 (=114) //
children.translated_text: making the mind favourable to himself — such a person is never censured by the virtuous. Suk_17.4 (=114)

children.text: iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text: Having heard this story, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau saptadaśī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the seventeenth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 18:
children.translated_text: START Suk 18:

children.text: anyadā sā calitā śukenoktā /
children.translated_text: On another day, as she was about to set out, the parrot said:

children.text: gaccha devi na te deṣo gacchantyāḥ paraveśmani /
children.translated_text: 'Go, O queen, there is no fault in your going to another's house,

children.text: yadi kāciccharīre te buddhiḥ sarṣapacauravat // Suk_18.1 (=115) //
children.translated_text: if you have some wit in your body, like the mustard-seed thief.' Suk_18.1 (=115)

children.text:
asti śubhasthānaṃ nāma nagaram /
tatra daridro nāma vaṇik /
tasya gṛhe cauraḥ praviṣṭaḥ /
so 'pi ca tatrānyatkimapyalabhamānaḥ sarṣapān gṛhītvā nirgato rājapuruṣaiḥ prāptaḥ /
sarṣapān gale baddhvā bhrāmito rājakulātsa kathaṃ mucyate /
uttaram-yo yaḥ pṛcchati tasya tasyāgre vadati-aho sarṣapāṇāṃ madhye na kiñcit /
tato rājñā sabhāyāmākārya pṛṣṭaḥ-tava vaco 'bhiprāyaṃ na jāne /
children.translated_text: There is a city named <s>Śubhasthāna</s>. There lived a merchant named <s>Daridra</s> (Poor). A thief entered his house. Finding nothing else there, he took some mustard seeds and went out, but was caught by the king's men. With the mustard seeds tied around his neck, he was paraded about. From the king's court, how could he be freed? The answer: to everyone who asked, he would say: 'Alas! Among the mustard seeds there is nothing at all!' Then the king, having summoned him to the assembly, asked: 'I do not understand the meaning of your words.'

children.text: prāha- balervarṣadine lokaḥ sarṣapānpañcarakṣakān /
children.translated_text: He said: 'On the festival day of <s>Bali</s>, people tie mustard seeds as protective amulets

children.text: haste badhnāti tannūnamapramāṇamataḥ param // Suk_18.2 (=116) //
children.translated_text: on their hands; therefore anything beyond that measure is of no account.' Suk_18.2 (=116)

children.text:
yato 'hametāvadbhirapi gale baddhairbaddhaḥ rājāpi tadākarṇya hasaṃstaṃ mumoca /
iti śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text:
'For I too, bound with these many (mustard seeds) tied around my neck, am a prisoner.' The king, hearing this, laughed and released him.
Having heard this, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau aṣṭādaśī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the eighteenth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 19:
children.translated_text: START Suk 19:

children.text: anyadā prabhāvatī calitā /
children.translated_text: On another day, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> was about to set out.

children.text: śukaḥ prāha- kuru yadrocate bhīru yadi kartuṃ tvamīśvarā /
children.translated_text: The parrot said: 'Do what pleases you, O timid one, if you are capable of doing it,

children.text: yathā santikayā bhartā svacchandā ca vimocitā // Suk_19.1 (=117) //
children.translated_text: as <s>Santikā</s> (freed) her husband and <s>Svacchandā</s> (the wilful one) was set free.' Suk_19.1 (=117)

children.text:
asti karahaḍābhidhaṃ puram /
tatra rājā guṇapriyo nāma yathārthaḥ /
tatra ca soḍhoko nāma śreṣṭhiḥ /
tadbhāryā santikā nāma pativratā /
tatraiva cānyo vaṇik /
tadbhāryā svacchandā nāma puṃścalī /
sā ca soḍhākaṃ nityamicchati paraṃ so 'bhivāñchāṃ na vidhatte /
anyadā ca manorathābhidhaṃ yakṣaṃ namaskartuṃ jagāma saḥ /
tataḥ svacchandā pṛṣṭhalagnā tatra praviṣṭā /
sa ca hāvabhāvādyairanukūlito bhuktaḥ /
yuktamuktañca-
children.translated_text: There is a city called <s>Karahaḍā</s>. There ruled a king named <s>Guṇapriya</s>, true to his name (lover of virtue). There was also a merchant chief named <s>Soḍhaka</s>. His wife, named <s>Santikā</s>, was devoted to her husband. In the same city there was another merchant whose wife, named <s>Svacchandā</s> (the Wilful), was a wanton woman. She constantly desired <s>Soḍhaka</s>, but he did not reciprocate her longing. One day he went to pay homage to a <s>Yakṣa</s> (nature spirit) named <s>Manoratha</s>. Then <s>Svacchandā</s>, following behind, entered that place. And he, won over by her amorous gestures and glances, enjoyed her company. And it is rightly said:

children.text: sanmārge tāvadāste prabhavati puruṣastāvadevendriyāṇāṃ lajjāṃ tāvadvidhatte vinayamapi samālambate tāvadeva /
children.translated_text: A man stays on the righteous path only so long as the senses remain under his control; he maintains modesty and upholds propriety only so long

children.text: bhrūcāpākṛṣṭamuktāḥ śravaṇapathajuṣo nīlapakṣmāṇa ete yāvallīlāvatīnāṃ na hṛdi dhṛtimuṣo dṛṣṭibāṇāḥ patanti // Suk_19.2 (=118) //
children.translated_text: as the glances of playful women — arrows shot from the bows of their eyebrows, with dark lashes, travelling the path of the ears — do not fall upon the heart and rob it of its steadfastness. Suk_19.2 (=118)

children.text:
tacca mithunaṃ dṛṣṭvā rājapuruṣaḥ tadbandhanāya yakṣagṛhaṃ veṣṭitam /
santikā ca śuddhiṃ jñātvā rātrau mahatā tūryaśabdena yakṣagṛhaṃ gatā /
teṣāmārakṣakāṇāṃ purata uktam-ahamadyadinavratā yakṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhojanaṃ vijane vidhāsye /
māṃ ca kiñciddhanaṃ gṛhītvā madhye praveśayatu /
tairapi tathaiva kṛtam /
tatastayā svacchandā svaveṣāṃ kārayitvā bahirniṣkāsitā /
svayaṃ madhye sthitā /
taṃ ca prātarnijakāntāsahitaṃ dṛṣṭvā ārakṣakā vilakṣībabhūvuḥ /
iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text:
Having seen that couple, the king's officer surrounded the <s>Yakṣa</s> temple to arrest them. <s>Santikā</s>, learning the truth, went at night with a great sound of musical instruments to the <s>Yakṣa</s> temple. Before the guards she said: 'Today I am observing a day-long vow; having beheld the <s>Yakṣa</s>, I shall take my meal in seclusion. Please accept some payment and let me enter.' They did exactly so. Then she had <s>Svacchandā</s> dress in her own clothes and sent her out, while she herself remained inside. When the guards saw him in the morning together with his own wife, they were embarrassed.
Having heard this story, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau ekonaviṃśatitamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the nineteenth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 20:
children.translated_text: START Suk 20:

children.text: anyadā prabhāvatī śukaṃ papraccha /
children.translated_text: On another day, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> questioned the parrot.

children.text: śukaḥ prāha- gaccha devi mano yatra ramate te narāntare /
children.translated_text: The parrot said: 'Go, O queen, wherever your mind delights in another man;

children.text: kelikāvadyadā vetsi pativañcanamadbhutam // Suk_20.1 (=119) //
children.translated_text: if, like <s>Kelikā</s>, you know the marvellous art of deceiving a husband.' Suk_20.1 (=119)

children.text:
asti sābhramatyā nadyāstaṭe śaṅkhapuraṃ nāma sthānam /
tatra ca karṣukaḥ sūrākhyo dhanī /
tasya kelikā bhāryā paraṃ kuṭilā kulaṭā ca /
sānyasminnadītīre siddheśvarapurasthaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ kāmayate /
tadāsaktā ca rātrau prātiveśikādūtikāsāhāyyānnadīṃ tīrtvā tadantikaṃ prāpnoti /
anyadā bhartrā jñātam /
sa ca tatra gatastaccaritragaveṣaṇāya /
yāvatsā nadītīre tatra samāgatā tayā ca tāvaddṛṣṭaḥ /
tatastaraṇaghaṭaṃ pānīyabhṛtaṃ vidhāya prātiveśmikāgṛhamadhye bhaṭṭārikāṃ maṇḍayitvā tena payasā snāpayitvā pratyuvāca prathamasaṃketitāṃ dūtikāmuddiśya-"svāmini! purā tvayā uktaṃ yadi tvaṃ siddheśvarīṃ na snāpayasi tataḥ pañcānāṃ dinānāṃ madhye tvadbhartṛbharaṇaṃ bhaviṣyati tato yadi tvadvacanapramāṇaṃ tadā mama patiściraṃ jīvatu /
prātiveśmikayoktam evamastviti śrutvā patistuṣṭo bhūtvālakṣita eva jagāma /
iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text:
There is a place called <s>Śaṅkhapura</s> on the bank of the river <s>Sābhramatī</s>. There lived a wealthy farmer named <s>Sūra</s>. His wife <s>Kelikā</s> was extremely crooked and unfaithful. She desired a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who lived near the temple of <s>Siddheśvara</s> on the other bank of that river. Devoted to him, at night, with the help of a go-between from the neighbourhood, she would cross the river and reach his dwelling. One day, her husband found out. He went there to investigate her conduct. Just then she arrived at the riverbank, and she saw him there. Then, having prepared a pot of water for crossing and filled it with water, she went to the neighbour's house, adorned the image of the goddess (<s>Bhaṭṭārikā</s>), bathed it with that water, and addressed (the neighbour), referring to the previously appointed go-between: 'O mistress! Previously you said that if I do not bathe the goddess <s>Siddheśvarī</s>, then within five days my husband will die. Therefore, if your word is to be trusted, may my husband live long!' The neighbour said: 'So be it.' Hearing this, her husband was pleased and went away unnoticed.
Having heard this story, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau viṃśatitamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twentieth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 21:
children.translated_text: START Suk 21:

children.text: anyasmindine prabhāvatyā puṣṭaḥ śukaḥ prāha-
children.translated_text: On another day, when questioned by <s>Prabhāvatī</s>, the parrot said:

children.text: vraja devi na doṣo 'sti vrajatāṃ sarvakarmasu /
children.translated_text: 'Go, O queen, there is no fault for those who set out on any undertaking,

children.text: buddhirasti yadā yeṣāṃ mandodaryāḥ sahāyinī // Suk_21.1 (=118) //
children.translated_text: when they have intelligence, with <s>Mandodarī</s> as their helper.' Suk_21.1 (=118)

children.text:
prabhāvatyāha-kathametat /
śukraḥ-asti pratiṣṭhānaṃ nāma nagaram /
tatra hemaprabho nāma rājā /
śrutaśīlo mantrī /
śreṣṭhī yaśodharaḥ /
mohinī bhāryā /
tayostanayā mandodarī /
sa śrīvatsāya vaṇije kāntipurīsamāgatāya dattā /
tanmithunamatīva snehalampaṭam /
sā ca prātiveśmikayā pitṛbhāryayā kuṭṭinyā daṃṣṭrākarālayā yojitamanyaṃ rājaputramupabhuṅke /
sā'pannasattvā bhūtā garbhasaṃbhavātsaṃjāte dohade rājavallabhaṃ mayūraṃ mārayitvā bhakṣitavatī /
rājā tu tasminmayūre samāgate bhuṅkte iti sthitiḥ /
tasmindivase tu bhojanavelāyāṃ na labdhaḥ /
ḍiṇḍimaghoṣaṇe kṛte kuṭṭinyā paṭahaḥ spṛṣṭaḥ /
tayā ca jñātaṃ yatkayācidāpannasattvayā mayūro dohadādbhakṣitaḥ /
tataḥ sā garbhavatī pṛṣṭā tayā kuṭṭino gṛhamāgatā sammānitā /
uktañca-
children.translated_text:
<s>Prabhāvatī</s> said: 'How is that?'
The parrot said: There is a city named <s>Pratiṣṭhāna</s>. There ruled a king named <s>Hemaprabha</s>. His minister was <s>Śrutaśīla</s>. The chief merchant was <s>Yaśodhara</s>. His wife was <s>Mohinī</s>. Their daughter was <s>Mandodarī</s>. She was given in marriage to a merchant named <s>Śrīvatsa</s>, who had come from the city of <s>Kāntipurī</s>. That couple was exceedingly devoted to each other in love. But she, led by the neighbouring woman — her father-in-law's wife, a procuress with fearsome fangs — enjoyed another man, a prince. She became pregnant, and when cravings arose due to the pregnancy, she killed and ate a peacock that was the king's favourite. Now the king's practice was to eat when that peacock arrived. On that day, at mealtime, it was not found. When a drum announcement was made, the <s>kuṭṭinī</s> (procuress) touched the drum (to give information). She had learned that some pregnant woman had eaten the peacock out of her craving. Then the pregnant woman was questioned, and the <s>kuṭṭinī</s> came to her house and was honoured. And it is said:

children.text: mādhuryaṃ pramadājane sulalitaṃ dākṣiṇyamārye jane, śauryaṃ śatruṣu mārdavaṃ gurujane dharmiṣṭhatā sādhuṣu /
children.translated_text: Sweetness towards women, graceful courtesy towards noble people, valour towards enemies, gentleness towards elders, righteousness towards the virtuous,

children.text: marmajñeṣvanuvartanaṃ bahuvidhaṃ mānaṃ jane garvite, śāṭhyaṃ pāpajane narasya kathitāḥ paryantamaṣṭau guṇāḥ // Suk_21.2 (=119) //
children.translated_text: compliance of many kinds towards those who know one's secrets, respect towards the proud, cunning towards the wicked — these are declared to be the eight complete virtues of a man. Suk_21.2 (=119)

children.text:
tayā ca sarvo 'pi mayūravṛttānto niveditaḥ /
sā cakuṭṭinī viśvāsaghātikā /
uktañca-
children.translated_text: And by her, the entire story of the peacock was reported. But that <s>kuṭṭinī</s> was a betrayer of trust. And it is said:

children.text: na viśvasedaviśvaste viśvaste 'pi na viśvaset /
children.translated_text: One should not trust the untrustworthy, and even in the trusted, one should not place trust;

children.text: viśvāsād bhayamutpannaṃ mūlādapi nikṛntati // Suk_21.3 (=120) //
children.translated_text: for danger born of trust cuts down even from the root. Suk_21.3 (=120)

children.text: dāreṣu gopyaṃ puruṣasya kiñcidgopyaṃ vayasyeṣu suteṣu kiñcit /
children.translated_text: A man should keep certain things secret from his wife, certain things from his friends, and certain things from his sons;

children.text: yuktaṃ na yuktaṃ manasā vicintya vadedvipaścinmahato 'nurodhāt // Suk_21.4 (=121) //
children.translated_text: having considered in his mind what is proper and improper, the wise man should speak only out of great necessity. Suk_21.4 (=121)

children.text: kiñca-
children.translated_text: Moreover:

children.text: sopacārāṇi vākyāni śatrūṇāmiha lakṣayet /
children.translated_text: One should discern the courteous words of enemies in this world;

children.text: avicāritagītārthāṃ mṛgā yānti parābhavam // Suk_21.5 (=122) //
children.translated_text: deer who do not consider the meaning of the song fall into ruin. Suk_21.5 (=122)

children.text: kirāte 'pyuktam-
children.translated_text: It is also said in the <s>Kirāta</s> (text):

children.text: vrajanti te mūḍhadhiyaḥ parābhavaṃ bhavanti māyāviṣu ye na māyinaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those of foolish minds who are not deceitful among the deceitful go to ruin;

children.text: praviśya hi ghnanti śaṭhāstathāvidhānasaṃvṛtāṅgānniśitāiveṣavaḥ // Suk_21.6 (=123) //
children.translated_text: for wicked people, entering thus, strike down those whose limbs are unprotected, like sharpened arrows. Suk_21.6 (=123)

children.text:
kuṭṭinyā tatsarvaṃ jñātvā mantriṇe niveditam /
mantriṇāpi rājñe /
rājā prāha-
children.translated_text: The <s>kuṭṭinī</s>, having learned everything, reported it to the minister. The minister in turn reported it to the king. The king said:

children.text: mā hohi suhaggāhi mā pattihi jaṃ ṇa diṭṭhapaccakkhaṃ /
children.translated_text: (In Prakrit:) 'Do not be quick to accept, do not believe what is not seen with your own eyes;

children.text: paccakkhammi vi diṭṭhe juttājuttaṃ viutaṇāhi // Suk_21.7 (=124) //
children.translated_text: and even in what is seen directly, discern what is proper and improper.' Suk_21.7 (=124)

children.text: [mā bhava sukhagrāhī mā pratyehi yanna dṛṣṭaṃ pratyakṣam /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] 'Do not be easy to convince, do not believe what is not seen as direct evidence;

children.text: pratyakṣe 'pi dṛṣṭe yuktāyuktaṃ vijānīhi] // Suk_21.7* (=124*) //
children.translated_text: and even in what is seen directly, know what is proper and improper.' Suk_21.7* (=124*)

children.text:
tadvaṇijo nagarapradhānasya vadhvā naitanniṣpadyate /
yāvadātmanā na dṛṣṭaṃ tāvadasau na viḍambyaḥ /
tacca kuṭṭinyā agre mantriṇā niveditam /
kuṭṭinī ca mantriṇaṃ peṭāyāṃ nikṣipya tadgṛhe nyāsavyājena mumoca /
svayaṃ ca tatra gatvā tāmabhāṣata- mugdhe! yanmayūrabhakṣaṇaṃ kṛtaṃ tattvaṃ me ślāghyā /
uktañca-
children.translated_text: This is the wife of a merchant who is a leading citizen — such a thing cannot be proved against her. As long as I have not seen it with my own eyes, she should not be disgraced.' This was reported by the minister to the <s>kuṭṭinī</s>. The <s>kuṭṭinī</s> then placed the minister inside a chest and, under the pretext of leaving it as a deposit, released it at that house. She herself went there and said to her: 'Dear naive girl! The eating of the peacock you did — I praise you for it! And it is said:

children.text: eṇaḥ kuraṅgo harimastittirirlāva eva ca /
children.translated_text: The deer, the antelope, the partridge, the quail,

children.text: mayūracarmikūrmāśca śreṣṭhā māṃsagaṇeṣvapi // Suk_21.8 (=125) //
children.translated_text: the peacock, the tortoise with its shell — these are the finest among all kinds of meat. Suk_21.8 (=125)

children.text:
punarapi samagro vṛttāntaḥ puṣṭaḥ /
kathyamānaśca peṭāhananakṛtasaṃjñena mantriṇā śrutaḥ /
tatkathaṃ sā śreṣṭhivadhūstatpitā śvaśuraśca mucyantām /
uktañca-
children.translated_text: Once again, the entire story was elicited. And as it was being narrated, the minister inside the chest, signalling by knocking, heard everything. Then how could that merchant's wife, her father, and her father-in-law be freed? And it is said:

children.text: na nīcajanasaṃsargānnaro bhadrāṇi paśyati /
children.translated_text: From association with the base, a man does not see good fortune;

children.text: darśayatyeva vikṛrtiṃ supriye 'pi khalo yataḥ // Suk_21.9 (=126) //
children.translated_text: for a wicked person shows only malice, even towards one who is dear. Suk_21.9 (=126)

children.text: nāśayitumeva nīcaḥ parakāryaṃ vetti na prasādhayitum /
children.translated_text: A base person knows only how to destroy another's undertaking, not how to accomplish it;

children.text: pāṭayitumeva śaktirnakhoruddhartumannapiṭam // Suk_21.10 (=127) //
children.translated_text: a fingernail has the power only to tear, not to extract a grain of rice (from a pot). Suk_21.10 (=127)

children.text: dujjaṇajaṇaṇaṃ sagge kāaccāo vi hoi vibuhāṇaṃ /
children.translated_text: (In Prakrit:) From association with the wicked, even the wise may lose their bodies;

children.text: pecchaha tilehi pattaṃ khalasaṃge pīḍaṇaṃ jatto // Suk_21.11 (=128) //
children.translated_text: behold — from association with the oil-press, even sesame seeds are crushed. Suk_21.11 (=128)

children.text: [durjanajanānāṃ saṃge kāyatyāgo 'pi bhavati vibudhānām /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] From association with wicked people, even the wise may lose their lives;

children.text: prekṣasva tilānāmapi khalasaṅge pīḍanaṃ yataḥ] // Suk_21.11* (=128*) //
children.translated_text: behold — from association with the oil-press, even sesame seeds are crushed. Suk_21.11* (=128*)

children.text: yāvatsā kuṭṭinī peṭāṃ hastena hanti tāvatsā vaṇikputrī savitarkamavādīt-
children.translated_text: While the <s>kuṭṭinī</s> was striking the chest with her hand, the merchant's daughter-in-law spoke with deliberation:

children.text: vibhātā rajanī tāvadyāvadevaṃ kṛtaṃ mayā /
children.translated_text: 'The night has passed; so much has been done by me —

children.text: prabuddhaṃ ca tadā mātarnāgre kiñcidvidṛśyate // Suk_21.12 (=129) //
children.translated_text: And when awakened then, O mother, nothing further was seen before me. Suk_21.12 (=129)

children.text: mārtamayā evaṃvidhaḥ svapno dṛṣṭa /
yaḥ kaścidarthapramāṇo me bhavati sa kathyatām /
children.translated_text: Whatever meaning it may hold for me, let that be told.

children.text: evaṃ śrutvā mantrī dvāramāhatya bahirnirgataḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard this, the minister struck the door and went outside.

children.text: tataḥ sammānitā vaṇigvadhūḥ sā tu kuṭṭinīti nirvāsitā /
children.translated_text: Then the merchant's wife was honored, but the procuress was banished.

children.text: iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā //
children.translated_text: Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.
Such a dream was seen by me.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau ekaviṃśatītamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-first tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 22:
children.translated_text: START Suk 22:

children.text: punaḥ prabhāvatyā pṛṣṭaḥ śukaḥ prāha-
children.translated_text: Again, when questioned by <s>Prabhāvatī</s>, the parrot said:

children.text: yāhi devi punaryāhi madīyaṃ matamīdṛśam /
children.translated_text: Go, O queen, go again — this is my opinion:

children.text: yadi vetsyuttaraṃ kicidyathā māḍhukayā kṛtam // Suk_22.1 (=130) //
children.translated_text: if you know a clever reply, as was done by <s>Māḍhukā</s>. Suk_22.1 (=130)

children.text:
tacchrutvā prabhāvatyāha-kathametat /
śukaḥ prāha-dāmbhilāgrāme soḍhāko nāma karṣukaḥ /
tadbhāryā māḍhuka nāma /
tāṃ ca bhaktahāriṇīṃ pathi gacchantīm eko bahiḥ sūrapālākhyo naro bhuṅkte /
sā kadācinmārge bhaktaṃ muktvā tena saha sthitā /
tato mūledavena dhūrtena tasminbhakte uṣṭrikā kṛtā /
tayā ca evaṃ jātaṃ bhaktamanutpāṭayitvā nīnam /
yāvacca bhartrā uṣṭikā dṛṣṭā tāvatkimiditi sā pṛṣṭā /
tatastayā tatkālottaraṃ kṛtvoktam-nātha! adya rātrau svapne uṣṭrikayā bhakṣito dṛṣṭastvam /
tato mayā vighnāpahārāya viparītamidaṃ kṛtam /
viśrabdhaṃ bhakṣaya yathā vighno naśyati /
iti śrutvā ratātmanā tenoṣṭrikāpi bhakṣitā /
iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text:
Hearing that, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked: 'How is that?'
The parrot said: In a village named <s>Dāmbhilā</s>, there was a farmer named <s>Soḍhāka</s>. His wife was named <s>Māḍhukā</s>. As she was going along the road carrying food, a man named <s>Sūrapāla</s>, who lived outside the village, enjoyed her company. She once left the food on the road and stayed with him. Then a rogue named <s>Mūladeva</s> spat in that food. And she, without removing what had been done to the food, took it away. When the spit was seen by her husband, she was asked: 'What is this?' Then she made up an answer on the spot and said: 'My lord! Last night in a dream I saw you being eaten by spit. So I did this opposite thing to avert the evil omen. Eat it with confidence, so that the evil may be destroyed.' Hearing this, the pleasure-loving man ate the food with the spit as well.
Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau dvāviṃśatitamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-second tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 23:
children.translated_text: START Suk 23:

children.text: anyadā sakhyastāṃ puruṣāntarābhisaraṇāyaivamūcuḥ-
children.translated_text: On another occasion, her friends said to her thus, urging her to go to another man:

children.text: yatra svedalavairalaṃ vilulitairvyālupyate candanaṃ sacchedairmaṇitaiśca yatra raṇitaṃ na śrūyate nūpuram /
children.translated_text: Where sandalwood paste is smeared away by drops of perspiration, where the anklet adorned with cut jewels does not make a jingling sound,

children.text: yatrāyāntyacireṇa sarvaviṣayāḥ kāmaṃ tadekāgrataḥ sakhyastatsurataṃ bhaṇāmi rataye śeṣā ca lokasthitiḥ // Suk_23.1 (=131) //
children.translated_text: where all the senses quickly come to a single focus of desire — O friends, I declare that to be true lovemaking, for delight; all else is mere worldly custom. Suk_23.1 (=131)

children.text: tathā ca- saṃsaatulaṇa jahiṃ caḍai tassuṇa jīviu dhaṇu /
children.translated_text: And also: [in Prakrit] He who does not ascend the scales of doubt — his life is not blessed;

children.text: āi parā jahi lahijjai taṃ ji bhaṇijjii pemmu // Suk_23.2 (=132) //
children.translated_text: when another comes, she who is obtained — that alone is called love. Suk_23.2 (=132)

children.text: [saṃśayatulāyāṃ na yaḥ ārohati tasya na jīvitaṃ dhanyam /
children.translated_text: [In Sanskrit: He who does not mount the balance of uncertainty — his life is not blessed;

children.text: āgate parā yā labhyate tadeva bhaṇyate prema] // Suk_23.2* (=132*) //
children.translated_text: when another arrives, she who is won — that alone is called love.] Suk_23.2* (=132*)

children.text: ārogyaṃ paramānandaḥ sukhamutsāha eva ca /
children.translated_text: Health, supreme joy, happiness, and enthusiasm,

children.text: aiśvaryaṃ priyasambhogaṃ vinā sarvaṃ nirarthakam // Suk_23.3 (=133) //
children.translated_text: sovereignty — without the enjoyment of the beloved, everything is meaningless. Suk_23.3 (=133)

children.text: uktañca-
children.translated_text: And it is said:

children.text: ātmānamālokya ca śobhamānamādarśabimbe stimitāyatākṣī /
children.translated_text: Gazing at her own beautiful reflection in the mirror-surface, with wide, motionless eyes,

children.text: haropayāne tvaritā babhūva strīṇāṃ priyālokaphalo hi veṣaḥ // Suk_23.4 (=134) //
children.translated_text: she hastened to the conveyance of <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) — for the adornment of women bears fruit only in the gaze of the beloved. Suk_23.4 (=134)

children.text: śukaḥ prāha-
children.translated_text: The parrot said:

children.text: sulabhāḥ puruṣā rājansatataṃ priyavādinaḥ /
children.translated_text: Easily found are men, O king, who always speak pleasantly;

children.text: apriyasya tu pathyasya vaktā śrotā ca durlabhaḥ // Suk_23.5 (=135) //
children.translated_text: but rare is one who speaks what is unpleasant yet beneficial, and rare too is one who listens. Suk_23.5 (=135)

children.text: tataḥ kiṃ bahunoktena tvaṃ caitāḥ kṛtyakovidāḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore, what need of many words? You and these women are skilled in their craft;

children.text: kuṭṭinīcaritaṃ śrutvā tadvicāryaṃ tvarānvitāḥ // Suk_23.6 (=136) //
children.translated_text: having heard the conduct of the procuress, consider it carefully and with haste. Suk_23.6 (=136)

children.text:
prabhāvatyāha-kathametat /
śuko 'bravīt-asti padmāvatī purī /
children.translated_text:
<s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked: 'How is that?'
The parrot said: There is a city named <s>Padmāvatī</s>.

children.text: yatra maṇikuṭṭimamārgeṣu śobhate ravivistaraḥ /
children.translated_text: Where the splendor of the sun shines upon the gem-paved streets,

children.text: śeṣaphaṇamaṇirāgo vasudhāmivopāgataḥ // Suk_23.7 (=137) //
children.translated_text: as if the ruby-glow of <s>Śeṣa</s>'s (the cosmic serpent's) hood-jewel had come upon the earth. Suk_23.7 (=137)

children.text: tatra śudarśano nāma rājā /
children.translated_text: There was a king named <s>Sudarśana</s>.

children.text: śaśinā hariṇā caiva balinā kuśabhūbhujā /
children.translated_text: Like the moon, like <s>Hari</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), like <s>Bali</s>, like <s>Kuśa</s> the ruler of the earth,

children.text: kuśaśakticchalatyāgasampadyasya na khaṇḍyate // Suk_23.8 (=138) //
children.translated_text: whose excellence in skill, power, cunning, generosity, and prosperity could not be diminished. Suk_23.8 (=138)

children.text: kiṃ tasya varṇyate rājñaḥ prajāpālanaśalinaḥ /
children.translated_text: What can be described of that king, devoted to the protection of his subjects,

children.text: yasmiṃlloke na dṛṣṭā hi doṣā ravikarairiva // Suk_23.9 (=139) //
children.translated_text: in whose realm faults were no more to be seen than they are in the rays of the sun? Suk_23.9 (=139)

children.text:
tasya śṛṅgārasundarī nāma bhāryā /
tasya nṛpatestayā saha krīḍato groṣmakālo 'vātarat /
children.translated_text: His wife was named <s>Śṛṅgārasundarī</s>. As that king was sporting with her, the summer season arrived,

children.text: yatra sūraḥ kharo ghasro yatra dīrgho 'tiduḥsahaḥ /
children.translated_text: when the sun is fierce, the days are harsh, long, and extremely unbearable,

children.text: kharaśca pavano bhīru grīṣme sarvamidaṃ kharam // Suk_23.10 (=140) //
children.translated_text: and the wind is hot — O timid one, in summer everything is harsh. Suk_23.10 (=140)

children.text: candanaṃ śucivastraṃ ca pānīyaṃ śuci śītalam /
children.translated_text: Sandalwood, clean garments, water that is pure and cool —

children.text: sevyamāno 'pi madhuraḥ śucirjayati nānyathā // Suk_23.11 (=141) //
children.translated_text: even when resorted to, only what is sweet and pure prevails, not otherwise. Suk_23.11 (=141)

children.text: madhyāhne candanaṃ yeṣāṃ sāyaṃ majjanasevanam /
children.translated_text: Those who apply sandalwood at midday, who bathe in the evening,

children.text: rātrau vyajanavātaśca teṣāṃ grīṣmo 'pi kiṅkaraḥ // Suk_23.12 (=142) //
