children.translated_text: and who enjoy the breeze of fans at night — for them, even summer is a servant. Suk_23.12 (=142)

children.text:
evaṃvidhe grīṣme ca candranāmā vaṇik prabhāvatībhāryāsameto gṛhoparibhūmikāyāmāruḍhaḥ /
karairyukto 'pi nirālambaḥ ādityaḥ paścimābhyonidhitaṭaṃ gataḥ /
uktañca-
children.translated_text: In such a summer, a merchant named <s>Candra</s>, together with his wife <s>Prabhāvatī</s>, ascended to the upper terrace of his house. The sun, though possessed of rays, being without support, sank to the shore of the western ocean. And it is said:

children.text: pratikūlatāmupagate hi vidhau viphalatvameti bahu sādhanatā /
children.translated_text: When fate turns hostile, even abundant means become fruitless;

children.text: avalambanāya dinabharturabhūnna patiṣyataḥ karasahasramapi // Suk_23.13 (=143) //
children.translated_text: even a thousand hands could not support the lord of the day as he fell. Suk_23.13 (=143)

children.text: tatrasthaḥ sa tathā bhānū rāgaśeṣo gatāṃśukaḥ /
children.translated_text: There, that sun, with only a residue of redness remaining, its rays departed,

children.text: bhātīva vidrumaghaṭaḥ srastaḥ saṃdhyāvadhūkarāt // Suk_23.14 (=144) //
children.translated_text: shone like a coral vessel slipping from the hand of the twilight-bride. Suk_23.14 (=144)

children.text: atrāntare viśālākṣi candro hantuṃ tamoripum /
children.translated_text: Meanwhile, O large-eyed one, the moon, in order to slay the enemy that is darkness,

children.text: udayādriśiraḥ sthātumudyatoṃ'śubhaṭairvṛtaḥ // Suk_23.15 (=145) //
children.translated_text: rose, prepared to stand atop the eastern mountain, surrounded by his ray-warriors. Suk_23.15 (=145)

children.text: prācīmukhe vibhātīndurudayādriśiraḥsthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the face of the east shines the moon, standing atop the peak of the eastern mountain,

children.text: dīpastribhuvanasyeva pracchannasya tamisrayā // Suk_23.16 (=146) //
children.translated_text: like a lamp of the three worlds concealed by darkness. Suk_23.16 (=146)

children.text: udayācalamāruḍho bhāti candro niśāmukhe /
children.translated_text: Having mounted the eastern mountain, the moon shines at the onset of night,

children.text: yāminīvanitotsaṅga śulkaḥ kṛṣṇaśiraḥsthitaḥ // Suk_23.17 (=147) //
children.translated_text: like the bride-price for the maiden of night, placed on the head of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> (the dark one). Suk_23.17 (=147)

children.text:
evaṃvidhe niśāmukhe sa vaṇik vikrīḍitayā tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍitaḥ /
asya rāmanāmā sutaḥ saṃjātaḥ /
tasmai pitrā vidyāścāśeṣā grāhitāḥ /
tasya mātānyadā candraṃ prāha-mama eka eva putraḥ /
tato 'hamatiśayena duḥkhārtā /
candraḥ prāha-eko 'pi tvadīyaḥ sutaḥ ślāghyaḥ /
uktañca-
children.translated_text: At such an onset of night, that merchant sported with his playful wife. A son named <s>Rāma</s> was born to them. The father had him taught all branches of learning. His mother once said to <s>Candra</s>: 'I have only one son, and therefore I am exceedingly distressed.' <s>Candra</s> said: 'Even your one son is praiseworthy.' And it is said:

children.text: caturo madhurastyāgī gambhīraśca kalālayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Clever, sweet-natured, generous, profound, and a repository of the arts,

children.text: guṇagrāhī tathā caivaṃ eko 'pīdṛgvaraḥ sutaḥ // Suk_23.18 (=148) //
children.translated_text: as well as one who appreciates qualities — even one such excellent son is sufficient. Suk_23.18 (=148)

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also:

children.text: kiṃ jātairbahubhiḥ putraiḥ śokasantāpakārakaiḥ /
children.translated_text: What use of many sons born, who only cause grief and sorrow?

children.text: varamekaḥ kulālambī yatra viśrūyate kulam // Suk_23.19 (=149) //
children.translated_text: Better is one who supports the family, through whom the family gains renown. Suk_23.19 (=149)

children.text:
ityuktvā dhūrtamāyāṃ kuṭṭinīmākāryedamabravīt--tava kanakasahasraṃ dāsye /
mama putraṃ strīmāyāvañcanadakṣaṃ kuru /
tatheti tayā pratijñāte putraṃ samākṣikaṃ tasyai dattvā yadyasmatputraḥ kvāpi veśyāyāḥ kapaṭena jito bhavati tadāhaṃ dviguṇaṃ kanakaṃ grahīṣye /
tayoktam evamastviti /
lekhayitvā putraṃ tadgṛhe preṣayāmāsa /
sa ca tatrastho veśyājanodbhavānvikārān gṛhṇāti /
tadyathā--
children.translated_text: Having said this, he summoned a cunning procuress named <s>Dhūrtamāyā</s> and said: 'I will give you a thousand gold coins. Make my son skilled in the deceptions and tricks of women.' When she agreed, he gave her the son together with sweets, saying: 'If our son is ever defeated by the treachery of any courtesan, then I shall take back double the gold.' She said: 'So be it.' Having had him educated, he sent the son to her house. And he, staying there, learned all the arts born of courtesan-folk, namely:

children.text: vaiśikīṃ kṛtrimāṃ vāṇīṃ vyalīkān śapathāṃstathā /
children.translated_text: The courtesan's speech, feigned words, false oaths,

children.text: kauṭilyaṃ kṛtrimaṃ bhāvaṃ kṛtrimaṃ ruditaṃ tathā // Suk_23.20 (=150) //
children.translated_text: crookedness, feigned emotion, and feigned weeping, Suk_23.20 (=150)

children.text: hāsyaṃ ca kṛtrimaṃ duḥkhaṃ sukhaṃ caivamapārthakam /
children.translated_text: feigned laughter, feigned sorrow, and equally meaningless displays of happiness,

children.text: yācanaṃ vinayopetaṃ snehabhāvo nirīhatā // Suk_23.21 (=151) //
children.translated_text: humble entreaties, pretenses of affection, and feigned indifference, Suk_23.21 (=151)

children.text: samatvaṃ sukhaduḥkheṣu dharmādharmasamakriyā /
children.translated_text: equanimity in pleasure and pain, acting alike in virtue and vice,

children.text: bhujaṅgapurataścaiva kauṭilyakramadarśanam // Suk_23.22 (=152) //
children.translated_text: and the observation of the ways of crookedness, as before a serpent. Suk_23.22 (=152)

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And also:

children.text: aharaṃ karaṃ kavolaṃ thaṇajualaṃ ṇāhimaṇḍalaṃ ramaṇaṃ /
children.translated_text: [In Prakrit:] The lip, the hand, the cheek, the pair of breasts, the region of the navel — all are delightful;

children.text: itthiajaṇasāmaṇṇaṃ hiaaṃ jaṃ jassa taṃ tassa // Suk_23.23 (=153) //
children.translated_text: these are common to all womankind — but the heart, whichever woman's it is, belongs to her alone. Suk_23.23 (=153)

children.text: [adharaḥ karaḥ kapolaḥ stanayugalaṃ nābhimaṇḍalaṃ ramaṇam /
children.translated_text: [In Sanskrit: The lip, the hand, the cheek, the pair of breasts, the region of the navel — all are delightful;

children.text: strījanasāmānyaṃ hṛdayaṃ yad yasyā tat tasyāḥ] // Suk_23.23* (=153*) //
children.translated_text: these are common to all womankind — but the heart, whichever woman's it is, belongs to her alone.] Suk_23.23* (=153*)

children.text:
ityevamādi samagraṃ veśyānugaṃ caritaṃ śikṣitam /
tataḥ sa putraḥ pratijñāpūrvaṃ vaṇije samarpitaḥ /
piturvākyena ca suvarṇadvīpe vāṇijyāya preṣitaḥ /
tatra ca kalāvatī veśyā /
tayā saha varṣamekaṃ sthitaḥ /
tāṃ vaiśikāni kurvantīṃ sa prāha-viśeṣaṃ vada /
eva mamānujāpi vadati /
tato bahubhirapi vaiśikairna tatsarvasvaṃ gṛhītuṃ śaknoti /
tatastayā sarvamapi māturniveditam /
mātāpi prāha-niścitameṣa veśyāsutaḥ /
nedṛśairgṛhyate /
prapañcenaiva grāhyaḥ /
tato yadāyaṃ svadeśaṃ gantukāmastvāmutkalāpayati tadā tvayā vācyam--"ahamapi tatra yāsyāmi /
yadi na nayasi tadā mariṣyāmītyuktvā kūpe jhampā deyā /
tato 'sau prītastvāṃ prati sarvaṃ dāsyati' /
tayoktam--mātarmāṃ vinā taddravyeṇa kim /
ūktañca--
children.translated_text: And it is said:

children.text: atikleśena ye hyarthā dharmasyātikrameṇa ca /
children.translated_text: Wealth that is obtained with excessive hardship, through transgression of <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: śatrūṇāṃ praṇipātena mā sma teṣu manaḥ kṛthāḥ // Suk_23.24 (=154) //
children.translated_text: or by bowing before enemies — do not set your heart upon it. Suk_23.24 (=154)

Thus all such conduct befitting courtesans was taught in full. Then the son, having fulfilled his pledge, was returned to the merchant. By his father's command, he was sent to <s>Suvarṇadvīpa</s> (the Golden Island) for trade. There was a courtesan named <s>Kalāvatī</s>. He stayed with her for one year. When she employed her courtesan arts on him, he said: 'Tell me something special — even my sister talks like that.' Thus, even with many courtesan tricks, she could not seize his entire fortune. She then reported everything to her mother. The mother said: 'Surely he is a courtesan's son. He cannot be caught by such means. He must be caught by a stratagem.' Then: 'When he wishes to return to his own country and bids you farewell, you should say: "I too will come there. If you do not take me, I shall die" — and saying so, jump into a well. Then he, being pleased, will give you everything.' She replied: 'O mother, without him, what use is that wealth to me?'

children.text:
mātā āha-bhīru! mā maivaṃ vada /
mṛtyudo 'rthaḥ prāṇadaśca /
uktañca-
children.translated_text: The mother said: 'O timid one! Do not speak thus. Wealth can both cause death and give life.' And it is said:

children.text: nāsāhasaṃ samālambya naro bhadrāṇi paśyati /
children.translated_text: Without resorting to daring, a man does not see good fortune;

children.text: sāhasī sarvakāryeṣu lakṣmībhājanamuttamam // Suk_23.25 (=155) //
children.translated_text: one who is bold in all undertakings is the supreme vessel of <s>Lakṣmī</s> (prosperity). Suk_23.25 (=155)

children.text: nābhittvā paramarmāṇi nākṛtvā karma duṣkaram /
children.translated_text: Without piercing the vital spots, without performing a difficult deed,

children.text: nāhatvā matsyaghātīva prāpnoti mahatīṃ śriyam // Suk_23.26 (=156) //
children.translated_text: like the fisher who kills the fish, one does not attain great prosperity. Suk_23.26 (=156)

children.text: kālaḥ samaviṣamakaraḥ paribhavasanmānakārakaḥ kālaḥ /
children.translated_text: Time is the maker of the equal and the unequal; time is the cause of disgrace and honor;

children.text: kālaḥ karoti puruṣaṃ dātāraṃ yācitārañca // Suk_23.27 (=157) //
children.translated_text: time makes a person a giver and also a beggar. Suk_23.27 (=157)

children.text:
ahaṃ ca tatrādho jālaṃ viracayiṣye /
iti kuṭṭinīvacanamākaṇyaṃ tayā tathā kṛtat /
tathā ca kṛte tena sarvasva dattam /
koṭisaṃkhyaṃ ca dravyaṃ gṛhītvā mānarahito niṣkāsitaḥ /
uktañca-
children.translated_text: And I will spread a net below.' Having heard the procuress's words, she did accordingly. And when she did so, he gave her his entire fortune. Having taken wealth amounting to a <s>koṭi</s> (ten million), he was stripped of honor and expelled. And it is said:

children.text: vesā vi ramanti jaṇaṃ piaṃ pi vañcanti atthaloheṇa /
children.translated_text: [In Prakrit:] Courtesans sport with men; they deceive even the beloved out of greed for wealth;

children.text: tāṇa ṇamo vesāṇaṃ appā vi ṇa vallaho jāṇa // Suk_23.28 (=158) //
children.translated_text: salutations to those courtesans, for whom not even their own self is dear. Suk_23.28 (=158)

children.text: [veśyā api ramante janaṃ priyamapi vañcayanti arthalobhena /
children.translated_text: [In Sanskrit: Courtesans sport with men; they deceive even the beloved out of greed for wealth;

children.text: tābhyo namo veśyābhyaḥ ātmāpi na vallabho yāsām] // Suk_23.28* (=158*) //
children.translated_text: salutations to those courtesans, for whom not even their own self is dear.] Suk_23.28* (=158*)

children.text:
sa ca tathā dhanamānaparibhavaṃ prāpitaḥ parapotamāruhya svagṛhamāgamat /
ekākinaṃ sutaṃ dhanaparijanavarjitaṃ dṛṣṭvā pitā sabāṣpaṃ dhanakṣayakāraṇaṃ pṛcchati /
so 'pi svayaṃ lajjan gṛhamantrimukhena niveditavān /
pitroktam-vatsa mā viṣādaṃ vidhehi /
vipadaḥ sampado 'pi puṃsaḥ sampadyante /
uktañca-
children.translated_text: And he, thus brought to the loss of wealth, honor, and dignity, boarded another's vessel and came home. Seeing his son alone, deprived of wealth and attendants, the father tearfully asked the cause of the loss of wealth. He, ashamed, had it reported through the household minister. The father said: 'Son, do not despair. Both misfortunes and fortunes befall a man.' And it is said:

children.text: cintāmimāṃ vahasi kiṃ gajayūthanātha yūthādviyogavinimīlitanetrayugm /
children.translated_text: Why do you bear this anxiety, O lord of the elephant herd, with both eyes closed from separation from the herd?

children.text: piṇḍaṃ gṛhāṇa piṣa vāri yathopanītaṃ daivādbhavanti vipadaḥ kila sampado vā // Suk_23.29 (=159) //
children.translated_text: Take the morsel, crush the water as it is brought — by fate come misfortunes or indeed fortunes. Suk_23.29 (=159)

children.text: kimanena dhanenāpi satvareṇa manasvinām /
children.translated_text: What grief is caused to the wise by wealth

children.text: gatena jāyate khedo darṣaścaivāgatena ca // Suk_23.30 (=160) //
children.translated_text: that has departed swiftly, and what joy by wealth that has come? Suk_23.30 (=160)

children.text:
evaṃ sutaṃ samāśvāsya dhūrtamāyāmākārya idamabravīt--śṛṇu yadatra kautukaṃ saṃvṛttam /
tvayyadhyuṣito 'pi suto gatasarvasvaḥ samāyayau /
sā'ha--strībhiḥ ko na khaṇḍitaḥ /
uktañca-
children.translated_text: Having thus consoled his son, he summoned <s>Dhūrtamāyā</s> and said: 'Listen to the curious thing that has happened here. Though educated under your care, my son has returned having lost everything.' She said: 'Who has not been deceived by women?' And it is said:

children.text: ko 'rthānprāpya na garvito viṣayiṇaḥ kasyāpado 'staṃ gatāḥ strībhiḥ kasya na khaṇḍitaṃ bhuvi manaḥ ko nāma rājñāṃ priyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Who, having obtained wealth, is not arrogant? Whose misfortunes have come to an end? Whose mind has not been shattered by women on this earth? Who is dear to kings?

children.text: kaḥ kālasya na gocarāntaragataḥ ko 'rthī gato gauravaṃ ko vā durjanavāgurāsu patitaḥ kṣemeṇa yātaḥ pumān // Suk_23.31 (=161) //
children.translated_text: Who has not fallen within the range of Time? What supplicant has attained respect? Who, having fallen into the snares of the wicked, has passed through safely? Suk_23.31 (=161)

children.text: ramaṇasihiṇantarāle bahalaare romarāitarugahaṇe /
children.translated_text: In the space between the lover's crest-hair, in the dense thicket adorned with body-hair,

children.text: hariharaṇaragobindā biḍambiā maaṇacoreṇa // Suk_23.32 (=162) //
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, <s>Hara</s>, <s>Nara</s>, and <s>Govinda</s> are mocked by the thief of love (<s>Madana</s>). Suk_23.32 (=162)

children.text: [ramaṇaśikhino 'ntarāle bahulatare rolarājitarugahane /
children.translated_text: [In the space between the lover's crest-hair, in the dense thicket adorned with body-hair,

children.text: hariharanaragovindāḥ viḍambitā madanacoreṇa] // Suk_23.32* (=162*) //
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, <s>Hara</s>, <s>Nara</s>, and <s>Govinda</s> are mocked by the thief of love (<s>Madana</s>).] Suk_23.32* (=162*)

children.text:
tattvaṃ punaḥ potaṃ bhṛtaṃ kṛtvā māṃ putrānvitāṃ tatra preṣaya /
uktañca-
children.translated_text:
Having wrapped the goods in cloth, send me together with my sons there on a ship.
And it is said:

children.text: kṛte pratikṛtaṃ kuryā hiṃsite pratihiṃsitam /
children.translated_text: One should repay deed for deed, injury for injury;

children.text: tvayā luñcāpitāḥ pakṣā mayā luñcāpitaṃ śiraḥ // Suk_23.33 (=163) //
children.translated_text: you had my wings plucked, and I had your head cut off. Suk_23.33 (=163)

children.text:
mayāpyuktam-yadi tvadīyaputraḥ kvāpi striyā vañcyate tadā mama dūṣaṇam /
uktañca-
children.translated_text:
I also said: 'If your son is ever deceived by a woman somewhere, then the blame is mine.'
And it is said:

children.text: diggajakūrmakulācalaphaṇipatividhṛtāpi calati vasudheyam /
children.translated_text: This earth, though supported by the elephants of the directions, the cosmic tortoise, the mountain ranges, and the lord of serpents, still trembles;

children.text: pratipannamamalamanasāṃ na calati puṃsāṃ yugānte 'pi // Suk_23.34 (=164) //
children.translated_text: but the commitment undertaken by those of pure mind does not waver even at the end of an age. Suk_23.34 (=164)

children.text: tathā ca-
children.translated_text: And likewise:

children.text: acalā calanti palae majjāaṃ sāarā vilaṅghanti /
children.translated_text: Mountains move at the time of dissolution, oceans transgress their boundaries;

children.text: karuā vi taha vikāle paḍivaṇṇa sādha siḍhilenti // Suk_23.35 (=165) //
children.translated_text: but even the weighty ones, in adverse times, do not slacken in what they have undertaken. Suk_23.35 (=165)

children.text: [acalāścalanti pralaye maryādāṃ sāgarā vilaṅghante /
children.translated_text: [Mountains move at the time of dissolution, oceans transgress their boundaries;

children.text: gurukā api tathā vikāle pratipannasādhanaṃ na śithilayanti] // Suk_23.35* (=165*) //
children.translated_text: but even the weighty ones, in adverse times, do not slacken in what they have undertaken.] Suk_23.35* (=165*)

children.text: dhīrā jāṇa pamāṇaṃ jimiavve taha vi jaṃpiavve a /
children.translated_text: The wise know the measure of what should be eaten and also of what should be spoken;

children.text: ai jimiajaṃpiāiṃ pacchā vacche apacchāiṃ // Suk_23.36 (=166) //
children.translated_text: having eaten and spoken, afterwards, O child, they do not regret. Suk_23.36 (=166)

children.text: [dhīrā jānanti pramāṇaṃ jemanasya tathāpi kathanasya ca /
children.translated_text: [The wise know the measure of eating and also of speaking;

children.text: api bhuktaṃ jalpitaṃ paścād vatse na tapyanti] // Suk_23.36* (=166*) //
children.translated_text: having eaten and spoken, afterwards, O child, they do not grieve.] Suk_23.36* (=166*)

children.text:
tataḥ śreṣṭhī taṃ putraṃ preṣayāmāsāśu tayā samaṃ suvarṇadvīpe /
tatastasminsarvo 'pi paurajanaḥ prīto babhūva /
sā ca kalāvatī sānukūlā taṃ vinayenājuhāva /
tathā ca sa tayāvarjito yathāsau ātmāyattaḥ kṛtaḥ /
dravyaṃ ca sarvaṃ gṛhītam /
tataḥ sā dhūrtamāyā kuṭṭinī kiṃ karotu-iti praśnaḥ /
sā prāha-śuka! na jāne /
tvaṃ vada /
śukaḥ-yadyadya na yāsi tadā kathayāmi /
sā āha-na yāsyāmi /
śukaḥ-yadā tasya sarvaṃ gṛhītam tasminsamaye kaiściddinaiścāgre 'pi cāṇḍālarūpadhāriṇī dhūrtamāyā nityaṃ nityaṃ gaveṣamāṇaiva kiñcit /
anyadā sa kalāvatyā sahitaḥ khaṭvāyāmupaviṣṭastayā dṛṣṭaḥ /
tā dvāri dṛṣṭvā sahasotthāya nāśayitumudyataḥ pūrvameva saṃketitam /
tamuttiṣṭhantamanu kalāvatyapyutthitā /
uktañca-kimidamiti /
rāmastāmuvāca-bhadre! iyaṃ mama jananī /
ahaṃ ca hṛtārthako bahudinebhyo na tayā dṛṣṭaḥ /
dhūrtamāyāpi taṃ saṃketasthaṃ dvārasthaiva saśaṅkā hastasaṃjñayā ājuhāva /
children.translated_text: Then the merchant sent his son along with her to <s>Suvarṇadvīpa</s> (the Golden Island) quickly on a ship. Thereupon, all the townspeople were delighted. And <s>Kalāvatī</s>, being well-disposed, invited him with courtesy. And she so captivated him that he was made subject to her will. And all his wealth was taken. Then the question arose: what should that cunning trickster, the procuress <s>Dhūrtamāyā</s>, do? She said: 'O parrot! I do not know. You tell me.' The parrot said: 'If you do not go today, then I will tell you.' She said: 'I will not go.' The parrot continued: 'When all his wealth had been taken, at that time, some days later, <s>Dhūrtamāyā</s>, disguised as a <s>Caṇḍāla</s> woman, was constantly searching for something more. One day, she saw him seated on a bed together with <s>Kalāvatī</s>. Seeing her at the door, he suddenly rose to drive her away — this had been prearranged as a signal. As he rose, <s>Kalāvatī</s> also rose and asked: "What is this?" <s>Rāma</s> said to her: "O good lady! This is my mother. I have been robbed of my wealth and she has not seen me for many days." <s>Dhūrtamāyā</s> too, standing at the door, seeing him at the appointed signal, suspicious, beckoned him with a hand gesture and said:

children.text: jāgadeti cirāllabdho veśyāgṛhagato bhavān /
children.translated_text: 'Wake up! After a long time I have found you, gone into a courtesan's house!

children.text: mlecchībhūtā iyaṃ veśyā sarvasvaṃ me tvayā hṛtam // Suk_23.37 (=167) //
children.translated_text: This courtesan has become a barbarian — all my property has been stolen by you!' Suk_23.37 (=167)

children.text:
yāvadevaṃ gṛhāṅgaṇagatā śapati tāvatsa vaṇik cāṇḍālarūpī samāgatya tatpādayoḥ patitaḥ /
etacca dṛṣṭvā kalāvatī kuṭṭinīsahitā tām gṛhamadhye nītvā pṛcchati sma--amba! ko 'yam? kiṃ jātīyaḥ? tvaṃ kā? tayoktam--padmāvatīpurīnāthasya rājñaḥ sudarśanasya mātaṅgī gāyinī aham /
ayaṃ ca madīyaṃ dravyaṃ hṛtvā ihāgataḥ /
tacca tvayā'ptam /
tanmayā jñātam paramadhunā sa samāgacchatu /
tataḥ kuṭṭinī kalāvatāsahitā tatpadāyorlagnā uvāca--gṛhāṇedaṃ dravyam /
dhūrtamāyā prāha--nāhaṃ gṛhakoṇe grahīṣye /
rājaviditaṃ grahīṣyāmi /
tato veśyāmātāpi atiśayena bhītā mātaṅgīṃ pratijagāda-imāṃ matsutāṃ rakṣa rakṣa /
pāramparyāgataṃ dravyaṃ gṛhāṇa sarvasvam, paraṃ māṃ maivaṃ viḍambaya /
dhūrtamāyā prāha-grahīṣye /
tataḥ sā veśyayā kuṭṭinyā saha hastapādau gṛhītvā sammānitā /
dhūrtamāyāpi nijaṃ tadīyaṃ dravyaṃ sarvasvaṃ ca gṛhītvā rāmeṇa saha potamāruhya svagṛhamāgatya bhahotsavamakārayat /
iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text: While she was cursing thus in the courtyard, that merchant, disguised as a <s>Caṇḍāla</s>, arrived and fell at her feet. Seeing this, <s>Kalāvatī</s>, together with the procuress, took her inside the house and asked: 'Mother! Who is this? Of what caste? And who are you?' She replied: 'I am a <s>Mātaṅgī</s> (low-caste) singer in the service of King <s>Sudarśana</s>, lord of the city of <s>Padmāvatīpurī</s>. This man stole my wealth and came here. And you have acquired it. I have found this out. Now let him come to me.' Then the procuress, together with <s>Kalāvatī</s>, fell at her feet and said: 'Take this wealth.' <s>Dhūrtamāyā</s> said: 'I will not accept it in the corner of a house. I will accept it only when the king is informed.' Then the courtesan's mother too, exceedingly frightened, said to the <s>Mātaṅgī</s>: 'Protect, protect my daughter! Take the hereditary wealth, take everything, but do not humiliate me thus.' <s>Dhūrtamāyā</s> said: 'I will accept.' Then she was honored by the courtesan and the procuress, who clasped her hands and feet. <s>Dhūrtamāyā</s>, having taken her own wealth, the other's wealth, and everything else, boarded a ship with <s>Rāma</s>, returned to her own home, and held a great celebration. Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau trayoviṃśatitamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-third tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 24:
children.translated_text: START Suk 24:

children.text:
athānyasmindine prabhāvatī śukaṃ papraccha /
śuko 'pyāha--
children.translated_text: Then on another day, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked the parrot. The parrot said:

children.text: yāhi devi vijānāsi yadi jārasamanvitā /
children.translated_text: 'Go, O queen, if you know, accompanied by a lover,

children.text: sajjanīva purā vaktuṃ bharturagre kacagrahe // Suk_24.1 (=168) //
children.translated_text: how to speak before your husband like the virtuous <s>Sajjanī</s> when seized by the hair.' Suk_24.1 (=168)

children.text:
prabhāvatyāha-kimetat /
kīro 'bravīt-asti candrapuraṃ nāma nagaram /
tatrābhūdvardhakiḥ sūrapālākhyaḥ śrīmān /
tasya sajjanī nāma bhāryā atyantaṃ parapuruṣalampaṭā /
tāṃ ca tadgṛhasthāṃ devako nāma ramate /
iti lokādetadākarṇya vardhakiḥ kapaṭena gṛhānnirgatya prātaḥsandhyāyāmācchannaḥ samāgatya talpasyādhobhāge sthitaḥ /
sā ca jāreṇa saha tatrārūḍhā patyā keśeṣu gṛhītā kathaṃ mucyate /
uttaram-sā patyā dhṛtā satī dvitīyapatimukhamālokya prāha-mayā tava kathitaṃ yadrathakāro mama patirgṛhena vidyate /
sa cāgatastava tadaiva aucityaṃ vidhāsyati /
yadyapi pūrvaṃ patyā tvadīyaṃ dravyamapahṛtaṃ tathāpi kṣantavyam /
rathakṛti samāgate tava gṛhaṃ gamiṣyāmi yuvayoḥ saṃgatiṃ vā kariṣye /
nātra saṃśayaḥ /
iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text: <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked: 'What is this?' The parrot said: There is a city named <s>Candrapura</s>. There lived a wealthy carpenter named <s>Sūrapāla</s>. His wife, named <s>Sajjanī</s>, was exceedingly desirous of other men. And a man named <s>Devaka</s> enjoyed her while she was at home. Having heard this from the townspeople, the carpenter deceitfully left the house and, returning secretly at the dawn hour, hid himself beneath the bed. She, having climbed upon the bed with her lover, was seized by the hair by her husband — how did she free herself? The answer: She, being held by her husband, looked at the face of the second man and said: 'I had told you that <s>Rathakāra</s> (the carpenter), my husband, is in the house. He has come, and he will immediately deal with you as is proper. Although my husband previously took your wealth, still you should be forgiven. When the carpenter comes, I will go to your house, or I will arrange a meeting between you two. There is no doubt about this.' Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau caturviśatitamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-fourth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 25:
children.translated_text: START Suk 25:

children.text:
anyadā prabhāvatī śukaṃ gamanāya pṛcchati /
śukaḥ prāha-
children.translated_text: On another day, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked the parrot about going. The parrot said:

children.text: kuru yadrocate kartuṃ yadi vetsi pratīṅgitam /
children.translated_text: 'Do what pleases you to do, if you understand counter-signs,

children.text: śvetāmbareṇa ruddhena yathā pūrvaṃ kṛtaṃ tathā // Suk_25.1 (=169) //
children.translated_text: as was done before by means of a white garment used as a cover.' Suk_25.1 (=169)

children.text:
asti candrapurī nāma nagarī /
tatra siddhaseno nāma kṣapaṇako janapūjitaḥ /
tasminneva nagare 'nyaḥ sitapaṭo guṇināṃ mukhyaḥ samāgataḥ /
tena ca guṇinā sarvo 'pi jana āvarjitaḥ śrāvakā apyātmāyattāḥ kṛtāḥ /
sa kṣapaṇako 'pi tasya pūjāṃ kriyamāṇāmasahamānaḥ svayaṃ tadīyopāśraye veśyāṃ preṣayitvā asau veśyālubdho na suśīla iti śvetāmbarasya lokapravādamakarot /
taddarśanāya janamākārayāmāsa /
brūte ca--kṣapaṇakā eva brahmacāriṇaḥ śvetāmbarāstu viplutāḥ /
so 'pi śvetāmbaro dīpāgninā upādhiṃ prajvālya prabhātaprāptāyāṃ rajanyāṃ nagnobhūya veśyāyā dattahasto nirgataḥ /
tato lokāpavādaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ /
yadasau kṣapaṇako na sitavastraḥ /
iti śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text: There is a city named <s>Candrapurī</s>. In it, a <s>Jain</s> monk named <s>Siddhasena</s> was honored by the people. In that very city, another ascetic named <s>Sitapaṭa</s> (White-Cloth), chief among the virtuous, arrived. That virtuous man won over all the people, and even the lay followers were brought under his influence. That <s>Jain</s> monk, unable to bear the worship being offered to him, sent a courtesan to his monastery and spread the rumor among the people that this <s>Śvetāmbara</s> (white-clad monk) was lustful and not of good conduct. He summoned people to witness this. And he declared: 'The <s>Kṣapaṇakas</s> (Digambara monks) alone are celibate; the <s>Śvetāmbaras</s> are fallen.' But that <s>Śvetāmbara</s> monk, having set fire to a contrivance by means of a lamp's flame, when dawn came, emerged naked, holding the courtesan by the hand. Then the public scandal turned around — for it was that <s>Kṣapaṇaka</s> monk, not the white-clad one, [who was implicated]. Having heard this, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau pañcaviṃśatitamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-fifth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 26:
children.translated_text: START Suk 26:

children.text:
anyadā sā calitā /
śukaḥ prāha--
children.translated_text: On another day, she set out. The parrot said:

children.text: yāhi devi na te doṣo yadi jānāsi bhāṣitum /
children.translated_text: 'Go, O queen, there is no fault for you, if you know how to speak,

children.text: ratnādevīva patyā tu prāptā jāradvayānvitā // Suk_26.1 (=170) //
children.translated_text: like <s>Ratnādevī</s>, who was caught by her husband in the company of two lovers.' Suk_26.1 (=170)

children.text:
asti jalaudābhidhāno grāmaḥ /
tatra rājaputraḥ kṣemarājaḥ śūraḥ /
ratnādevī tasya bhāryā /
tatraiva grāmaṇīrdevasākhyaḥ /
tasya suto dhavalo nāma /
tau dvāvapi ramete ratnādevīṃ parasparamajñātau /
anyadā pitṛputrau tadgṛhasthau yadā tadā rājaputraḥ samāgataḥ /
tadā kimuttaram? śuka āha-tatastayā kṛtasaṃjño gṛhādaṅgulyā tarjayannayāt /
tasmiṃścaiva gacchati bhayātpatiḥ kimidamityāha /
tataḥ sā hasantī prāha-asya putrastvadgṛhe śaraṇāgataḥ /
mayā ca nārpitaḥ /
yataḥ-
children.translated_text: There is a village called <s>Jalaudā</s>. There lived a brave prince named <s>Kṣemarāja</s>. <s>Ratnādevī</s> was his wife. In that very village lived a headman named <s>Devasa</s>. His son was named <s>Dhavala</s>. Both of them enjoyed <s>Ratnādevī</s>, each unknown to the other. One day, when both father and son were at her house, the prince arrived. What then was the answer? The parrot said: Then, at her prearranged signal, [the son] left the house, shaking his finger threateningly. As he was leaving, the husband, out of fear, asked: 'What is this?' Then she, laughing, said: 'His son has taken refuge in your house. And I had not handed him over. Because:

children.text: sa kṣatriyastrāṇasahaḥ satāṃ yastatkārmukaṃ karmasu yasya śaktiḥ /
children.translated_text: He is a <s>Kṣatriya</s> capable of protection, his bow is skilled in deeds,

children.text: vahandvayīmapyaphale 'rthajāte karotyasaṃskārahatāmivoktim // Suk_26.2 (=171) //
children.translated_text: bearing both (bow and arrow) even when the purpose fails, he renders speech as if uncultivated.' Suk_26.2 (=171)

children.text:
ato ruṣṭo vrajati /
gaccha tvaṃ samarpaya sutam /
tena ca tathā kṛtam /
iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text: Therefore he leaves in anger. Go, you hand over the son to him.' And he did so. Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau ṣaḍviṃśatitamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-sixth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 27:
children.translated_text: START Suk 27:

children.text:
anyadā prabhāvatī gamanāya śukaṃ pṛcchati sma /
śukaḥ prāha-
children.translated_text: On another day, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked the parrot about going. The parrot said:

children.text: rambhoru gaccha kāmināṃ ko vighnaṃ kartumarhati /
children.translated_text: 'O beautiful-thighed one, go! Who can obstruct the passionate?

children.text: mohinīva samarthā cedvicārīkartumīśvari // Suk_27.1 (=172) //
children.translated_text: If you are as capable as <s>Mohinī</s> in devising a stratagem, O mistress!' Suk_27.1 (=172)

children.text:
asti śaṅkhapuraṃ nāma nagaram /
tatrāryo vaṇigabhūt /
tasya mohinī nāma bhāryā /
tāñcabahirgatāṃ kumukho nāma dhūrto ramate /
tatpatinā cābhijñāyi /
tatpatiścātiśayena bhīruḥ /
tato 'sau tāṃ bahiryāntīṃ nivārya pārśvasthita eva tiṣṭhati /
tathāpi tayā dhūrtasya kathitam-māṃ rātrau bhartṛkhaṭvāsthitāmarvāksuptāṃ bhaja tvam /
tena tathā kṛtam /
tacca kurvanbhartrāsau puṃścihne dhṛtaḥ kathaṃ gacchatu? uttaram-dhṛtvā ca patiḥ prāha-pradopamānaya mayā coro dhṛto 'sti /
tayoktam-bahiryāntī bibhemyaham /
enaṃ grahīṣye tvaṃ dīpamānaya /
tena ca tathā kṛtam /
sā ca jāraṃ muktvā gṛhāntarbaddhasya paṭṭakasya jihvāṃ gṛhītvā tathaiva suptā yāvatpatirlakuṭahasto dīpaṃ gṛhītvā samāyātaḥ pṛcchati-kimiyaṃ paṭṭakasya jihvā kathamatra? tayoktam-kṣudhārto 'yam /
anena muktā lālākṛśā sthitā /
uktipratyuktivādena nirjitaḥ /
uktaśca-hataka! anena pauruṣeṇa kṣayaṃ vrajasi /
iti nirbhartsito lajjitaśca suptaḥ /
iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text: There is a city named <s>Śaṅkhapura</s>. There lived a merchant. His wife was named <s>Mohinī</s>. A rogue named <s>Kumukha</s> enjoyed her when she went out. And her husband came to know of it. Her husband was extremely timid. So he prevented her from going out and stood always by her side. Even so, she told the rogue: 'Come to me at night while I lie facing downward on my husband's bed.' He did so. But while doing this, he was caught by the husband at the mark of masculinity — how was he to escape? The answer: Having caught him, the husband said: 'Bring a lamp! I have caught a thief!' She said: 'I am afraid to go outside. I will hold him while you bring the lamp.' He did so. And she, releasing the lover, grasped the tongue of a wooden puppet that was fastened inside the house and lay down just as before. When the husband came back with a stick in hand carrying a lamp and asked, [she said]: 'This is the tongue of a puppet — how did it get here?' She replied: 'He was hungry. I was left weakened by his saliva.' She defeated him by argument and counter-argument. And she said: 'Wretch! With such manliness you will come to ruin.' Thus rebuked, he went to sleep in shame. Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau saptaviṃśatitamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-seventh tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 28:
children.translated_text: START Suk 28:

children.text:
anyadā prabhāvatī gamanāya śukaṃ papraccha /
śukaḥ prāha--
children.translated_text: On another day, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked the parrot about going. The parrot said:

children.text: kṛśodari vrajādya tvaṃ yadi jānāsi bhāṣitum /
children.translated_text: 'O slender-waisted one, go today if you know how to speak,

children.text: jārasaṃyuktayā pūrvaṃ yathā devikayā kṛtam // Suk_28.1 (=173) //
children.translated_text: as <s>Devikā</s> formerly did when caught with her lover.' Suk_28.1 (=173)

children.text:
asti kuhāḍākhyo mahāgrāmaḥ tatra jarasākhyo kauṭumbiko mahāmūrkhaḥ /
tadbhāryā devikā puṃścalī /
tāṃ ca prabhākaro brāhmaṇaḥ kṣetramadhye vibhītakavṛkṣasamīpe guptasthāne mudā ramater /
idṛśaṃ vyatikaraṃ janācchratvā tatpatistatrāvalokanāya svayaṃ gataḥ /
tena ca vṛkṣārūḍhena tattathaiva dṛṣṭam /
dṛṣṭvā tatrasthenāpi jalpitam, dhūrtike! bahudinebhyo 'dya samprāptā-ityuktā kathamiyaṃ bhartāraṃ pratyāyayatu /
tayoktam--nāhaṃ jāne tvameva kathaya /
"yadi na yāsi tadā kathayāmi' /
tayā tatheti pratipanne śukaḥ prāha--sā ca tadvacaḥ śrutvā taṃ jāraṃ preṣayāmāsa patyā cāvatīrya samāgatena upālabdhā /
sā'ha--he prabhor! idṛśa eva vṛkṣaḥ, atrārūḍhairmithunaṃ dṛśyate /
tena patinā uktam--tvamāruhya avalokaya /
tayā tathā kṛtam /
vṛkṣārūḍhayā ca tayā proktaṃ kapaṭena /
"vahudivasebhyo 'nyāṃ nārīmabhigaman dṛṣṭo 'si" /
tena mūrkheṇa jñātam--satyamidam /
sa ca tāṃ śāntayitvā gṛhaṃ nināya /
iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text: There is a great village named <s>Kuhāḍā</s>. There lived a householder named <s>Jarasā</s>, a great fool. His wife <s>Devikā</s> was an adulteress. A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Prabhākara</s> would joyfully make love to her at a secret place near a <s>vibhītaka</s> tree in the middle of a field. Having heard of this affair from people, her husband himself went there to see. And he, having climbed the tree, saw everything just as it was. Even while standing there he called out, 'O wanton woman! After so many days you have come today!' — thus being addressed, how should she convince her husband? She said: 'I do not know; you yourself tell me.' 'If you do not go, then I shall tell.' When she agreed, the parrot said: She, having heard his words, sent away her lover, and when her husband, having climbed down, came and rebuked her, she said: 'O lord! Such indeed is this tree — those who climb it see a couple.' Her husband said: 'You climb up and look.' She did so. And having climbed the tree, she said deceitfully: 'After many days I have seen you approaching another woman!' That fool then understood: 'This is true [about the tree].' And he, having pacified her, led her home. Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau aṣṭāviṃśatitamo kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-eighth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 29:
children.translated_text: START Suk 29:

children.text:
anyedyuḥ prabhāvatī gamanāya śukaṃ pṛcchati sma /
so 'pyāha--
children.translated_text: On the next day, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked the parrot about going out. He said:

children.text: vraja devi vicāraṃ cetkartuṃ jānāsi bhāmini /
children.translated_text: Go, O lady, if you know how to deliberate, O beautiful one,

children.text: samaṃ jāreṇa samprāptā sundarīva yathā gṛhe // Suk_29.1 (=174) //
children.translated_text: just as the fair <s>Sundarī</s> arrived home together with her lover. Suk_29.1 (=174)

children.text:
"kathametat'? so 'bravīt--asti sīhūlo nāma grāmaḥ /
tatra mahādhano vaṇik /
tadbhāryā sundarī /
tāṃ ca mohano nāma upapatirnityaṃ gṛhamāgatya bhuṅkte /
anyadā yāvatsā tathā tiṣṭhati tāvattatpatiḥ samāgataḥ /
sā kathaṃ bhavatu /
uttaram--sā patimāgacchantaṃ dṛṣṭvā jāraṃ vivastraṃ śikye kṛtvā muktakeśā gṛhānnirgatya dūrasthā patimāha-asmadgṛhamadhye nagnabhūtaṃ śikyārūḍhaṃ vidyate /
māntrikānākārayituṃ gacchetyukte sa mūrkhastadarthaṃ jagāma /
tadā ca tadantare tayā ulmukaṃ haste kṛtvā upapatirniṣkāsitaḥ /
patyau ca āgate sā jagāda-yadulmukenāpi bhūtaṃ naṣṭam /
iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text: 'How so?' He said: There is a village named <s>Sīhūla</s>. There lived a very wealthy merchant. His wife was <s>Sundarī</s>. Her paramour, named <s>Mohana</s>, would regularly come to the house and enjoy her. One day, while she was thus engaged, her husband arrived. What should she do? The answer: She, seeing her husband approaching, placed her naked lover in the hanging basket, and with her hair loose, came out of the house and standing at a distance said to her husband: 'Inside our house there is a naked ghost sitting in the hanging basket. Go and summon exorcists!' That fool went for that purpose. Meanwhile, she took a firebrand in her hand and led her paramour out. When her husband returned, she said: 'The ghost has been driven away by the firebrand.' Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau ekonatriṃśattamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-ninth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 30:
children.translated_text: START Suk 30:

children.text: anyedyuḥ prabhāvatyā pṛṣṭaḥ śukaḥ prāha /
children.translated_text: On the next day, when asked by <s>Prabhāvatī</s>, the parrot said:

children.text: gaccha devi viruddhaṃ te gamanaṃ na mataṃ mama /
children.translated_text: Go, O lady; your going is not approved by me as it is improper,

children.text: viṣame yadi vetsi tvamuttaraṃ mūladevavat // Suk_30.1 (=175) //
children.translated_text: [but go] if in a difficult situation you know the answer, like <s>Mūladeva</s>. Suk_30.1 (=175)

children.text:
astīha pṛthivyāṃ bhūtavāsaṃ nāma śmaśānam /
tatra dvau piśācau karālottālanāmānau /
bhārye ca dhūmaprabhāmeghaprabhākhye, tayośca bhāryārāmaṇīya katve vivādaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ /
anyadā ca tābhyāṃ bhāryāsahitābhyāṃ mūledavodṛṣṭo bāhubhyāṃ vidhṛtya pṛṣṭaḥ-kā anayormadhyādramaṇīyā, anṛtaṃ vadantaṃvyāpādayiṣyāvaḥ /
tatkalatre virūpe bhīṣaṇe vṛddhe piśācinyau /
sa ca yathārthavādī bhakṣitaḥ syāt kimuttaraṃ kuryāditi /
uttaram--tenoktam-
children.translated_text: There is on this earth a cremation ground named <s>Bhūtavāsa</s> (Abode of Ghosts). There lived two <s>piśācas</s> (ghouls) named <s>Karāla</s> and <s>Uttāla</s>. Their wives were named <s>Dhūmaprabhā</s> and <s>Meghaprabhā</s>. A quarrel arose between them regarding which wife was more beautiful. One day, these two, together with their wives, seized <s>Mūladeva</s> by the arms and asked: 'Which of these two is more beautiful? If you speak falsely, we shall kill you.' Now both their wives were ugly, hideous, old she-ghouls. If he spoke truthfully, he would be devoured — so what answer should he give? The answer: He said —

children.text: yā yasya vallabhā loke ramyā sā tasya nāparā /
children.translated_text: She who is beloved to each one in this world, she is beautiful to him and no other.

children.text: gadite dhūrtarājena tābhyāṃ muktaśca tatkṣaṇāt // Suk_30.2 (=176) //
children.translated_text: When the clever <s>Mūladeva</s> spoke thus, he was released by them at once. Suk_30.2 (=176)

children.text: iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text: Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau triṃśattamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the thirtieth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 31:
children.translated_text: START Suk 31:

children.text: anyadā ca prabhāvatyā pṛṣṭaḥ śukaḥ provāca-
children.translated_text: On another day, when asked by <s>Prabhāvatī</s>, the parrot said:

children.text: yatheṣṭaṃ vraja kalyāṇi keliṃ karttuṃ kṛśodari /
children.translated_text: Go as you wish, O auspicious one, to sport, O slender-waisted lady,

children.text: śaśakasyeva te buddhirasti cetsusahāyinī // Suk_31.1 (=177) //
children.translated_text: if your intellect is as resourceful as that of the hare. Suk_31.1 (=177)

children.text:
madhurākhye vane piṅgalanāmā siṃhaḥ /
sa sattvāni bahūni hanansarvaiḥ paśubhirvicārya pratidinamekaikasattvaparikalpanavyavasthayā nivāritaḥ /
anyadā śaśakasyaikasya vārakaḥ sañjātaḥ /
sa ca na yāti śvāpadairbhaṇito 'pi-"gaccha tvamanyathā pūrvavatsarvāṇi bhūtāni sa bhakṣayiṣyati /
sa cādyaprabhṛti tadantike sattvāni na yāsyanti'-ityuktvā bahukālakṣepaṃ cakāra /
madhyāhnasamaye eva ca mandaṃ mandaṃ siṃhasyāgre gantuṃ vyasitaḥ /
tenāpi sahasākrāntaḥ kathaṃ mucyate? uttaram-śaśakaḥ siṃhiṃ prāha-svaminnahaṃ śaśakacatuṣṭayena saha āgacchanmārge tava śatruṇā dhṛto 'to velātikramo babhūva /
tenoktam-sa śatruṃ kvāste? tataḥ sa śaśakena dhūrtena vāṭīṃ nītvā tasyaiva pratibimbaḥ kūpe darśitaḥ /
siṃho 'pi mūrkhastaṃ jale dṛṣṭvā kupito jhampādānmṛtaśca /
children.translated_text: In a forest named <s>Madhurā</s> there lived a lion named <s>Piṅgala</s>. As he was killing many animals, all the beasts deliberated and restrained him with an arrangement whereby one animal would be offered each day. One day it was a certain hare's turn. He would not go, even when urged by the other animals: 'Go, otherwise, as before, he will devour all creatures. And from today onward, no animals will go to him' — saying thus, he wasted much time. Only at midday did he slowly set out to approach the lion. When the lion fiercely pounced on him, how could he be saved? The answer: The hare said to the lion: 'O master, I was coming with four other hares, but on the way I was seized by your enemy, hence the delay.' The lion said: 'Where is that enemy?' Then the clever hare led him to a well and showed him his own reflection [in the water]. The foolish lion, seeing him in the water and becoming enraged, leapt in and died.

children.text: buddhirbalavatī bhīru sattvānāṃ na parākramaḥ /
children.translated_text: Intelligence is the strength of the fearful among creatures, not physical prowess;

children.text: śaśakenālpasattvena hataḥ siṃhaḥ parākramī // Suk_31.2 (=178) //
children.translated_text: by the hare, a creature of little strength, the mighty lion was slain. Suk_31.2 (=178)

children.text: uktañca-
children.translated_text: And it is also said:

children.text: ekaṃ hanyānna vā hanyādiṣurmukto dhanuṣmatā /
children.translated_text: An arrow released by a bowman may kill one or may not kill;

children.text: sarārṣṭa saprajaṃ hanti rājānaṃ mantriniścayaḥ // Suk_31.3 (=179) //
children.translated_text: but a firm resolution of a minister destroys the king together with his kingdom and subjects. Suk_31.3 (=179)

children.text: iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text: Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau ekatriṃśattamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the thirty-first tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 32:
children.translated_text: START Suk 32:

children.text:
athānyedyuḥ prabhāvatī calitā śukaṃ papraccha gamanāya /
śukaḥ-
children.translated_text: Then on the next day, <s>Prabhāvatī</s>, having set out, asked the parrot about going. The parrot said:

children.text: yādi devi mano yatra gantuṃ te kamalānane /
children.translated_text: Go where your mind desires, O lotus-faced lady,

children.text: rājinīva vijānāsi vaktuṃ dhūliviparyaye // Suk_32.1 (=180) //
children.translated_text: if, like <s>Rājinī</s>, you know what to say when dust is substituted. Suk_32.1 (=180)

children.text:
asti śāntipuraṃ nāma nagaram /
tatra mādhavaḥ śreṣṭhī /
tasya mohinī bhāryā /
tayostanayaḥ sohaḍābhidhaḥ /
tasya bhāryā rājinīnāmnī rūpasampannā caturā puṃścalī /
sānyadā drammarpayitvā śvaśrvajñaptā "godhūmān haṭṭe gṛhītvā gaccha' /
sā ca haṭṭe gatā /
krīṇatyā copapatirdṛṣṭaḥ saṃjñitaśca samīpamāyayau /
godhūmānmoṭāyāṃ baddhvā haṭṭe muktvā tena sārdhaṃ sā yayau /
vaṇijāpi godhūmānutsārya moṭāyāṃ dhūlirbaddhā /
sāpi tena saha ciraṃ sthitvā āgatyākulā moṭāmanutpāṭayitvā gṛhaṃ yayau /
tāṃ choṭayitvā yāvat śvaśrūḥ paśyati kodṛśā godhūmā iti tāvaddhūliṃ paśyati /
atra kimuttaram /
śukaḥ-kimidamiti yadā śvaśrvā pṛṣṭā tadā tayoktam-"mātarmama hastād drammaḥ haṭṭāgre bhūmau patitaḥ /
children.translated_text: The parrot said: When she was asked by her mother-in-law 'What is this?', she replied: 'Mother, the coin fell from my hand to the ground in front of the market.

children.text: tato mayā dhūlirāhṛtā /
children.translated_text: So I brought back the dust [instead].'

children.text: tataḥ sā śvaśrūrdrammamanavalokamānā vikalībhūtā /
children.translated_text: Then her mother-in-law, not finding the coin, became confused [and believed her].

children.text: iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā iti śukasaptatau dvātriṃśattamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep. Thus ends the thirty-second tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

There is a city named <s>Śāntipura</s>. There lived a merchant named <s>Mādhava</s>. His wife was <s>Mohinī</s>. Their son was named <s>Sohaḍa</s>. His wife, named <s>Rājinī</s>, was beautiful, clever, and an adulteress. One day, having been given a coin by her mother-in-law with the instruction 'Go to the market and buy wheat,' she went to the market. While buying, she saw her paramour, signaled to him, and he came near. She tied the wheat in a bundle, left it at the market, and went off with him. The merchant, however, removed the wheat and tied dust in the bundle. She, having spent a long time with him, came back flustered, and without opening the bundle, went home. When her mother-in-law opened it to see what kind of wheat it was, she found dust. What was the answer to this?

children.text: START Suk 33:
children.translated_text: START Suk 33:

children.text:
athānyedyuḥ prabhāvatī gamanāyotsukā śukaṃ papraccha /
śukaḥ prāha-
children.translated_text: Then on the next day, <s>Prabhāvatī</s>, eager to go out, asked the parrot. The parrot said:

children.text: ko doṣo gamyatāṃ devi yadi kartuṃ tvamīśvarā /
children.translated_text: What fault is there? Go, O lady, if you are capable of acting

children.text: viṣame mālinī yadvadrambhikā patisannidhau // Suk_33.1 (=181) //
children.translated_text: as <s>Mālinī</s> and <s>Rambhikā</s> did in a difficult situation before their husbands. Suk_33.1 (=181)

children.text:
prabhāvatī-"kathametat'? śuko 'bravīt-asti śaṅkhapuraṃ nāma nagaram /
tatra śaṅkaro nāma mālikaḥ samṛddhimān /
tasya rambhikā nāma bhāryā bahuratipriyā subhagā surūpā bahubhartṛkā ca /
anyadā śaṅkaragṛhe pitṛkāryamāgatam tasmindine tayopapatayaścatvāro nimantritāḥ puṣpāṇāṃ vikrayāya gatayā catuṣpathe grāmaṇīrvaṇiksūnustalāraśca balādhipaśca pratyekaṃ te te pṛthakpṛthak ākāritāḥ parasparamajānantaḥ-madīyaṃ bhavanaṃ prati prāgeva samāgantavyamiti /
dvitīye 'hni mālike vāṭikāṃ gate vaṇiksūnuḥ snātvā bhuktvā ca tayā saha rantuṃ samāyayau /
vaṇiji ardhasnāte grāmakūṭo gṛhadvāraṃ samāpatandṛṣṭaḥ tataḥ snānaṃ kurvanvaṇiktathābhūto vaṃśamaye koṣṭhe khaliyukte kṣipto bhayayuktaśca /
grāmakūṭe 'pyardhasnāte bahistalāraḥ samāyātaḥ /
taṃ dṛṣṭvā so 'pi tasminneva koṣṭhe kṣipta uktaśca-yadadhaḥ sarpiṇī prasūtāsti /
tato 'pyanatarāla evaṃ sthātavyamiti talāro 'pyardhasnāto balādhipaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhāṇḍasamūhe kṣiptaḥ /
balādhipo 'pyardhasnāto mālikaṃ dṛṣṭvā tatraiva kṣiptaḥ /
tato māliko lokaśca tasmin pitṛkārye yadṛcchayā bhijitāḥ /
evaṃ kṛtvā te ṣāṃ caturṇāmapi parasparamalakṣitānāṃ pṛthakpṛthak bhojanaṃ paramānnāmṛtaṃ samarpitam /
vaṇijā tu bhuñjānena bahu phūtkṛtam /
tadoparisthitena ca sarpiṇīṃ śaṅkamānena mūtritam /
vaṇijā tu ghṛtāmiti jñātvā bhājanamutkṣiptam /
uparisthitasya mukhe lagnam /
tataḥ sa śaṅkitaḥ /
so 'pi ca lagnaṃ lagnamiti vadandattajhampo niryayau /
anye 'pi lagnākṣarabhayākulā yāvannirgatāḥ śaṅkareṇa janaiśca dṛṣṭāḥ savismayaṃ khalikharaḍitāḥ /
tataḥ sā kathaṃ bhavatu? uttam-yadā sā patyā pṛṣṭā kimidamiti tadā tayoktam-
children.translated_text: <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked: 'How so?' The parrot said: There is a city named <s>Śaṅkhapura</s>. There lived a prosperous garland-maker named <s>Śaṅkara</s>. His wife, named <s>Rambhikā</s>, was very amorous, charming, beautiful, and had many lovers. One day, a <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rite) came to be performed at <s>Śaṅkara</s>'s house. On that day, she had invited her four paramours — a village headman, a merchant's son, a watchman, and a military commander — ostensibly to sell flowers. She summoned each one separately at the crossroads, each unaware of the others, saying: 'Come to my house early.' On the second day, when the garland-maker had gone to the garden, the merchant's son, having bathed and eaten, came to sport with her. While the merchant was still half-bathed, the village headman was seen approaching the door. So the merchant, in that state, was thrown into a bamboo granary with chaff, terrified. When the village headman too was half-bathed, the watchman arrived from outside. Seeing him, the headman too was thrown into that same granary, being told: 'There is a she-snake that has given birth below, so you must stand in the space above.' The watchman too, half-bathed, seeing the military commander, was thrown among the goods. The military commander too, half-bathed, seeing the garland-maker, was thrown in there as well. Then the garland-maker and the people attended the <s>śrāddha</s> by chance. Having done so, food and sacred rice pudding were offered separately to each of the four, undetected by one another. But the merchant, while eating, blew repeatedly [on the hot food]. The one above him, fearing the supposed she-snake, urinated. The merchant, thinking it was ghee, tossed up his vessel. It stuck to the face of the one above. He then, crying 'It has stuck! It has stuck!', jumped down and rushed out. The others too, terrified by the word 'stuck,' came out and were seen by <s>Śaṅkara</s> and the people, who were astonished and laughed at them, covered in chaff. Then what should she do? The answer: When she was asked by her husband 'What is this?', she said:

children.text: śraddhāhīnaṃ kṛtaṃ śrāddhamidaṃ nūnaṃ tvayā priya /
children.translated_text: 'Surely this <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rite) was performed by you without faith, O dear one;

children.text: ato 'bhuktvā kṣudhākrāntāḥ pitaraste vinirgatāḥ // Suk_33.2 (=182) //
children.translated_text: therefore your ancestors have departed unfed, overcome by hunger.' Suk_33.2 (=182)

children.text:
tataḥ sa punaḥ śrāddhaṃ cakāra /
rambhikāvacanāttena nirgatāḥ /
iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text: Then he performed the <s>śrāddha</s> again. At <s>Rambhikā</s>'s word, he [accepted that] they had departed. Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau trayastriṃśattamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the thirty-third tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 34:
children.translated_text: START Suk 34:

children.text:
athānyasmindine gamanārthaṃ prabhāvatī śukaṃ papraccha /
śukaḥ prāha-
children.translated_text: Then on another day, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked the parrot about going out. The parrot said:

children.text: yāhi devi gatā vetsi bhaṅguraṃ yadi bhāṣitum /
children.translated_text: Go, O lady, if you know how to speak with deception upon arriving,

children.text: kumāryai pāraḍī dattvā yathoktaṃ śambhunā purā // Suk_34.1 (=183) //
children.translated_text: as <s>Śambhu</s> once did, having given a <s>pāraḍī</s> (dice/garment) to the maiden. Suk_34.1 (=183)

children.text:
prabhāvatyāha-kathametat /
śukaḥ prāha--purā kasmiṃścinnagare śambhunāmā vipro 'bhūt dyūtakṛnnānādeśaparibhramaṇaśīlo mārge gacchan kṣetrarakṣikāṃ surūpāṃ bālikāṃ dṛṣṭvā tāmbūlaṃ datvā sāntvayannidamuvāca yanmatsambhogakaraṇe imāṃ madīyāṃ pāraḍīṃ gṛhāṇa mayā saha rataṃ kuru /
sukhāśrayaṃ tayā tathā vihitam /
sa ca siddhe kārye tāṃ yācate /
kathaṃ labhate? uttaram-yāvattena yācitā tāvatsā calitā gṛhaṃ prati /
so 'pi ca pañca kaṇiśāni gṛhītvā pṛṣṭhe lagnaḥ /
tena ca grāmagatena phūtkṛtam-aho grāmamukhyāḥ! paśyata /
grāme 'sminmahadadbhutam /
pañcakaṇiśakāraṇenānayā madīyaṃ vastramapahṛtam /
grāmyaistatsamarpitam /
tayā ca na kiñciduktaṃ lajjayā /
iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text: <s>Prabhāvatī</s> said: 'How so?' The parrot said: Once in a certain city there lived a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Śambhu</s>, a gambler accustomed to wandering through various lands. While traveling on the road, seeing a beautiful young girl guarding a field, he gave her betel and, flattering her, said: 'If you make love with me, take this garment of mine; sport with me.' She gladly agreed. When the deed was done, he asked her for it back. How did he get it? The answer: As soon as he asked, she ran toward her home. He too, having taken five small ears of grain, followed close behind. And that man, having reached the village, cried out: 'O village elders! Look! There is a great wonder in this village! For the sake of five small ears of grain, this woman has stolen my garment!' The villagers made her return it. And she, out of shame, said nothing. Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau catustriṃśattamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the thirty-fourth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 35:
children.translated_text: START Suk 35:

children.text:
apare 'hni sā śṛṅgārānvitā śukaṃ papraccha /
śukaḥ prāha-
children.translated_text: On the next day, she, adorned for love, asked the parrot. The parrot said:

children.text: gaccha devi na te doṣo yadi tatra gatā satī /
children.translated_text: Go, O lady, there is no fault for you if, having gone there,

children.text: svārthaṃ kartuṃ vijānāsi tilakrayakaro yathā // Suk_35.1 (=184) //
children.translated_text: you know how to serve your own interest, like the sesame-seed seller. Suk_35.1 (=184)

children.text:
"kathametat? śukaḥ prāha-purā kasmiṃścid grāme śambakanāmā vaṇiktilagrāhakaḥ /
sa ca saragrāmaṃ yathau /
tatrasthasya bhāṇḍaśālikasya gṛhe gataḥ /
sa gṛhe nāsti /
tasya bhāryāsti paraṃ kulaṭā /
netrasaṃjñayā parasparaṃ prītirutpannā /
tatraiva sā bhuktā aṅgulīyakaṃ dattvā /
sambandhādanantaraṃ sa tadaṅgulīyakaṃ jighṛkṣati /
anena vidhinā dattamaṅgulīyakaṃ sa kathaṃ gṛhṇātviti praśnaḥ /
śukaḥ prāha-tilagrāhakastadalabhamāno vipaṇisthaṃ bhāṇḍaśālikamāha-"dehi me tilaprasthaśataṃ yatsatyaṅkāritaṃ mayā' /
evamuktaḥ sa āha-"ke tilāḥ kaśca vaktā tvaṃ satyaṅkāraśca kīdṛśaḥ? tenoktam-prasthaṃ prati dvikapravṛddhyā tvadbhāryayā satyaṅkāre 'ṅgulīyakaṃ gṛhītam /
tato ruṣṭena vaṇijā bhāryāpāraśve nijaṃ sutaṃ preṣayitvā iti kathayāmāsa-tvadīyenedṛśena vyavahāreṇāsmadgṛhaṃ vṛddhimāpsyati /
putro 'pyaṅgulīyakamādāya tilagrāhakasyārpayāmāsa /
so 'pi yathāgataṃ tathā yayau /
tato yadi prabhāvi tavāpyevaṃ buddhirasti tadā gamyatāṃ nānyathā /
iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text: "How is this [to be understood]?" The parrot said: "Formerly, in a certain village, there was a merchant named <s>Śambaka</s>, a sesame-dealer. He went to the village of <s>Sara</s>. There he went to the house of a grain-merchant. The grain-merchant was not at home. His wife was an utter adulteress. Through an exchange of glances, mutual desire arose between them. He enjoyed her right there, giving her a ring. After the liaison, he wished to take back the ring. 'How shall he recover the ring given in this manner?' — this is the question. The parrot said: The sesame-dealer, unable to obtain it [back], said to the grain-merchant at his shop: 'Give me a hundred <s>prasthas</s> (measures) of sesame, for which a pledge has been given by me.' Thus addressed, the grain-merchant said: 'What sesame? And who are you to speak? What kind of pledge is this?' The sesame-dealer replied: 'At the rate of two [measures] increase per <s>prastha</s>, your wife has taken a ring as pledge.' Then the angry merchant, sending his own son to his wife, told [him] thus: 'By such dealings of yours, our household will come to ruin.' The son too, taking the ring, delivered it to the sesame-dealer. And the sesame-dealer departed as he had come. Therefore, O <s>Prabhāvatī</s>, if you too possess such wit, then go — otherwise not." Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau pañcatriṃśattamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the thirty-fifth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s>.

children.text: START Suk 36:
children.translated_text: Beginning of the thirty-sixth tale of the <s>Śukasaptati</s>:

children.text:
niśāmukhe 'nyedyuḥ prabhāvatī śukaṃ punarāha-he kīra! gamiṣyāmi cirakāṅkṣitaṃ sukhaṃ bhoktum /
śuka āha-
children.translated_text: At nightfall on the next day, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> again said to the parrot: "O parrot! I shall go to enjoy the long-desired pleasure." The parrot said —

children.text: sukhamevānubhoktavyaṃ saṃsāre sundari! dhruvam /
children.translated_text: "Pleasure alone is surely to be enjoyed in this world, O beautiful one;

children.text: nāyinīva vijānāsi yadi vaktuṃ tvamuttaram // Suk_36.1 (=185) //
children.translated_text: If you know how to give an answer, like <s>Nāyinī</s>." // Suk_36.1 (=185) //

children.text: prabhāvatyāha-kathametat /
children.translated_text: <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked: "How is this [to be understood]?"

children.text: kā kīra nāyinī kutra tayā kiṃ kṛtamuttaram /
children.translated_text: "Who, O parrot, is <s>Nāyinī</s>? Where [was she]? What answer did she give?

children.text: kathāṃ kathaya kalyāṇīṃ kautukaṃ me kathākrame // Suk_36.2 (=186) //
children.translated_text: Tell me the auspicious tale — I am curious about the story." // Suk_36.2 (=186) //

children.text:
śuka āha-asti saraḍākhye grāme grāmaṇīḥ śūrapālaḥ /
tasya bhāryā nāyinī /
sā ātmapatiṃ nityaṃ paṭṭasūtrakañcukaṃ yācate /
sa āha-vayaṃ karṣukāḥ kārpāsacīvarāḥ /
asmadgṛhe paṭṭasūtravārttāmapi ko 'pi na jānāti /
anyadā sā taṃ grāmasaṃsadisthaṃ jagāda-gṛhamehi gṛhādhipa! rāvaḍī bhuṅkṣva /
sa ca tadvacanaṃ śrutvā bhāryāmāha gṛhāgataḥ-bhadre! tvayā ninditaṃ vaco lajjākārakaṃ mamāpriyaṃ saṃsadi kimitthamuktam? tayoktam--tvayā mama priyaṃ kathaṃ na kṛtam? grāmaṇīrāha--dāsyāmi kañcukaṃ te 'dya /
nijaṃ vākyaṃ vṛthā kuru /
tayoktam--kañcuke datte uttārayiṣye /
dattaḥ kañcukastena /
tadvacaḥ kathaṃ vṛthā bhavatviti praśnaḥ /
śukaḥ prāha-anyadā nāyinī jagāda-yadādya tvāṃ saṃsadisthaṃ pūrvavadākārayāmi tadā tvayā saṃsadā saha gṛhamāgantavyam /
tena ca evameva kṛtam /
tayā ca gṛhāgatāyāḥ saṃsado bhavyarotyā bhojanaṃ dattam /
tato grāmajano vadati-śūrapālaḥ samṛddhaḥ /
paraṃ tadbhāryā auddhatyaparihāreṇa evaṃ vadati /
iti vacanamuttāritam /
iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text: The parrot said: In a village called <s>Saraḍa</s>, there was a village headman named <s>Śūrapāla</s>. His wife was <s>Nāyinī</s>. She constantly begged her husband for a silk-threaded bodice. He said: 'We are farmers, wearing cotton garments. In our house, no one even knows about silk.' On another occasion, she said to him in the village assembly: 'Come home, O master of the house! Eat <s>rāvaḍī</s> (a sweet dish).' Having heard her words, he came home and said to his wife: 'Good woman! Why did you speak those contemptible, embarrassing, and unpleasant words to me in the assembly?' She replied: 'How have you not done something pleasing for me?' The headman said: 'I shall give you the bodice today. Make your own words prove false.' She said: 'When the bodice is given, I shall retract [my words].' He gave the bodice. 'How shall her words be proven false?' — this is the question. The parrot said: On another occasion, <s>Nāyinī</s> said: 'When today I summon you from the assembly as before, you must come home together with the assembly.' And he did exactly so. And she served a fine meal to the assembly that had come to the house. Then the village folk said: '<s>Śūrapāla</s> is prosperous!' — but his wife speaks thus merely out of boldness. Thus her words were retracted. Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau ṣaṭtriṃśattamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the thirty-sixth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s>.

children.text: START Suk 37:
children.translated_text: Beginning of the thirty-seventh tale of the <s>Śukasaptati</s>:

children.text:
athāpare 'hni prabhāvatī gamanāya śukaṃ pṛcchati sma /
śuko 'pyāha-
children.translated_text: On the next day, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked the parrot for permission to go. The parrot said —

children.text: yatheṣṭaṃ vraja kalyāṇi na te doṣo 'sti kaścana /
children.translated_text: "Go as you wish, O auspicious one — there is no fault in you,

children.text: lāṅgalīva vijānāsi yadi kartuṃ tvamuttaram // Suk_37.1 (=189) //
children.translated_text: If you know how to give an answer, like <s>Lāṅgalī</s>." // Suk_37.1 (=189) //

children.text:
prabhāvatyāha-kathametat /
śuko 'pyāhṛ-saṅgamākhye grāme śūraḥ kauṭumbikaḥ /
tasyāsti pūrṇapālastu hālikaḥ /
sarvatra ca tasya śūrapaterveśmani kṣetre khale pramāṇam /
tasya ca hālikasya kṣetrasthasya śūrapatisutā subhagā nāma nityaṃ bhuktiṃ nayati /
sa tāṃ kāmayate kṣetragahvare śūrapālānniḥśaṅkitaḥ /
taṃ ca vṛttāntamasamañjasamiti kṛtvā prativeśmahālikāstasya kathayāmāsuḥ /
anyadāsau śūrastayorhālikasutayoḥ sambandhaṃ pratyakṣīkartuṃ kṣetraṃ gatvā gahvarasyādūrasamante 'lakṣitastasthau /
tanmithunaṃ ratasthaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ kathaṃ bhavatu? uttarañca kimiti praśnaḥ /
śukaḥ prāha-yāvatsa hālikastāṃ bhuktvotthitaḥ tāvat śūrapatiṃ dadarśa /
tadā sa niḥśvasannāha-dhiṅme karmārjanāṃ ca yanmayā halakheṭanaṃ vidheyam, iyaṃ ca granthirogiṇī /
ato dvayorapi jīvitaṃ rasātalaṃ yātu /
mayā tu nityaṃ halekheṭanaṃ grantherākarṣaṇaṃ ca dvayamapi vidheyam /
tadahaṃ kimarthamasya śūrapālasya hāliko bhavāmi /
itthamevāhaṃ kṣayaṃ yāsyāmi /
children.translated_text: 'In this very manner, I shall waste away.'

children.text: iti hālikavacanaṃ śrutvā nirdeṣo 'yamiti lokasya vacanaṃ vitathīkṛtya śūrapatirlajjito gṛhaṃ yayau /
children.translated_text: Having heard the ploughman's words, <s>Śūrapati</s>, [accepting] that 'this is [just] an accusation,' thus proving false the people's words, went home ashamed.

children.text: sā ca prabhāvatī śukoktāṃ kathāṃ śrutvā suptā /
children.translated_text: And <s>Prabhāvatī</s>, having heard the tale told by the parrot, fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau saptatriṃśattamo kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the thirty-seventh tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s>.

<s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked: "How is this [to be understood]?" The parrot said: In a village called <s>Saṅgama</s>, there was a householder named <s>Śūra</s>. He had a ploughman named <s>Pūrṇapāla</s>. This <s>Pūrṇapāla</s> had authority everywhere — in <s>Śūrapati</s>'s house, field, and threshing floor. <s>Śūrapati</s>'s daughter named <s>Subhagā</s> would always bring food to this ploughman when he was in the field. He desired her, and being unafraid of <s>Śūrapāla</s> in the secluded part of the field, [he enjoyed her]. The neighboring ploughmen, considering this conduct improper, reported it to him. One day, <s>Śūra</s>, wishing to witness firsthand the relationship between the ploughman and his daughter, went to the field and stood undetected not far from the secluded spot. He saw the couple in the act of love — 'What shall be done? And what answer [can be given]?' — this is the question. The parrot said: As soon as the ploughman, having enjoyed her, stood up, he saw <s>Śūrapati</s>. Then, sighing, he said: 'Alas for my laborious work — that I must do the ploughing, and this woman is afflicted with a tumor! So let the lives of both of us go to the netherworld. I must always do two tasks — ploughing and extracting the tumor. Why then should I be the ploughman of this <s>Śūrapāla</s>?'

children.text: START Suk 38:
children.translated_text: Beginning of the thirty-eighth tale of the <s>Śukasaptati</s>:

children.text:
aparedyuryāminīsamaye prabhāvatī gamanāya śukaṃ papraccha /
śukaḥ-
children.translated_text: On the next day, at nighttime, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked the parrot for permission to go. The parrot [said] —

children.text: vāñchitaṃ kartukāmānāṃ nāntarāyaṃ kṛśodari /
children.translated_text: "For those who desire to act as they wish, there is no obstacle, O slender-waisted one,

children.text: yadi kartuṃ vijānāsi yathā vipraḥ priyaṃvadaḥ // Suk_38.1 (=188) //
children.translated_text: If you know how to act like the brahmin <s>Priyaṃvada</s>." // Suk_38.1 (=188) //

children.text:
prabhāvatī papraccha-kathametat? śukaḥ-purābhūd devi? priyaṃvado nāma vipraḥ pathikaḥ /
ekadā mārge gacchansudarśanagrāme kasyacidvaṇijo gṛhaṃ yayau /
tatpatnī ca puṃścalī /
sa ca brāhmaṇastāṃ dṛṣṭvā ātmānaṃ susthānakṛtavāsakaṃ mene /
sa ca rātrau sakāmastāṃ prārthayāmāsa /
aṅgulīyakadānena ca haṭṭamārgaṃ vaṇiksute gate reme tayā samam /
prātaḥ so 'ṅgulīyakaṃ yācate /
sā nārpayati /
anena vidhinā dattamaṅgulīyakaṃ sa kathaṃ gṛhṇātu-iti praśnaḥ /
uttaram-yadā tu yācitā na dadāti tadā sa brāhmaṇaḥ khaṭvācaraṇaṃ gṛhītvā vaṇijaḥ sannidhiṃ yayau /
khaṭvācaraṇaṃ darśayitvā phūtkṛtam /
vaṇik prāha-bho dvijaḥ! kimetat? sa āha-bhagne 'smintvadīyabhāryayā madīyamagulīyakaṃ jagṛhe /
sa ca vaṇik tadvacanaṃ śrutvā kupito bhāryāmāha-anena pramādena asmadgṛhe ko 'pi pathiko na sameṣyati /
ityuktvā niṣṭhuraṃ vacastatkuṇḍāduttīrya aṅgulīyakaṃ pathikāya samarpitam /
sa ca yathāgataṃ yayau /
iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text: <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked: "How is this [to be understood]?" The parrot [said]: Once upon a time, O queen, there was a brahmin traveler named <s>Priyaṃvada</s>. One day, while traveling, he went to the house of a certain merchant in a village called <s>Sudarśana</s>. The merchant's wife was an unchaste woman. The brahmin, seeing her, considered himself well-lodged. At night, being desirous, he solicited her. Having given a ring, when the merchant's son had gone to the market-road, he enjoyed her. In the morning, he asked for the ring back. She would not return it. 'How shall he recover the ring given in this manner?' — this is the question. The answer: When, though asked, she would not give it back, the brahmin seized a leg of the cot and went to the merchant's presence. Showing the cot-leg, he blew upon it [as if inspecting it]. The merchant said: 'O brahmin! What is this?' He said: 'When this [leg] broke, your wife took my ring [as collateral].' The merchant, hearing those words, angrily said to his wife: 'Because of this carelessness, no traveler will ever come to our house again!' Having said these harsh words, she took the ring out of her box and gave it to the traveler. And he departed as he had come. Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau aṣṭatriṃśattamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the thirty-eighth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s>.

children.text: START Suk 39:
children.translated_text: Beginning of the thirty-ninth tale of the <s>Śukasaptati</s>:

children.text:
apare 'hni sandhyāsamaye puruṣāntaragamanāya prabhāvatī śukaṃ pṛcchati sma-he śuka! ahaṃ gamiṣyāmi /
śukaḥ prāha-
children.translated_text: On the next day, at twilight, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked the parrot for permission to go to another man: "O parrot! I shall go." The parrot said —

children.text: vraja devi! varaṃ yānaṃ tvaṃ bhoktuṃ subhagaṃ naram /
children.translated_text: "Go, O queen! Going is excellent, for you to enjoy a handsome man,

children.text: vaktuṃ cedviṣame vetsi tulāgrāhīva bhāmini // Suk_39.1 (=189) //
children.translated_text: If you know how to speak in a difficult situation, like the balance-holder, O fair one." // Suk_39.1 (=189) //

children.text: prabhāvatī prāha-"kathametat?
children.translated_text: <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked: "How is this [to be understood]?"

children.text: kastulāgrāhakaḥ kīra! gṛhītā ca tulā kutaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Who is the balance-holder, O parrot? Where was the balance seized?

children.text: viṣamaṃ ca kimāyātaṃ kathāṃ kathaya śobhanām // Suk_39.2 (=190) //
children.translated_text: And what was the difficult situation? Tell me the beautiful tale." // Suk_39.2 (=190) //

children.text:
astyatra kuṇḍinaṃ nāma nagaram /
tatra bhūdharo nāma vaṇikpuṇyakṣayātkṣīṇadhano janaistyaktaḥ /
uktañca-
children.translated_text: "There is a city called <s>Kuṇḍina</s>. There, a merchant named <s>Bhūdhara</s>, his wealth exhausted through the depletion of merit, was abandoned by people. And it is said —

children.text: vidvāndhanī dhanī dātā dhanī sādhurguṇāgraṇīḥ /
children.translated_text: A wealthy man is learned, a wealthy man is generous, a wealthy man is virtuous and foremost in qualities;

children.text: sarvabandhurdhanī pujyo dhanahīno gataprabhaḥ // Suk_39.3 (=191) //
children.translated_text: A wealthy man is everyone's kinsman, a wealthy man is honored — one bereft of wealth is bereft of radiance. // Suk_39.3 (=191) //

children.text:
yadā tu sa tulāmātradhano 'bhavattadānyavaṇiggṛhe tulāṃ muktvā deśāntaraṃ gataḥ /
tatra dhanamarjayitvā nijanagaramāgatya taṃ vaṇijaṃ tulāṃ yayāce /
vaṇikpārśvāttulā na labdhā /
tulāyāṃ tu lubdho vaṇikmūrkha uttaraṃ cakre yattvadīyā tulā mūṣikairbhakṣiteti śrutvā bhūdharastūṣṇīṃ sthitaḥ /
sa ca ekadā tasya veśmani bhojanāya gataḥ krīḍantaṃ bālakaṃ dṛṣṭvā pracchannaṃ gṛhītvā nijagṛhaṃ yayau /
bālakapitā ca duḥkhapūritāṅgo ruroda sakuṭumbaḥ /
tañca rudantaṃ dṛṣṭvā prativeśmiko jagāda-re tvadīyaḥ suto bhūdhareṇa gṛhītaḥ /
tato 'sau tadgṛhaṃ gatvā bhūdharātsutaṃ yācitavān /
bhūdhareṇoktam-mitra! tvatputro matsaṃge snānārthe nadītīre gatastatra śyenenāpahṛtaḥ /
iti śrutvā tena vaṇijā rājakule gatvā putraharaṇavṛttānto niveditaḥ /
bhūdharo 'pi rājakulaṃ yayau /
tatkathaya sa bālahartā kathaṃ mucyatāmiti-praśnaḥ /
śukaḥ yadā bhūdharo rājasamakṣaṃ mantriṇā pṛṣṭastadā evaṃ jagāda-
children.translated_text: When he had nothing left but a balance, he deposited the balance at another merchant's house and went abroad. Having earned wealth there, he returned to his own city and asked that merchant for the balance. The balance was not returned by the merchant. The greedy, foolish merchant gave this answer: 'Your balance has been eaten by mice.' Hearing this, <s>Bhūdhara</s> remained silent. One day, having gone to that man's house for a meal, seeing his boy playing, he secretly took the child and went to his own house. The boy's father, his body filled with grief, wept together with his family. Seeing him weeping, a neighbor said: 'Sir, your son has been taken by <s>Bhūdhara</s>.' Then he went to <s>Bhūdhara</s>'s house and asked for his son back. <s>Bhūdhara</s> said: 'Friend! Your son went with me to the riverbank for bathing, and there a hawk carried him off.' Hearing this, the merchant went to the royal court and reported the incident of the child's abduction. <s>Bhūdhara</s> also went to the royal court. 'Tell how the child-abductor shall be freed' — this is the question. The parrot [said]: When <s>Bhūdhara</s> was questioned by the minister before the king, he spoke thus —

children.text: tulāṃ lohamayīṃ yatra khādante deva! mūṣakāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Where mice devour an iron balance, O lord,

children.text: gajaṃ tatra haret śyeno dārake ko 'tra vismayaḥ // Suk_39.4 (=192) //
children.translated_text: There a hawk may carry off an elephant — what wonder then about a boy?" // Suk_39.4 (=192) //

children.text:
śrutvaitadvacanaṃ mantriṇoktam-yadāyaṃ dhūrtastava tulāṃ samarpayati tadā dārako 'pi dātavyo nānyathā /
tena dārakaḥ samarpitaḥ /
tulāgrāhī daṇḍitaḥ san tulāṃ samarpayāmāsa /
iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text: Having heard these words, the minister said: 'When this cheat returns your balance to you, then the boy too shall be given back — not otherwise.' The boy was returned. The balance-seizer, being punished, surrendered the balance. Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau ekonacatvāriṃśattamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the thirty-ninth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s>.

children.text: START Suk 40:
children.translated_text: Beginning of the fortieth tale of the <s>Śukasaptati</s>:

children.text:
anyedyuḥ sā prabhāvatī gamanāya śukaṃ pṛcchati sma /
śukaḥ-
children.translated_text: On the next day, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked the parrot for permission to go. The parrot [said] —

children.text: gaccha tvaṃ gantukāmānāṃ gamanaṃ ca śubhaṃ bhuvi /
children.translated_text: "Go, for the going of those who wish to go is auspicious in this world,

children.text: subiddhiriva cedvaktuṃ vijānāsi kṛtākṛtām // Suk_40.1 (=193) //
children.translated_text: If you know how to speak of what is done and undone, like <s>Subuddhi</s>." // Suk_40.1 (=193) //

children.text:
prabhāvatyāha-kathametat? śukaḥ-nagarābhighe pattane subuddhi- kubuddhiśceti mitradvayaṃ jane prasiddham /
anyadā subuddhirdeśāntaraṃ yayau /
kubuddhistu mitrastriyaṃ yayau /
subuddhiśca dhanamarjayitvā deśāntarātsamāgataḥ /
tataḥ kubuddhiḥ subuddheḥ kapaṭasnehaṃ darśayati /
subuddhināpi sammānitaḥ /
kubuddhistaṃ pratyāha-bhavatā kvāpi kiñcitkautukaṃ dṛṣṭam? tenoktam-sarasvatīnadītīre kūpamadhye taramāṇamakālajamāmraphalaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ manoramanāmini grāme /
kubuddhirāha-mithyedam /
subuddhirāha-satyametat /
tenoktam-yadi satyaṃ bhavati tadā yadasmadgṛhe dvābhyāṃ hastābhyāṃ grahītuṃ śakyate tattvayā grāhyam /
alīke tvadīyagṛhādahaṃ gṛhṇāmi /
iti paṇbandhaṃ kṛtvā kubuddhī rātrau kūpāttatphalaṃ jagrāha /
phalābhāve tu subuddhinā haritam /
atha sa tadbhāryāṃ grahītukāmaḥ paṇabandhaṃ yācate /
tadatra subuddhirnijabhāryārakṣaṇe kamupāyaṃ karotviti praśnaḥ /
uttaraṃ śuka āha-subuddhistaṃ duṣṭāśayaṃ jñātvā nijagṛhavastujātaṃ nijakalatraṃ ca prāsādopari kṣiptvā /
ārohaṇikāṃ pātayāmāsa /
kubuddhiḥ samāyātaḥ /
subuddhirāha-evaṃ yadrocate tadasmadgṛhād gṛhyatām /
sa ca kalatrāharaṇāya niḥśreṇikāṃ dvābhyāṃ hastābhyāṃ jagrāha /
tadā subuddhinoktam-mayaivaṃ pūrvaṃ gaditañca yad dvābhyāṃ hastābhyāṃ grahīṣyase tava tadave nānyat /
tataḥ kubuddhirvilakṣo bhūtvā bahiryayau /
janaiśca ninditaḥ /
iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text: <s>Prabhāvatī</s> says: 'How is this [to be understood]?' The parrot [says]: In a town near the city, a pair of friends named <s>Subuddhi</s> (Good-Wit) and <s>Kubuddhi</s> (Bad-Wit) were well known among the people. Once, <s>Subuddhi</s> went to a foreign land. <s>Kubuddhi</s>, however, went to his friend's wife. <s>Subuddhi</s>, having earned wealth, returned from abroad. Then <s>Kubuddhi</s> showed deceitful affection toward <s>Subuddhi</s>, and <s>Subuddhi</s> also honored him. <s>Kubuddhi</s> said to him: 'Did you see anything remarkable anywhere?' He replied: 'On the bank of the <s>Sarasvatī</s> river, I saw an out-of-season mango fruit ripening inside a well, in a village called <s>Manorama</s>.' <s>Kubuddhi</s> said: 'This is false.' <s>Subuddhi</s> said: 'This is true.' [<s>Kubuddhi</s>] said: 'If it is true, then you must take whatever in our house can be grasped with both hands. If it is false, I shall take from your house.' Having made this wager, <s>Kubuddhi</s> took the fruit from the well at night. In the absence of the fruit, <s>Subuddhi</s> lost. Then [<s>Kubuddhi</s>], desiring to seize his wife, demands [fulfillment of] the wager. Here, the question is: what stratagem should <s>Subuddhi</s> employ to protect his own wife? The parrot gives the answer: <s>Subuddhi</s>, knowing his evil intention, threw all his household goods and his wife up onto the upper story of his house, and pulled away the ladder. <s>Kubuddhi</s> arrived. <s>Subuddhi</s> said: 'Very well, take whatever you like from our house.' And he, in order to seize the wife, grasped the ladder with both hands. Then <s>Subuddhi</s> said: 'I stated earlier that whatever you grasp with both hands is yours — that [ladder] alone, nothing else.' Then <s>Kubuddhi</s>, abashed, went out and was mocked by the people. Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau catvāriṃśattamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fortieth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s>.

children.text: START Suk 41:
children.translated_text: Beginning of the forty-first tale of the <s>Śukasaptati</s>:

children.text:
anyadā vaṇigvadhūḥ prāha-kīra! yadi tvaṃ manyase tadā gacchāmi /
śukaḥ prāha--
children.translated_text: On another day, the merchant's wife says: 'O parrot, if you approve, then I shall go.' The parrot says —

children.text: yuktaṃ te gamanaṃ devi yadi tatra gatā satī /
children.translated_text: 'Your going is fitting, O queen, if having gone there,

children.text: saṅkaṭe khalu vetsi tvaṃ kiñcidvaktuṃ dvijo yathā // Suk_41.1 (=194) //
children.translated_text: You know, in difficulty, how to say something [clever], like the brahmin.'

children.text:
prabhāvatī prāha-"kathametat'? śukaḥ-asti pañcapuraṃ nāma nagaram /
tatra śatrumardano nāma rājā /
tatsutāyā madanarekhāyā gale granthirbabhūva /
vaidyairasādhyetyuktvā parityaktā tato rājñā ḍiṇḍimāghoṣaṇaṃ kāritaṃ yathā yaḥ ko 'pi matsutāṃ gatarogāṃ karoti tamahaṃ dāridryarahita karomīti śrutvā paragrāmādāgatayā kayāciddvijabhāryayā ḍiṇḍimaḥ spṛṣṭaḥ /
tasminpṛṣṭe tayoktam-yanmama patirmāntrikaḥ /
sa rājasutā praguṇāṃ vidhāsyati /
tato rājapuruṣaiḥ samānītaḥ /
tasya ca nīyamānasya bhāryā jagāda-"nātha! gaccha nagaram /
rājasutāyāṃ praguṇīkṛtāyāṃ tava bahu phalaṃ bhāvi /
sa ca maṇḍalopaviṣṭo mantrādikamajānam kathaṃ bhavatviti praśnaḥ /
śuka uttaraṃ prāha-sa māntrika ācāryavistāraṃ kṛtvā mantramityuccārayāmāsa /
children.translated_text: <s>Prabhāvatī</s> says: 'How is this [to be understood]?' The parrot [says]: There is a city called <s>Pañcapura</s>. There [rules] a king named <s>Śatrumardhana</s>. His daughter <s>Madanarekhā</s> developed a lump in her throat. The physicians, saying it was incurable, abandoned [her]. Then the king had a drum-proclamation made: 'Whoever cures my daughter of her disease, I shall make him free from poverty.' Hearing this, a brahmin's wife who had come from another village touched the drum [signaling she could help]. When questioned, she said: 'My husband is a healer. He will cure the princess.'
