Then [the husband] was brought by the king's men. And as he was being led away, his wife said: 'Go to the city, my lord. When the princess is cured, you shall receive a great reward.' But he, seated in the healing circle, not knowing any <s>mantras</s> or such — how should it turn out? This is the question. The parrot gives the answer: That healer, having made an elaborate show like a master, uttered [the following] as a <s>mantra</s>:

children.text: hauṃ jīvaṇu jāṇauṃ kāiṃ caḍuḍai vāvai sāiṃ /
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] 'I know life — what is being ground and what is being wasted;

children.text: ghalliu bambhaṇi vīsāsu paiṃ bhuñjasu sukaasu hāiṃ // Suk_41.2 (=195) //
children.translated_text: Go home, O brahmin woman, rest, serve your husband, and thus be happy.'

children.text: [ahaṃ jīvanaṃ jānāmi kim tat piṣyate vihīyate /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit chāyā:] 'I know life — what is being crushed and what is being lost;

children.text: vaṇaṃ iha ākhuriadantappahasantaaṃ /

children.translated_text: Somewhere adorned with sandalwood and <s>agaru</s> trees.'

children.text: dīhaghaṇavāsa jalīrhi aikhohiaṃ /

children.text:
ityevaṃ bāhmaṇasya vadato rājaputryā hasitam /
hāsyatirekeṇa galagrandhirdvidhā babhūva /
dvidhā jāte ca tasmin rājasutāyāḥ sukhamutpannam /
nṛpeṇa ca kṛtārthīkṛto vipraḥ svasadana gataḥ /
iti kathāṃ śrutvo prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text: Thus, as the brahmin spoke, the princess laughed. By the excess of laughter, the throat-lump split in two. When it split, the princess found relief. The brahmin, his purpose fulfilled by the king, went to his own home. Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau ekacatvāriṃśattamo kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the forty-first tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s>.

children.text: START Suk 42:
children.translated_text: Beginning of the forty-second tale of the <s>Śukasaptati</s>:

children.text: arepadyuḥ prabhāvatī "gacchāmī"ti śukaṃ pratyāha /
śukaḥ-
children.translated_text: The parrot [says] —

children.text: sukhopabhogaḥ saṃsāre sāraṃ sarvāṅgasundari /
children.translated_text: 'The enjoyment of pleasure is the essence of worldly life, O woman beautiful in every limb;

children.text: vraja cedvyāghramārīva vetsi vaktuṃ tvamuttaram // Suk_42.1 (=208) //
children.translated_text: Go, if like the tiger-slayer woman, you know how to speak an answer [in danger].'
The next day, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> says to the parrot: 'I am going.'

children.text:
tacchrutvā prabhāvatyāha-"sukhopabhogaḥ saṃsāre kora! kathāṃ kathaya" /
śukaḥ kathāṃ prāha- asti deulākhyo grāmaḥ /
tatra rājasiṃho nāma rājaputraḥ tadbhāryā kalahapriyeti viśrutā /
sānyadā bhartrā sārdhaṃ kalahaṃ vidhāya putradvayopetā piturgṛhaṃ prati calitā /
sā ca kopavaśātpattanāni bahūni vanāni ca bahūnyatikramya gatā malayapāśvasthaṃ mahākānanam /
tacca kathaṃ bhūtam /
children.translated_text: Hearing this, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> says: 'The enjoyment of pleasure is the essence of worldly life, O parrot! Tell the tale.' The parrot tells the tale: There is a village called <s>Deula</s>. There [lives] a prince named <s>Rājasiṃha</s>. His wife was known as <s>Kalahapriyā</s> (Quarrel-Lover). Once, having quarreled with her husband, she set off for her father's house along with her two sons. In her rage, she traversed many towns and many forests and arrived at a great wilderness on the slopes of the <s>Malaya</s> [mountains]. And what was that [forest] like?

children.text: candaṇasattacchaāsaṇṇaaṃ saralavaratuṅgatarusāhasaṃchaṇṇaaṃ /
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] 'Bound with seven-leaved sandalwood, covered by the branches of tall and noble <s>sarala</s> (pine) trees,

children.text: kahiṃ pi sahaārakhajjūriaṃ phaṇasaa mattālivihaṅgabhāriaṃ // Suk_42.2 (=209) //
children.translated_text: Somewhere with <s>sahakāra</s> (grafted mango) and date palms, filled with intoxicated birds [hovering around] jackfruit [trees].'

children.text: [candanasaptacchadasannaddhaṃ saralavaratuṅgataruśākhāsaṃcchannam /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit chāyā:] 'Bound with seven-leaved sandalwood, covered by the branches of tall and noble <s>sarala</s> trees,

children.text: kvāpi sahakārakharjūrikaṃ panase mattālivihaṅgabharitam] // Suk_42.2* (=209*) //
children.translated_text: Somewhere with <s>sahakāra</s> and date palms, filled with intoxicated birds [hovering around] jackfruit.'

children.text: kahiṃ pi selupīluphapūriantaaṃ sarasavorabahutintaḍīchaṇṇaaṃ dāḍimīphalabillaphalasugandhivāaaṃ // Suk_42.3 (=210) //
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] 'Somewhere with its interior filled with <s>selu</s> and <s>pīlu</s> trees, covered with abundant fresh <s>tintiḍī</s> (tamarind) [branches], with winds bearing the fragrance of pomegranate and <s>bilva</s> (wood-apple) fruits.'

children.text: kvāpi selupīlūprapūritāntaraṃ sarasabadarabahutintiḍīcchannam dāḍimīphalabilvaphalasugandhivātakam
children.translated_text: Sanskrit chāyā:
'Somewhere with its interior filled with <s>selu</s> and <s>pīlu</s>, covered by abundant fresh <s>tintiḍī</s>, carrying the scent of pomegranate and <s>bilva</s> fruits.'

children.text:
evaṃvidhe gahane gatā sā kalahapriyā vyāghraṃ dadarśa /
sa ca vyāghrastava saputrāṃ dṛṣṭvā pucchena bhūmimāhatya dhāvitaḥ /
tataḥ sā kathaṃ bhavatu? iti praśnaḥ /
uttaraṃ śukaḥ prāha-sā vyāghramāgacchamānaṃ dṛṣṭvā ghārṣṭyāt putrau capeṭayā hatvā iti jagāda- kathamekaikaśo vyāghrabhakṣaṇāya kalahaṃ kuruthaḥ /
ayamekastāvadvibhajya bhujyatām /
paścādanyo dvitīyaḥ kaścillakṣyate /
iti śrutvā vyāghramārī kācidiyamiti matvā vyāghro bhayākulacitto naṣṭaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having gone into such a dense [forest], <s>Kalahapriyā</s> saw a tiger. That tiger, seeing her with her sons, struck the ground with its tail and charged. Then what should she do? — this is the question. The parrot gives the answer: She, seeing the tiger approaching, with boldness struck her sons with slaps and said: 'Why do you two quarrel, [each wanting] to eat a tiger one by one? Let this one first be divided and eaten. Afterward, some other second [tiger] will be found.' Hearing this, the tiger, thinking 'this is some tiger-slaying woman,' fled with a mind full of terror.

children.text: nijabuddhyā vimuktā sā bhayādvyāghrasya bhāmini /
children.translated_text: By her own wit, she was freed from the tiger's danger, O beautiful one;

children.text: anyo 'pi buddhimāṃlloke mucyate mahato bhayāt // Suk_42.4 (=211) //
children.translated_text: So too in this world, a person of intelligence is freed from great danger.

children.text: iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text: Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau dvicatvāriṃśattamo kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the forty-second tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s>.

children.text: START Suk 43:
children.translated_text: Beginning of the forty-third tale of the <s>Śukasaptati</s>:

children.text:
anyedyuḥ śukamāpṛcchati sma kāminī /
śukaḥ prāha-
children.translated_text: The next day, the amorous woman asks the parrot. The parrot says —

children.text: vraja devi na te 'yuktaṃ vrajanaṃ gajagāmini /
children.translated_text: 'Go, O queen — your going is not unfitting, O one who walks like an elephant,

children.text: vyāghramārīva buddhiste dvitīyāpi yadi sthirā // Suk_43.1 (=212) //
children.translated_text: If your intelligence, like the tiger-slayer's, is also firm in a second [test].'

children.text: prabhāvatī pṛcchati, kathametat?
children.translated_text: <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asks: 'How is this [to be understood]?'

children.text: vyāghramāryāḥ kṛtāṃ buddhiṃ dvitīyāṃ vivadādhunā /
children.translated_text: 'Now tell of the second stratagem employed by the tiger-slayer woman;

children.text: mahatkautukamatrārthe vidyate me priyaṃvada! // Suk_43.2 (=213) //
children.translated_text: There is great curiosity in this matter for me, O sweet-speaker!'

children.text: śukaḥ-
children.translated_text: The parrot [says] —

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā kānane vyāghraṃ naṣṭaṃ jātaṃ bhayākulam /
children.translated_text: 'Seeing that tiger in the forest, fled and full of fear,

children.text: mṛgadhūrto hasannāha vyāghro naṣṭaḥ kuto bhayāt // Suk_43.3 (=214) //
children.translated_text: A cunning jackal, laughing, said: "Why has the tiger fled in fear?"'

children.text:
vyāghraḥ-gaccha gaccha jambuka tvamapi kiṃñcidgūgpradeśam /
yato vyāghramārīti yā śāstre śrūyate tayāhaṃ hantumārabdhaḥ paraṃ gṛhītakarajīvito naṣṭaḥ śīghraṃ tadagrataḥ /
mṛgadhūrtaḥ-vyāghra! tvayā mahatkautukamāveditaṃ yanmāṃsapiṇḍād mānuṣādapi bibheṣi /
vyāghraḥ-pratyakṣameva mayā sātmaputrāvekaikaśo māmattuṃ kalahāyamānau capeṭayā ghnannī dṛṣṭā /
jambukaḥ-svāmin! yatrāste sā dhūrtā tatra gamyatām /
yadi vyāghra! tava tatra gatasya sā sammukhamapīkṣate tadā mama tvadīyā velā smaraṇīyā /
vyāghraḥ-śṛgāla! yadi tvaṃ māṃ muktvā yāsi tadā velāpyavelā syāt /
jambukaḥ-yadyevaṃ tahi māṃ nijagale baddhvā cala śīghram /
sa vyāghrastathā kṛtvā kānana yayau /
vyāghramāryapi prāptā putrasahitā tena jambukakṛtotsāhād vyāghrātsā kathaṃ mucyatām /
iti praśnaḥ /
śukaḥ-tayā vyāghramāryā tadā cintitaṃ yadayaṃ mṛgadhūrtenānītastasmādamumeva jambukamākṣipantyaṅgulyā tarjayantyuvāca-
children.translated_text: The tiger [said]: 'Go, go, jackal — you too go to some hiding place! For [the woman] who is known in the texts as a "tiger-slayer" — she began to kill me, and I fled having barely escaped with my life. [Go] quickly before her!' The cunning jackal [said]: 'O tiger, you have told me a great wonder — that you are afraid even of a lump of flesh, a human! The tiger [said]: 'I saw with my own eyes — she was striking her two sons with slaps, [saying they were] quarreling [over who would] eat me one by one!' The jackal [said]: 'My lord, let us go to where that crafty woman is. O tiger, if when you have gone there, she even looks at you, then my condition should be remembered by you [i.e., you may blame me].' The tiger [said]: 'O jackal, if you abandon me and flee, then that condition [guarantee] would be no condition at all.' The jackal [said]: 'If so, then tie me to your neck and go quickly.' The tiger, having done so, went into the forest. The tiger-slayer woman too arrived with her sons. How should she escape from the tiger, emboldened by the jackal? — this is the question. The parrot [says]: That tiger-slayer woman then thought: 'This one has been brought by the cunning jackal.' Therefore, pointing her finger at that very jackal and threatening [him], she said —

children.text: re re dhūrta tvayā dattaṃ mahyaṃ vyāghratrayaṃ purā /
children.translated_text: Hey, hey, rogue! You formerly gave me three tigers!

children.text: viśvasyādyaikamānīya kathaṃ yāsi vadādhunā // Suk_43.4 (=215) //
children.translated_text: Now, having brought one from the whole world, how do you go away? Tell me now! // Suk_43.4 (=215) //

children.text: ityuktvā dhāvitā tūrṇaṃ vyāghramārī bhayaṅkarā /
children.translated_text: Having said this, the fearsome tigress-slayer ran swiftly,

children.text: vyāghro 'pi sahasā naṣṭo galabaddhaśṛgālakaḥ // Suk_43.5 (=216) //
children.translated_text: And the tiger too suddenly fled, with the jackal bound to its neck. // Suk_43.5 (=216) //

children.text: nijabuddhyā punarmuktā vyāghrajād devi sā bhayāt /
children.translated_text: By her own wit, O goddess, she was freed again from the danger of the tiger;

children.text: buddhirvalavatī tanvi sarvakāryeṣu sarvadā // Suk_43.6 (=217) //
children.translated_text: Intelligence is powerful, O slender one, in all matters at all times. // Suk_43.6 (=217) //

children.text: iti kathāṃ śratvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text: Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau tricatvāriṃśattamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the forty-third tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s>.

children.text: START Suk 44:
children.translated_text: START Suk 44:

children.text:
athānyedyardināvasāne prabhāvatī śukaṃ pṛcchati /
śukaḥ-
children.translated_text: Then on another day, at the close of the day, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asks the parrot. The parrot [says] —

children.text: ātmānaṃ saṅkaṭād devi yāhi cedvetsi rakṣitum /
children.translated_text: If you know how to save yourself from danger, O goddess, then go,

children.text: yathātmā saṅkaṭāttena jambukenāpi rakṣitaḥ // Suk_44.1 (=218) //
children.translated_text: Just as that jackal too saved himself from danger. // Suk_44.1 (=218) //

children.text:
sa ca jambuko galabaddho nighṛṣṭapṛṣṭhacaraṇo galadrudhirapravāho mūmūrṣuriva deśāntaraṃ gantumicchatā vyāghramārībhayādvyāghreṇa noyate /
tato mahato 'pāyāt śṛgālaḥ kathaṃ mucyate-iti praśnaḥ /
uttaraṃ prāha śukaḥ-tatastaṃ vyāghraṃ bahunadīkānanaviṣamasamapredeśaparvatānullaṅghayantaṃ satvaraṃ dṛṣṭvā ātmānaṃ mocayitukāmaḥ śṛgālo bhṛśaṃ jahāsa pīḍito 'pi san /
vyāgreṇoktam-kathaṃ hasitam /
sa āha-deva! sā mayā vyāghramārīti dhūrtikā jñātā /
tvatprasādācca dūradeśamāgato 'haṃ jīvitaḥ /
paraṃ yadi sāsmadraktasrāvasaṃlagnā pāpinī pṛṣṭhataḥ sameti tadā kathaṃ jīvitavyam /
ato 'ha hasitaḥ /
vyāghrasvāmin! sthirībhūya vicāraya /
atha tuṣṭo vyāghrastena vākyena "tathe'tyuktvā jambukaṃ muktvā sahasā naṣṭaḥ /
śṛgālo 'pi sukhaṃ tasthau /
children.translated_text: That jackal, bound at the neck, with his back and legs scraped raw, streaming with flowing blood, as if about to die, was being carried by the tiger who wished to go to another region out of fear of the tigress-slayer. Then the question is: how does the jackal free himself from such great peril? The parrot replies: Then, seeing that tiger swiftly crossing many rivers, forests, rough terrains, and mountains, the jackal, wishing to free himself, laughed loudly despite being in pain. The tiger asked: 'Why did you laugh?' He said: 'Lord! I recognized that she was a fraud, that so-called tigress-slayer. And by your grace, having come to a distant land, I am alive. But if that wicked woman, smeared with our flowing blood, follows behind, then how shall we survive? That is why I laughed. O tiger-lord! Stand firm and consider.' Then the tiger, pleased by those words, saying 'So be it,' released the jackal and suddenly fled. The jackal too rested happily.

children.text: buddhirvaraṃ varāroha dhanamānasukhaiṣiṇām /
children.translated_text: Intelligence is supreme, O beautiful-thighed one, for those who desire wealth, honor, and happiness;

children.text: buddhihīnāḥ paraṃ kleśaṃ prāpnuvanti kṛśodari // Suk_44.2 (=219) //
children.translated_text: Those devoid of intelligence attain only great suffering, O slender-waisted one. // Suk_44.2 (=219) //

children.text: balaṃ prajñāvihīnasya parakāryāya kevalam /
children.translated_text: The strength of one devoid of wisdom serves only the purposes of others,

children.text: girikūṭopamāṅgasya kuñjarasyeva dṛśyate // Suk_44.3 (=220) //
children.translated_text: As is seen in the case of an elephant whose limbs are massive as mountain peaks. // Suk_44.3 (=220) //

children.text: iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī śukavākyavismitā suptā /
children.translated_text: Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s>, amazed by the parrot's words, fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau catuścatvāriṃśattamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the forty-fourth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s>.

children.text: START Suk 45:
children.translated_text: START Suk 45:

children.text:
anyedyuḥ sā kāminī sandhyāyāṃ śukaṃ papraccha-"gamiṣyāmī'ti /
śukaḥ prāha--
children.translated_text: On the next day, that amorous woman at twilight asked the parrot: 'I shall go.' The parrot said —

children.text: samayojyaṃ priyaṃ bhoktuṃ tava bhāmini samprati /
children.translated_text: It is time for you to enjoy your lover now, O beautiful one;

children.text: vañcitā vetsi cetkartuṃ kiñcidviṣṇuḥ purā yathā // Suk_45.1 (=221) //
children.translated_text: If you know how to act when deceived, as <s>Viṣṇu</s> did formerly. // Suk_45.1 (=221) //

children.text:
prabhāvatyāha--"kathametat' /
śukaḥ prāha-asti vilāsapuraṃ nāma nagaram /
tatra arindamo nāma rājā /
tatra ca viṣṇunāmā brāhmaṇo ratilolupaḥ kuṭumbavarjito ratikarmaṇi sarvanārīduḥsaha iti nagare prasiddho babhūva /
veśyābhirapi na śakyate jetuṃ kimpunaḥ kulāṅganābhiḥ /
tatra ratipriyā nāma gaṇikā /
atha sā ṣoḍaśa drammān gṛhītvā tamājuhāva /
tamāyāntaṃ dṛṣṭvā sā cāṭūktibhiḥ paricaryāṃ cakāra /
so 'pi cānyakāryanivṛttastasminneva ratikarmaṇi dattamanāstāṃ rantu jetumārebhe /
tayā ca sa ratilolupaḥ dravyārthaṃ vā parājayārthaṃ vā praharadvayaṃ yāvatsoḍhaḥ /
niśīthe cādhobhūmikāmāgatya kuṭṭinyagrato niveditaṃ "yadduḥsaho 'yaṃ dvijaḥ /
paṇabandhaṃ samarpayitvā tamutkālaya /
mayi jīvantyāṃ prāgeva bāhulyaṃ bhaviṣyati' /
kuṭṭinyāha-"asmadgṛhe na ko 'pi kāmuko gaṇikāṃ jitvā paṇabandhaṃ jagrāha /
tato 'hamenaṃ yāvatprapañcena niḥsārayāmi tāvatsoḍhavya iti /
yadā cāhaṃ pippalamāruhya sūrpadvayena pakṣaśabdaṃ kukkuṭadhvaniṃ vidadhāni tadā vibhātamiti kṛtvā niḥsāraṇayaḥ'-ityuktvā preṣitoparibhūmau gaṇikā /
yathoktaṃ ca kuṭṭinyā tāvatkṛtam /
tasminkṛte vibhātamiti kṛtvā niḥsārito dvijaḥ /
yāvad gṛhadvarastho vyomamālokayate tadopari niśīthovartate /
tadā sa vipraḥ kuṭṭinīparājito janamadhye parājayaṃ kathaṃ vahatu-iti praśnaḥ /
śukaḥ-yadā vipraḥ kukkuṭadhvanisthānamavalokayati tāvatsūrpadvayayutāṃ kuṭṭinīṃ dadarśa /
tena ca sā loṣṭenāhatya bhūmau pātitā pramādajanaiśca dhikkṛtā /
sa ca brāhmaṇo grahaṇakaṃ dviguṇaṃ gṛhītvā puramadhye gaṇikāṃ vinindya /
svagṛhaṃ yayau /
children.translated_text: <s>Prabhāvatī</s> said: 'How is this [to be understood]?' The parrot said: There is a city called <s>Vilāsapura</s>. There [rules] a king named <s>Arindama</s>. And there [lives] a brahmin named <s>Viṣṇu</s>, lustful for love-making, without family, who became famous in the city as one unbearable to all women in the art of love. Even courtesans could not defeat him, let alone women of good family. There [lives] a courtesan named <s>Ratipriyā</s>. She, having taken sixteen <s>drammas</s> (coins), invited him. Seeing him arrive, she attended to him with flattering words. And he, having set aside all other business and fixing his mind solely on love-making, began to sport with her in order to defeat her. And she endured that lustful man for two watches — whether for the sake of money or for the sake of [his] defeat. At midnight, having come to the ground floor, she informed the bawd: 'This brahmin is unbearable. Give him back the wager-money and expel him. While I am alive, it will only get worse hereafter.' The bawd said: 'In our house, no lover has ever defeated a courtesan and taken the wager-money. Therefore, I shall contrive to get him out; until then, endure it.' 'When I climb the <s>pippala</s> (fig) tree and make the sound of wings with two winnowing fans and the cry of a rooster, then thinking it is dawn, he is to be sent out' — having said this, she sent the courtesan back upstairs. And the bawd did just as instructed. When that was done, thinking it was dawn, the brahmin was sent out. As he stood at the door and looked up at the sky, it was still the middle of the night. Then the question is: how does the brahmin, defeated by the bawd, bear his defeat among the people? The parrot [says]: When the brahmin looked toward the source of the rooster's cry, he saw the bawd with the two winnowing fans. He struck her with a clod of earth and knocked her to the ground, and she was reviled by the prostitutes. And that brahmin, having taken double the wager, denounced the courtesan throughout the city and went to his own home.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau pañcacatvāriṃśattamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the forty-fifth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s>.

children.text: START Suk 46:
children.translated_text: START Suk 46:

children.text:
athānyedyuḥ prabhāvatī śukaṃ pṛcchati /
śukaḥ-
children.translated_text: Then on the next day, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asks the parrot. The parrot [says] —

children.text: yāhi devi gṛhaṃ muktvā yadi vetsi tvamuttaram /
children.translated_text: Go, O goddess, leaving home, if you know the answer,

children.text: yathā karagarānāthaḥ kṛtavānbhūtanigrahe // Suk_46.1 (=222) //
children.translated_text: As <s>Karagarā</s>'s husband accomplished in subduing the ghost. // Suk_46.1 (=222) //

children.text:
asti devi vatsomaṃ nāma nagaram /
tatra vidvāndaridro brāhmaṇaḥ /
tasya priyā ca karagarābhidhānā yathārthanāmno sarvajantūdvegakāriṇī, yattaddvāradeśavṛkṣasthito bhūtastasyāḥ karagarāyā bhayātpalāyyāṭavyāṃ gataḥ /
brāhmaṇo 'pi tasyā udvegāddeśāntarābhimukho 'bhūt /
so 'pi ca tena bhūtena dṛṣṭo jalpitaśca mārgaśrāntastvam /
tena tvayādya mamātithinā bhāvyam /
vipreṇa bhīruṇoktam-yadātithyaṃ karoṣi tadvidhehi śīghram /
bhūtenoktam-na tvayā bhetavyam /
tvaṃ mama svāmī yato 'haṃ tvadgṛhadvāravṛkṣastho bhūtaḥ karagarābhayenehāgataḥ /
tatastava nijasvāminī guṇavadupakartavyameva /
tasmāttvaṃ dvija mṛgāvatīṃ rājadhānīṃ madanabhūpatisanāthāṃ gaccha /
tatra cāhaṃ tatputrīṃ mṛgalocanāṃ grahīṣye /
sā cānyairmantrikairnorujā na bhaviṣyati /
tattvayi samāgate tava darśanādevāhaṃ tyakṣyāmi /
tataḥ paraṃ tu mantravādo na vidheyaḥ /
iti bhaṇitvā so 'pi bhūto gatvā tāṃ rājaputrīṃ jagrāha /
vipro 'pi tatra yayau /
tena ca ḍiṇḍimaḥ spṛṣṭaḥ /
tato rājakulaṃ gato vipra ācāryavistaraṃ vidadhe /
bhūta ācāryavistaraṃ yāvannamuñcati tāvatkiṃ karotviti praśnaḥ /
śuka-bhūtagrahe 'nivartite vipreṇoktam-
children.translated_text: There is, O goddess, a city called <s>Vatsoma</s>. There [lives] a learned but poor brahmin. His wife, named <s>Karagarā</s>, true to her name, caused distress to all creatures — so much so that a ghost stationed at a tree near her doorway fled to the forest out of fear of <s>Karagarā</s>. The brahmin too, out of distress from her, set out for another land. He was seen by that ghost, who spoke to him: 'You are weary from the road. Therefore today you must be my guest.' The timid brahmin said: 'If you wish to offer hospitality, do so quickly.' The ghost said: 'You need not fear. You are my master, for I am the ghost who was stationed at the tree by your door — I came here out of fear of <s>Karagarā</s>. Therefore, something beneficial must be done for your own mistress. So, O brahmin, go to the royal capital <s>Mṛgāvatī</s>, governed by King <s>Madana</s>. There I shall possess his daughter <s>Mṛgalocanā</s>. She will not be cured by any other exorcists. But when you arrive, at the mere sight of you, I shall leave her. After that, however, no incantation should be performed.' Having said this, the ghost went and possessed that princess. The brahmin too went there. And he beat a drum [to announce himself]. Then, having gone to the royal court, the brahmin made elaborate preparations for an exorcism. The question is: when the ghost does not leave despite the elaborate exorcism, what should he do? The parrot [says]: When the ghost-possession did not relent, the brahmin said —

children.text: karagaraṇāhau āiau bhūa eu vīsasiu ṭhiu dhutta /
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] O husband of <s>Karagarā</s>, I came here; O ghost, you stood here trusting, O rogue!

children.text: āpiṇi boliu saṃbhari re kūḍauṃ kiṃ maiṃ deva jutta // Suk_46.2 (=223) //
children.translated_text: Remember your own promise — hey, false one, is this deception proper toward me? // Suk_46.2 (=223) //

children.text: [karagarānātho 'hamāgatya bhūta iha viśvasya sthito dhūrta /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit chāyā:] 'I, the husband of <s>Karagarā</s>, have come; O ghost, you stood here trusting, O rogue!

children.text: ātmano vacanaṃ saṃbhṛhi re kūṭakaṃ kiṃ mayi deva yuktam] // Suk_46.2* (=223*) //
children.translated_text: Remember your own word — hey, deceitful one, is this trickery fitting toward me?' // Suk_46.2* (=223*) //

children.text: uktañca-
children.translated_text: And it is said —

children.text: manuṣyāḥ sukulotpannā api ca brahmacārimaḥ /
children.translated_text: Humans born of good family, and even celibates,

children.text: na bhavanti mṛṣāvācaḥ kiṃ punardevayonayaḥ // Suk_46.3 (=224) //
children.translated_text: Do not speak falsehood — how much less those born of divine origin! // Suk_46.3 (=224) //

children.text:
tato bhūtaḥ tyaktvā jagāma /
iyaṃ muktetyuktvā brāhmaṇāya rājñā sutāḥ rājyārdhañca pradattam /
vipro 'pi pūrṇamanoratho jagāma /
iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text: Then the ghost departed, having left [her]. Saying 'She is freed,' the king gave his daughter and half the kingdom to the brahmin. The brahmin too, his desires fulfilled, went on his way. Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau ṣaṭcatvāriṃśattamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the forty-sixth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s>.

children.text: START Suk 47:
children.translated_text: START Suk 47:

children.text:
dinamativāhya prabhāvatī śukaṃ pṛcchati /
śukaḥ-
children.translated_text: Having passed the day, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asks the parrot. The parrot [says] —

children.text: gaccha devi gatā vetsi yadi kartuṃ tvamuttaram /
children.translated_text: Go, O goddess, if you know how to give the answer,

children.text: yathā karagarānāthaḥ kṛtavānbhūtasaṅkaṭe // Suk_47.1 (=225) //
children.translated_text: As <s>Karagarā</s>'s husband accomplished when in danger from the ghost. // Suk_47.1 (=225) //

children.text:
sa karagarāpatiḥ rājakanyayā saha rājalakṣmīṃ bhuṅkte /
atrāntare sa bhūtaḥ karṇāvatīṃ gatvā rājño bhāryāṃ sulocanāṃ jagrāha /
sā madanasya pitṛṣvasā /
sā cātyarthaṃ pīḍitā jīvitaśeṣābhūt /
sāpi śatrughnanarapaterbhāryā mātṛrājye keśavamāntrikamākārayāmāsa /
sa ca nijadūtāpreṣayitvā keśavo 'pi rājñā priyavākyaiḥ prahito 'pyagantukāmukaḥ /
tadā sa karagarāpatirbhāryānurodhato jagāma /
tatra gataḥ sanmānito mahībhujā śatrughnena gataḥ sulocanāveśmani /
sa ca bhūtastamāyāntaṃ dṛṣṭvā paruṣairvākyaistarjayannityāha-"mayā pratipannamekadeśe kṛtam /
adhunā tu vipra tvayā ātmā rakṣaṇīyaḥ' /
sa ca dvijo na mantraṃ na tantraṃ vijānāti /
kathaṃ bhavatviti praśnaḥ /
śukaḥ- tadā taṃ bhūtaṃ jñātvā kālavedī kṛtāñjalirbhūtvā tatkarṇamāśrityeti jagāda dvijaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Karagarā</s>'s husband enjoys royal fortune with the princess. Meanwhile, that ghost, having gone to <s>Karṇāvatī</s>, possessed the king's wife <s>Sulocanā</s>. She was <s>Madana</s>'s paternal aunt. She was tormented exceedingly and was barely clinging to life. She, being the wife of King <s>Śatrughna</s>, in her maternal kingdom summoned the exorcist <s>Keśava</s>. But even when <s>Keśava</s>, having sent his own messengers and being urged by the king with kind words, was still unwilling to come. Then <s>Karagarā</s>'s husband went, at his wife's insistence. Having arrived there and been honored by King <s>Śatrughna</s>, he went to <s>Sulocanā</s>'s quarters. That ghost, seeing him arrive, threatening with harsh words, said: 'I fulfilled my promise in one instance. But now, O brahmin, you must protect yourself.' And that brahmin knew neither <s>mantra</s> (incantation) nor <s>tantra</s> (ritual method). The question is: what should he do? The parrot [says]: Then, recognizing the ghost and knowing the right moment, he joined his palms, approached its ear, and the brahmin whispered —

children.text: prāptā karagarā bhūta pṛṣṭhalagnātra me 'dhunā /
children.translated_text: '<s>Karagarā</s> has arrived, O ghost, clinging to my back, here, now;

children.text: yadbhartā cātra samprāptastadvyākhyātumihāgataḥ // Suk_47.2 (=226) //
children.translated_text: That her husband has arrived here — she has come to announce that.' // Suk_47.2 (=226) //

children.text: śrutvaitadvacanaṃ bhīto bhūto vismitamānasaḥ /
children.translated_text: Hearing these words, the ghost, terrified and astonished in mind,

children.text: yāmīti brāhmaṇaṃ proktvā pātraṃ tyaktvā jagāma tat // Suk_47.3 (=227) //
children.translated_text: Saying 'I am going!' to the brahmin, abandoned the vessel and departed. // Suk_47.3 (=227) //

children.text:
tadā pātre svasthībhūte śatrughnarājñā satkṛto brāhmaṇo mṛgāvatīnagaraṃ yayau /
iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text: Then, when the vessel [i.e. the possessed person] had recovered, the brahmin, honored by King <s>Śatrughna</s>, went to the city of <s>Mṛgāvatī</s>. Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau saptacatvāriṃśattamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the forty-seventh tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s>.

children.text: START Suk 48:
children.translated_text: START Suk 48:

children.text:
athānyedyuḥ prabhāvatī śukaṃ pṛcchati-gacchāmi narāntaramiti /
śukaḥ-
children.translated_text: Then on the next day, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asks the parrot: 'I shall go to another man.' The parrot [says] —

children.text: sambhogasukhamevātra paramaṃ vraja sundari /
children.translated_text: The pleasure of love-making alone is supreme here — go, O beautiful one,

children.text: viṣame nirṇayaṃ kartuṃ vetsi cecchakaṭālavat // Suk_48.1 (=228) //
children.translated_text: If you know how to make a judgment in a difficult matter, as <s>Śakaṭāla</s> did. // Suk_48.1 (=228) //

children.text:
pāṭalīpurapaṭṭane sārvabhaumo nando nāma rājabhūt /
śakaṭālastasya nṛpateḥ sacivāgraṇīrabhat /
tadbuddhivibhavākrāntāśca bhūpālāḥ sarve 'pi karadā abhavan /
uktañca-
children.translated_text: In the city of <s>Pāṭalīpura</s>, there was a sovereign king named <s>Nanda</s>. <s>Śakaṭāla</s> was the foremost minister of that king. Overwhelmed by his intellectual prowess, all the [neighboring] kings became tributaries. And it is said —

children.text: aprājñena ca kātareṇa ca guṇaḥ syātsānurāgeṇa kaḥ prajñāvikramaśālino 'pi hi bhavet kiṃ bhaktihīnātphalam /
children.translated_text: What virtue can there be in one who is unwise, cowardly, yet devoted? And what fruit [comes] from one who possesses wisdom and valor but lacks devotion?

children.text: prajñāvikramabhaktayaḥ samuditā yeṣāṃ guṇā bhūtaye te bhṛtyā nṛpateḥ kalatramitare sampatsu cāpatsu ca // Suk_48.2 (=229) //
children.translated_text: Those in whom wisdom, valor, and devotion are combined — such servants are a blessing to the king, like a spouse, in prosperity and adversity alike. // Suk_48.2 (=229) //

children.text: kiñca-
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: prajñāguptaśarīrasya kiṃ kariṣyanti saṃhatāḥ /
children.translated_text: What can enemies, even united, do to one whose body is guarded by wisdom,

children.text: hastopadhṛtachatrasya vāridhārā ivārayaḥ // Suk_48.3 (=230) //
children.translated_text: Just as streams of rain [cannot harm] one who holds an umbrella in hand? // Suk_48.3 (=230) //

children.text:
sa ca rājā dharmanāśakaṃ kurvannirdravyāṃ ca medinīṃ vidadhāno niṣiddho mantriṇā /
tatastenāpi mūrkheṇa rājñā sacivo 'vaṭe nikṣiptaḥ /
sa ca saputrastatra ciraṃ tasthau /
tataḥ śakaṭāle mahāmātye tatrasthe sarvatra mṛto mṛta iti vārttābhūt /
tato baṅgālanāthena tatparīkṣārthamātmoyapuruṣā ghoṭikādvayaṃ samarpya nandapārśve preṣitāḥ /
yadetayormadhyātkā mātā kā ca putrī iti jñātvā samāgantavyam /
sarvalakṣaṇasampūrṇe sadṛśe ghoṭiketāni ca lakṣaṇāni śālihotrajñātavyāni /
yadā ca ko 'pi nandarājye ghoṭikānirṇayaṃ kartuṃ na kṣamastadā nando rājā vyacintayāt-"śakaṭālaṃ vināhaṃ paribhavāspadaṃ jātaḥ" /
uktañca-
children.translated_text: That king, destroying <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) and draining the land of wealth, was admonished by the minister. Then that foolish king threw the minister into a pit. And he remained there with his son for a long time. Then, while the great minister <s>Śakaṭāla</s> was confined there, the rumor spread everywhere that he was dead. Then the lord of <s>Baṅgāla</s> (Bengal), in order to test [<s>Nanda</s>], sent his own men to <s>Nanda</s>'s court, presenting a pair of mares: 'Of these two, which is the mother and which the daughter? — determine this and return.' The two mares were identical in all marks and features, and their characteristics required knowledge of <s>Śālīhotra</s> (equine science). When no one in <s>Nanda</s>'s kingdom was able to determine [which mare was which], King <s>Nanda</s> thought: 'Without <s>Śakaṭāla</s>, I have become an object of ridicule.' And it is said —

children.text: bhūmeśca deśasya guṇānvitasya bhṛtyasya vā buddhimataḥ praṇāśe /
children.translated_text: When a land of virtues, a country, or a wise servant is destroyed,

children.text: bhṛtyapraṇāśe maraṇaṃ nṛpāṇāṃ naṣṭāpi bhūmiḥ sulabhā na bhṛtyāḥ // Suk_48.4 (=231) //
children.translated_text: When servants are lost, it is death for kings — even lost land is easily regained, but not servants. // Suk_48.4 (=231) //

children.text:
vicintyaiva daṇḍapāśikamabravīt "yacchakaṭālakule kaścitkūpagato vidyate na vā" /
tenoktam-"kaścidasti paraṃ vyaktito na jñāyate /
yataḥ pūrvoddiṣṭaṃ bhaktaṃ kaścitkūpagato gṛhṇāti /
taṃ ca kūpādākṛṣya sammānya ca eva muktavān-
children.translated_text:
Having reflected thus, he said to the chief of police: 'Is there anyone in the well in the <s>Śakaṭāla</s> household or not?'
He replied: 'There is someone, but his identity is not clearly known.
For someone in the well takes the food that was offered earlier.'
Then, having drawn him out of the well and honored him, he released him [saying]:

children.text: mānyastvaṃ mama mitraṃ ca guruḥ svāmī niyogakaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'You are honored by me, my friend, my teacher, my master, my commander,

children.text: āśrayasya sadā dātā ki ka na tvaṃ sadānagha // Suk_48.5 (=232) //
children.translated_text: the constant giver of refuge — what indeed are you not to me, O sinless one?' // Suk_48.5 (=232) //

children.text: uktañca-
children.translated_text: And it is said:

children.text: svāmī durṇayavāraṇavyatikare śāstropadeśe gururviśrambhe hṛdayaṃ niyogasamaye dāso bhaye cāśrayaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'A master in warding off injustice, a teacher in scriptural instruction, a heart in matters of trust, a servant at the time of commission, a refuge in times of fear,

children.text: dātā saptasamudrasīmaraśanādāmāntikāyāḥ kṣiteḥ sarvākāramabhūtsvayaṃ varasuhṛtko na karṇo mama // Suk_48.6 (=233) //
children.translated_text: a giver of the earth girdled by the seven oceans — who embodied all these forms by himself as the best of friends, who is not my <s>Karṇa</s>?' // Suk_48.6 (=233) //

children.text:
mantriṇoktam-"svāmin kiṃ vidheyaṃ tadādiśa' /
rājñoktam-"asya vaḍavāyugalasya madhye kā mātā kā ca putrī iti sandehamamīṣāṃ chalātmanāṃ dūtānāṃ śīghraṃ chindhi /
sa kathaṃ chinattu tatsandehamiti praśnaḥ /
śukaḥ-tato mantriṇā tadvaḍavāyugaṃ saparyāṇaṃ kārayitvā bāhyālyāmativāhya paryāṇarahitaṃ vidhāya śrāntaṃ sammocitam /
tadanu tadyugalaṃ ca mātṛsutāviceṣṭitaṃ cakāra /
mātā jihvayā sutāṃ lileha sutā ca tāṃ prati ativatsalābhūt /
tataḥ sumantriṇā mātṛsutāviśeṣā rājño 'gre niveditaḥ /
tataśca śakaṭālaḥ parāṃ lakṣmīṃ prasiddhiṃ ca lebhe /
iti kathāṃ śratvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text:
The minister said: 'O lord, what is to be done? Command it.'
The king said: 'Between this pair of mares, which is the mother and which is the daughter — resolve this doubt of these deceitful envoys quickly.'
How should he resolve that doubt? — that is the question.
The parrot [said]: Then the minister had that pair of mares saddled and led outside; then, having removed the saddles, released them when they were tired.
Thereupon that pair displayed the behavior of mother and daughter.
The mother licked the daughter with her tongue, and the daughter became very affectionate toward her.
Then the wise minister reported the distinction between mother and daughter before the king.
And thus <s>Śakaṭāla</s> obtained supreme glory and renown.
Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau aṣṭacatvāriṃśattamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus [ends] the forty-eighth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 49:
children.translated_text: [Beginning of the Forty-ninth Tale (<s>Suk</s> 49)]

children.text:
athāparedyuḥ dinakṛtyaṃ sā vidhāya śukamāpṛcchate /
śukaḥ-
children.translated_text:
Then on the next day, having completed her daily duties, she asked the parrot.
The parrot [said]:

children.text: sambhogasukhamevādya bhoktuṃ te devi yujyate /
children.translated_text: 'It is fitting for you, O queen, to enjoy the pleasure of union today,

children.text: viṣame 'pi pravīṇāsi punaścecchakaṭālavat // Suk_49.1 (=234) //
children.translated_text: if you are skilled [even] in a difficult situation, like <s>Śakaṭāla</s> once again.' // Suk_49.1 (=234) //

children.text:
yathāpūrvaṃ tathaiva baṅgālanātho yaṣṭikāṃ suvṛttāṃ dhvajācchidriṇīmayīṃ jīvacachakaṭālaparīkṣāyai taireva puṃbhiḥ preṣayāmāsa /
yathā yuṣmābhirnandarājye gatvā asyā yaṣṭikāyā ratnasuvarmavajrairkhacitāyā ādimantaṃ jñātvā samāgantavyamityādeśātte pumāṃso nandapārśvamāgatya yaṣṭikāṃ tatpurato muktvā ādimantaṃ ca papracchuḥ /
tacchratvā pradhānaiḥ kalābhijñairvaṇigvaraistolitā ānyaiśca kovidairavalokitā /
paraṃ kenāpi ādyantavibhāgo na jñātaḥ /
tato rājā śakaṭālamādiśat yattvāṃ vinā ādyantavibhāgaṃ na ko 'pi jānāti /
tatastvayā nirṇayo vidheya eva /
tato mantrī vadati-"svāmin! yuṣmatkṛtā sambhāvanāpi na niṣphalā /
children.translated_text:
As before, the lord of <s>Baṅgāla</s> (Bengal) sent, through those same men, a staff — well-rounded, made with a hole [at one end marked by] a flag — for testing the living <s>Śakaṭāla</s>.
'You should go to the <s>Nanda</s> kingdom, determine the top and bottom of this staff studded with gems, gold, and diamonds, and return' — with this instruction, the men came to <s>Nanda</s>'s presence, placed the staff before him, and asked about its top and bottom.
Hearing this, it was weighed by the chief men, those skilled in arts, and the best merchants, and examined by other experts.
But no one could determine the distinction of top from bottom.
Then the king directed <s>Śakaṭāla</s>: 'No one but you knows the distinction of top from bottom.
Therefore the determination must be made by you.'
Then the minister said: 'O lord! Your confidence [in me] is not in vain either.

children.text: uktañca suvaṃśasyāvadātasya śaśāṅkasyeva lāñchanam /
children.translated_text: And it is said: Like a mark on the spotless moon of a noble lineage,

children.text: kṛcchreṣu vyarthayā yatra bhūpaterbharturājñayā // Suk_49.2 (=235) //
children.translated_text: [is trust] made fruitless in difficult times by a meaningless command of the king, the master.' // Suk_49.2 (=235) //

children.text:
tataśca sa mantrī sambhāvito 'pi kathaṃ jñāsyatīti praśnaḥ /
uttaram-śukaḥ prāha-"tato 'sau buddhimānmantrī yaṣṭikāṃ jale cikṣepa /
jñātañca yato yanmūlaṃ tadīṣajjale magnam /
tacca nṛpaterniveditam /
tena ca teṣāṃ dūtānāmapi kathitam /
tataste śrutvāsvarājñe nyavedayan /
tataśca te rājāno nandādhirājasya pūrvajalpitaṃ karaṃ daduḥ /
iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text:
Then, how will that honored minister know? — that is the question.
The answer — the parrot said: 'Then that intelligent minister threw the staff into water.
It was known [which end was which], since the root-end sank slightly in the water.
This was reported to the king.
And by him it was told to those envoys.
They, having heard, reported to their own king.
Then those kings paid the tribute previously boasted of by the supreme sovereign <s>Nanda</s>.'
Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau ekonapañcāśattamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus [ends] the forty-ninth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 50:
children.translated_text: [Beginning of the Fiftieth Tale (<s>Suk</s> 50)]

children.text:
anyadā pradoṣe prabhāvatī calitā śukaṃ papraccha /
śukaḥ-
children.translated_text:
On another occasion, at twilight, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> set out and asked the parrot.
The parrot [said]:

children.text: gaccha devi na te doṣo gamane ko 'pi dṛśyate /
children.translated_text: 'Go, O queen — no fault is seen in your going,

children.text: viṣame yadi vetsi tvaṃ dharmabuddhirivehitam // Suk_50.1 (=236) //
children.translated_text: if, in a difficult situation, you know how to act like <s>Dharmabuddhi</s>.' // Suk_50.1 (=236) //

children.text:
"kathametat?" śukaḥ-astiḥ devi dharāpṛṣṭhe jāṅgalābhidho grāmaḥ /
tatra mitradvayaṃ vartate dharmabuddhirduṣṭabuddhiśceti /
anyadā tau dvāvapi dhanāśayā deśāntaraṃ gatau /
kiyadbhirdinaiḥ pracuraṃ dhanamarjayitvā svagrāmāgatau parasparaṃ mantraṃ cakrāte yatpippalādho dhanaṃ kiñchitkṣiptvānyadgṛhe nīyate /
paścātkrameṇa vibhajyate lagnam /
iti kṛtvā tau nijagṛhaṃ jagmaturhṛṣṭatuṣṭau sukhāsvādatatparau sthitau /
atrāntare yatkṛta duṣṭabuddhinā tanniśamyatām /
naca yujyate vaktum /
yataḥ-
children.translated_text:
'How so?' The parrot [said]: 'There is, O queen, on the surface of the earth a village called <s>Jāṅgala</s>.
There live two friends — <s>Dharmabuddhi</s> (Righteous-minded) and <s>Duṣṭabuddhi</s> (Wicked-minded).
Once, both of them, desiring wealth, went to a foreign land.
After some days, having earned abundant wealth, they returned to their village and conferred together: "Let us bury some wealth beneath the <s>pippala</s> tree, and take the rest home.
Later, we shall gradually divide what is deposited."
Having done so, the two went to their respective homes, delighted and content, devoted to the enjoyment of happiness.
Meanwhile, what <s>Duṣṭabuddhi</s> did — hear that.
But it is not proper to tell, for:

children.text: na vaktavyaṃ dhruvaṃ devi pāpaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ śrutaṃ mayā /
children.translated_text: 'One should certainly not speak of it, O queen — the sin I have seen and heard,

children.text: kathāpi khalu pāpānāmalamaśreyase yataḥ // Suk_50.2 (=237) //
children.translated_text: for even the tale of the wicked is sufficient to bring misfortune.' // Suk_50.2 (=237) //

children.text:
tena ca duṣṭabuddhinā taddravyamutpāṭya gṛhītvā nijagṛhamānītam /
kālakrameṇa ca sammilitau pippalādhaḥsthitaṃ dravyaṃ grahītuṃ gatau yāvadālokayataḥ tāvaddravyaṃ nāsti /
dharmabuddhistato gatvā mantriṇo 'gre ācakhyau dhanavṛttāntaṃ hṛtaṃ cāpi kubuddhinā /
kubuddhināhṛtena uttaraṃ kṛtam /
sahasrasya paṇo muktaḥ /
etadarthe śapathaṃ dāpayiṣyāmi /
mantriṇoktamevamevāstu /
dvitīyenāpi pratipannaṃ yadā tadā mantriṇā pratibhuvau gṛhītvā muktau gatau gehaṃ pṛthakpṛthak /
tato duṣṭabuddhirnijaṃ pitaraṃ viditārthaṃ kṛtvā vṛkṣakoṭare cikṣepa /
prabhāte sacivastau ca vādino kotukī lokaśca taṃ pippalaṃ yayuḥ /
duṣṭabuddhiḥ snātaḥ kṛtāñjaliḥ satyaṃ kṛtvā jagāda /
"idaṃsatyaṃ brūhi nagottama yadi mayā dravyamapahṛtaṃ tadānena hṛtamiti vācyam /
yadi na hṛtaṃ tadānena na hṛtamiti vācyam" /
iti śrutvā tatpitrā nahīti jalpitaṃ sarvalokapratyakṣam /
tato dharmabuddhiḥ kathaṃ bhavatu-iti praśnaḥ /
tatsandiṣṭaḥ śuka-prāha--"dharmabuddhistaṃ śabdaṃ tatpiturjñātvā koṭare vahniṃ jajvāla /
taṃ pitaraṃ koṭarāt phūtkūrvantamardhajvalitaṃ ca patitaṃ dṛṣṭvā duṣṭabuddhernigrahaṃ vidhāya mantrī dharmabuddhimānandayāmāsa /
iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text:
That <s>Duṣṭabuddhi</s> dug up that wealth, took it, and brought it to his own home.
In due course, the two met and went to take the wealth deposited beneath the <s>pippala</s> tree — but when they looked, the wealth was not there.
<s>Dharmabuddhi</s> then went before the minister and reported the affair of the wealth, and that it had been stolen by <s>Kubuddhi</s> (the wicked-minded one).
<s>Kubuddhi</s> denied the theft.
A wager of a thousand [coins] was laid.
'I will administer an oath for this matter.'
The minister said: 'So be it.'
When the second also agreed, the minister took sureties from both and released them to go to their separate homes.
Then <s>Duṣṭabuddhi</s>, having informed his own father, hid him in the hollow of the tree.
At dawn, the magistrate, the two litigants, the curious onlookers, and the public went to that <s>pippala</s> tree.
<s>Duṣṭabuddhi</s>, having bathed and joined his palms, swearing truthfully, said:
'Speak the truth, O best of trees — if I have stolen the wealth, say "it was taken by him"; if I have not stolen it, say "it was not taken by him."'
Hearing this, his father [hidden inside] said 'No [he did not take it]' — in full view of all the people.
Then what should <s>Dharmabuddhi</s> do? — that is the question.
The parrot said: '<s>Dharmabuddhi</s>, recognizing that voice as his [<s>Duṣṭabuddhi</s>'s] father's, set fire to the hollow.
Seeing the father come tumbling out of the hollow, gasping and half-burnt, the minister punished <s>Duṣṭabuddhi</s> and brought joy to <s>Dharmabuddhi</s>.'
Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau pañcāśattamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus [ends] the fiftieth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 51:
children.translated_text: [Beginning of the Fifty-first Tale (<s>Suk</s> 51)]

children.text:
anyadā sā bālā śukaṃ papraccha /
śukaḥ-
children.translated_text:
On another occasion, that young woman asked the parrot.
The parrot [said]:

children.text: yādi devi ratāsvādalubdhe kāmini taṃ naram /
children.translated_text: 'Go, O queen, to that man [you are] greedy for the taste of love, O amorous one,

children.text: gāṅgilavadvijānāsi viṣame yadi bhāṣitum // Suk_51.1 (=238) //
children.translated_text: if, like <s>Gāṅgila</s>, you know how to speak in a difficult situation.' // Suk_51.1 (=238) //

children.text:
prabhāvatī brūte-"nāhe vedmi /
tatkathaya" /
śukaḥ-"asti camatkārapuraṃ nāma nagaram /
tacca caturvedacaturvarṇacaturāśramasamākulam /
tataḥ kadācittatrasthā brāhmaṇā vallabhīnāthayātrāyāṃ calitā gantrībhiraśvavāhanaiḥ sakautukā vṛddhimantaḥ pūrṇapārthayādisāmagrīkā sāranepathyāḥ saputrakalatrāḥ /
mārge caurairgṛhītumārabdhāḥ /
te 'pi sarve bhayākulā naṣṭāḥ /
gāṅgilanāmā viprastairvipraiḥ saha gantumaśaktaḥ khañjaḥ san samantato gantryārūḍho dhṛtaḥ /
tataḥ sa kathaṃ bhavatviti praśnaḥ /
śukaḥ-tataḥ sarveṣu dvijepu naṣṭeṣu sa śakaṭasthaḥ udbhrāntaṃ bhrātaraṃ sāhasika iva jagāda /
bhrātaḥ kiyanto gajāḥ kiyantaśca vājinaḥ santi /
iti kathaya satūrmaṃ ca tvaṃ dhanurarpaya yathaitāndivyāstreṇa yugapanmārayāmi /
iti vacaḥ śrutvā te taskarāḥ sarve 'pi naṣṭāḥ /
children.translated_text:
<s>Prabhāvatī</s> said: 'I do not know [that story].
Tell it.' The parrot [said]: 'There is a city called <s>Camatkārapura</s>.
It was bustling with the four <s>Vedas</s>, the four <s>varṇas</s> (social classes), and the four <s>āśramas</s> (life-stages).
Once, <s>brāhmaṇas</s> residing there set out on a pilgrimage to <s>Vallabhīnātha</s>, equipped with carts and horse-vehicles, full of curiosity and prosperity, with complete supplies for their journey, finely attired, accompanied by their sons and wives.
On the road they were set upon by robbers.
All of them, overcome with fear, fled.
A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Gāṅgila</s>, being lame and unable to go with those <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, remained seated in a cart.
Then what happened to him? — that is the question.
The parrot [said]: Then, when all the twice-born had fled, he, seated in the cart, spoke boldly to his agitated brother as if he were a warrior:
"Brother, how many elephants and how many horses are there?
Tell me quickly, and hand me the bow, so that I may slay them all at once with divine weapons!"
Hearing these words, all those robbers fled.

children.text: tasmādyo bhāṣituṃ vetti dharme cārthe smare tathā /
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, one who knows how to speak in matters of <s>dharma</s> (duty), <s>artha</s> (wealth), and <s>smara</s> (love),

children.text: kastaṃ dharṣayituṃ śakto nareṣu kamalānane // Suk_51.2 (=239) //
children.translated_text: who among men can overcome him, O lotus-faced one?' // Suk_51.2 (=239) //

children.text: iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text: Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau ekapañcāśattamo kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus [ends] the fifty-first tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 52:
children.translated_text: [Beginning of the Fifty-second Tale (<s>Suk</s> 52)]

children.text:
atikramya divā prabhāvatī triyāmāsamaye dvijaṃ prāha-vrajāmīti /
śukaḥ-
children.translated_text:
Having passed the day, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> at nightfall said to the parrot: 'I am going.'
The parrot [said]:

children.text: vrajābhoṣṭaṃ naraṃ devi yadi kāryaṃ nijaṃ gatā /
children.translated_text: 'Go, O queen, to that desirable man, if, having gone about your own affair,

children.text: jayaśrīriva jānāsi kāryaṃ kartuṃ nijaṃ hitam // Suk_52.1 (=240) //
children.translated_text: you know how to accomplish your own good, like <s>Jayaśrī</s>.' // Suk_52.1 (=240) //

children.text:
kathametat? śukaḥ-śṛṇu devi! asti dharāpṛṣṭhe pratiṣṭhānaṃ nāma pattanam /
tatra sattvaśīlo rājā /
tatputro durdamano nāma /

children.translated_text:
'How so?' The parrot [said]: 'Listen, O queen! There is on the surface of the earth a city called <s>Pratiṣṭhāna</s>.
There [ruled] a righteous king.
His son was named <s>Durdamana</s>.
He resolved: "I shall enjoy only what is earned by my own arms, not my father's wealth," and, having left his own city, set out for foreign lands with friends of equal temperament — a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>'s son, a carpenter's son, and a merchant's son.
Then, having met together, they decided: "It is fitting to seek the great ocean, <s>Aramāka</s>, the land of gems."
For it is said:

children.text: vidyāvatāṃ kulīnānāṃ śauryasampattiśālinām /

children.translated_text: Then that wicked man, overcome by greed, placed the four jewels between his legs and sewed [them in]. On another occasion, on the road, he blew [air] loudly, and afterwards, standing at a distance, the merchants said 'I have been robbed!' They asked: 'For what reason?' She said: 'When I stepped aside to relieve myself, a thief standing behind me stole my purse, including everything.' When this was reported, they realized: 'Look, this one is a rogue. Surely this merchant must have done something' — thinking thus, disputing amongst themselves, they went to the city of <s>Airāvatī</s>. There the king was called <s>Nītisāra</s> (Essence of Policy). His minister, named <s>Buddhisāra</s> (Essence of Wisdom), was world-renowned, whose fame was such in his own land and in foreign lands that he could discern the truth merely from hearing the words of disputants. Then the prince and the others reported to that minister the full account of the jewel-journey as it had happened: 'Likewise, examine [the matter] and, without killing or imprisonment, have each one separately hand over the jewels from among us. And if you cannot recover them, then your famous reputation will prove worthless.' <s>Buddhisāra</s>, hearing this, stood seized by anxiety. How the king <s>Nītisāra</s> should [resolve this] — this is the question. The parrot said: When the minister could not determine [who had] the four jewels hidden among them, he went home dejected. Meanwhile, the minister's daughter, <s>Jayaśrī</s> by name, having just attained her youth, having bowed to <s>Pārvatī</s>, went to pay respects to her father. Seeing her father in such an anxious state, she asked the cause of his distress. The minister told [her] the situation as it was. The daughter said: 'Father! Do not despair. I shall make the determination for them. When those disputing men come for the hearing, send them to our house, so that I may identify the jewel-thief from among them.' He said: 'Daughter! How will you know the truth that even I could not discern?' She said:

children.text: na caitattāta vaktavyaṃ bhinnā buddhirhi dehiṣu /
children.translated_text: 'This should not be said, father — for intelligence differs among embodied beings;

children.translated_text: someone knows something [that another does not] — in this world, each is skilled in some art.' Suk_52.5 (=244)

children.translated_text: 'Therefore, father! No anxiety should be felt in this matter. Send those foreigners [to me] so that I may enlighten them.' They were sent by the minister, and she bathed them, fed them, and had them sleep separately. Then she, having adorned herself, said to the chief one, the prince: 'I have come to your side desiring lovemaking. Give me a hundred gold [coins] and enjoy me.' He said: 'I shall earn wealth and a kingdom for you and give them. But right now I have nothing.' Knowing him to be penniless, she went to the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. She said the same thing to the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> said: 'Whatever wealth is with my father, and land secured by royal grant — I shall give it all to you.' Knowing him too to be without wealth, she left him and went to the carpenter. He said: 'At present I have nothing, but later I shall give a hundred thousand.' Leaving him too as without wealth, she went to the merchant's son. She said the same to him. He said: 'My lady! Take these four jewels and enjoy me.' Then, pulling out the jewels from his leg, he handed them over. Then she, rising with a pretense [of modesty], preserving her virtue, <s>Jayaśrī</s> went home and gave the four jewels to her father. The minister too, summoning them, returned to each his own jewel. And they, having obtained their own jewels, went to their respective homes satisfied. Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.translated_text: <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked: 'How is this?' The parrot [said]: On the bank of the river <s>Carmaṇvatī</s>, there is a village called <s>Carmakūṭa</s>. There lived a leather-worker named <s>Dohaḍa</s>. His wife was named <s>Devikā</s>, but she was wanton with other men. When the leather-worker went outside to purchase hides, she brought in her paramour. While those two were in the final act of lovemaking, the husband returned from outside with his hides. Then — what should the paramour and she do? — this is the question. When asked, the parrot said: When she recognized her husband approaching, then —

children.translated_text: <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked: 'How is this?' The parrot [said]: There is a city named <s>Śakrāvatī</s>. In it there was a king named <s>Dharmadatta</s>, endowed with <s>dharma</s> (righteousness) and other virtues. His minister was named <s>Suśīla</s>. His son, named <s>Viṣṇu</s>, had formerly been the minister of peace and war. When he fell from that position, being without wealth yet proud of being a hereditary minister, he was harsh [in manner]. So the king said nothing. But once the minister said to the king: 'My lord, this <s>Viṣṇu</s> is devoted, loyal, and skilled in the duties of an envoy. Therefore, Your Majesty should test him by sending him somewhere.' Then the king, hearing those words, being hostile toward him, gave him a gift of ashes sealed with the royal seal and sent him to the city of <s>Vidiśā</s>, to the presence of king <s>Śatrudamana</s>. And he, having gone there, not knowing that the gift was [merely] ashes, opened the sealed [package] before the king. When that inauspicious gift was opened before the king, the king became filled with a surge of anger. Then — how should the envoy obtain safety when that gift had been presented? — this is the question. The parrot gave the answer: <s>Viṣṇu</s>, seeing him enraged, being clever, spoke thus: 'My lord! My master performed an <s>Aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice). The sacred, auspicious, sin-destroying ashes born of the <s>tretāgni</s> (three sacred fires) of that sacrificial pit have been presented to you as an offering of reverence. For:

children.text: gajāḥ santi hayāḥ santi vicitrāḥ santi sampadaḥ /

children.translated_text: Having said this, he quickly rose, placed the ashes in [the king's] hand, and presented them to the king. And he, pleased by those words, bowed [in acceptance]. The pleased [king] also sent a great return-gift. And <s>Viṣṇu</s> was honored and sent off. 'Therefore, O passionate one, if you know an answer in a difficult situation, then go — otherwise stay.' Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.translated_text: <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked: 'How is this?' The parrot said: In the village of <s>Carmakūṭa</s>, there was a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Śrīdhara</s>. In that very place there was a cobbler named <s>Candana</s>. <s>Śrīdhara</s> had a pair of sandals made by him. The cobbler kept asking for payment constantly. The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> kept saying: 'I shall make you happy.' A very long time passed in this way. One day the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> was seized by the cobbler. How should the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> be freed without money? Tell that — this is the question. The answer: The parrot said: In the meantime, a son was born in the village headman's house. Then the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, seeking a pretext, said: 'O leather-worker, I said to you before: I shall make you happy. Now that this son is born, are you happy or not?' If he says 'I am not happy,' then the king would arrest him [for disloyalty]. Otherwise, the money [claim] is lost. So he said: 'I have become happy.' Then the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, having freed himself through the stratagem, departed. 'Therefore, O passionate one, if you know such an answer, then go.' Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau pañcapañcāśattamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifty-fifth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s>.

children.text: START Suk 56:
children.translated_text: START Suk 56:

children.text:
athāparedyuḥ prabhāvatī gamanāya śukaṃ pṛcchati /
śukaḥ--
children.translated_text: Then on the next day, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked the parrot for permission to go. The parrot [said]:

children.text: yādi devi gatā vetsi yadi kartuṃ tvamuttaram /
children.translated_text: 'Go, O queen — if you know how to give an answer

children.text: viṣame sāntako yadvadvaṇikputraḥ purākarot // Suk_56.1 (=251) //
children.translated_text: in a difficult situation, as the merchant's son <s>Sāntaka</s> once did.' Suk_56.1 (=251)

children.text:
astyatra tripatho nāma grāmaḥ /
tatra sāntako nāma vaṇik mahādhanī kṛpaṇo duṣṭaśīlo grāmāntarapriyaśca /
tataśca grāmāntarādudgrahaṇikāṃ kṛtvā āgacchanpathi caurairdhṛtaḥ sa bhāmini kathaṃ corabhayānmucyate iti praśnaḥ /
uttaram /
śukaḥ-sa vaṇikputraḥ ātmānaṃ corairdhṛtaṃ jñātvā galagrahanāmno yakṣasya samīpavartino 'ntikaṃ yayau /
tasyāgrataśca dravyaṃ muktvā haste ca khaṭikāmādāya yakṣādhāśāmidamabravīt-
children.translated_text: There is a village named <s>Tripatha</s> (Three-roads). There lived a merchant named <s>Sāntaka</s>, very wealthy but miserly, of wicked character, and fond of [traveling to] other villages. Once, returning from another village after making a collection of debts, he was seized on the road by robbers. How should she — O passionate one — how should he be freed from the danger of thieves? — this is the question. The answer: The parrot [said]: That merchant's son, knowing himself to be seized by robbers, went to the nearby shrine of a <s>Yakṣa</s> (spirit) named <s>Galagraha</s> (Throat-Seizer). Before it, he placed the money, took chalk in his hand, and spoke thus beneath the <s>Yakṣa</s>:

children.text: dhanodgrāhaṇikā deva kṛteyaṃ tava sarvataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'O god! A collection of debts has been made everywhere on your behalf;

children.text: idaṃ dravyaṃ mayā labdhaṃ tiṣṭhatyanyacca vṛddhimat // Suk_56.2 (=252) //
children.translated_text: this wealth has been obtained by me, and more remains, bearing interest.' Suk_56.2 (=252)

children.text:
taṃ lekhakaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā yakṣadhanamiti jñātvā taṃ praṇamya te gatāścorāḥ /
sa ca dravyaṃ gṛhītvā kṣemeṇa gṛhaṃ yayau /
children.translated_text: Seeing him writing [accounts] and thinking 'This is the <s>Yakṣa</s>'s wealth,' bowing to him, the robbers departed. And he, taking the wealth, went home safely.

children.text: iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text: Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: itiśukasaptatau ṣaṭpañcāśattamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifty-sixth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s>.

children.text: START Suk 57:
children.translated_text: START Suk 57:

children.text: pradoṣe 'nyatra sā bālā punaḥ prāha vihaṅgamam /
children.translated_text: At dusk on another day, that young woman again said to the bird:

children.text: sukhaṃ bhoktuṃ vrajāmyadya narāntararatodbhavam // Suk_57.1 (=253) //
children.translated_text: 'I am going today to enjoy the pleasure born of another man's company.' Suk_57.1 (=253)

children.text: śakuḥ-
children.translated_text: The parrot [said]:

children.text: yādi devi yadā jñātā bhartrā tvaṃ vetsi bhāṣitum /
children.translated_text: 'Go, O queen — when discovered by your husband, if you know how to speak

children.text: yatā jñātaḥ purā rājñā vadadvidvāñ śubhaṅkaraḥ // Suk_57.2 (=254) //
children.translated_text: as the learned <s>Śubhaṅkara</s> formerly spoke when discovered by the king.' Suk_57.2 (=254)

children.text:
avantopuryāṃ vikramārko nṛpaḥ /
tasya candralekhānāmnī rājñī /
sā rājapaṇḍitaṃ śubhaṅkaranāmānaṃ kāmārtā iyeṣa ramate ca dūtīdāsīviparyayāt /
nityaṃ tadgṛhaṃ gatvā yadṛcchayā krīḍate /
evaṃ ca vilasatostayoḥ paṇḍitarājñyoḥ prāvṛṭkālaḥ samāyayau /
yatra ca-
children.translated_text:
In the city of <s>Avantī</s>, there was a king named <s>Vikramārka</s>.
His queen was named <s>Candralekhā</s>.
She, overcome by desire, wished to enjoy the royal scholar named <s>Śubhaṅkara</s>, and through the reversal of [roles between] messenger and maidservant, she did make love [with him].
She would always go to his house and sport with him at will.
Thus, while those two — the scholar and the queen — were dallying, the rainy season arrived.
Wherein —

children.text: taḍinnirghoṣapaṭaho ghanagarjitagītakaḥ /
children.translated_text: With lightning's crash as its kettledrum, the rumbling of clouds as its song,

children.text: śikhisvarajayadhvajaḥ prāvṛṭkālanṛpo yayau // Suk_57.3 (=255) //
children.translated_text: and the peacock's cry as its victory-banner — the king that is the rainy season arrived. Suk_57.3 (=255)

children.text: durdinaṃ vegavṛṣṭiśca paṅkaśca taḍitaḥ prabhā /
children.translated_text: Overcast skies, torrential rain, mud, and the flash of lightning,

children.text: sadābhisārikāṇāṃ ca snehavyatikarāṇi ha // Suk_57.4 (=256) //
children.translated_text: and the transgressions of love by women who always go forth to meet their lovers — Suk_57.4 (=256)

children.text: uktañca-
children.translated_text: And it is said:

children.text: jai sasaṇehī to muai aha jīvai ṇiṇṇeha /
children.translated_text: [In Prakrit:] If she is full of love, then she is dead; if she lives, she is devoid of love —

children.text: duhia payārehiṃ gaia dhaṇa kiṃ gajjahi khalameha // Suk_57.5 (=257) //
children.translated_text: in both ways she is gone, the blessed one. Why do you thunder, O wicked cloud? Suk_57.5 (=257)

children.text: [yadi sasnehā tat mṛtā atha jīvati niḥsnehā /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] If she is full of love, then she is dead; if she lives, she is devoid of love —

children.text: dvābhyāmapi prakārābhyāṃ gatā dhanyā, kiṃ garjasi khalamegha] // Suk_57.5* (=257*) //
children.translated_text: in both ways she is gone, the blessed one. Why do you thunder, O wicked cloud? Suk_57.5* (=257*)

children.text: kiñca-
children.translated_text: Moreover —

children.text: x x x x x /
children.translated_text: [verse lost/illegible]
[verse lost/illegible] Suk_57.6 (=258)

children.text:
etasminsamaye rātrau rājñīṃ śubhaṅkaragṛhaṃ calitāṃ jñātvā pṛṣṭhata ajñātacaryayā haste khaḍgamādāya nīlavāsāḥ san kautuko vikramārko rājā tāmanucalitaḥ /
śubhaṅkaro 'pi tāṃ rājñīṃ gṛhadvārasamāgatāṃ dṛṣṭvā jagāda-
children.translated_text:
At this time, the king, learning that the queen had set out for <s>Śubhaṅkara</s>'s house at night, curious, followed her secretly, wearing dark garments, with sword in hand, moving undetected.
<s>Śubhaṅkara</s> too, seeing the queen arriving at his door, said:

children.text: unnādāmbudavarddhitāndhatamasi prabhṛṣṭadiṅmaṇḍale kāle yāmikajāgarūkasubhaṭavyākīrṇakolāhale /
children.translated_text: 'In the pitch darkness swelled by roaring clouds, when the quarters of the sky are obscured, at a time filled with the clamor of vigilant watchmen and warriors,

children.text: bhūpasyāsuhṛdarṇavāmbuvaḍavāvahnestvamantaḥpurādāyātāsi yadambujākṣi kṛtakaṃ manye bhayaṃ yoṣitām // Suk_57.7 (=259) //
children.translated_text: you have come from the inner apartments of the king — who is like the submarine fire in the ocean of enemies — O lotus-eyed one! I think that the fear of women is merely feigned.' Suk_57.7 (=259)

children.text:
idaṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā nṛpatiḥ svaprāsādamājagām /
śubhaṅkaro 'pi bhogasaṃskāraiścāṭūktibhiśca mahiṣīṃ toṣayāmāsa /
uktañca-
children.translated_text:
Hearing these words, the king returned to his own palace.
<s>Śubhaṅkara</s> then gratified the queen with the arts of pleasure and with flattering words.
And it is said:

children.text: ṇa kuṇanti je pahuttaṃ kuviaṃ dāsa vya je pasāanti /
children.translated_text: [In Prakrit:] Those who do not lord it over [a woman], who appease her when angered like servants —

children.text: te ccia mahilāṇa piā sesā sāmīciavarāā // Suk_57.8 (=260) //
children.translated_text: they alone are dear to women; the rest, though they be masters, are wretches. Suk_57.8 (=260)

children.text: [na kurvanti ye prabhutvaṃ kupitāṃ dāsa iva ye prasādayanti /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] Those who do not exercise authority, who appease her when angered like servants —

children.text: te eva mahilānāṃ priyāḥ śeṣāḥ svāmina eva varākāḥ] // Suk_57.8* (=260*) //
children.translated_text: they alone are dear to women; the rest, though they be masters, are wretches. Suk_57.8* (=260*)

children.text: nāyakeṣūttamaḥ so 'tha mahiṣī nāyikāsu ca /
children.translated_text: He was the foremost among heroes, and she [the foremost] among heroines;

children.text: śayanaṃ cottamaṃ ninye tridhā bhedavikalpanāt // Suk_57.9 (=261) //
children.translated_text: and the bed was the finest — threefold by the classification of types. Suk_57.9 (=261)

children.text: uttamādhamamadhyaiśca bhedaiḥ snayānnāyakastridhā /
children.translated_text: Heroes are of three kinds — superior, inferior, and middling;

children.text: nāyikāśca tathā jñeyāstayośca śayanaṃ tridhā // Suk_57.10 (=262) //
children.translated_text: heroines are likewise to be known [as threefold], and the bed of the two is also threefold. Suk_57.10 (=262)

children.text: tatra nāyakaguṇāḥ-
children.translated_text: Therein, the qualities of the hero [are as follows]:

children.text: hato manyuhasrairyaḥ santapto madanāgninā /
children.translated_text: He who is struck by thousands of indignations, scorched by the fire of desire,

children.text: raktaśca yo viraktāyāṃ so 'dhamaḥ parikīrtitaḥ // Suk_57.11 (=263) //
children.translated_text: and who is attached to one who is indifferent — he is declared the inferior [hero]. Suk_57.11 (=263)

children.text: kāminībhiḥ smarārtābhiḥ satataṃ kāmyate hi yaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who is constantly desired by women afflicted with love,

children.text: na tāḥ kāmayate namro madhyamo nāyakaḥ smṛtaḥ // Suk_57.12 (=264) //
children.translated_text: yet does not desire them, being modest — he is considered the middling hero. Suk_57.12 (=264)

children.text: raktāṃ yo bhāminīṃ devi saktāṃ kāmayate sadā /
children.translated_text: He who always desires, O lady, a passionate and devoted woman,

children.text: tayāpi kāmyate 'tyarthamuttamaḥ so 'bhidhīyate // Suk_57.13 (=265) //
children.translated_text: and is also exceedingly desired by her — he is called the superior [hero]. Suk_57.13 (=265)

children.text: nāyikāstridhā-
children.translated_text: Heroines are of three kinds:

children.text: kārye gṛhṇāti roṣaṃ yā gataroṣā priyānugā /
children.translated_text: She who shows anger only when there is cause, who follows her beloved when her anger subsides,

children.text: rasajñā kṛtyakuśalā sottamā nāyikā smṛtā // Suk_57.14 (=266) //
children.translated_text: who is versed in <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) and skilled in her duties — she is considered the superior heroine. Suk_57.14 (=266)

children.text: asthāne kopamānā yā yā duḥkhānunayā tathā /
children.translated_text: She who shows anger without cause, who is difficult to placate,

children.text: māninī mānahīnā ca kṣaṇātsā madhyamā smṛtā // Suk_57.15 (=267) //
children.translated_text: sulky yet abandoning her sulkiness in a moment — she is considered the middling heroine. Suk_57.15 (=267)

children.text: lubdhā yātīva capalā vacane nīrasākṣarā /
children.translated_text: She who is greedy, excessively fickle, dry and harsh in speech,

children.text: duḥkhaprasādhanābhijñākṛtajñā sādhamā matā // Suk_57.16 (=268) //
children.translated_text: unskilled in the art of appeasing through suffering, and ungrateful — she is considered the lowest heroine. Suk_57.16 (=268)

children.text: tayośca śayanaṃ tridhā-
children.translated_text: And the bed of those two is of three kinds:

children.text: pārśvayorunnati nītaṃ nimnamadhye priyasya tat /
children.translated_text: Raised on the sides, low in the middle — that [bed] of the beloved

children.text: vimardaṃ sahate 'tyarthaṃ suratāsaktayostayoḥ // Suk_57.17 (=269) //
children.translated_text: bears the intense pressure of the two who are absorbed in lovemaking. Suk_57.17 (=269)

children.text: madhyamasya punaḥ kāryaṃ śayanaṃ samabhūmikam /
children.translated_text: For the middling [couple], the bed should be made on level ground,

children.text: praviralāṅgasaṃsparśā nityaṃ yāti niśā yathā // Suk_57.18 (=270) //
children.translated_text: with sparse bodily contact, the night always passing [uneventfully]. Suk_57.18 (=270)

children.text: dveṣyasya tulyamuttuṅgaṃ madhye nīcaṃ ca pārśvayoḥ /
children.translated_text: For one who is hostile, it is equally high, low in the middle and at the sides —

children.text: na śakyeta kalākalpo yatra rantuṃ nirantaram // Suk_57.19 (=271) //
children.translated_text: where even the attempt at amorous art cannot be sustained continuously. Suk_57.19 (=271)

children.text: ityanunnatatalpasthā bhuktā muktā vipaścitā /
children.translated_text: Thus, lying on the raised bed, enjoyed and released by the wise [scholar],

children.text: mahiṣī ratisantuṣṭā pratyūṣe svagṛhaṃ yayau // Suk_57.20 (=272) //
children.translated_text: the queen, satisfied with lovemaking, went to her own house at dawn. Suk_57.20 (=272)

children.text:
rājā ca prātaḥ sarvāvasarānantaram paṇḍitaṃ rājñīṃ cājuhāva /
siṃhāsane ca paṇḍitamupaveśayāmāsa /
śubhaṅkaraṃ prati hasanvārtāprabandheneti jagāda-"kṛtakaṃ manye bhayaṃ yoṣitā"miti vacanaṃ śrutvā svadoṣavismitamānasaḥ sañjātaḥ /
sa rājñā jñātaḥ kathaṃ bhavitviti praśnaḥ /
yataḥ-
children.translated_text:
And the king, in the morning after all [official] occasions, summoned the scholar and the queen.
He seated the scholar on a throne.
Smiling at <s>Śubhaṅkara</s>, he said in the course of conversation: 'I think that the fear of women is merely feigned' — hearing [his own] words [quoted back], his mind was struck with astonishment at his own offense.
'He has been discovered by the king — what shall happen?' — that is the question.
Because —

children.text: dīnasyāpi gṛhe doṣe kṛte bhavati nigrahaḥ /
children.translated_text: Even in the house of a wretch, when a fault is committed, there is punishment;

children.text: kiṃ punaḥ pṛthivīpālagṛhe doṣo vimucyate // Suk_57.21 (=273) //
children.translated_text: how much more so when an offense is committed in the house of the lord of the earth — is it forgiven? Suk_57.21 (=273)

children.text:
uttaram /
śukaḥ prāha-tataśca sa budho rājñā jñāto 'hamiti sañcintyeti vāṇībhudairayat-
children.translated_text: The answer: The parrot said: Then the wise man, realizing 'I have been discovered by the king,' uttered these words:

children.text: ugragrāhamudanvato jalamatikrāmatyanālambane vyomni sthāpi ca durgamakṣitibhṛtāṃ mūrdhānamārohati /
children.translated_text: 'She crosses the ocean of fierce crocodiles, unsupported in the trackless sky she stands, and climbs the peaks of impassable mountains;

children.text: vyāptaṃ yāti viṣākulairahikulaiḥ pātālamekākinī kīrtiste madanāvatāra kṛtakaṃ manye bhayaṃ yoṣitām // Suk_57.22 (=274) //
children.translated_text: she goes alone to the netherworld swarming with agitated serpents — your fame, O incarnation of <s>Madana</s> (Love)! I think the fear of women is merely feigned.' Suk_57.22 (=274)

children.text:
iti paṇḍite paṭhitaṃ śrutvā rājā taṃ budhaṃ tāṃ ca rājñīṃ dṛṣṭvā iti cintayāmāsa-"durlabho 'yaṃ budhaḥ /
sulabhāḥ khalu nārya' iti vicintya mahiṣīṃ haste dhṛtvā tasmai viduṣe dadau /
uvāca ca-"gṛhāṇemāṃ mahiṣīm' /
paritoṣitaḥ paṇḍito 'pi "mahāprasāda' ityavocat /
uktañca-
children.translated_text:
Hearing what the scholar had recited, the king, looking at the wise man and the queen, reflected: 'This wise man is rare.
Women, indeed, are easily found.' Having thus deliberated, he took the queen by the hand and gave her to the scholar.
And he said: 'Accept this queen.'
The gratified scholar said: 'What great grace!'
And it is said:

children.text: guṇadoṣau na śāstrajñaḥ kathaṃ vibhajate janaḥ /
children.translated_text: How does a person who does not know the scriptures distinguish between merit and fault?

children.text: kimandhasyādhikāro 'sti rūpadoṣopalavdhiṣu // Suk_57.23 (=275) //
children.translated_text: What authority has a blind man in perceiving beauty and defect? Suk_57.23 (=275)

children.text:
paṇḍito 'pi rājñaḥ prasādātsukhaṃ bhuṅkte tayā samam /
yadyevaṃ prabhāvati! tvamapi samaye vaktuṃ jānāsi tadā gamyatām /
anyathā sthīyatām /
iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text:
And the scholar, by the king's grace, lived happily with her.
'If, O <s>Prabhāvatī</s>, you too know how to speak at the right moment, then go — otherwise, stay.'
Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau saptapañcāśattamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifty-seventh tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 58:
children.translated_text: START Suk 58:

children.text:
anyadā pradoṣe calitā prabhāvatī śukaṃ pṛcchati /
śukaḥ-
children.translated_text:
On another occasion, <s>Prabhāvatī</s>, having set out at dusk, questioned the parrot.
The parrot said:

children.text: ratyarthino vrajātha tvaṃ rantuṃ cetsamayocitam /
children.translated_text: 'If you go seeking pleasure, and wish to enjoy [yourself] with a timely response,

children.text: duḥśīlāpativadvetsi kartuṃ gaṇapateḥ puraḥ // Suk_58.1 (=276) //
children.translated_text: [knowing how to act] like <s>Duḥśīlā</s> did with her husband before [the image of] <s>Gaṇapati</s> —' Suk_58.1 (=276)

children.text:
prabhāvatyāha-kathametata? śukaḥ-asti lohapurī nāma nagaram /
tasmiṃśca rājaḍo nāma pāmaraḥ /
tasyāpi patnī parapuruṣalampaṭā duḥśīletyāhvayā /
sā ca sūtravikrayārthaṃ sakhībhiḥ sametya padmāvatīṃ purīṃ prayāti /
tataśca grāmasamīpasthasya gaṇapatestābhiḥ pṛthakpṛthak upayācitamuktam /
tayā ca cumbanamupayācitamuktaṃ madanākrāntadehayā /
sa ca tāsāṃ prabhūtaṃ lābhaṃ cakre /
tataḥ sarvābhiranyābhirātmīyamupayācitaṃ tasmai gaṇeśāya pradattam /
tayā ca nagnībhūya cumbanaṃ kṛtam /
tataḥ kelipriyeṇa tena sā adhare dhṛtā /
tasmiṃśca dhṛte sā kukkuṭīva tatra sthitā /
tañca vṛttāntaṃ tanmokṣaṇāya tadbhartuḥ sakhyopahasamānā nivedayāmāsuḥ /
so 'pi tadvacanaṃ śrutvā tatrāgamat tāṃ tathāvidhāṃ dṛṣṭvā sa vyacintayat-kathamiyaṃ mucyata iti praśnaḥ /
śukaḥ-tāṃ tathāsthitāṃ dṛṣṭvā sakāmaḥ san rāsabhaṃ rantumārebhe /
tataśca sa gaṇapatistatāvidhaṃ kautukaṃ dṛṣṭvā jahāsa /
hasatastasya oṣṭhau śithilau jātau /
tataḥ sā muktā satī praṇamya nijaṃ nāthaṃ tarjayantī gṛhaṃ yayau /
children.translated_text:
<s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked: 'How so?' The parrot said: There is a city named <s>Lohapurī</s>.
In it there was a lowly man named <s>Rājaḍa</s>.
His wife, lustful for other men, was called <s>Duḥśīlā</s>.
She, together with her friends, would go to the city of <s>Padmāvatī</s> on the pretext of selling thread.
Then, passing by a <s>Gaṇapati</s> [image] near the village, each of them separately offered something and made a request.
She, her body overcome by desire, offered and requested a kiss.
And he [<s>Gaṇapati</s>] bestowed abundant gain upon all of them.
Then all the other women gave their individually requested offerings to that <s>Gaṇeśa</s>.
But she, having stripped naked, gave a kiss.
Then the playful [deity] seized her by the lip.
And when she was held thus, she remained there like a hen.
Her friends, laughing, reported the incident to her husband so as to secure her release.
He too, hearing their words, came there and, seeing her in that state, thought: 'How shall she be freed?' — that is the question.
The parrot said: Seeing her in that state, being desirous himself, he began to mate with a she-donkey.
Then that <s>Gaṇapati</s>, seeing such a spectacle, laughed.
As he laughed, his lips loosened.
Then she, being released, bowed and, threatening her husband, went home.

children.text: kṛtaṃ tena rataṃ devi samayocitamīdṛśam /
children.translated_text: 'He performed such lovemaking, O lady, fitting for the occasion;

children.text: svakārye mocitā sāpi duḥśīlā vighnanāyakāt // Suk_58.2 (=277) //
children.translated_text: and she, <s>Duḥśīlā</s>, was freed from the Lord of Obstacles by her own device.' Suk_58.2 (=277)

children.text: samayocitamārambhaṃ kurute yastu kṛtyavit /
children.translated_text: 'He who, knowing what must be done, undertakes action fitting for the occasion,

children.text: sarvadā tu phalaṃ tasya samayajño di śiṣyate // Suk_58.3 (=278) //
children.translated_text: for him there is always fruit — one who knows the right moment is called wise.' Suk_58.3 (=278)

children.text: iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text: Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau aṣṭapañcāśattamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifty-eighth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 59:
children.translated_text: START Suk 59:

children.text:
atha dinānte sā śukaṃ gamanāya pṛcchati sma /
śukaḥ-
children.translated_text:
Then at the end of the day, she asked the parrot for permission to go.
The parrot said:

children.text: gaccha devi svakāryañca kuru cintitamadbhutam /
children.translated_text: 'Go, O lady, and accomplish your desire — [do] something marvelous;

children.text: rukmiṇīvadvijānāsi patiṃ vañcitumuddhatam // Suk_59.1 (=279) //
children.translated_text: if you know how to deceive your proud husband, like <s>Rukmiṇī</s>.' Suk_59.1 (=279)

children.text:
prabhāvatyāha-kathametat? śukaḥ-asti saṅgamo nāma grāmaḥ /
tatra rāhaḍo nāma rājaputraḥ sakopaḥ /
tasya bhāryā rukmiṇī nāma /
sa ca tayā sārdhaṃ devayātrāyāṃ calitaḥ /
sā ca narāntaraṃ kaṭākṣayanto tena dṛṣṭā pumāṃśca /
tataḥ sa tanmithunaṃ tathāvidhaṃ jñātvā tāṃ tadanuraktāṃ mene /
uktañca
children.translated_text: And it is said:

children.text: baddhamaṇiāi kanto tahea addhacchipicchilā dhāri /
children.translated_text: [In Prakrit:] The beloved of a woman whose heart is captivated, whose eyes are slippery with half-glances —

children.text: asasiaṃ pi muṇijjai chaillajanasaṃkule gāme // Suk_59.2 (=280) //
children.translated_text: even a sigh is noticed in a village full of sophisticated people. Suk_59.2 (=280)

<s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked: 'How so?' The parrot said: There is a village called <s>Saṅgama</s>.
There lived an irascible prince named <s>Rāhaḍa</s>.
His wife was named <s>Rukmiṇī</s>.
He had set out with her to a temple festival.
