She was seen exchanging sidelong glances with another man, and the man [was seen too].
Then he, knowing that couple's [exchange], considered her to be enamored of that man.

children.text: [baddhahṛdayāyāḥ kāntaḥ tathaiva arddhākṣapicchilā vāmā /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit rendering:] The beloved of a woman whose heart is captivated, the wanton one with eyes slippery with half-glances —

children.text: niḥśvasitamapi jñākṣayate vidagdhajanasaṃkule grāme] // Suk_59.2* (=280*) //
children.translated_text: even a sigh is perceived in a village full of sophisticated people. Suk_59.2* (=280*)

children.text:
tāṃ tathāvidhāṃ vikṛtāṃ jñātvā ca rāhaḍo gṛhamagamat /
dhikkṛtya paruṣākṣarairgṛhāntare yantritāṃ dhārayāmāsa /
sā ca cintayati-mama janma jīvitaṃ yauvanaṃ ca tadā saphalaṃ yadā etasya pratyakṣaṃ narāntaramupabhokṣye /
pratijñātaṃ ca manasā dṛḍham /
tata ātmoyapratijñāṃ kathaṃ nirvāhayatviti praśnaḥ /
śukaḥ-tataḥ sā kadācittaṃ hṛdayasthaṃ naraṃ gṛhapārśve gacchantaṃ dṛṣṭvā taṃ pratyāha-adya rātrau tvayāsmadgṛhāṅgaṇasthaciñciṇīmūle nijakāyākāragartāyāmūrdhvaliṅginā śayanaṃ vidheyamiti /
sa tatheti pratijñāya rātrau tathā bhūtvā sthitaḥ /
sā ca kāmārtā sarvakaraṇacaturā tatra yayau /
āgārabhūmimuddiśya bhartāramāhvayati sma /
sā ciñciṇīcchāyāyāṃ gatvā tasya liṅgasyopari upaviśya satūmadhanuṣaṃ tamabravīt /
children.translated_text:
Knowing her thus altered, <s>Rāhaḍa</s> went home,
and, rebuking her with harsh words, kept her confined inside the house.
She thought: 'My birth, life, and youth will be fruitful only when I enjoy another man before his very eyes.'
And this she firmly resolved in her mind.
'How shall she fulfill her self-made vow?' — that is the question.
The parrot said: Then one day, seeing the man who dwelt in her heart passing by the side of the house, she said to him: 'Tonight, you must lie at the foot of the tamarind tree in the courtyard of our house, in a pit [shaped like] your own body, with your [organ] erect.'
He, having agreed 'So be it,' assumed that posture at night and waited.
She, overcome by desire and clever in all ways, went there.
Pointing toward the house, she called to her husband.
Having gone to the shade of the tamarind tree, she sat upon his [erect] member, and holding a bowstring, said to him:

children.text: dhānuṣko 'si pradhāno 'si loke khyātiṃ gato 'si ca /
children.translated_text: 'You are an archer, you are foremost, you are renowned in the world;

children.text: chindhi me candrikāmadya pauruṣaṃ gaṇayāmi te // Suk_59.3 (=281) //
children.translated_text: shoot down the moonlight for me tonight — I shall esteem your valor.' Suk_59.3 (=281)

children.text:
sa ca mūrkhastadvacanamidaṃ śrutvā saśaraṃ dhanurādāya candrikāṃ lakṣīkṛtya bāṇaṃ mumoca /
tena mukto 'pi bāṇo nākāśagatāṃ candrikāṃ bhinatti /
adhaḥ sa vedhyād bhraṣṭaḥ /
tasmiṃśca patyāvaparāddheṣau sati sā viṃparītaratakṣamā sahastatālaṃ tamidamāha-
children.translated_text:
And that fool, hearing her words, took up a bow with arrow and, aiming at the moonlight, released the arrow.
But the arrow, once released, could not strike the moonlight in the sky.
It fell below, having missed the target.
And while her husband failed at the task, she, capable of making love in the reversed position, clapping her hands, said to him:

children.text: X X X
children.translated_text: [verse corrupt/illegible]

children.text: [rāhaḍa bhūlaḍaṃ cāndraṇīyāhaṃ hiṃ rūpavadīsai nīyaḍaḍaṃ /
children.translated_text: [In Prakrit:] 'O <s>Rāhaḍa</s>, you blundering fool! I am like the moonlight — will you drive me to another man's house?

children.text: tāhaṃ valikījinhaṃ tādahīvāhaṃ maiṃ rāṣajjevadraḍhīchāhaṃ] // Suk_59.3* (=282*) //
children.translated_text: I am [devoted] to you like a vine, I am a serpent-wife to you, I am firmly attached to you like a king's daughter.' Suk_59.3* (=282*)

children.text:
rāhaḍo 'pi tāmevaṃ jalpantīṃ śrutvā taṃ śaraṃ gaveṣayan ciraṃ babhrāma /
tatastayā yadṛcchayā viparītaṃ vihitam /
evamuktaśca patiḥ-
children.translated_text:
<s>Rāhaḍa</s>, hearing her speak thus, searched for the arrow and wandered about for a long time.
Meanwhile, she accomplished her desire at her pleasure.
And the husband was told:

children.text: yadṛcchayā rataṃ mūrkha te puro 'dya mayā kṛtam /
children.translated_text: 'The love that was made before your very eyes today, O fool, by me —

children.text: śūro hi kuhito 'si tvaṃ yāsyāmīti jagāda tam // Suk_59.4 (=283) //
children.translated_text: truly, you are a hero who has been outwitted! I shall go now,' she said to him. Suk_59.4 (=283)

children.text:
ityuktvopapattyā samānītaṃ hayamāruhyajagāma /
gacchantīṃ ca tāṃ tato dṛṣṭvā rāhaḍo 'pi lajjito viguptaśca /
tataḥ strīṇāṃ vaśagaḥ ko na viḍambitaḥ /
yataḥ-
children.translated_text: Having said this, with a pretext she had a horse brought and rode away. Seeing her depart, <s>Rāhaḍa</s> was both ashamed and outwitted. Thus, who among those subject to women has not been made a fool of? For:

children.text: ānanarta purā śambhurgovindo rāsakṛttathā /
children.translated_text: In the past, <s>Śambhu</s> (Śiva) danced, and <s>Govinda</s> (Viṣṇu) likewise performed the <s>rāsa</s> dance;

children.text: brahmā paśutvamāpannaḥ strībhiḥ ko na viḍambitaḥ // Suk_59.5 (=284) //
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> attained the state of a beast — who has not been mocked by women? Suk_59.5 (=284)

children.text: saṃsāravṛkṣamūlaṃ yāḥ pāpakandalabhūmikā /
children.translated_text: Women are the root of the tree of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence), the ground of sinful thorns;

children.text: santāpaphalapuṣpāṇi yoṣitaḥ kiṃ sukhāvahāḥ // Suk_59.6 (=285) //
children.translated_text: their fruits and flowers are torment — how can women bring happiness? Suk_59.6 (=285)

children.text: māyāmūlamidaṃ sarvaṃ tasyā mūlaṃ hi yoṣitaḥ /
children.translated_text: All this is rooted in <s>māyā</s> (illusion), and the root of that illusion is women;

children.text: saṃyogo yoṣitāṃ mūlaṃ taṃ tyaktvā ca sukhāni naḥ // Suk_59.7 (=286) //
children.translated_text: union with women is the root — having abandoned that, happiness is ours. Suk_59.7 (=286)

children.text: tasyedaṃ vacaḥ śrutvā prabhāvatī prāha-
children.translated_text: Having heard these words, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> said:

children.text: utpattikāraṇaṃ tanvī tanvī vṛddheśca kāraṇam /
children.translated_text: A slender woman is the cause of birth, a slender woman is the cause of growth;

children.text: sukhasya kāraṇaṃ tanvī sā kathaṃ kīra duṣyate // Suk_59.8 (=287) //
children.translated_text: a slender woman is the cause of happiness — how then, O parrot, can she be blamed? Suk_59.8 (=287)

children.text: vinā tābhirna sambhogo vinā tābhiḥ sukhaṃ na ca /
children.translated_text: Without them there is no enjoyment, without them there is no happiness;

children.text: vinā tābhirna cātmānaṃ kṛtārthaṃ manyete janaḥ // Suk_59.9 (=288) //
children.translated_text: without them, no one considers himself fulfilled. Suk_59.9 (=288)

children.text: uktañca-
children.translated_text: And it is said:

children.text: amṛtasyeva kuṇḍāni sukhānāmiva khānayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Women are like vessels of <s>amṛta</s> (nectar), like mines of happiness,

children.text: rateriva nidhānāni yoṣitaḥ kena nirmitāḥ // Suk_59.10 (=289) //
children.translated_text: like treasuries of love — by whom were they created? Suk_59.10 (=289)

children.text: priyādarśanemevāstu kimanyairdarśanāntaraiḥ /
children.translated_text: Let there be only the sight of the beloved — what need of other sights?

children.text: prāpyate yatra nirvāṇaṃ sarogeṇāpi cetasā // Suk_59.11 (=290) //
children.translated_text: For through that, even a diseased mind attains <s>nirvāṇa</s> (bliss). Suk_59.11 (=290)

children.text: iti tasyā vacaḥ śrutvā śukaḥ prāha-
children.translated_text: Having heard her words, the parrot said:

children.text: vājivāraṇalohānāṃ kāṣṭhapāṣāṇavāsasām /
children.translated_text: Between horses, elephants, and iron; between wood, stone, and cloth;

children.text: nārīpuruṣatoyānāmantaraṃ bahu vidyate // Suk_59.12 (=291) //
children.translated_text: between women, men, and water — great indeed is the difference. Suk_59.12 (=291)

children.text: etattvayoktaṃ pativratāviṣayaṃ nānyāsu /
children.translated_text: What you have said applies to the faithful wife (<s>pativratā</s>), not to others.

children.text: iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text: Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau ekonapaṣṭitamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifty-ninth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 60:
children.translated_text: START Suk 60:

children.text:
anyadā sā prabhāvatī gamanāya śukaṃ prapaccha /
śukaḥ prāha-
children.translated_text: On another day, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked the parrot about going. The parrot said:

children.text: gaccha devi yadā vetsi saṃśaye kṛtyamāgate /
children.translated_text: 'Go, O queen, if you know what to do when doubt arises,

children.text: vīrasya napateryadvatsabhāyāṃ nṛpadūtakaḥ // Suk_60.1 (=292) //
children.translated_text: as the king's envoy did in the assembly of <s>Vīra</s>'s grandson.' Suk_60.1 (=292)

children.text: prabhāvatyāha-kathametat? śukaḥ-
children.translated_text: <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked: 'How is this?' The parrot said:

children.text: kacchādhipatinā devi tasya rājñaḥ sabhā śrutā /
children.translated_text: 'O queen, the lord of <s>Kaccha</s> heard of that king's assembly,

children.text: vicitrā devanirmitā sarvaratnavibhūṣitā // Suk_60.2 (=293) //
children.translated_text: wondrous, fashioned by the gods, adorned with all manner of gems.' Suk_60.2 (=293)

children.text: tāṃ draṣṭuṃ prahito dūto haridatta iti śrutaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'A messenger named <s>Haridatta</s> was sent to see it,

children.text: sahasraprābhṛto bhīru suratnahayahastakaḥ // Suk_60.3 (=294) //
children.translated_text: bearing gifts worth a thousand, O timid one, along with fine jewels, horses, and elephants.' Suk_60.3 (=294)

children.text:
sa dūtastatpurīṃ gatvā nṛpaṃ dṛṣṭvā taṃ jagāda, "matsvāmināhaṃ sacitrāṃ tava sabhāmavalokayitumutkalitaḥ /
rājā prāha-prātardarśayiṣye /
tato rājñā dvitīyadine dūta ākāritaḥ /
sa ca sahasāgatastāṃ sabhāṃ vicitraratnakhacitāṃ dṛṣṭvā jalamayīṃ sthalamayīṃ veti niścetumaśaktaḥ kathaṃ bhavatviti praśnaḥ /
śukaḥ tataḥ sa pūgīphalaṃ puraḥ kṣiptvā sthalaṃ jñātvā gṛhaṃ yayau /
iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text: That envoy, having gone to that city and seen the king, said to him: 'My master has sent me, eager to behold your wondrous assembly hall.' The king said: 'I shall show it to you in the morning.' Then on the second day, the envoy was summoned by the king. He, having come quickly and seen that assembly hall studded with wondrous gems, was unable to determine whether it was made of water or of solid ground — 'How shall he resolve this?' was the question. The parrot said: He threw an areca nut before him, and knowing it to be solid ground, went home. Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau ṣaṣṭitamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the sixtieth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 61:
children.translated_text: START Suk 61:

children.text:
anyadā sā śukaṃ pacchati sma /
śuka prāha-
children.translated_text: On another day, she asked the parrot. The parrot said:

children.text: gaccha devi gatā vetsi rantuṃ cettvaṃ nijaṃ naram /
children.translated_text: 'Go, O queen, if having gone you know how to enjoy your own man,

children.text: yathā tejukayā pūrvaṃ kṛtaṃ ciramākāṅkṣitam // Suk_61.1 (=295) //
children.translated_text: as <s>Tejukā</s> formerly did, fulfilling her long-cherished desire.' Suk_61.1 (=295)

children.text:
prabhāvatyāha-kathametat? śukaḥ kathayati-asti khorasamabhidhāno grāmaḥ /
tatra vaṇikputraḥ pārśvanāganāmā /
tasya bhāryā rūpasampannā ratalolupā kulaṭā tejukā nāma /
sānyadā sakhībhirvṛtā devayātrālokanāya gatā surūpasyaikasya puṃsaḥ rūpa prekṣya saṅgamāya manaścakre /
yataḥ-
children.translated_text: <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked: 'How is this?' The parrot narrated: There is a village called <s>Khorasama</s>. There lived a merchant's son named <s>Pārśvanāga</s>. His wife, beautiful in form, lustful and wanton, was named <s>Tejukā</s>. One day, accompanied by her friends, she went to see a festival procession and, seeing the beauty of a handsome man, set her mind on union with him. For:

children.text: vivāha devayātrāyāṃ rājaveśmani saṅkaṭe /
children.translated_text: 'At a wedding, at a festival procession, in a king's palace, in a crowd,

children.text: paragehe vivāde ca devi nārī vinaśyati // Suk_61.2 (=296) //
children.translated_text: in another's house, or in a dispute, O queen, a woman is ruined.' Suk_61.2 (=296)

children.text: uktañca-
children.translated_text: And it is said:

children.text: gṛhe 'raṇye tathā deve havye tīrthe jalāśaye /
children.translated_text: 'At home, in a forest, at a temple, at a sacrifice, at a pilgrimage site, at a lake,

children.text: vivāhe cotsave nityaṃ mālinīnilaye tathā // Suk_61.3 (=297) //
children.translated_text: at a wedding, at a festival, always, at a garland-maker's dwelling likewise,' Suk_61.3 (=297)

children.text: yātrāyāṃ strīsamūhe ca nirjane janasaṅkule /
children.translated_text: 'at a procession, in a group of women, in a deserted place, in a crowded place,

children.text: pattane ca tathā grāme svacchandā dvāravartinī // Suk_61.4 (=298) //
children.translated_text: in a town, in a village, a woman who stands freely at the door,' Suk_61.4 (=298)

children.text: khale kṣetre pravāse ca mārge veśmani catvare /
children.translated_text: 'at a threshing floor, in a field, while traveling, on a road, in a house, at a crossroads,

children.text: praveśe nirgame rājñāṃ sadā yā kautukapriyā // Suk_61.5 (=299) //
children.translated_text: at the entrance and exit of kings, a woman who always delights in spectacles,' Suk_61.5 (=299)

children.text: prativeśmagṛhe śūnye rajakīsūcikīgṛhe /
children.translated_text: 'at a neighbor's house, in an empty house, at a washerwoman's or seamstress's house,

children.text: divā rātrau ca sandhyāyāṃ durdine rājacatvare /
children.translated_text: by day, by night, at twilight, on a rainy day, at the royal square,

children.text: śoke ca vyasane bhartuḥ svacchandā strī vinaśyati // Suk_61.6 (=300) //
children.translated_text: in grief and in her husband's misfortune — a woman who acts freely is ruined.' Suk_61.6 (=300)

children.text:
tejukā ca taṃ dṛṣṭvā bhrūsaṃjñayā āhūyedamabravīt-ahaṃ tavāsaktā paraṃ madīyo bhartā duḥsaho niṣṭhuraśca gṛhādbahirnirgantuṃ notsahe /
ato yasmiṃstasmindivase 'smadgṛhadvāri ghaṭe kṣiptvā vṛściko moktavyaḥ /
tadāhaṃ paścikadaṣṭā bhaviṣyāmi /
tvayāsmadgṛhadvāri vaidyena bhāvyam /
iti saṅketaṃ vidhāya svagṛhaṃ jagmatuḥ /
tenāpi tathā kṛtam /
sāpi ghaṭaṃ khaṭvocchīrṣake kṣiptvā iti jagāda-ahamanena vṛścikena ghaṭasthena daṣṭā'-iti rāraṭīti /
so 'pi ca puruṣastadā vaidyo bhūtvā tadgṛhadvāri tasthau /
"tāḍaṃ bandhau poṭṭaṃ malau sūlaṃ pheḍau visaṃ harau"
[tālaṃ badhnāmi, udaraṃ marddayāmi, śūlaṃ spheṭayāmi, viṣaṃ harāmi] iti jalpati /
tadā ca sā bhartāraṃ jagāda /
children.translated_text: <s>Tejukā</s>, having seen him, beckoned him with a gesture of her brows and said: 'I am attached to you, but my husband is unbearable and harsh, and I dare not go out of the house. Therefore, on whatever day [you come], you must place a scorpion in a pot and release it at the door of our house. Then I shall pretend to have been stung by a scorpion. You must present yourself as a physician at the door of our house.' Having arranged this signal, both went to their homes. He did exactly so. She too, throwing the pot at the head of the bed, cried out: 'I have been stung by this scorpion that was in the pot!' — and wailed. That man, having become a physician, stood at the door of her house and called out: 'I tie up swellings, I massage the belly, I lance abscesses, I remove poison!' [In Prakrit: tāḍaṃ bandhau poṭṭaṃ malau sūlaṃ pheḍau visaṃ harau.] Then she said to her husband:

children.text: dehi kāṣṭhāni me nātha mariṣyāmi na saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Give me wood, O lord — I shall surely die, there is no doubt;

children.text: āhūya mantrikānvaidyān gatārttiṃ vā kuruṣva mām // Suk_61.7 (=301) //
children.translated_text: or summon healers and physicians and free me from this affliction.' Suk_61.7 (=301)

children.text:
tatastadbhartā gṛhādbahiḥ sthitaṃ tamākārayāmāsa /
vaidyo 'pi tāṃ dṛṣṭvā tatpatiṃ jagāda /
yadyeṣā kāladaṣṭā jīvati tatastvaṃ bhāgyavānahamapi yaśaḥpātraṃ bhavāmi /
vaṇigāha-vaidya! prasādaṃ vidhāya enāṃ viṣarahitāṃ kuru /
tataḥ sa vaidyaḥ kenāpi kaṭukabhaiṣajyena vanitauṣṭhamālipya tatpatimāha- aho vaṇiksarveṣāmapi viṣāṇāṃ samadhikaṃ mānuṣaviṣameva /
tato viṣasya viṣamauṣadhamiti kṛtvā tvamasyā oṣṭhaṃ dhāva /
tato vaṇik tathā kartumārebhe /
kṣaṇamātreṇatasya vaṇijaḥ kaṭukauṣadhamiśrauṣṭhāsvādena mukhaṃ kaṭukaṃ sañjātam /
tato vaṇigāha-tvamevoṣṭha dhāvetyuktvā vaṇik sthitaḥ /
vaṇijo 'pi viṣaśaṅkārūḍhā /
tato bahirgate vaṇiji vaidyena sā kāmārtā yathecchaṃ bhojitā /
tadanantaraṃ sā māyinī svasthābhūt /
vaṇigapi kṣaṇena svastho babhūva /
upakṛtaśca vaidyastena caraṇaiḥ spṛṣṭvā tvadīyo 'smīti /
tataḥ sa vaidyacchadmanā gṛhamāyāti satataṃ vaṇiji bahirgate bhuṅkte ca tāṃ nityam /
tato bhāmini evaṃ kartuṃ vaktuṃ ca yadi jānāsi tato yāhi /
children.translated_text: Then her husband summoned that man standing outside the house. The physician, seeing her, said to her husband: 'If this woman, bitten at a fatal hour, survives, then you are fortunate and I too shall become renowned.' The merchant said: 'Physician! Show your grace and free her from the poison.' Then that physician, having smeared the woman's lips with some bitter medicine, said to her husband: 'O merchant, of all poisons, human poison is the most potent. Therefore, since poison is the medicine for poison, you must lick her lips.' Then the merchant began to do so. In a moment, from tasting the bitter medicine mixed on her lips, his mouth became bitter. Then the merchant said: 'You yourself lick her lips' — and the merchant stood by. The merchant's suspicion of poison grew. Then, when the merchant had gone outside, the physician, [being her lover], satisfied that desire-afflicted woman as she wished. Afterwards, that crafty woman became well. The merchant too recovered in a moment. And the physician was honored by him — touching his feet, [the merchant said]: 'I am yours.' Thereafter, under the guise of a physician, he would come to the house constantly, and whenever the merchant went out, he would enjoy her regularly. Therefore, O beautiful one, if you know how to act and speak thus, then go.

children.text: evaṃ kartuṃ ca vaktuṃ ca yo jānāti chalapriyaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who knows how to act and speak thus, being fond of trickery,

children.text: sa karotu sa yātvevaṃ kartuṃ bhoktuṃ nijaṃ hitam // Suk_61.8 (=302) //
children.translated_text: let him act, let him go as he pleases — to do and enjoy what is in his own interest. Suk_61.8 (=302)

children.text: iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text: Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau ekaṣaṣṭitamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the sixty-first tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 62:
children.translated_text: START Suk 62:

children.text:
anyadā sā prabhāvatī śukamāpṛcchati /
śakuḥ prāha-
children.translated_text: On another day, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked the parrot. The parrot said:

children.text: priyamevānubhoktavyaṃ yāhi devi tadarthinī /
children.translated_text: 'Pleasure alone is to be enjoyed — go, O queen, desirous of that,

children.text: kuhanasya yathā kānte saṅkaṭe 'si kṣamottare // Suk_62.1 (=303) //
children.translated_text: if you are able to endure a difficult situation, like the wife of <s>Kuhana</s>, O beloved.' Suk_62.1 (=303)

children.text:
asti gambhīrākhyo grāmaḥ /
tatra kuhano nāma rājaputrar irṣyāluḥ śūro jaḍaḥ strīpriyo durdharaśca /
tasyābhūtāṃ dve kalatre śobhikātejikākhye ratalolupe parapuruṣalampaṭe surūpe /
tadbhartā tadrakṣaṇāya grāmādbahirnadītīre gṛhaṃ keca dvārasthaste rakṣayati /
anyadā sa tābhyāmuktaḥ-yadā kaścinnāpitaḥ samabhyeti tadā bhavyaṃ bhavati /
tatastenāpi bhrāmako nāpitaḥ preṣitaḥ pratisīrāntaraistayornakhakalpanāya /
tataśca tayoścaraṇān tiraskariṇībahiḥsthānnāpitaḥ prakṣalayati /
patiścādūre pathi niviṣṭaḥ /
tābhyāṃ ca sa nāpitaḥ suvarṇakaṭakamarpayitvā pracchannamevamuktaḥ-etad dravyaṃ gṛhītvā āvayoḥ kenāpi sārdhaṃ saṃyogaṃ vidhehi /
divākīrtirapi tatheti pratijñāya rājaputramāpṛcchya jagāma /
anyadātmamitraṃ navayauvanaṃ kalāpātramanudgataśmaśruṃ strīveṣaṃ kārayitvā tayoḥ patyuḥ pārśve tena saha samāgatya nāpita idamāha-mameyaṃ vallabhā /
ahaṃ ca grāmāntaraṃ jigamiṣuryuṣmadgṛhaṃ vinānyatra moktuṃ na śaknomi /
yato bhavatāṃ gṛhe strīyantraṇā bhavyā /
ityukte tena pratipannaṃ muñceti /
tataścaṇḍālo 'pi taṃ muktvā tayoḥ pārśve gato jagāda-yadiyaṃ yuṣmābhirātmīyā karaṇīyā /
tataste taṃ caṇḍālānītaṃ jñātvā bahu menāte /
sa ca divā strīrūpī rātrau ca kāmukaḥ rājaputrakalatre prativāraṃ bhuṅkta /
sa ca rājaputraḥ strīlolupastatsaṅgamāya spṛhayati /
yayāce ca tāṃ nityam /
sā tu kapaṭīstrī neti jagāda /
rājaputrasya strītve bhrāntirutpannā tadbhāntimapanetuṃ nijakalatre jagāda-tato devyādeśānmayā prātarmahotsavo vidheyaḥ /
tatra bhavatībhirvivastrābhistisṛbhirapi nartitavyam /
tataḥ sa strīcchannā kathaṃ nṛtyatu iti praśnaḥ /
uttaram śukaḥ-tantryā liṅgāgraṃ niyamya gudamadhyagamānamya sphuṭāṃ bhagākṛtiṃ kṛtvā patyau samāgate sahastatālaṃ sarvā evaṃ vadantyo nanṛtuḥ /
children.translated_text: There is a village called <s>Gambhīrā</s>. There lived a prince named <s>Kuhana</s>, who was jealous, brave, dull-witted, fond of women, and overbearing. He had two wives named <s>Śobhikā</s> and <s>Tejikā</s>, who were lustful, desirous of other men, and beautiful. Their husband, to guard them, built a house outside the village on the riverbank and posted guards at the door to watch them. One day, they said to him: 'Whenever a certain barber comes, it will be auspicious.' Then he also sent a barber named <s>Bhrāmaka</s> behind the screens to trim their nails. And that barber would wash their feet outside the screen. The husband was seated on the path at a distance. They gave that barber a golden bracelet and secretly told him: 'Take this wealth and arrange a meeting for us with some man.' <s>Divākīrti</s> (the barber), having promised to do so, took leave of the prince and departed. On another occasion, he dressed his own young friend — a beardless youth skilled in the arts — in women's clothing, and bringing him along, came to the prince's presence and said: 'This is my wife. I wish to go to another village and cannot leave her anywhere except in your house. For in your house, there is strict control of women.' When told thus, the prince agreed: 'Leave her.' Then a <s>Caṇḍāla</s> (guard) also, leaving that person with the two wives, went and said: 'You should treat this woman as your own.' They, knowing that [person] was brought by the <s>Caṇḍāla</s> (barber), esteemed him greatly. By day he appeared in woman's dress; by night, as a lover, he enjoyed the prince's two wives in turn. And that prince, being fond of women, desired union with that [supposed woman]. He constantly solicited her. But that woman-disguised man said no. The prince developed the delusion that she was truly a woman. To remove his delusion, his wives said to him: 'By the queen's command, I must hold a great festival tomorrow morning. At that festival, all three of us must dance naked.' Then how would the one disguised as a woman dance? — this is the question. The parrot answered: Having tied the tip of the male organ with a string, bending it back through the buttocks, making a convincing appearance of female anatomy, when the husband arrived, all of them danced together clapping their hands and singing:

children.text: nisuhara ṇāccai saṃkalidaṃ jaṃ manasi kidaṃ makkaṭījālaṃ /
children.translated_text: 'Watch! She dances as she has contrived in her mind — this monkey's trick!

children.text: ṇāhi ṇāhi pṛchaha attha dharei ṇāda bhilukalattu karei // Suk_62.2 (=304) //
children.translated_text: No, no — ask [her], otherwise she holds [it] back; know this: she is making a split household!' Suk_62.2 (=304)

children.text: [niśāmaya nṛtyati saṅkalitaṃ yanmanasi kṛtaṃ markaṭījālam /
children.translated_text: ['Watch! She dances as she has contrived in her mind — this monkey's trick!

children.text: nahi nahi pṛccha athodhriyate jñātaṃ bhinnakalatraṃ karoti] // Suk_62.2* (=304*) //
children.translated_text: No, no — ask [her], otherwise she holds [it] back; know this: she is making a split household!'] Suk_62.2* (=304*)

children.text:
rājaputro 'rthaṃ papraccha /
tābhyāmuktam-markaṭā kaṭisandhirucyate /
tatastasyāṃ truṭitāyāṃ rājaputronyatkalatraṃ kuryādityarthaḥ /
tato rājaputraḥ strīcaritraparāṅmukho mūḍhadhīḥ pratītaḥ, itarastu tathaiva strīveṣeṇa kalatre bhuṅkte /
children.translated_text: The prince asked the meaning. They said: 'The "monkey's waist-joint" refers to [her] hip-joint. When that breaks, the prince will take another wife' — such was the meaning. Then the prince, his mind turned away from women's nature, convinced in his dull understanding, [accepted this]. And the other one, still in woman's disguise, continued to enjoy the wives.

children.text: tasmādyaḥ saṅkaṭe vetti kartuṃ vaktuṃ ca bhāmini /
children.translated_text: Therefore, one who knows how to act and speak in a difficult situation, O beautiful one,

children.text: sa yātvatra yathākāmaṃ yathākālaṃ yathāsukham // Suk_62.3 (=305) //
children.translated_text: let that one go as desired, at the right time, at ease. Suk_62.3 (=305)

children.text: iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text: Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau dviṣaṣṭitamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the sixty-second tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 63:
children.translated_text: START Suk 63:

children.text:
anyasminpradoṣe prabhāvatī yāmīti śukaṃ pratyāha /
śukaḥ prāha-
children.translated_text: On another evening, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> said to the parrot: 'I shall go.' The parrot said:

children.text: yāhi devi na doṣo 'tra manoduḥkhe samāgate /
children.translated_text: 'Go, O queen — there is no fault in this when mental anguish has come;

children.text: tadrduḥkhaśamanaṃ kartuṃ vetsi cecchakaṭālavat // Suk_63.1 (=306) //
children.translated_text: if you know how to allay that sorrow, like <s>Śakaṭāla</s>.' Suk_63.1 (=306)

children.text:
yathā śakaṭālena nijakuṭumbabharaṇāya samudbhavadduḥkhaṃ cāṇakyapārśvannandakulamucchedya duḥkhaśamanaṃ kṛtaṃ tathā tvameva.................... tasmāttava paragṛhaṃ gantuṃ na yujyate /
uktañca-
children.translated_text: Just as <s>Śakaṭāla</s>, in order to alleviate the suffering arising from maintaining his own family, destroyed the <s>Nanda</s> dynasty with the help of <s>Cāṇakya</s> and thus removed his suffering, so you too.................... Therefore it is not proper for you to go to another's house. And it is said:

children.text: uḍugaṇaparivāro nāyako 'pyoṣadhīnāmamṛtamayaśarīraḥ kāntiyukto 'pi candraḥ /
children.translated_text: Even the moon, who is the leader of the stars, his retinue, and the lord of herbs, whose body is made of nectar and who is endowed with beauty,

children.text: bhavati vikalamūrtirmaṇḍalaṃ prāpya bhānoḥ parasadananiviṣṭaḥ ko na dhatte laghutvam // Suk_63.2 (=307) //
children.translated_text: becomes diminished in form upon reaching the orb of the sun — who does not become diminished when dwelling in another's house? Suk_63.2 (=307)

children.text: iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text: Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau triṣaṣṭitamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the sixty-third tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 64:
children.translated_text: START Suk 64:

children.text:
anyadā prabhāvatī śukamāpṛcchati sma /
so 'pyāha-
children.translated_text: On another day, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked the parrot for permission. He said:

children.text: gaccha cedviṣame vetsi kartuṃ kiñcitkṛśodari /
children.translated_text: Go, if in a difficult situation you know how to do something, O slender-waisted one,

children.text: kṛtaṃ devikayā yadvatsakhījāravimuktaye // Suk_64.1 (=308) //
children.translated_text: as <s>Devikā</s> did to free her friend's lover. Suk_64.1 (=308)

children.text:
prabhāvatī prāha-kathametat? śukaḥ asti kūṭapurābhidho grāmaḥ /
rājaputraḥ somarājaḥ /
tasya maṇḍukā nāma patnī priyadarśanā narāntaralolupā /
tāñcaiko naraḥ kṛtasaṃketaḥ saghaṇṭako rātrau gṛhāṅgaṇe bhuṅkte /
tatpatirghaṇṭāśabdaṃ śṛṇvannekadā laguḍamādāya pradhāvitaḥ ṣaṇḍaśaṅkayā /
tataḥ ṣaṇḍaveśadhārī upapatiḥ /
kathaṃ bhavitviti praśnaḥ /
śukaḥ-devikā nāma sakho maṇḍukāyāḥ patiṃ ghaṇṭāśabdānusāriṇamāgacchantaṃ dṛṣṭvā jārasya naśyato ghaṇṭātālāṃ haste dhṛtvā taṃ prati jagāda bhāvuka! kāndiśīko vṛṣo naṣṭaḥ /
tataḥ sa vyāvṛtya nijapauruṣaṃ patnyai kathayāmāsa /
iti katāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text: <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked: 'How so?' The parrot said: There is a village called <s>Kūṭapura</s>. The prince was <s>Somarāja</s>. His wife, named <s>Maṇḍukā</s>, was fair-faced and desirous of other men. A certain man, who had arranged a signal with her, wearing a bell, would enjoy her in the courtyard of the house at night. Her husband, hearing the sound of the bell one night, seized a cudgel and rushed out, suspecting a bull. Thereupon the paramour came wearing the disguise of a bull. 'What should happen?' — this is the question. The parrot said: <s>Devikā</s>, a friend of <s>Maṇḍukā</s>, seeing her husband approaching, following the sound of the bell, seized the bell-clapper from the fleeing lover's hand and said to [the husband]: 'Good sir! A stray bull has run away!' Thereupon he turned back and told his wife of his own valor. Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau catuḥṣaṣṭitamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the sixty-fourth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 65:
children.translated_text: START Suk 65:

children.text:
anyadā prabhāvatī śukaṃ pṛcchati /
śukaḥ-
children.translated_text: On another day, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked the parrot. The parrot said:

children.text: yujyate gamanaṃ devi tava tatra prabhāvati /
children.translated_text: Going is proper for you, O lady <s>Prabhāvatī</s>, to that place,

children.text: vetsi cedviṣame vaktuṃ sitavastra ivākulaḥ // Suk_65.1 (=309) //
children.translated_text: if in a difficult situation you know what to say, like the white-clothed one in confusion. Suk_65.1 (=309)

children.text:
asti devi janasthānaṃ nāma pattanam /
tatra nandano nāma rājā yathārthaḥ /
tatpattane śrīvatso nāma śrāvakaḥ paraṃ maheśvararataḥ /
tena anyadā vāraṇasīṃ nagarīṃ prati prasthitena saśiṣyena pathi gacchatā /
ekaḥ śiṣyaḥ māṃsaharaṇāya sthāpitaḥ /
anyaśrāvakairdṛṣṭaḥ sa kathaṃ bhavatviti praśnaḥ /
śukaḥ prāha-yadā sarvaśrāvakā āgatyopaviṣṭāḥ tadāṭṭahāsaṃ jahāsa /
pṛṣṭaḥ sarvairjagādar-idṛśo 'yaṃ śiṣya- /
mayoktaṃ māṃ saṃvartata abuddhyā anena māṃsasya........ /
iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text: There is, O lady, a town called <s>Janasthāna</s>. There was a king named <s>Nandana</s>, true to his name. In that town there was a <s>Śrāvaka</s> (Jain layman) named <s>Śrīvatsa</s>, who was supremely devoted to Lord <s>Maheśvara</s>. One day, having set out toward the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, traveling on the road with his disciples, he stationed one disciple to procure meat. He was seen by other <s>Śrāvakas</s>. 'What should happen?' — this is the question. The parrot said: When all the <s>Śrāvakas</s> came and sat down, he burst into loud laughter. When asked by all, he said: 'Such is this disciple! I told him to attend to me, but out of foolishness he [went after] meat......' Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau pañcaṣaṣṭitamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the sixty-fifth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 66:
children.translated_text: START Suk 66:

children.text:
anyadā sā prabhāvatī calitā śukaṃ pṛcchati /
śukaḥ-
children.translated_text: On another day, <s>Prabhāvatī</s>, having set out, asked the parrot. The parrot said:

children.text: gaccha devi na kartavyo vilambaḥ puṇyakarmaṇi /
children.translated_text: Go, O lady, one should not delay in meritorious deeds,

children.text: yadi vetsi bhaye kartuṃ subuddhirhaṃsarāḍiva // Suk_66.1 (=310) //
children.translated_text: if in a fearful situation you know how to act wisely, like the king of swans. Suk_66.1 (=310)

children.text: asti devi dharāpṛṣṭhe ramyaṃ kṣīṇanarākulam /
children.translated_text: There is, O lady, on the surface of the earth, a delightful [forest] teeming with small creatures,

children.text: daśayojanavistīrṇaṃ vanaṃ vihagavallabham // Suk_66.2 (=311) //
children.translated_text: a forest ten <s>yojanas</s> (leagues) wide, beloved of birds. Suk_66.2 (=311)

children.text:
tatra gavyūtivistīrṇe śītacchāye jalāśayatīrasthite vaṭe śaṅkhadhavalo nāma haṃsarāṭ sakuṭumbo medinīṃ bhrāntvā dinātyaye śete /
anyadā teṣu haṃseṣu bhramaṇāya gateṣu pāparddhinā jālaṃ baddham /
pradoṣāgatāḥ patitāḥ sarve 'pi kathaṃ mucyante-iti praśnaḥ /
śukaḥ-tatastu svaṃ kuṭumbaṃ tathā baddhaṃ jñātvā rātrau śaṅkhadhavalaḥ prāha-re re putrāḥ! yādasau lubdhakaḥ prātarbhūruhaṃ samāruhya yuṣmānavalokayati tadā bhavadbhirmṛtakalpairucchvāsaniḥśvāsarahitaiḥ sthātavyam /
so 'pi yuṣmānmṛtāniti jñātvā yadā bhūmau sarvān kṣipati tadā sarvairapyuḍḍīya gantavyam /
iti kṛte lubdhakaḥ prātaḥ samāyayau /
tena te mṛtā iti jñātvā bhūmau kṣiptāstadā te uḍḍīya kāṅkṣitaṃ deśaṃ yayuḥ /
iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text: There, on a banyan tree situated by the shore of a cool, shady lake, one <s>gavyūti</s> (league) wide, a swan-king named <s>Śaṅkhadhavala</s> (Conch-White), with his family, would sleep at the end of each day after roaming the earth. One day, when the swans had gone out to forage, an evil hunter set a net. When they returned at dusk, they all fell into it. 'How shall they be freed?' — this is the question. The parrot said: Then <s>Śaṅkhadhavala</s>, knowing that his family was thus trapped, said at night: 'O children! When that hunter climbs the tree at dawn and observes you, you must all remain as if dead, without breathing in or out. When he, thinking you are dead, throws you all to the ground, then you must all fly away.' This being done, the hunter came in the morning. Thinking them dead, he threw them to the ground, and then they all flew away to the desired land. Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau ṣaṭṣaṣṭitamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the sixty-sixth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 67:
children.translated_text: START Suk 67:

children.text:
anyadā calitā prabhāvatī śukaṃ pṛcchati sma /
śukaḥ-
children.translated_text: On another day, <s>Prabhāvatī</s>, having set out, asked the parrot. The parrot said:

children.text: atha cedyāsi kāmārtā yāhi bhīru gatā satī /
children.translated_text: If you go, tormented by desire, then go, O timid one, having resolved,

children.text: plavaṅgama ivātmīyaṃ vaktuṃ vetsi yathāhitam // Suk_67.1 (=312) //
children.translated_text: if, like the monkey, you know how to speak what is beneficial to yourself. Suk_67.1 (=312)

children.text:
asti puṣpākaraṃ nāma vanam /
tatra vanapriyo nāma vāmanavānaraḥ /
sa kadācitsamudrāntamaryādājale luṭhantaṃ makaraṃ dṛṣṭvā prāha-"mitra! kiṃ jīvitanirviṇṇastvaṃ yadadya dharābhūmau samāgataḥ' /
iti vacaḥ śrutvā makaro 'pyāha-
children.translated_text: There is a forest named <s>Puṣpākara</s> (Flower-Mine). There lived a dwarf monkey named <s>Vanapriya</s> (Forest-Lover). One day, seeing a crocodile rolling about in the water at the ocean's boundary, he said: 'Friend! Are you so weary of life that you have come today to the land?' Hearing these words, the crocodile replied:

children.text: yasya yadvihitaṃ sthānaṃ yasya yadvetanaṃ kṛtam /
children.translated_text: The mind of a person delights only in the place allotted to him and in the livelihood appointed for him,

children.text: tatraiva ramate cittaṃ tasya nānyatra vānara // Suk_67.2 (=313) //
children.translated_text: and not elsewhere, O monkey. Suk_67.2 (=313)

children.text: uktañca-
children.translated_text: And it is said:

children.text: sarvasvarṇamayī laṅkā na me lakṣmaṇa rocate /
children.translated_text: All-golden <s>Laṅkā</s> does not please me, O <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>;

children.text: pitṛkramāgatāyodhyā nirdhanāpi sukhāyate // Suk_67.3 (=314) //
children.translated_text: <s>Ayodhyā</s>, inherited from my fathers, brings happiness even without wealth. Suk_67.3 (=314)

children.text: jaṇaṇīṃ jammaṇabhūmiṃ piasaṃgaṃ jīviaṃ dhaṇāsaṃghaṃ /
children.translated_text: One's mother, one's birthplace, the company of the beloved, one's life, the accumulation of wealth,

children.text: pacchimaṇiddā virikāmiṇiṃ ca dukkhehi muñcanti // Suk_67.4 (=315) //
children.translated_text: the last sleep, and a beautiful woman — these are relinquished only with suffering. Suk_67.4 (=315)

children.text: [jananīṃ janmabhūmiṃ priyasaṅgaṃ jīvitaṃ dhanāsaṅgam /
children.translated_text: [One's mother, one's birthplace, the company of the beloved, one's life, the accumulation of wealth,

children.text: paścimanidrāṃ varakāminīñca duḥkhena muñcanti] // Suk_67.4* (=315*) //
children.translated_text: the last sleep, and a beautiful woman — these are relinquished only with suffering.] Suk_67.4* (=315*)

children.text:
tadahaṃ saphalajanmā saṃvṛttastvadīyadarśanena /
uktañca-
children.translated_text: 'Thus my birth has become fruitful through seeing you.' And it is said:

children.text: sādhūnāṃ darśanaṃ puṇyaṃ tīrthabhūtā hi sādhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: The sight of the virtuous is meritorious, for the virtuous are like sacred fords;

children.text: tīrthaṃ phalati kālena sadyaḥ sādhusamāmamaḥ // Suk_67.5 (=316) //
children.translated_text: a sacred ford bears fruit in time, but the company of the virtuous bears fruit immediately. Suk_67.5 (=316)

children.text:
tasmātsthalotpannaḥ prāṇivargastu dhanyo yatra bhavādṛsaśāḥ priyavādino vartante /
iti śrutvā vānara āha-"aho makara! tvamadyaprabhṛti me prāṇādhikaṃ mitram /
tvameva sauhṛdyavacasāṃ vaktā /
uktañca- yataḥ satāṃ sannatagātri saṅgataṃ manīṣibhiḥ sāptapadīnasucyate /
ityuktvā punaḥ prāha-mitra! tvamadyātithirasmākaṃ bhava' /
iti bhaṇitvā amṛtasadṛśāni pakvaphalāni dadau /
tataḥ prabhṛti pratidinaṃ kadalīphalāni yacchati /
makaro 'pi nijadayitāyā arpayati /
sā ca patiṃ tatphalavṛttāntaṃ pṛcchati /
sa ca sarvaṃ yathāsthitaṃ nivedayati /
tataḥ sā garbhānubhāvataścintayāmāsa-"yo vānaro nityamīdṛśāni phalāni bhuṅkte tasyaurasyaṃ māṃsamamṛtopamaṃ syāt' /
iti vicintya patiṃ prāha-"mama garbhānubhāvato vānarahṛdayapiśitabhakṣaṇe dohado vidyate /
tadyadi pūrayasi tadā jīvāmi anyathāsaṃśayaṃ mama mṛtyurbhaviṣyati' /
iti śrutvā dayitāgrahācca samudrataṭamāgatya vānaraṃ prāha-"mitra! tvadīyabhrātuḥ priyā tvāmākārayati /
asmadīyo gṛhopacāro vilokanīyaḥ' /
ityuktvā viśvāsya pṛṣṭhe cāropya pracalitaḥ /
vānarastaṃ gacchantaṃ śaṅkitaḥ prāha-tatra gatena mayā kiṃ videyam? ityākarṇya makareṇa cintitam-"vānaro 'sau tasmātsthānānmayā nītaḥ kathamambhonidhitaṭaṃ yāsyati, tasmātkathayāmi'-ityavadhārya yathāsthitaṃ jagāda /
tato vānaraḥ kathaṃ bhavatviti praśnaḥ /
śukaḥ-vānaraḥ prāha-bho makara! tarhi tvaṃ māṃ tatra vṛthā nayasi yato 'haṃ hṛdayahīno bhavāmi /
mama hṛdayaṃ mama pārśve nāsti /
makaraḥ-kva muktaṃ tvayā /
vānaraḥ-mitra! kiṃ na śrutaṃ tvayā?
children.translated_text: 'Therefore the community of land-dwelling creatures is blessed where there are sweet-spoken beings like you.' Hearing this, the monkey said: 'O crocodile! From this day onward, you are a friend dearer to me than life itself. You alone are the speaker of words of friendship.' And it is said: 'Because the company of the virtuous, O one of graceful limbs, is declared by the wise as a seven-step bond.' Having said this, he further said: 'Friend! Be our guest today.' Having said this, he gave him ripe fruits equal to nectar. From that day onward, he gave him banana fruits every day. The crocodile would also give them to his own beloved. She asked her husband about the origin of those fruits. He told her everything as it was. Then she, under the influence of pregnancy cravings, thought: 'A monkey who constantly eats such fruits — his heart-flesh must be like nectar.' Having thus reflected, she said to her husband: 'I have a pregnancy craving to eat the heart-flesh of the monkey. If you fulfill it, I shall live; otherwise, without doubt, death will befall me.' Hearing this, and compelled by his wife's insistence, he came to the seashore and said to the monkey: 'Friend! Your brother's wife invites you. Our household hospitality should be seen.' Having thus gained his trust and mounted him on his back, he set off. The monkey, suspicious of him as he went, said: 'What is to be done by me upon going there?' Hearing this, the crocodile thought: 'That monkey has been brought by me from that place — how will he reach the ocean shore [to escape]? Therefore I shall tell him' — and having so resolved, he told him everything as it was. Then 'What shall the monkey do?' — this is the question. The parrot said: The monkey said: 'O crocodile! Then you are taking me there in vain, since I am without a heart. My heart is not with me.' The crocodile said: 'Where did you leave it?' The monkey said: 'Friend! Have you not heard?'

children.text: sarvadodumbaro vṛkṣe hṛdayaṃ vṛṭabhūruhe /
children.translated_text: The heart of [a monkey] is always in the <s>udumbara</s> (fig) tree, in the broad tree;

children.text: cittamasti gṛhītvā tadāgacchāmi punarjalam // Suk_67.6 (=317) //
children.translated_text: my heart is there — having taken it, I shall return to the water. Suk_67.6 (=317)

children.text:
ityukte tadā makaro mūrkhaḥ samudrāntamāyayau /
vānaro 'pi tatpṛṣṭhataḥ samuttīrya śākhinamārohati sma /
tato makaraṃ jagāda gaccha /
nāhaṃ bhāvadṛśairatrastho gṛhītuṃ śakyaḥ /
children.translated_text: When this was said, the foolish crocodile came to the ocean's edge. The monkey, having dismounted from his back, climbed a tree. Then he said to the crocodile: 'Go! I cannot be caught by those like you who dwell here.'

children.text: jalajantucarairnityaṃ jalamārgānusāribhiḥ /
children.translated_text: With water-creatures who always follow the water-paths,

children.text: sthalajaiḥ saṃgatirna syāt dhruveti munibhāṣitam // Suk_67.7 (=318) //
children.translated_text: land-dwellers should never associate — this is certainly the saying of sages. Suk_67.7 (=318)

children.text:
iti nirbhartsito vānareṇa makaraḥ svagṛhaṃ yayau /
uktañca-
children.translated_text: Thus rebuked by the monkey, the crocodile went to his own home. And it is said:

children.text: utpannā yuktikāryeṣu buddhiryasya na hīyate /
children.translated_text: He whose intelligence, born in matters requiring resourcefulness, does not diminish,

children.text: sa eva tarate durgaṃ jalānte vānaro yathā // Suk_67.8 (=319) //
children.translated_text: he alone crosses danger, like the monkey at the water's edge. Suk_67.8 (=319)

children.text: iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text: Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau saptaṣaṣṭitamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the sixty-seventh tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 68:
children.translated_text: START Suk 68:

children.text:
athānyedyuḥ śukaṃ prāha prabhāvatī /
śukaḥ-
children.translated_text: Then on the next day, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> addressed the parrot. The parrot said:

children.text: yāhi devi sukhaṃ bhuṅkṣva yadi te 'sti sahāyinī /
children.translated_text: Go, O lady, and enjoy happiness, if you have an ally

children.text: vitarkasadṛśī kāle viṣame varavarṇini // Suk_68.1 (=320) //
children.translated_text: whose resourcefulness matches the occasion in a difficult situation, O fair-complexioned one. Suk_68.1 (=320)

children.text:
asti vidyāsthānaṃ nāma grāmaḥ brāhmaṇānām /
tatra keśavo brāhmaṇaḥ /
tena ca snānāya gatena taṭāke ramyā vaṇikputrī dṛṣṭā /
sa ca tāṃ rantumicchati /
anyadā tayā prokto dvijaḥ snānādutthitaḥ-"yattvaṃ mama śirasi dvitīyaṃ ghaṭamāropaya' /
atastena ghaṭamāropayatā tasyā oṣṭhaścumbitaḥ sa ca tathā kurvan patinā dṛṣṭaḥ /
nīto rājakulaṃ kathaṃ mucyatām iti praśnaḥ /
uttaraṃ śukaḥ prāha-atha tanmitraṃ vitarko nāma /
sa ca tatsamīpamāgagatyedamabravīt-"mitra! tvayā rājakulagatena vacacevatyeva vākyaṃ jalpanīyaṃ nānyat /
tathā kṛte ca mantriṇoktam-"nāyaṃ doṣabhāk /
prakṛtirevaṃvidhaivāsya /
tenaiva cottareṇa loke sādhutāṃ gato vitarkasāhāyikabuddhyā /
yadi tvamapi tathā jānāsi tadā gaccha /
iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī supta /
children.translated_text: There is a village of <s>brāhmaṇas</s> named <s>Vidyāsthāna</s> (Seat of Learning). There lived a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Keśava</s>. One day, having gone to a tank for bathing, he saw a beautiful merchant's daughter. He desired to sport with her. On another occasion, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, having risen from his bath, was addressed by her: 'Please place a second water-pot upon my head.' While placing the pot, he kissed her lips, and was seen doing so by her husband. He was taken to the royal court. 'How shall he be freed?' — this is the question. The answer: The parrot said: His friend, named <s>Vitarka</s>, came to him and said: 'Friend! When you have gone to the royal court, you must only utter the words "indeed, indeed" and nothing else.' When this was done, the minister said: 'This man is not guilty. Such is simply his nature.' And by that very answer, through the wit of his friend <s>Vitarka</s>, he attained a reputation for virtue in the world. If you too know such [wit], then go. Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau aṣṭaṣṭitamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the sixty-eighth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 69:
children.translated_text: START Suk 69:

children.text:
anyadā prabhāvatī śukaṃ pṛcchati /
śukaḥ prāha-
children.translated_text: On another day, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> asked the parrot. The parrot said:

children.text: kuru jāraṃ viśālākṣi vijāraṃ kuruṣe yadi /
children.translated_text: Take a lover, O large-eyed one — you would be without a lover otherwise;

children.text: yathā vejikayā pūrvamardhasnāte patau kṛtam // Suk_69.1 (=321) //
children.translated_text: as <s>Vejikā</s> formerly did when her husband was half-bathed. Suk_69.1 (=321)

children.text:
asti sthānaṃ kalāsthānaṃ nāma /
tatraiko vaṇiksutaḥ tasya bhāryā ca vejikā nāmātivallabhā /
anyadā ca taṃ bhartāraṃ snāpayantī upapatiṃ pūrvakṛtasaṅkenaṃ pathi gacchataṃ dṛṣṭvā nātra pānīyaṃ pracuramiti miṣāntaraṃ kṛtvā pānīyānayanavyājādgṛhānnirgatā jāreṇa sākaṃ bahukālaṃ ca sthitā /
tato 'rdhasnātaṃ patiṃ muktvā tathā sthitā kumuttaraṃ karotviti praśnaḥ /
uttaram- śukaḥ tataḥ jāreṇa bhuktā svapativañcanaṃ vicintyātmānaṃ kūpe cikṣepaḥ /
tataḥ kolāhalaḥsaṃvṛttaḥ /
kūpe kāpi varākī patitāstīti pravādaḥ sañjātaḥ /
tena tatpatistadvacanaṃ śrutvā vyacintayat-nūnaṃ sā matpatnī kūpe patitā bhaviṣyati-iti drutaṃ gatvāvalokayāmāsa /
tatastāṃ kūpādākṛṣyānīyāmānayat /
iti kathāṃ śrutvā prabhāvatī suptā /
children.translated_text: There is a place called <s>Kalāsthāna</s> (Seat of Arts). There lived a merchant's son, and his wife, named <s>Vejikā</s>, was very dear to him. One day, while she was bathing her husband, she saw her paramour — with whom she had a prior arrangement — walking along the road. Making the excuse 'There is not enough water here,' under the pretext of fetching water, she left the house and stayed a long time with her lover. Then, having left her half-bathed husband and remained thus — 'What answer should she give?' — this is the question. The answer: The parrot said: Then, having been enjoyed by her lover, and thinking of how to deceive her husband, she threw herself into a well. A commotion arose. The rumor spread: 'Some poor woman has fallen into the well!' Her husband, hearing those words, thought: 'Surely that is my wife who has fallen into the well!' — and went quickly to look. Then he pulled her out of the well and brought her home. Having heard this tale, <s>Prabhāvatī</s> fell asleep.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau ekonasaptatitamī kathā //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the sixty-ninth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot).

children.text: START Suk 70:
children.translated_text: START Suk 70:

children.text:
etāvatīnāṃ kathānāṃ paryante tadbhatī madano deśāntarādāgataḥ /
tasmiṃścāgate sā tathaiva tasminsnehalābhūt /
śuka evaṃ mandaṃ mandaṃ paṭhati-
children.translated_text: At the conclusion of all these tales, her husband <s>Madana</s> returned from abroad. And when he arrived, she felt the same affection for him as before. The parrot then softly recited —

children.text: anurāgo vṛthā stroṣu strīṣu garvo vṛthā tathā /
children.translated_text: "Attachment to women is in vain; pride in women is likewise in vain.

children.text: priyo 'haṃ sarvadā haysyā mamaiṣā sarvadā priyā // Suk_70.1 (=322) //
children.translated_text: 'I am always dear to her, and she is always dear to me' — // Suk_70.1 (=322) //

children.text:
paraṃ madano na śṛṇoti /
upahāsya tadā caivaṃ vadati-"yaḥ kaściddhitaṃ vākyaṃ śṛṇoti karoti ca sa paratreha ca śarmabhāgbhavati' /
iti muhurmuhuḥ paṭhitaṃ madanaḥ śrutvā pṛcchati /
tataḥ sā svayameva śaṅkitā kathayati /
uktañca-
children.translated_text: But <s>Madana</s> does not listen. Laughing, [the parrot] then speaks thus: 'Whoever hears and acts upon beneficial words attains happiness both in this world and the next.' When <s>Madana</s>, hearing this recited again and again, inquired, she herself, being apprehensive, confessed. And it is said —

children.text: sarvatra śucayo dhīrāḥ sukarmabalagarvitāḥ /
children.translated_text: "The virtuous are everywhere pure, proud of their good deeds and strength;

children.text: kukarmamayasaṃtrastāḥ pāpāḥ sarvatra śaṅkitāḥ // Suk_70.2 (=323) //
children.translated_text: The wicked, trembling from their evil deeds, are everywhere suspicious." // Suk_70.2 (=323) //

children.text:
āryaputra! tvameva vandyo yasya veśmani trivikramānītayugamadhyādekaḥ śukaḥ sarveṣā lokānāṃ hitabhāṣako 'tra bandhupitṛsthānīyo viśeṣato mama /
yathā yathā sā śukaṃ stauti tathā tathā śuko lajjate /
uktañca-
children.translated_text: "O noble husband! You alone are to be honored, in whose house there is one parrot brought by <s>Trivikrama</s> from a former age, who speaks for the welfare of all people — here he stands in the place of a kinsman and a father, especially to me." The more she praised the parrot, the more the parrot felt ashamed. And it is said —

children.text: bau jai mārai macchalī to uṇṇau karei /
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] If a crane kills fish, it does not rise [in esteem];

children.text: sīhu ju mārai mattagaaṇahacampiā dharei // Suk_70.3 (=324) //
children.translated_text: A lion that kills a maddened elephant is served and honored. // Suk_70.3 (=324) //

children.text: [bakaḥ yadi mārayati matsyān sa punarna karoti /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit chāyā:] If a crane kills fish, it gains nothing thereby;

children.text: siṃho yo mārayati mattagajanātha sevito dhriyate] // Suk_70.3* (=324*) //
children.translated_text: A lion that slays a maddened elephant is served and sustained. // Suk_70.3* (=324*) //

children.text:
tato madanastadvacanaṃ śrutvāha-kiṃ tava śukenopakṛtan /
kathamīdṛgguṇo 'sau jātaḥ /
sā prāha--svāmin! satyasya vāco vaktā śrotā ca na labhyate /
uktañca--
children.translated_text: Then <s>Madana</s>, having heard her words, asked: "What good has your parrot done for you? How has he become so virtuous?" She said: "My lord! A speaker of truth and a listener of truth are both rare to find. And it is said —

children.text: sulabhā puruṣā rājan satataṃ priyavādinaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Easy to find, O king, are men who always speak pleasant words;

children.text: apriyasya tu patyasya vaktā śrotā ca durlabhaḥ // Suk_70.4 (=325) //
children.translated_text: But one who speaks the unpleasant truth, and one who listens to it — both are rare." // Suk_70.4 (=325) //

children.text: mahilā capalā svāminniḥsnehā guṇavarjitā /
children.translated_text: "Women are fickle, O lord, devoid of affection, lacking in virtue,

children.text: kuvikalpā tanuprajñā yathoktaṃ satyameva tat // Suk_70.5 (=326) //
children.translated_text: Of wicked designs and feeble understanding — what has been said [about them] is indeed true." // Suk_70.5 (=326) //

children.text: manyate sukṛtaṃ naiva patiputraparāṅmukhī /
children.translated_text: "She considers no good deed [worthy], turning away from husband and son,

children.text: pūrvasnehamayī mṛdvī kṛtakāryātiniṣṭhurā // Suk_70.6 (=327) //
children.translated_text: Affectionate at first and gentle, but utterly cruel once her purpose is achieved." // Suk_70.6 (=327) //

children.text: uktañca-
children.translated_text: And it is said —

children.text: kurvanti tāvatprathamaṃ priyāṇi yāvanna jānanti naraṃ prasaktam /
children.translated_text: "They perform pleasing acts at first, so long as they do not know the man to be ensnared;

children.text: jñātvā ca taṃ manmathapāśabaddhaṃ grastāmiṣaṃ mīnamivoddharanni // Suk_70.7 (=328) //
children.translated_text: But once they know him bound by the noose of <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love), they cast him off like a fish after swallowing the bait." // Suk_70.7 (=328) //

children.text: samudravīcīva calasvabhāvāḥ sandhyābhrarekheva muhurtarāgāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Fickle by nature like ocean waves, their passion as fleeting as an evening cloud-streak,

children.text: striyaḥ kṛtārthāḥ puruṣaṃ nirarthaṃ niṣpīḍitālaktakavattyajanti // Suk_70.8 (=329) //
children.translated_text: Women, once their purpose is fulfilled, discard a man rendered useless, like squeezed-out lac dye." // Suk_70.8 (=329) //

children.text: sammohayanti madayanti viḍambayanti nirbhartsayanti ramayanti viṣādayanti /
children.translated_text: "They bewitch, intoxicate, mock, rebuke, delight, and distress —

children.text: etāḥ praviśya hṛdayaṃ sadayaṃ narāṇāṃ kiṃ nāma vāmanayanā na samācaranti // Suk_70.9 (=330) //
children.translated_text: Entering the tender hearts of men, what do these women with sidelong glances not do?" // Suk_70.9 (=330) //

children.text:
svāmin! tvayi proṣite mayā kañcitkālaṃ tvadviyogaḥ soḍhaḥ /
paścācca kusakhīsaṅgatā /
puruṣāntaraṃ rantukāmayā mayā gamanavighātinī sārikā hatā /
anena śukena tu vacanaprapañcena saptatidināni sthāpitāham /
ato mayā karmaṇā pāpaṃ na vihitaṃ manasā tu kṛtam /
adyaprabhṛti tvaṃ mama jīvanamaramasvāmī /
iti śrutvā madanaḥ śukaṃ pṛcchati /
sa āha-
children.translated_text: "My lord! When you were abroad, I endured your separation for some time. But afterward, through the company of a wicked female friend, I, desiring to take pleasure with another man, killed the <s>sārikā</s> (mynah bird) who obstructed my going. But this parrot, through the artifice of his words, kept me in place for seventy nights. Thus, I have not committed sin by deed, though I did so in thought. From this day forth, you are the lord of my life and death." Having heard this, <s>Madana</s> questioned the parrot. He said —

children.text: prayojanamavijñāya jñātvā cātha manīṣiṇā /
children.translated_text: "A wise man should not speak rashly without understanding the purpose [first],

children.text: sahasaiva na vaktavyamacintyo vidhinirṇayaḥ // Suk_70.10 (=331) //
children.translated_text: And even after understanding it — for the decree of fate is inscrutable." // Suk_70.10 (=331) //

children.text: vihivihiaṃ laddha piasaṃgo jīviaṃ dhaṇaṃ dhaṇṇaṃ /
children.translated_text: [Prakrit:] What is ordained by fate has been obtained: the company of the beloved, life, wealth, and grain;

children.text: juttaṃ savvaṃ jaṇavaaṇaṃ viaṇaviḍambaṇā ṇihilā // Suk_70.11 (=332) //
children.translated_text: All that is fitting is [mere] people's talk — the mockery of words is utterly empty. // Suk_70.11 (=332) //

children.text: [vidhivihitaṃ ciralabdhaṃ priyasaṅgo jīvitaṃ dhana dhānyam /
children.translated_text: [Sanskrit chāyā:] What is ordained by fate has been obtained after long waiting: the company of the beloved, life, wealth, and grain;

children.text: yuktaṃ sarvaṃ janavacanaṃ vacanaviḍambanā nikhilā] // Suk_70.11* (=332*) //
children.translated_text: All that is fitting is [mere] people's talk — the mockery of words is entirely empty. // Suk_70.11* (=332*) //

children.text: svāmin! yadyapi kathayituṃ na yujyate tarhi śṛṇu /
children.translated_text: "My lord! Although it is not proper to speak [of this], still, listen:

children.text: mūrkhāṇāṃ madyapānāṃ ca nārīṇāṃ rogiṇāmapi /
children.translated_text: "Of fools, of drunkards, of women, of the sick,

children.text: svāminkāmāturāṇāṃ ca khinnānāṃ kopināṃ tathā // Suk_70.12 (=333) //
children.translated_text: Of those tormented by desire, O lord, of the weary, and of the angry, // Suk_70.12 (=333) //

children.text: mattapramattabhīrūṇāṃ kṣudhārtānāṃ viśeṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: Of the intoxicated, the heedless, the frightened, and especially the hungry —

children.text: sukṛtaṃ skhalitaṃ cāryā na gṛhṇānti kṣamānvitāḥ // Suk_70.13 (=334) //
children.translated_text: The noble, endowed with forbearance, do not take note of either their good deeds or their lapses." // Suk_70.13 (=334) //

children.text: uktañca bhārate-
children.translated_text: And it is said in the <s>Mahābhārata</s> —

children.text: daśa dharmaṃ na jānanti dhṛtarāṣṭra nibodha tān /
children.translated_text: "Ten do not know <s>dharma</s> — hear them, O <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>:

children.text: mattaḥ pramatta unmattaḥ śrāntaḥ kruddho bubhukṣitaḥ /
children.translated_text: The intoxicated, the heedless, the mad, the exhausted, the angry, the hungry,

children.text: tvaramāṇaśca lubdhaśca bhītaḥ kāmī ca te daśa // Suk_70.14 (=335) //
children.translated_text: The hasty, the greedy, the frightened, and the lustful — these are the ten." // Suk_70.14 (=335) //

children.text:
asyāśca kukṛtaṃ kṣamyatām /
atrārthe nāsyā doṣaḥ /
kusakhīsaṅgādiyam /
uktam-
children.translated_text: "Her misdeed should be forgiven. In this matter, no fault attaches to her. It was due to the company of a wicked female friend. It is said —

children.text: asatāṃ saṅgadoṣeṇa sādhavo yānti vikriyām /
children.translated_text: "Through the fault of association with the wicked, even the virtuous undergo corruption;

children.text: duryodhanaprasaṅgena bhīṣmo goharaṇe gataḥ // Suk_70.15 (=336) //
children.translated_text: Through association with <s>Duryodhana</s>, <s>Bhīṣma</s> went along with the cattle raid." // Suk_70.15 (=336) //

children.text: vidyādhareṇa tanayā bhuktā rājñaḥ purā chalāt /
children.translated_text: "A <s>Vidyādhara</s> (celestial being) once enjoyed a king's daughter by deception;

children.text: patināpi subhuktāpi nirdeṣiti vicāritā // Suk_70.16 (=337) //
children.translated_text: Even though she had been well-enjoyed by her husband, upon examination she was found blameless." // Suk_70.16 (=337) //

children.text:
śukaḥ kathāṃ madanāgre kathayāmāsa-asti jagatītale malayo nāma parvataḥ /
tasya śṛṅge manoharaṃ nāma gandharvapuram /
tatra madanonāma gandharvaḥ /
tasya bhāryā ratnāvalī /
tayoḥ sutā madanamañjarī /
tasyā rūpasampadaṃ dṛṣṭvā devo vā dānavo vādhomukho muhyati /
na ko 'pi tadanurūpo varo labhyate yasya sā dīyate /
athānyadā nāradaḥ samāyātaḥ /
so 'pyasyā rūpamavalokya mūrcchitaḥ sakāmo 'bhūt /
paścāllabdhasaṃjñena ṛṣiṇā sā śaptā /
uktañca-
children.translated_text: The parrot then narrated a tale before <s>Madana</s>: "There exists on the surface of the earth a mountain called <s>Malaya</s>. On its peak is a <s>Gandharva</s> city called <s>Manohara</s>. There [lives] a <s>Gandharva</s> named <s>Madana</s>. His wife is <s>Ratnāvalī</s>. Their daughter is <s>Madanamañjarī</s>. Seeing the abundance of her beauty, even a god or a demon would be overcome with desire, casting down his eyes. No suitor worthy of her could be found to whom she might be given. Then one day <s>Nārada</s> arrived. He too, beholding her beauty, became faint and filled with desire. Afterward, having recovered his senses, the sage cursed her. And it is said —

children.text: taruṇī ramaṇī ratiramyatayā pramadā sukhadā ca sadā samadā /
children.translated_text: "She is a young woman, a charming one, delightful in the joy of love, a beauty granting pleasure, ever proud;

children.text: yadi sā subhagā hṛdayenihitā kva jayaḥ kva jayaḥ kva jayaḥ kva jayaḥ // Suk_70.17 (=338) //
children.translated_text: If such a fortunate one is established in the heart — where is victory, where is victory, where is victory, where is victory?" // Suk_70.17 (=338) //

children.text:
yadetasyā rūpe dṛṣṭe me smarajvaro jātaḥ tadiyaṃ śīlaviḍambanāṃ prāpsyate /
tato rājā praṇamya prāha--svāmin! prasanno bhūtvā prasādaṃ kuru /
nārada āha- "nāsyāḥ śīlakhaṇḍena doṣo bhaviṣyati na ca pativirahaḥ /
meruparvate vipulāpurīnivāsī kanakaprabho nāma gandharvaḥ /
sa tava putryā varo bhaviṣyati' /
ityuktvā nārado yayau /
tato munivacanena tena gandharveṇa sodvāhitā /
so 'nyadā tāṃ muktvā kailāsaṃ yayau /
sāpi tadvayogārtā śilāpaṭṭe luṭhantī vastrādirahitā kenacidvidyādhareṇa rūpātiśamavalokya saṃyogārthaṃ prārthitā /
sā taṃ na vācchati /
tatastena tadbharturgandharvarūpa kṛtvā sā bhuktā /
tataḥ kālakrameṇa tasyā bhartā gṛhamāgataḥ /
tāṃ suratasukhasantuṣṭāmapaśyat /
"paropabhuktadeheyam' iti tāṃ dṛṣṭāṃ matvā sāvaśyaṃ vadhyeti niścitya caṇḍikālayaṃ yayau /
yāvattadagrato mārayati tāvadanyayā phūtkṛtam-"svāmini! mama tvayā varo datto yattava gandharvacakravartī putro bhaviṣyati /
tatkathaṃ putramukhama dṛṣṭvā vipatsye' /
evaṃ vilapantyāstasyāḥ puratastāṃ prati devī prāha-he gandharvavīra! nāsyāḥ ko 'pi doṣaḥ /
kintu vidyādhareṇeyaṃ tvadīyarūpamayena māyayā bhuktā /
tato 'jānantyā asyā na doṣaḥ /
anyacca muniśāpo vidyate /
tata idaṃ sañjātam-"śāpavṛttāntaśca niveditaḥ, tato munivacanādiyaṃ nirdeṣā tvayā grāhyā'-iti gaurīvacanaṃ śrutvā sa niḥśaṅkaṃ tayā saha svasthānaṃ gatastathaiva sukhato 'bhūt" /
tato vaṇikputra /
yadi madvacaḥ pramāṇaṃ tadaināmaduṣṭāṃ prati prasādaṃ kartumarhasi' /
iti kīravacanānmadanenānugṛhītā /
tato haridatto 'pi putrāgamanatuṣṭo mahotsavaṃ cakāra /
tasminmahotsave divyamālā patitā /
taddarśane śukasārikātrivikramāṇāṃ śāpamokṣātsvargagamanaṃ babhūva /
madano 'pi priyayā prabhāvatyā saha sukhāni bhuṅkte /
children.translated_text: "'Since the fever of desire arose in me upon seeing her beauty, she shall suffer the ruin of her chastity.' Then the king bowed and said: 'O lord! Be gracious and grant your favor.' <s>Nārada</s> said: 'There shall be no fault from the breach of her chastity, nor separation from her husband. On Mount <s>Meru</s>, in the city of <s>Vipulā</s>, there dwells a <s>Gandharva</s> named <s>Kanakaprabha</s>. He shall be your daughter's husband.' Having spoken thus, <s>Nārada</s> departed. Then, by the sage's word, she was married to that <s>Gandharva</s>. One day, he left her and went to <s>Kailāsa</s>. She, tormented by separation from him, rolling upon the stone slab, divested of her garments, was seen by a certain <s>Vidyādhara</s> who, beholding the surpassing beauty of her form, solicited her for union. She did not desire him. Then he, assuming the form of her <s>Gandharva</s> husband, enjoyed her. In due course, her husband came home. He saw her satisfied with the pleasure of lovemaking. Thinking 'This woman's body has been enjoyed by another,' and upon seeing her, resolving 'She must certainly be killed,' he went to the temple of <s>Caṇḍikā</s>. Just as he was about to slay her before [the goddess], another voice cried out: 'O mistress! You granted me the boon that your son, a <s>Gandharva</s> emperor, would be born to me. How then shall I perish without seeing my son's face?' As she wailed thus, the goddess spoke to him regarding her: 'O <s>Gandharva</s> hero! There is no fault in her. Rather, a <s>Vidyādhara</s>, assuming your very form, enjoyed her through illusion. Therefore, no blame attaches to her who did not know [the truth]. Moreover, there is the sage's curse. Hence this came to pass.' The circumstances of the curse were also reported. 'Therefore, by the sage's word, she is blameless and should be accepted by you.' Hearing the words of <s>Gaurī</s> (the goddess), he went without suspicion with her to his own abode and lived happily as before." "Therefore, O merchant's son, if my word is authoritative, you should be gracious toward this blameless woman." By the parrot's words, [<s>Prabhāvatī</s>] was forgiven by <s>Madana</s>. Then <s>Haridatta</s> too, delighted by his son's return, held a great festival. At that festival, a divine garland fell [from heaven]. Upon seeing it, the parrot, the mynah bird, and <s>Trivikrama</s> were released from their curse and ascended to heaven. And <s>Madana</s> enjoyed happiness with his beloved <s>Prabhāvatī</s>.

children.text: iti śukasaptatau saptatitamī kathā /
children.translated_text: Thus ends the seventieth tale in the <s>Śukasaptati</s>.

children.text: iti śukasaptatiḥ samāptā //
children.translated_text: Thus the <s>Śukasaptati</s> (Seventy Tales of the Parrot) is concluded.
